why_it_matters: Reference ROS integration for DVL-aided navigation.
hackathon_notes: Archived; port the parsing to ROS 2 or use dvl-python directly (also archived). No LICENSE file, so all rights reserved by default.

name: Ping Python
summary: Python library and examples for Blue Robotics Ping echosounder and Ping360 scanning sonar using the Ping protocol.
why_it_matters: Cheap altimeter and sonar input for underwater navigation and obstacle sensing.
hackathon_notes: pip install bluerobotics-ping; requires the hardware or Ping Viewer logs.

name: Ping Viewer
summary: Desktop application to view and record data from Blue Robotics Ping echosounder and Ping360 sonar.
why_it_matters: Fast way to record sonar logs for offline SLAM or odometry experiments.
hackathon_notes: Prebuilt releases; logs can be replayed into ping-python.

name: ping360_sonar ROS package
summary: ROS package that drives the Ping360 scanning sonar and publishes scans as images and laser-scan style messages.
why_it_matters: Gets low-cost scanning sonar into a ROS SLAM or obstacle pipeline.
hackathon_notes: Needs the sonar; the laser-scan output plugs into standard 2D SLAM tools.

name: Project DAVE
summary: Gazebo-based underwater simulation environment from the Naval Postgraduate School and partners, extending UUV Simulator with DVL, sonar, bathymetry and manipulation models.
why_it_matters: Navy-funded underwater sim with realistic DVL and sonar sensors for testing AUV nav without water.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1 Noetic + Gazebo 11 via Docker; setup is heavy, budget half a day. No push here since 2024-08; the ROS 2 port continues in the IOES-Lab/dave fork.

name: NPS underwater multibeam sonar plugin
summary: GPU (CUDA) multibeam sonar simulation plugin for Gazebo producing physically motivated sonar imagery.
why_it_matters: Synthetic sonar data for testing sonar odometry and SLAM.
hackathon_notes: Needs an NVIDIA GPU; used within DAVE.

name: UUV Simulator
summary: Gazebo/ROS packages for underwater vehicle simulation with hydrodynamics, thrusters and sensors; archived.
why_it_matters: Many underwater-nav papers and DAVE build on it; useful for reference models.
hackathon_notes: Archived and tied to old ROS/Gazebo; use Stonefish or DAVE instead.

name: Stonefish
summary: C++ simulation library for marine robotics with hydrodynamics, underwater rendering and sensors including DVL, USBL, multibeam and forward-looking sonar; has a ROS wrapper.
why_it_matters: One of the few open sims with credible underwater nav sensors for AUV dead reckoning and sonar-based localization work.
hackathon_notes: Build with CMake; use stonefish_ros for ROS integration. Good for a DVL+USBL EKF demo.

name: HoloOcean ROS bridge
summary: ROS bridge for HoloOcean, BYU's Unreal Engine based underwater simulator with DVL, IMU, depth, sonar and acoustic modem sensors.
why_it_matters: Photo-realistic underwater sim with multi-agent acoustic comms, useful for cooperative AUV nav.
hackathon_notes: HoloOcean itself is not installed from PyPI (that package is an old 0.5.x): the source repo is only visible to a GitHub account linked to Epic Games, then pip install the client and run holoocean.install('Ocean') for the world package. The bridge is ROS 2 (Humble/Jazzy), Docker recommended. Needs a decent GPU.

name: USBL Simulator
summary: C++ library and ROS 2 (Humble) node that simulates ultra-short baseline acoustic positioning measurements; a Gazebo plugin is only listed as a planned feature.
why_it_matters: USBL is the main absolute fix for submerged vehicles; simulated USBL lets a team test an aided-INS filter.
hackathon_notes: ROS 2 colcon build; generate USBL fixes to fuse with DVL dead reckoning.

name: AuvEstimator
summary: Work-in-progress AUV state estimator fusing DVL, IMU and barometer two ways, a 15-state EKF and a GTSAM factor graph with custom DVL and barometer factors, with ROS 1 (Kinetic/Melodic, Python 2.7) wrappers.
why_it_matters: Small, readable DVL-aided INS example to start a GNSS-free underwater nav filter from.
hackathon_notes: Dormant since 2021; treat as a starting template, not a dependency. No LICENSE file, so all rights reserved by default.

name: SMARC navigation
summary: Localization and SLAM components for the SMARC AUVs (KTH), including EKF localization with IMU, DVL and multibeam sonar against a feature map.
why_it_matters: Research AUV navigation from a Swedish maritime robotics centre, showing map-aided underwater localization.
hackathon_notes: Fork of smarc-project/smarc_navigation frozen in 2021; the upstream was updated until 2024, so start there. ROS 1 era; read for architecture.

name: sonar-SLAM
summary: Underwater SLAM for robots with multibeam imaging sonar, from Stevens Institute research on BlueROV-class vehicles, combining sonar feature extraction and pose-graph optimization.
why_it_matters: One of the more complete open sonar SLAM pipelines; directly relevant to GNSS-free underwater navigation.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1 with sample bags; budget time for dependencies.

name: BRUCE
summary: BlueROV underwater SLAM and exploration code from Stevens Institute, combining sonar-based SLAM with active exploration planning.
why_it_matters: Predecessor to sonar-SLAM; shows SLAM-driven exploration underwater.
hackathon_notes: Dormant since 2020.

name: DISO
summary: Direct imaging sonar odometry: estimates vehicle motion directly from forward-looking imaging sonar frames without feature extraction.
why_it_matters: Sonar odometry is a key aid when DVL bottom-lock or vision fails in turbid water.
hackathon_notes: C++ with ROS; try on the provided datasets first.

name: Vortex AUV
summary: Guidance, navigation and control software from NTNU's student Vortex team for competition AUVs and ROVs, built on ROS 2.
why_it_matters: A complete, actively maintained student AUV GNC stack to borrow structure from.
hackathon_notes: ROS 2 workspace; sim integration via their companion repos.

name: Autoware
summary: Meta-repository for Autoware, the open-source ROS 2 autonomous driving stack covering localization (NDT, EKF), perception, planning and control.
why_it_matters: The biggest open ground-vehicle autonomy stack; its localization modules are a mature map-based alternative when GNSS is degraded.
hackathon_notes: Heavy: use the Docker images and the planning simulator. For a hackathon, lift single packages such as NDT scan matcher or the EKF localizer.

name: Autoware Universe
summary: The broad package collection of Autoware with experimental and production-candidate modules, including localization add-ons such as YabLoc, landmark-based localizers and the pose estimator arbiter.
why_it_matters: Holds Autoware's extra localization modules; the core NDT scan matcher and EKF localizer have moved to autoware_core.
hackathon_notes: Pick packages and run them standalone with rosbags; autoware_ndt_scan_matcher and autoware_ekf_localizer now live in autoware_core, not here.

name: AWSIM
summary: Unity-based digital-twin simulator for Autoware with simulated lidar, camera, GNSS and IMU.
why_it_matters: Lets a team exercise Autoware localization without a car.
hackathon_notes: Prebuilt binaries for Ubuntu with an NVIDIA GPU. Licence is split: code Apache-2.0, but assets (including release content) are CC BY-NC, so non-commercial use only, and the docs may not be publicly re-hosted.

name: Baidu Apollo
summary: Baidu's open autonomous driving platform, including the multi-sensor fusion localization module combining GNSS RTK, IMU and lidar map matching.
why_it_matters: Its MSF localization design is a well-documented reference for GNSS/INS/lidar fusion in vehicles.
hackathon_notes: Very heavy to build; read the localization module docs and code rather than deploy.

name: grid_map
summary: C++ library and ROS integration for multi-layer 2.5D grid maps, widely used for elevation and traversability mapping.
why_it_matters: Standard data structure for terrain-aware off-road navigation.
hackathon_notes: apt install ros-<distro>-grid-map; convert DEMs or point clouds to layers quickly.

name: elevation_mapping
summary: Robot-centric elevation mapping for rough terrain navigation, started at ETH Zurich and now maintained by ANYbotics, that fuses range data into a probabilistic 2.5D map. This entry is the leggedrobotics fork of ANYbotics/elevation_mapping.
why_it_matters: Classic baseline for terrain mapping on legged and wheeled robots.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1; this fork is dormant since 2022, while upstream ANYbotics/elevation_mapping was updated in 2024. Prefer the GPU version.

name: elevation_mapping_cupy
summary: GPU-accelerated elevation and traversability mapping from ETH Zurich, supporting semantic layers and learned traversability, used on ANYmal robots.
why_it_matters: Terrain-aware planning for off-road robots needs a live elevation and traversability map; this is the modern GPU version.
hackathon_notes: Needs CUDA; Docker image available. Feed a depth camera or lidar and get a traversability layer.

name: traversability_estimation
summary: ETH package that computes traversability from elevation maps using slope, roughness and step-height filters.
why_it_matters: Simple, explainable geometric traversability baseline.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1, dormant; reimplement the filters with grid_map.

name: Wild Visual Navigation
summary: System that learns visual traversability online from pre-trained vision features and robot self-supervision, deployed on legged robots in forests.
why_it_matters: Learned traversability that adapts in minutes, relevant for unstructured off-road nav.
hackathon_notes: Needs a GPU and a camera bag; offline demo scripts help.

name: WayFAST
summary: Self-supervised traversability prediction for wheeled field robots that learns from RGB-D, with labels from kinodynamic traction estimates. The repo holds only the network models, one training notebook and a dataset download link; the traction estimator and navigation stack are not included.
why_it_matters: Agricultural/field traversability learning without hand labels.
hackathon_notes: Dormant; use for method reference. No LICENSE file, so all rights reserved by default.

name: BenchNav
summary: Gymnasium-based PyTorch simulator for benchmarking off-road navigation planners under uncertain, probabilistic traversability, with synthetic terrain generation.
why_it_matters: Lightweight way to compare off-road planners without a robot.
hackathon_notes: Docker setup via make build-gpu or build-cpu, or pip install from the clone (not on PyPI); fetch the dataset and models with scripts/download_dataset_and_model.sh, then run the tutorial notebooks. No LICENSE file, so all rights reserved by default.

name: RELLIS-3D
summary: Multi-modal off-road dataset from Texas A&M with lidar, camera, IMU and GNSS plus semantic annotations collected on a ground robot.
why_it_matters: A standard benchmark for off-road perception and localization.
hackathon_notes: Download only the sequences you need; ROS bags are large. Unmaintained since 2022; the data itself is static and still usable. Data and code are CC BY-NC-SA 3.0, so non-commercial use only.

name: TartanDrive
summary: Tools and utilities for the TartanDrive off-road driving dataset from CMU's AirLab, recorded on an ATV with multi-modal sensors.
why_it_matters: Large-scale off-road vehicle dynamics and perception data for learning traversability.
hackathon_notes: Data is large; use the provided loaders and a subset.

name: HOUND
summary: Autonomy stack for a small-scale high-speed off-road vehicle from the UW MuSHR group, with BeamNG simulator integration and Jetson Orin deployment.
why_it_matters: Affordable off-road platform with sim-to-real tooling.
hackathon_notes: Docker-based install; real hardware optional. BeamNG license needed for sim.

name: Loco Positioning node firmware
summary: Firmware for Bitcraze Loco Positioning UWB anchors and tags (DW1000), supporting two-way ranging and TDoA modes.
why_it_matters: Off-the-shelf UWB infrastructure for GNSS-denied indoor positioning tests.
hackathon_notes: Needs Loco nodes; configure anchors with the Crazyflie client.

name: Crazyflie simulation
summary: Minimal simulation models and tooling for Crazyflie in Webots and Gazebo; the README says it is not actively maintained and not realistic in dynamics.
why_it_matters: Hardware-free swarm prototyping.
hackathon_notes: Webots is the easiest entry.

name: MRS UAV System
summary: Czech Technical University's multi-robot UAV platform with control, estimation (including GNSS-denied modes), planning and simulation, field-tested in outdoor swarm deployments.
why_it_matters: Mature outdoor-swarm stack with several localization back-ends to choose from.
hackathon_notes: Install via apt; simulation tutorials are good. Moving between ROS 1 and ROS 2 versions, so check the branch.

name: UVDAR
summary: Mutual relative localization for UAV swarms using blinking ultraviolet LEDs and UV-sensitive cameras, from CTU MRS.
why_it_matters: Radio-silent relative localization, attractive when RF is jammed or must stay off.
hackathon_notes: Needs special UV hardware for real use; simulated in the MRS Gazebo setup.

name: Buzz
summary: Domain-specific programming language for robot swarms with swarm-level primitives such as neighbour queries, virtual stigmergy and swarm membership.
why_it_matters: Expresses swarm behaviours compactly; used with ROS and drones in MIST Lab research.
hackathon_notes: Builds cleanly; bindings to real robots require extra work.

name: ROS2swarm
summary: ROS 2 package providing a library of swarm behaviours (aggregation, dispersion, flocking) and an easy-to-extend framework, tested on TurtleBot-class robots.
why_it_matters: Ready-made ground swarm behaviours in ROS 2.
hackathon_notes: Launch in Gazebo with multiple TurtleBots. Not maintained any more (README); branches target ROS 2 Dashing, Foxy and Galactic.

name: Swarm-SLAM
summary: Sparse, decentralized collaborative SLAM for multi-robot systems on ROS 2, supporting lidar, stereo and RGB-D with inter-robot loop closures under limited communication.
why_it_matters: Shared map and relative localization across a team without central infrastructure.
hackathon_notes: ROS 2 with heavy deps; try on the provided datasets before robots.

name: DCL-SLAM
summary: Distributed collaborative lidar SLAM for robotic swarms with lightweight LiDAR-Iris descriptors for inter-robot place recognition and minimal data exchange.
why_it_matters: Low-bandwidth multi-robot lidar mapping.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1 package; test with multi-robot bags.

name: CoLRIO
summary: Placeholder repo: it only holds a README pointing to zhongshp/Co-LRIO, where the code lives. CoLRIO is ROS 2 centralized lidar-ranging-inertial state estimation for robotic swarms that offloads optimization to a server and uses UWB inter-robot ranges (ICRA 2024).
why_it_matters: Shows how UWB ranging tightens swarm state estimation when GNSS is out.
hackathon_notes: Use zhongshp/Co-LRIO (Apache-2.0, C++). ROS 2 Foxy and GTSAM 4.2a8; build is sensitive to versions.

name: Kimera-Multi
summary: Index repo for Kimera-Multi, a distributed multi-robot metric-semantic SLAM system with robust distributed pose-graph optimization.
why_it_matters: Multi-robot mapping with peer-to-peer communication is core to swarm and team operations.
hackathon_notes: Multi-repo install; budget a full day. Use their datasets for a demo.

name: Omni-swarm
summary: Decentralized omnidirectional visual-inertial-UWB state estimation for aerial swarms from HKUST, combining VIO, UWB ranges and map-based place recognition.
why_it_matters: Shows fusing UWB ranging with VIO for drift-bounded relative swarm localization.
hackathon_notes: Dormant since 2022; superseded by D2SLAM.

name: D2SLAM
summary: Decentralized and distributed collaborative visual-inertial SLAM for aerial swarms from HKUST.
why_it_matters: Swarm-scale relative localization and mapping for UAV teams.
hackathon_notes: Needs a CUDA GPU and the provided Docker images; runs on a quad fisheye rig, RealSense stereo or TUM datasets. Study rather than deploy.

name: EGO-Swarm
summary: Decentralized multi-quadrotor extension of EGO-Planner with inter-agent collision avoidance and trajectory sharing over a network.
why_it_matters: Open reference for drone swarms that coordinate paths without a central server, relevant to contested comms scenarios.
hackathon_notes: Simulation launches many drones on one machine; trajectory broadcast assumes reliable comms - an interesting knob to degrade in a hackathon.

name: uwb-localization (MAV swarm)
summary: ROS library fusing UWB ranging with IMU for accurate 3D localization of MAV swarms, used in a 2017 drone light show.
why_it_matters: Compact UWB+IMU fusion reference.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1 and dormant since 2018.

name: Swarm relative localization (ETH PBL)
summary: Infrastructure-less relative localization for decentralized swarm formation of nano-drones using UWB ranging (IROS 2023).
why_it_matters: Relative positioning without anchors, the realistic case for field swarms.
hackathon_notes: The repo holds only a Python demo of the algorithm (demo.py) and a PDF supplement; no Crazyflie or UWB firmware is included.

name: UWB Software Library (USL)
summary: FreeRTOS UWB library for DW1000 on Crazyflie providing double-sided two-way ranging and UWB data messaging between drones.
why_it_matters: Peer-to-peer ranging building block for anchor-free relative localization.
hackathon_notes: Flash as Crazyflie app; ranging between two nodes in a few lines. Fork of iGNSS/uwb-software-library, tested against a pinned crazyflie-firmware commit. No LICENSE file, so all rights reserved by default.

name: GEARdrones
summary: Lightweight STM32 drone control and multi-agent localization system combining a flight controller, UWB relative localization and a monitor tool.
why_it_matters: Low-cost hardware+software reference for UWB relative swarm localization.
hackathon_notes: Custom hardware; dormant since 2023.

name: UTIL UWB TDoA dataset tools
summary: Dataset and scripts for UWB time-difference-of-arrival measurements from Bitcraze's Loco Positioning System, collected by University of Toronto.
why_it_matters: Real UWB data for testing ranging-based estimators without hardware.
hackathon_notes: Download and run the provided EKF example as a baseline. Unmaintained since 2021; the data itself is static and still usable.

name: pyMHT
summary: Track-oriented multi-hypothesis multi-target tracker in Python developed for maritime radar tracking research.
why_it_matters: Compact MHT implementation for comparison against Stone Soup.
hackathon_notes: Dormant; useful as a readable algorithm reference.

name: motpy
summary: Simple Python library for tracking-by-detection multi-object tracking with Kalman filters and IoU/feature association.
why_it_matters: Fast, minimal tracker to sit behind a drone detector in a demo.
hackathon_notes: pip install motpy; a few lines to track YOLO boxes.

name: BoxMOT
summary: Pluggable collection of modern multi-object trackers (ByteTrack, BoT-SORT, OC-SORT, StrongSORT and others) for detector outputs, in Python and C++.
why_it_matters: Drop-in visual tracking for camera-based drone detection.
hackathon_notes: pip install boxmot and wrap your detector; pick ByteTrack for speed.

name: ByteTrack
summary: ECCV 2022 multi-object tracker that associates both high- and low-confidence detections, improving tracking through occlusion.
why_it_matters: Strong baseline for tracking small, intermittently detected drones in video.
hackathon_notes: Use via BoxMOT or Ultralytics tracker configs rather than the original training code.

name: Ultralytics YOLO
summary: Widely used Python package for YOLO-family detection, segmentation and tracking with training, export to edge runtimes and built-in trackers.
why_it_matters: Fastest route to a custom vision drone detector trained on Anti-UAV or similar data.
hackathon_notes: pip install ultralytics; fine-tune on a drone dataset in hours with a GPU. Check AGPL licensing for deployment.

name: Anti-UAV
summary: Official repository of the Anti-UAV challenge and benchmark for detecting and tracking UAVs in RGB and thermal infrared video, with dataset links (Anti-UAV300/410/600) and baselines.
why_it_matters: The main public benchmark for vision-based C-UAS tracking, including thermal.
hackathon_notes: Download a subset, train a YOLO detector plus tracker, report on their metric.

name: UAV Detection and Tracking Benchmark
summary: Code and configs for benchmarking drone detection and tracking across Anti-UAV, Drone-vs-Bird and MAV-VID datasets, including format converters.
why_it_matters: Saves time on dataset wrangling for a vision C-UAS comparison.
hackathon_notes: Use the COCO conversion scripts first. No LICENSE file, so all rights reserved by default. The three datasets keep their own terms.

name: Open Drone ID Wireshark dissector
summary: Lua Wireshark dissector that decodes Remote ID broadcast frames over Wi-Fi and Bluetooth.
why_it_matters: Debugging aid for Remote ID sniffers.
hackathon_notes: Drop the Lua into the Wireshark plugin folder.

name: RID (ESP32 Remote ID receiver)
summary: ESP32 Remote ID receiver built on opendroneid-core-c and a fork of sxjack's electronic ID classes.
why_it_matters: Ten-dollar Remote ID sensor node.
hackathon_notes: PlatformIO project for VS Code (not the Arduino IDE), developed on a TTGO ESP32 board with a 1.14-inch LCD; it shows lat/lon of one UAV on the display.

name: WarDragon docs
summary: Documentation hub for WarDragon, an SDR-based RF sensing appliance for drone detection; open components are documented here, while commercial kits add closed features.
why_it_matters: Useful architecture reference for a low-cost RF C-UAS sensor.
hackathon_notes: Docs only; follow links to the open component repos.

name: WarDragon FPV energy scan
summary: GNU Radio based scanner that checks known analog FPV video frequencies for energy and publishes alerts over ZMQ; the optional confirmation detector is closed source.
why_it_matters: Simple, explainable RF detection of FPV drones, a growing threat class.
hackathon_notes: Needs GNU Radio 3.10, gr-inspector and an SDR such as Pluto.

name: samples2djidroneid
summary: Decodes DJI DroneID (OcuSync 2.0) frames from SDR I/Q recordings, building on proto17's reverse engineering and Kismet.
why_it_matters: Recovers DJI drone and pilot location telemetry from RF, filling the gap for drones without standard Remote ID.
hackathon_notes: Needs high-rate I/Q captures; decoding is slow with interference.

name: dji_droneid
summary: Original reverse engineering of DJI DroneID with MATLAB/Octave scripts that demodulate frames, C++ turbo-code helpers and a GNU Radio correlation test flowgraph.
why_it_matters: Foundational work behind open DJI DroneID decoders.
hackathon_notes: Use for understanding the PHY; prefer samples2djidroneid for decoding.

name: RFUAV
summary: Code for the RFUAV benchmark dataset for UAV detection and identification from RF signals, using a two-stage STFT spectrogram detection and classification model.
why_it_matters: Recent learned RF drone classification with a public dataset.
hackathon_notes: Start from the provided spectrogram models; raw data size is large.

name: DroneRF
summary: LabVIEW programs to record RF signals plus MATLAB and Python code for drone detection and identification, accompanying the DroneRF dataset (Mendeley Data, CC BY 4.0).
why_it_matters: Widely cited RF detection baseline.
hackathon_notes: Dormant since 2021; good for a quick baseline classifier.

name: VolAnti
summary: Open-source acoustic drone detector that listens for propeller noise; explicitly detection and alerting only.
why_it_matters: Acoustic sensing covers drones that emit no RF, such as fibre-optic FPVs.
hackathon_notes: Breadboard build guide; new project, verify claims on your own recordings.

name: Batear
summary: Low-cost edge-only acoustic drone detector on ESP32-S3 with encrypted LoRa or Ethernet alerting.
why_it_matters: Cheap distributed acoustic sensor network for perimeter awareness.
hackathon_notes: ESP-IDF build; tune thresholds per site.

name: cnspy trajectory evaluation
summary: Python package that aligns an estimated trajectory with ground truth from CSV files, associates timestamps and reports position/attitude error metrics, including NEES from pose covariance.
why_it_matters: Consistency checks (NEES) matter as much as RMSE when judging a GNSS-denied filter; this tool computes both from plain CSV.
hackathon_notes: pip install cnspy-trajectory-evaluation; estimated CSV must carry pose covariance. Use evo for quick plots, this when you need filter consistency.

name: GTSfM
summary: End-to-end structure-from-motion pipeline built on GTSAM, with pluggable front-ends (classical and learned matchers) and distributed execution via Dask.
why_it_matters: Builds georeferenceable 3D maps from drone or ground imagery, which can serve as prior maps for visual localization.
hackathon_notes: No compilation: `uv tool install .` (or `pip install .` in Python 3.12) from a recursive checkout, then `gtsfm run` opens a browser workspace with sample scenes; `gtsfm execute` is the CLI path for your own image folders. Expect long runtimes on large sets - downsample.

name: CANboat
summary: Toolkit for NMEA 2000 networks: a PGN decoder/analyzer plus utilities to read, write and convert N2K and NMEA 0183 messages, used largely for reverse-engineering marine bus traffic.
why_it_matters: Gives raw access to ship sensor buses (GNSS, heading, AIS, depth), useful for maritime nav integrity monitoring and spoofing detection research.
hackathon_notes: Build analyzer and pipe candump/actisense logs through it to JSON. Needs a CAN or N2K gateway for live data; sample logs work offline.

name: Beluga
summary: Modern C++17 library of Monte Carlo Localization algorithms with a ROS 2 node that is a drop-in replacement for the Nav2 AMCL package.
why_it_matters: Map-based particle-filter localization for ground robots operating without GNSS; easier to extend than legacy AMCL.
hackathon_notes: Swap beluga_amcl for nav2_amcl in a Nav2 launch file; same parameters. Good base for adding custom sensor models.

name: Fraunhofer IIS Jammertest 2025 dataset
summary: Real-world GNSS interference recordings from Jammertest 2025 at Andoya, Norway, covering jamming, spoofing, meaconing and multi-emitter scenarios, with metadata for classification, characterization and direction finding.
why_it_matters: Rare open real-world interference data from live jamming trials, suited to training and testing interference detectors and classifiers.
hackathon_notes: Data is chunked HDF5 under dataset/ (Git LFS; the README points to an identical GitLab mirror for the full download) plus train/test split lists. There are no loader modules - the README only gives an h5py inspection snippet, so budget time to write your own loader before building a jamming/spoofing classifier on one scenario class.

name: 14 Lectures on Visual SLAM (2nd ed.) code
summary: Companion code for the second edition of Gao Xiang's visual SLAM textbook: Lie groups, nonlinear optimization, feature VO, direct methods, back-end and loop closure examples in C++.
why_it_matters: One of the most-used hands-on routes into visual SLAM internals; good for bringing a team up to speed fast.
hackathon_notes: Each chapter builds standalone; dependency versions (Pangolin, Sophus, g2o) are old - use the bundled 3rdparty or a Docker image.

name: CU Boulder GNSS SDR Collection
summary: University of Colorado Boulder collection of MATLAB software-defined GNSS receiver code-bases, organized per constellation (GPS, Galileo, GLONASS, BeiDou), with linked sample data sets.
why_it_matters: Teaching-grade multi-constellation receivers you can read end to end, from acquisition to tracking and navigation.
hackathon_notes: Point the settings file at one of the provided IQ data sets and run. MATLAB licence required; slow on long recordings.

name: GVINS
summary: Tightly coupled GNSS-visual-inertial estimator that fuses raw GNSS pseudorange and Doppler with VIO in a factor graph, giving drift-free global poses and smooth local tracking.
why_it_matters: Shows how raw GNSS measurements degrade gracefully into VIO when satellites are blocked, a core pattern for contested or urban PNT.
hackathon_notes: ROS1 (Melodic/Noetic) only; run on the GVINS dataset bags. Porting to ROS 2 is non-trivial.

name: SLAM Toolbox (MATLAB)
summary: Joan Sola's MATLAB SLAM toolbox with EKF-SLAM (`ekf` branch) and graph-SLAM (`graph` branch) variants, landmark parameterizations (points, lines, inverse depth) and simulated or real sensor support, written for teaching and prototyping.
why_it_matters: Readable reference for EKF-SLAM landmark handling, by the author of the widely cited Lie theory and quaternion kinematics notes.
hackathon_notes: Runs in MATLAB with simulated worlds out of the box; not maintained, use for understanding rather than deployment.

name: fuse
summary: ROS framework for sensor fusion as factor-graph optimization: plugin sensor models, motion models and publishers on top of Ceres, supporting both smoothing and fixed-lag estimation.
why_it_matters: A more flexible alternative to robot_localization EKF when you need delayed measurements, robust losses or custom constraints.
hackathon_notes: Use the fuse tutorials or the ROSCon UK 2025 workshop Docker image; plugin config in YAML. Ceres dependency builds slowly.

name: ROSCon UK 2025 State Estimation workshop
summary: Materials for an eight-task ROS 2 state estimation workshop at ROSCon UK 2025, with a Docker image, recorded bags and step-by-step exercises using robot_localization and fuse.
why_it_matters: Ready-made, containerized curriculum for wiring wheel odometry, IMU and GNSS into a ROS 2 estimator.
hackathon_notes: docker compose run with the provided compose file; work through tasks in order. Fastest way to get a fused ROS 2 pose estimate running.

name: mil-sym-ts
summary: TypeScript/JavaScript renderer for MIL-STD-2525 (D and later) military symbology, producing single-point and multi-point tactical graphics for web maps.
why_it_matters: Standard-conformant symbols are the expected visual language for any common operational picture or C2 demo.
hackathon_notes: npm package; render SIDC codes to SVG/canvas and drop onto Leaflet/Cesium/OpenLayers layers. Multi-point graphics need control-point ordering per the standard.

name: MIT VNAV lab data
summary: Pointer repo for the ROS bag files used in MIT's Visual Navigation for Autonomous Vehicles course exercises.
why_it_matters: Supplies the datasets that make the VNAV labs runnable outside MIT.
hackathon_notes: Only a README with a download link; fetch bags alongside VNAV-labs.

name: MIT VNAV labs
summary: Lab assignments for MIT 16.485 Visual Navigation for Autonomous Vehicles: ROS, 3D geometry, trajectory optimization, feature tracking, two-view geometry, VIO and place recognition.
why_it_matters: A structured, graded path from ROS basics to visual-inertial navigation, built by the SPARK lab behind Kimera.
hackathon_notes: Labs assume Ubuntu + ROS; pick individual labs (feature tracking, two-view geometry) as warm-ups.

name: MoveIt 2
summary: Motion planning framework for ROS 2 manipulators: kinematics, collision checking, planners (OMPL, Pilz, STOMP) and real-time servoing.
why_it_matters: Relevant when a vehicle carries an arm or gimbal-like mechanism; outside pure navigation but the ROS 2 standard for manipulation planning.
hackathon_notes: Binary install via apt; use the MoveIt Setup Assistant for a new robot. Overkill unless your platform has an arm.

name: Jammertest test plan
summary: Official test catalog and plan for Jammertest, Norway's annual live GNSS jamming and spoofing event, maintained by the Norwegian Public Roads Administration.
why_it_matters: The reference for which interference scenarios were transmitted when, needed to label any Jammertest recording.
hackathon_notes: Use the per-year plan to map timestamps in Jammertest datasets to emitted scenarios.

name: Isaac ROS Visual SLAM
summary: ROS 2 package wrapping NVIDIA's GPU-accelerated cuVSLAM for stereo visual(-inertial) odometry and SLAM on Jetson and x86 GPUs.
why_it_matters: Real-time VIO on embedded Jetson hardware with low CPU load, a practical GNSS-denied odometry source for drones and UGVs.
hackathon_notes: Use the Isaac ROS dev container; RealSense or ZED stereo works out of the box. Jetson Orin recommended.

name: Nav2 tutorials
summary: Tutorial packages referenced by docs.nav2.org: example planner, controller and behavior-tree plugins, SLAM and GPS waypoint following setups.
why_it_matters: Shortest path to custom Nav2 plugins and GPS-based outdoor navigation in ROS 2.
hackathon_notes: Clone into a ROS 2 workspace matching your distro branch; the GPS waypoint follower demo runs in Gazebo.

name: SLAM Handbook (public release)
summary: Release repo for the SLAM Handbook (Cambridge University Press), edited by Carlone, Kim, Barfoot, Cremers and Dellaert, published incrementally in three parts from late 2024.
why_it_matters: Current, expert-written reference covering factor graphs through spatial AI; free drafts for the whole team.
hackathon_notes: Download chapter PDFs from the release page; factor-graph chapter is the best starting point.

name: VAARA Jammertest dataset
summary: University of Vaasa public GNSS dataset recorded at Jammertest 2024, released in batches from autumn 2025 under a Finland-NSF project on secure satellite navigation.
why_it_matters: Second independent real-world interference dataset, useful for cross-dataset validation of detectors.
hackathon_notes: Check README for which batches are released; pair with the Jammertest plan for labels.

name: STEAM
summary: Simultaneous Trajectory Estimation and Mapping engine from UTIAS: a C++ nonlinear least-squares library with continuous-time Gaussian-process trajectory priors on Lie groups.
why_it_matters: Continuous-time estimation handles asynchronous, motion-distorted sensors such as spinning radar and lidar.
hackathon_notes: Library, not an application; see steam_icp for a ready odometry pipeline built on it.

name: ROSA (ROS Agent)
summary: NASA JPL's LangChain-based AI agent that lets operators query and command ROS 1 and ROS 2 systems in natural language through a set of ROS introspection and control tools.
why_it_matters: A credible, lab-backed reference for putting an LLM in the loop of a robot stack, with tool boundaries an operator can audit.
hackathon_notes: pip install jpl-rosa; demo runs against turtlesim in Docker. Add custom tools for your MAVROS/Nav2 topics.

name: ROS MCP Server
summary: Model Context Protocol server that exposes ROS topics, services and parameters (via rosbridge) to LLM clients such as Claude or GPT, for ROS 1 and ROS 2.
why_it_matters: Fastest way to let an LLM inspect and drive an existing robot without changing robot code.
hackathon_notes: Run rosbridge on the robot and point the MCP client config at the server; works with sim (Gazebo/Isaac). Add safety limits before anything flies.

name: ROS MCP Server demos
summary: Standalone demos for driving robots with natural language through the ROS MCP server: a Tugbot in a Gazebo warehouse, a Unitree Go2 with the CHAMP controller, a PX4 drone via MAVROS (Gazebo and real hardware) and TurtleBot3 in Ignition Gazebo.
why_it_matters: Worked examples shorten the path from install to a talking robot demo.
hackathon_notes: Each sub-folder is a self-contained project with its own README; the PX4 demo (takeoff, patterns, orbit, RTL via MAVROS) is the most relevant. Run one demo end to end before customizing the server.

name: WiseVision ROS 2 MCP
summary: MCP server that lets AI agents discover and operate ROS 2 robots: topic echo/publish, services, actions and introspection, implemented natively in ROS 2 rather than through rosbridge.
why_it_matters: Native ROS 2 alternative for LLM control without a rosbridge hop.
hackathon_notes: Fastest path is the Docker image (wisevision/ros2_mcp:jazzy or :humble) as the MCP client's stdio command - ROS 2 does not need to be installed on the host. Start with ROS2_MCP_READONLY=1 so the agent can inspect but not publish.

name: LCAS ROS 2 MCP
summary: ROS 2 MCP server from the Lincoln Centre for Autonomous Systems: tools to list and echo topics, inspect message/service/action interfaces, fetch camera images for VLM analysis and send simple drive commands, plus canned analysis prompts. Runs as a ROS 2 package or via Docker Compose (SSE on port 8000).
why_it_matters: University-maintained option for agricultural/field robot agent experiments.
hackathon_notes: Smaller project; compare with ros-mcp-server before committing.

name: MAVLinkMCP
summary: MCP server bridging an LLM to a drone over MAVLink, exposing arming, takeoff, waypoint and telemetry tools via MAVSDK.
why_it_matters: Direct template for a natural-language drone mission interface on PX4/ArduPilot SITL.
hackathon_notes: Pair with PX4 or ArduPilot SITL; never point at a real vehicle without geofence and human confirm.

name: mavlink-mcp (ArduPilot)
summary: MCP server for flying ArduPilot vehicles from AI agents over MAVLink, covering missions, camera vision and SITL workflows.
why_it_matters: Another ready LLM-to-autopilot bridge, oriented to ArduPilot missions.
hackathon_notes: Young project; test thoroughly in SITL.

name: ardupilot-mcp (safety-gated)
summary: SITL-first MCP server for talking to ArduPilot vehicles over MAVLink, with explicit safety gating of commands.
why_it_matters: Its safety-gate design is a useful pattern for keeping an LLM from issuing unsafe flight commands.
hackathon_notes: `pipx install ardupilot-mavlink-mcp`, point it at SITL (tcp:127.0.0.1:5760). Read-only by default; arming needs `--enable-actuation`, and real (non-loopback) links also need `--allow-real-vehicle`. Its prearm-diagnosis and single-reader-thread design are worth copying.

name: QGIS MCP
summary: MCP server plus QGIS plugin that lets an LLM create projects, load layers, run processing algorithms and execute PyQGIS code in QGIS Desktop.
why_it_matters: Natural-language GIS analysis for terrain, route and coverage products in a mission-planning demo.
hackathon_notes: Install the plugin, start the socket server in QGIS, add the MCP server to the client. Arbitrary code execution - sandbox it.

name: qgis-mcp (nkarasiak)
summary: MCP bridge that lets AI agents drive QGIS Desktop: a QGIS plugin runs a TCP socket server inside QGIS and a FastMCP server exposes about 125 tools (layers, feature editing, processing, rendering, styling, layouts/atlas, cross-layer SQL). Supports QGIS 3.28 to 4.x; the plugin installs from the QGIS plugin manager and the server runs via uvx.
why_it_matters: More recent alternative if the original QGIS MCP lags behind QGIS releases.
hackathon_notes: Same plugin-plus-server pattern; check QGIS version compatibility.

name: GIS MCP Server
summary: MCP server giving LLMs geospatial operations through Shapely, PyProj, GeoPandas and Rasterio: geometry ops, CRS transforms, distances and raster analysis, without a desktop GIS.
why_it_matters: Headless geodesy/GIS tool layer an agent can call for coordinate conversion and spatial reasoning.
hackathon_notes: pip install gis-mcp; no QGIS needed. Good for an agent that must reason about coordinates and areas.

name: LLM-Geo (Autonomous GIS)
summary: Research prototype of an LLM-driven 'autonomous GIS' that turns a spatial question into a solution graph, generates code and executes the analysis to return maps and numbers.
why_it_matters: Early worked example of LLM planning over geospatial workflows, a building block for agentic mission planning.
hackathon_notes: Notebook-driven; needs an LLM API key. Use as design reference rather than a dependency.

name: TypeFly
summary: LLM-based robot control framework: an OpenAI model turns a natural-language request plus a YOLO scene description into a short Python plan built from the robot's registered skills, which is then executed. Ships wrappers for a virtual webcam robot, DJI Tello, Unitree Go2 and Petoi.
why_it_matters: Shows how to constrain LLM output into a small, verifiable command language for drones, cutting latency and risk.
hackathon_notes: `pip install -e .`, add an OpenAI key and run `typefly-run`; the default virtual robot uses a webcam, so no hardware is needed. A Tello needs both a Wi-Fi and an ethernet adapter. Swap in a MAVSDK-based robot wrapper to target PX4.

name: PromptCraft-Robotics
summary: Microsoft's collection of prompts and an AirSim-based ChatGPT drone simulator accompanying the 'ChatGPT for Robotics' work.
why_it_matters: Classic starting point for prompting LLMs to produce drone control code in simulation.
hackathon_notes: No longer updated and AirSim itself is archived; mine the prompts, run elsewhere.

name: ROS-LLM
summary: Framework for natural-language interaction with ROS robots, letting an LLM call robot functions and chain behaviors.
why_it_matters: Earlier ROS-native LLM integration; useful comparison to MCP-based designs.
hackathon_notes: Not updated since 2023; prefer ROSA or the MCP servers for new work.

name: OpenFly
summary: Platform for outdoor aerial vision-language navigation: multi-engine simulators (UE, GTA V, Google Earth, 3DGS), automated data collection toolchain, a large benchmark and a keyframe-aware VLN model.
why_it_matters: Largest open aerial VLN benchmark, for agents that fly to places described in words.
hackathon_notes: Heavy downloads and GPU; use the released dataset with the baseline model rather than regenerating data.

name: AerialVLN
summary: Benchmark and simulator (AirSim/UE-based) for vision-and-language navigation by UAVs in city-scale environments, with baseline agents.
why_it_matters: The first widely used aerial VLN benchmark; baseline for language-commanded drone navigation.
hackathon_notes: Large simulator assets; plan download time. Linux + GPU.

name: CityNav
summary: Language-goal aerial navigation dataset over real-city 3D point clouds with geographic information, plus baselines that use map-based landmark grounding.
why_it_matters: Links language goals to real geography, close to how operators describe destinations.
hackathon_notes: Dataset plus training code; GPU needed for baselines.

name: SatNav
summary: Scalable benchmark and platform for long-horizon UAV vision-language navigation built from satellite imagery (NeurIPS 2026 Datasets track).
why_it_matters: Satellite-imagery grounding matches what a real UAV can carry as a prior map, so results transfer better to GNSS-denied ops.
hackathon_notes: New release; check README for data availability before planning around it.

name: 3DG-VLN
summary: UAV vision-language navigation method that feeds high-resolution front and downward views plus a coarse 3D target direction, updated online, into waypoint prediction for precise see-and-reach flight. Releases the UAV-VLN-FOV benchmark (2,717 trajectories, seen/unseen-object/unseen-scene splits), code and weights; runs in AirSim with TravelUAV environments.
why_it_matters: Recent aerial VLN method to compare against benchmark baselines.
hackathon_notes: Research code; reproduce only if you need a SOTA aerial VLN baseline.

name: InternNav
summary: PyTorch toolbox for embodied navigation on Habitat and Isaac Sim, covering vision-language navigation (VLN-CE and continuous-trajectory VLN) and point, image or trajectory goal navigation, with 10+ baselines, 6 benchmarks, the InternData-N1 dataset and the InternVLA-N1 dual-system model.
why_it_matters: Brings recent VLA-style navigation models into one toolkit.
hackathon_notes: Large models and simulators; use the provided checkpoints.

name: NaVid / Uni-NaVid
summary: Evaluation code for NaVid and Uni-NaVid, video-based VLMs that plan the next navigation step from monocular RGB history in continuous VLN environments.
why_it_matters: Shows map-free, camera-only language navigation, relevant when maps and GNSS are unavailable.
hackathon_notes: Requires Habitat and large checkpoints; evaluation only.

name: GNM / ViNT / NoMaD
summary: Code and checkpoints for general visual navigation foundation models (GNM, ViNT, NoMaD) that drive robots from camera images toward image goals or explore, with ROS deployment code.
why_it_matters: Pretrained camera-only navigation policies that run on small robots, a ready learned navigation baseline.
hackathon_notes: Deploy NoMaD on a Jetson-class robot with a fisheye camera; topological graph from a teleop run.

name: LM-Nav
summary: Code for LM-Nav, which composes a language model, CLIP and a visual navigation model to follow natural-language route instructions without language-annotated robot data.
why_it_matters: Early demonstration of building language navigation from off-the-shelf pretrained parts.
hackathon_notes: Mostly notebook-level; read for the architecture.

name: VLMaps
summary: Builds visual-language maps by fusing pretrained visual-language features into a 3D reconstruction, enabling open-vocabulary landmark navigation from natural language.
why_it_matters: Language-queryable maps are a natural interface for operators tasking robots.
hackathon_notes: Habitat-based data; GPU needed for feature extraction.

name: ConceptGraphs
summary: Builds open-vocabulary 3D scene graphs from RGB-D by associating 2D foundation-model detections across views, then lets an LLM plan over the graph.
why_it_matters: Object-level semantic maps an LLM can reason about, useful for tasking and situational awareness.
hackathon_notes: Heavy dependencies (SAM, CLIP, GroundingDINO); start from Replica examples.

name: NavGPT
summary: Purely LLM-based vision-and-language navigation agent that reasons explicitly over textual observations to choose actions (AAAI 2024).
why_it_matters: Readable baseline for LLM reasoning in navigation, with prompts you can adapt.
hackathon_notes: Needs an LLM API and R2R/Matterport data.

name: Co-NavGPT
summary: Multi-robot exploration and object search where an LLM assigns frontier goals to robots from a merged semantic map.
why_it_matters: LLM as a multi-agent tasker, a pattern for swarm search missions.
hackathon_notes: Habitat simulation; adapt the goal-assignment prompt for your own swarm sim.

name: IEZ (INS-EKF-ZUPT)
summary: Python implementation (one 9-state script, plus ESP32 logger firmware) of a foot-mounted INS with EKF and zero-velocity updates for pedestrian dead reckoning, with sample datasets from two foot-mounted MPU6050 IMUs.
why_it_matters: Compact reference for the standard ZUPT pedestrian tracker that underpins dismounted soldier navigation.
hackathon_notes: Runs offline on included data; reproduce with any cheap IMU strapped to a boot.

name: MPU6050 ZUPT
summary: Arduino library forked from MPU6050_tockn that reads and calibrates an MPU6050 and streams angles and time series to Python plotting scripts. The README says foot-mounted INS / ZUPT support is planned but the repo is under construction; no zero-velocity detector or INS code is in it yet.
why_it_matters: Low-cost hardware path to a working foot-mounted INS demo.
hackathon_notes: Only the IMU reading and calibration part exists; you would write the ZUPT detector and INS yourself (see pajaraca/IEZ or OpenShoe for the algorithm). Needs an MPU6050 and an Arduino-class board; expect heading drift without magnetometer aiding.

name: OpenPDR
summary: Planned device-independent pedestrian dead reckoning platform that never got past its outline: the repo holds MATLAB ellipsoid-fit accelerometer and magnetometer calibration scripts with sample logs, an Allan-variance note, and reference papers on filtering and AHRS. No step detection or step-length code is present.
why_it_matters: Simple step-and-heading baseline for phone-based indoor navigation.
hackathon_notes: Unmaintained since 2017. Only the ellipsoid-fit IMU/magnetometer calibration scripts are reusable; for actual PDR code look elsewhere.

name: PDR Android app
summary: Android app implementing pedestrian dead reckoning with step detection and orientation from phone sensors.
why_it_matters: Phone-native PDR demo you can install and walk with during a hackathon.
hackathon_notes: The author marks it unmaintained (written in 2014). It is an Eclipse ADT project, so expect to import and migrate it into Android Studio, and the manifest lacks a Google Maps API key. Use the step-detection and heading code as reference; fuse with Wi-Fi or UWB for correction.

name: RIDI
summary: Code for RIDI, which regresses velocity from smartphone IMU data with learned models to reduce inertial drift for pedestrian navigation.
why_it_matters: Ancestor of RoNIN/TLIO-style learned inertial odometry.
hackathon_notes: Old dependencies; prefer RoNIN for new work.

name: Indoor Location Competition 2.0
summary: Data and baseline code from Microsoft Research's Indoor Location Competition 2.0: smartphone IMU, Wi-Fi, BLE and magnetic traces across many buildings with floor maps.
why_it_matters: Large real indoor dataset for Wi-Fi/magnetic fingerprinting plus PDR fusion.
hackathon_notes: Sample data in repo; full set on Kaggle. Good for a fingerprinting + PDR fusion demo.

name: MILUV devkit
summary: Python devkit for MILUV, a multi-UAV indoor localization dataset with UWB ranging (including inter-robot), vision and IMU data.
why_it_matters: UWB plus vision data with multiple vehicles, for relative and indoor localization.
hackathon_notes: Download the dataset via devkit scripts; examples include UWB EKF.

name: PVI polarization navigation dataset
summary: Dataset combining stereo camera, IMU, polarization camera and high-precision GPS for polarization-aided navigation research.
why_it_matters: Polarized skylight gives a GNSS-free heading reference; open data for it is rare.
hackathon_notes: README only links a Google Drive; check data format before planning.

name: celnav
summary: Small Tkinter desktop app for celestial navigation on a boat: computes the Nautical Almanac daily-page data with PyEphem, reduces sights and fixes position from two LOPs, correcting for vessel motion between sights.
why_it_matters: Scriptable sight reduction for a GNSS-free position fix.
hackathon_notes: Python 2 code (imports ConfigParser, Tkinter) with no commits since 2018; port the celnav.py core to Python 3 or use it as an algorithm reference. Pair with a camera-based sun or star altitude to automate a fix.

name: OpenCPN celestial navigation plugin
summary: OpenCPN plugin for entering sextant sights and plotting lines of position and fixes on the chart.
why_it_matters: Puts celestial fixes into a real chart plotter workflow.
hackathon_notes: Build against OpenCPN SDK; useful as UI reference.

name: SPEL Open Star Tracker
summary: Open star tracker software from the University of Chile space lab, flown on SUCHAI nanosatellites.
why_it_matters: Flight-tested open star tracker code, a basis for attitude from stars.
hackathon_notes: Python prototype; compare with tetra3/LOST.

name: Astrometry.net
summary: Blind astrometric solver that identifies star fields in arbitrary images and returns the precise sky pointing, using geometric hash indexes of star catalogs.
why_it_matters: Proven lost-in-space plate solving; with a known time and gravity vector it yields attitude and coarse position.
hackathon_notes: apt install astrometry.net plus index files for your field of view; solve-field on a night-sky photo.

name: Skyfield
summary: Python library for high-accuracy positions of stars, planets and Earth satellites, with proper time scales and reference frames.
why_it_matters: Gives the ephemerides any celestial or satellite-based nav prototype needs.
hackathon_notes: pip install skyfield; downloads ephemeris files on first use.

name: navalm
summary: Nautical almanac and celestial sight reduction for Unix/Linux with CLI, ncurses and web interfaces.
why_it_matters: Self-contained offline almanac, handy for air-gapped demos.
hackathon_notes: Very new and small; verify outputs against a published almanac.

name: REVE
summary: Radar Ego Velocity Estimator: robust 3D ego-velocity from 4D mmWave radar Doppler point clouds, the front-end used by Doer's radar-inertial odometry.
why_it_matters: Radar velocity works in smoke, fog and darkness, a strong aid for GNSS-denied drones.
hackathon_notes: ROS1; run on the provided datasets, pairs with christopherdoer/rio.

name: Yeti radar odometry
summary: Radar odometry for Navtech spinning radar that compensates motion distortion and Doppler effects.
why_it_matters: Shows the corrections needed to make scanning radar odometry accurate.
hackathon_notes: Unmaintained; evaluated on Oxford Radar RobotCar.

name: STEAM-ICP
summary: Continuous-time lidar, radar, lidar-inertial and radar-inertial odometry built on the STEAM library.
why_it_matters: Ready continuous-time radar odometry pipeline evaluated on Boreas.
hackathon_notes: Docker build; test on Boreas sequences.

name: HKUST 4D Radar-Inertial Odometry
summary: Optimization-based, point-uncertainty-aware radar-inertial odometry for 4D radar.
why_it_matters: Sliding-window alternative to EKF radar-inertial methods.
hackathon_notes: ROS1 build; run on public 4D radar datasets.

name: ETH Radar-Inertial Odometry
summary: Graph-based, sparse radar-inertial odometry estimation from ETH ASL, using GTSAM.
why_it_matters: Factor-graph radar-inertial baseline for drones in degraded visual environments.
hackathon_notes: ROS build; datasets linked in README.

name: RINO
summary: Non-iterative, adaptively loosely coupled radar-inertial odometry for spinning (scanning) radar, built on the ORORA radar odometry baseline; the radar pose uncertainty from its voting step feeds a Kalman filter (T-ASE 2025).
why_it_matters: Recent scanning-radar inertial method to benchmark against.
hackathon_notes: ROS Noetic / Ubuntu 20.04, catkin build, Sophus built manually. Replay MulRan with its file player (radar + IMU); a Boreas demo is shown.

name: ORORA
summary: Outlier-robust radar odometry using graduated non-convexity-style estimation on radar feature correspondences (ICRA 2023).
why_it_matters: Robust estimation is what keeps radar odometry stable amid clutter and multipath.
hackathon_notes: Evaluated on MulRan and Oxford Radar; ROS build.

name: TBV Radar SLAM
summary: Radar SLAM with verified loop closures built on CFEAR radar odometry.
why_it_matters: Full radar-only SLAM, including loop closure, for long GNSS-denied drives.
hackathon_notes: ROS1 + Docker; pairs with CFEAR.

name: ReFeree
summary: Lightweight radar global descriptor for radar place recognition (RA-L 2024).
why_it_matters: Cheap loop-closure and relocalization for radar-only navigation.
hackathon_notes: Small codebase; test on MulRan/Oxford Radar.

name: Open-RadVLAD
summary: Fast radar place recognition using VLAD-style aggregation over radar polar scans.
why_it_matters: Simple radar relocalization baseline.
hackathon_notes: Evaluate on Oxford Radar RobotCar.

name: K-Radar
summary: 4D radar dataset and benchmark for object detection in diverse weather, with raw 4D tensors, lidar, cameras and GNSS.
why_it_matters: Bad-weather 4D radar data, also usable for radar odometry and perception experiments.
hackathon_notes: Very large dataset; request access and use subsets.

name: RadarHD
summary: Learns to generate high-resolution, lidar-like point clouds from low-cost single-chip mmWave radar.
why_it_matters: Makes cheap radar usable for mapping and localization in smoke or darkness.
hackathon_notes: Pretrained model and data provided; GPU needed.

name: pylgrim
summary: Playground GNSS positioning code in Python/numpy that computes a static GPS position (50-100 m accuracy per the README) from RINEX 2.11 observations, with parsers for RINEX nav/obs, SP3 and IONEX plus Klobuchar, IONEX and VMF1 delay models. Works on RINEX files, not raw IF samples, so there is no acquisition or tracking stage.
why_it_matters: Python-readable receiver chain for teaching and quick experiments.
hackathon_notes: Unmaintained since 2020; use for learning.

name: GNSS-DSP-tools
summary: Python code generators, acquisition and tracking scripts for GPS, Galileo, GLONASS, BeiDou and Xona Pulsar LEO signals, operating on IQ recordings.
why_it_matters: Broadest signal coverage among lightweight SDR toolkits; quick to test a new recording.
hackathon_notes: Install numpy, scipy and numba (conda is the easy route), then run acquire-<system>-<signal>.py or track-*.py on an IQ file from any SDR. No compile step beyond Numba's JIT.

name: GNSS-matlab
summary: MATLAB code to generate GNSS PRN and secondary codes, dataless signals and spectra, with real captures.
why_it_matters: Reference signal generation for interference and receiver studies.
hackathon_notes: Old but self-contained; MATLAB needed.

name: TRN particle filter examples
summary: MATLAB particle filtering examples for terrain-referenced navigation, comparing standard, auxiliary, mixture and out-of-sequence measurement particle filters (accompanies an IEEE TAES 2018 paper).
why_it_matters: Directly addresses the ambiguous-terrain problem that breaks naive TRN.
hackathon_notes: Runs in MATLAB with simulated terrain; port the update logic to Python for a DEM demo.

name: Deep-TERNALOC
summary: Deep-learning-based terrain-referenced navigation and localization project from ITU Aerospace Research Center, with particle filter baselines.
why_it_matters: Learning-based TRN reference from an aerospace lab.
hackathon_notes: Partial code; read with the project website.

name: FederNet
summary: Terrain relative navigation for planetary landing that detects craters with a Mask R-CNN and matches them to a catalog using projective invariants.
why_it_matters: Crater-based TRN, the space analogue of map-matching navigation.
hackathon_notes: Thesis code; TensorFlow 2 and pretrained weights needed.

name: ESVIO
summary: Event-based stereo visual-inertial odometry combining stereo event and image streams with IMU (RA-L/IROS 2023).
why_it_matters: Event cameras keep tracking under fast motion and HDR where frame VIO fails.
hackathon_notes: ROS1; run on provided event datasets.

name: EKLT
summary: Asynchronous photometric feature tracking that combines events and frames (IJCV 2019).
why_it_matters: Feature tracks with very low latency, a front-end for event VIO.
hackathon_notes: Old ROS1 code; use for reference.

name: EMVS
summary: Event-based multi-view stereo: semi-dense 3D reconstruction from a moving event camera with known poses (IJCV 2018).
why_it_matters: Mapping from event cameras for depth in HDR scenes.
hackathon_notes: ROS1; reference implementation.

name: DEVO
summary: Deep Event Visual Odometry: learned monocular event-only VO trained on simulated events, generalizing to real benchmarks (3DV 2024).
why_it_matters: Event-only odometry without frames, useful at night or under strobing light.
hackathon_notes: PyTorch + CUDA; pretrained checkpoint available.

name: rpg_dvs_ros
summary: ROS drivers and tools for DVS/DAVIS event cameras, including calibration and rendering.
why_it_matters: Standard way to get event-camera data into ROS 1.
hackathon_notes: ROS1 only; for ROS 2 look at vendor drivers.

name: OpenEB
summary: Prophesee's open SDK for event-based vision: camera drivers, data formats, visualization and algorithm building blocks.
why_it_matters: Entry point for the most common commercial event sensors.
hackathon_notes: Build from source or packages; sample recordings available without hardware.

name: Tonic
summary: Python library for event-based datasets and transforms, in the style of torchvision.
why_it_matters: Fast access to many event datasets for learning-based event navigation.
hackathon_notes: pip install tonic (or conda-forge); use transforms such as ToFrame or voxel grids. The project is looking for a new maintainer, so pin a version.

name: v2e
summary: Converts conventional video into realistic synthetic DVS event streams with sensor noise modeling.
why_it_matters: Lets you produce event data for training/testing without owning an event camera.
hackathon_notes: Not on PyPI: create a conda env, install CUDA PyTorch, then `pip install -e .` from a clone (or use the Colab notebook). Needs a GPU; conversion runs far slower than real time, so test with --stop on a short clip of drone footage first.

name: E2VID
summary: Reconstructs intensity video from event streams with a recurrent network, enabling frame-based methods on event data.
why_it_matters: Bridge that lets standard VO/feature pipelines consume event camera data.
hackathon_notes: Pretrained model; PyTorch.

name: Event feature tracking (EM-ICP)
summary: MATLAB implementations of event-based feature tracking methods from the Penn GRASP lab.
why_it_matters: Reference algorithms for event-based VIO front-ends.
hackathon_notes: MATLAB; pair with MVSEC data.

name: LoranC receiver
summary: Hobby project to build a DSP-based Loran-C receiver that can also lock onto the Russian Chayka chain. The published repo holds only KiCad hardware designs (loop antenna preamp, power supply, processing board, RF prototype); no DSP firmware or software.
why_it_matters: One of very few open receivers for low-frequency hyperbolic navigation, the basis of eLoran.
hackathon_notes: Hardware reference only, last touched 2014: the loop-antenna preamp and RF front-end schematics are the useful part for an LF receiver build. No signal processing code to reuse.

name: Loran-C reference signal generator
summary: NumPy API that generates Loran-C master and secondary station pulse groups with phase codes for simulation (Korean docs).
why_it_matters: Synthetic Loran/eLoran signals for testing receivers without LF hardware.
hackathon_notes: Small; translate README; combine with a tracking loop for a toy eLoran receiver.

name: torch2trt
summary: Converts PyTorch models to TensorRT engines with a single call, aimed at Jetson deployment.
why_it_matters: Simplest path to fast onboard inference for learned nav models.
hackathon_notes: Install on a Jetson with JetPack; not every layer converts - check supported ops.

name: Hello AI World (jetson-inference)
summary: NVIDIA's guide and library for deploying detection, segmentation and depth networks with TensorRT on Jetson, with camera streaming.
why_it_matters: Get onboard perception running on a Jetson in hours.
hackathon_notes: Use the Docker container; works with CSI/USB cameras.

name: jetson-containers
summary: Build system and prebuilt containers for ML on Jetson (PyTorch, ROS, LLMs, VLMs) matched to JetPack versions.
why_it_matters: Avoids the dependency hell of getting ROS and PyTorch onto a Jetson.
hackathon_notes: Use autotag to pull a container matching your JetPack.

name: ros_deep_learning
summary: ROS/ROS 2 nodes wrapping jetson-inference for detection, classification and segmentation with TensorRT.
why_it_matters: Drop-in onboard perception topics for a ROS robot on Jetson.
hackathon_notes: Build inside jetson-containers ROS image.

name: Isaac ROS nvblox
summary: GPU-accelerated 3D reconstruction (TSDF/ESDF) that provides Nav2 local costmaps from depth cameras.
why_it_matters: Real-time onboard mapping for obstacle avoidance without lidar.
hackathon_notes: Isaac ROS dev container; RealSense quickstart.

name: Isaac ROS DNN Inference
summary: ROS 2 packages for TensorRT and Triton inference on Jetson and x86, with encoder/decoder nodes for common model types.
why_it_matters: Standard ROS 2 path to run custom learned models onboard.
hackathon_notes: Use with an ONNX model; dev container required.

name: cuVSLAM
summary: NVIDIA's CUDA-accelerated visual odometry and SLAM library supporting mono to multi-camera rigs with optional IMU, with Python bindings.
why_it_matters: The engine behind Isaac ROS Visual SLAM, now usable directly from Python.
hackathon_notes: Download the prebuilt wheel (cuvslam-cu12 or -cu13) from the GitHub releases page, not PyPI; wheels cover x86_64, Jetson Orin (JetPack 6) and Jetson Thor with Python 3.10+, other combos need a source build. Needs CUDA Toolkit libraries; examples include EuRoC and KITTI.

name: LightGlue-ONNX
summary: ONNX export and inference of LightGlue matching with SuperPoint, DISK and ALIKED extractors (including RaCo-ALIKED-LightGlue+), with TensorRT, OpenVINO and FP8 quantization workflows.
why_it_matters: Fast learned matching on embedded hardware for visual geolocalization and VO.
hackathon_notes: Download prebuilt ONNX models from Releases and run with onnxruntime-gpu or TensorRT; for export, the repo now uses uv (uv sync with export/cuda/trt groups) and a lightglue-onnx CLI.

name: PINTO model zoo
summary: Large collection of models converted between TensorFlow, TFLite, ONNX, OpenVINO, TensorRT and others.
why_it_matters: Saves conversion time when a needed model must run on an edge accelerator.
hackathon_notes: Use the download scripts per model; check licences per model.

name: RKNN Model Zoo
summary: Rockchip's examples and converted models for its NPU (RK3588 and similar), with deployment code.
why_it_matters: Low-cost non-NVIDIA edge AI option common on small drones and UGVs.
hackathon_notes: Needs rknn-toolkit2 for conversion; run demos on an RK3588 board.

name: DepthAI
summary: Landing repository for Luxonis OAK cameras, which run neural networks and stereo depth on the camera; the default branch now only points to the docs, and the old examples live on the `main` branch. The current Python API (DepthAI v3) is built from luxonis/depthai-core.
why_it_matters: Puts inference and depth on the sensor, freeing the companion computer.
hackathon_notes: `pip install depthai` (v3 API; examples in luxonis/depthai-core). OAK camera required. Older v2 tutorials and examples will not run unchanged on v3.

name: DepthAI ROS
summary: ROS 1/2 driver for Luxonis OAK cameras publishing depth, detections and IMU.
why_it_matters: Plug OAK cameras into a ROS nav stack.
hackathon_notes: Binary packages for major ROS 2 distros.

name: Hailo Raspberry Pi 5 examples
summary: Examples for Hailo-8/8L accelerators on Raspberry Pi 5 (AI Kit/HAT): detection, pose and segmentation pipelines; marked outdated in favor of hailo-apps.
why_it_matters: Cheapest route to real-time onboard inference on a Pi-based vehicle.
hackathon_notes: Repo points to hailo-ai/hailo-apps for current code; start there.

name: RTKLIB
summary: The original open-source GNSS positioning package by T. Takasu: SPP, DGNSS, RTK, PPK and PPP engines in portable C, plus CLI tools (rnx2rtkp, rtkrcv, str2str, convbin) and Windows GUIs.
why_it_matters: The reference implementation most GNSS research and low-cost RTK work is built on; reading its rtkpos.c is the fastest way to understand RTK.
hackathon_notes: Use str2str to relay NTRIP/serial streams and rnx2rtkp for post-processing. Upstream is quiet since 2024; prefer the demo5 fork for current receivers.

name: RTKLIB demo5 (rtklibexplorer)
summary: Actively maintained RTKLIB fork tuned for low-cost receivers (especially u-blox), with many robustness fixes to ambiguity resolution, cycle-slip handling and receiver decoders.
why_it_matters: The practical default for RTK/PPK with cheap F9P-class hardware; well documented through the rtklibexplorer blog.
hackathon_notes: Prebuilt Windows binaries and Linux builds are easy. Pair with a u-blox F9P and a free NTRIP caster for cm-level fixes in an afternoon.

name: rtklib-py
summary: Python port of the demo5 RTKLIB positioning core, currently focused on post-processed kinematic (PPK) solutions.
why_it_matters: Readable Python version of RTK math, good for teaching, prototyping new filters or swapping in ML components.
hackathon_notes: Slow compared to C RTKLIB and PPK only; last pushed 2023. Ideal for instrumenting or modifying the filter during a hackathon.

name: MatRTKLIB
summary: MATLAB wrapper exposing RTKLIB functions and data structures (observations, navigation data, solutions) as MATLAB objects.
why_it_matters: Lets MATLAB users script RTKLIB processing and analysis without writing C.
hackathon_notes: Requires MATLAB. Useful if the team already lives in MATLAB for analysis plots. Since January 2025 the backend is MALIB (the RTKLIB successor), not RTKLIB 2.4.3; pre-compiled mex files ship for Windows, Ubuntu and macOS.

name: GNSS-SDR
summary: Full software-defined GNSS receiver built on GNU Radio: acquisition, tracking, navigation message decoding and PVT for GPS, Galileo, GLONASS and BeiDou signals from SDR front-ends or IQ files, including Galileo OSNMA support.
why_it_matters: The most complete open receiver for experimenting with signal-level defenses (tracking monitors, authentication, interference) on real or simulated IQ.
hackathon_notes: Install from distro packages (apt install gnss-sdr) to skip a long build. Feed it GPS-SDR-SIM or recorded IQ files; works with HackRF/USRP/RTL-SDR front-ends.

name: PocketSDR
summary: Open hardware GNSS front-end plus a software receiver (Python and C) by the RTKLIB author, supporting a wide range of GNSS signals across L1/L2/L5/L6 bands.
why_it_matters: Cheap path to multi-band raw IF capture and a readable receiver implementation, ideal for signal-level research.
hackathon_notes: Software runs on recorded IF without the hardware; building the board is out of hackathon scope unless pre-built.

name: GNSS-SDRLIB
summary: Older open-source GNSS software receiver library in C with a GUI, supporting several front-ends and real-time RTKLIB output.
why_it_matters: Compact receiver codebase that is easier to read than GNSS-SDR; historically a common teaching receiver.
hackathon_notes: Not updated since 2015 (repo not formally archived). v2.0 only runs on 64-bit Windows (Visual Studio 2012 build). Use for reference only; prefer PocketSDR or GNSS-SDR for live work.

name: FGI-GSRx
summary: Multi-GNSS software receiver in MATLAB from the Finnish Geospatial Research Institute, with modular acquisition, tracking and navigation stages.
why_it_matters: MATLAB receiver suitable for quick algorithm swaps (e.g. new tracking or interference mitigation) with readable code.
hackathon_notes: Needs MATLAB and IQ files; slow but transparent.

name: SoftGNSS v3.0 (maintained copy)
summary: Maintained copy of the classic Borre/Akos SoftGNSS MATLAB GPS L1 receiver with updates for several sampler front-ends.
why_it_matters: The receiver code that accompanies the standard textbook on software GPS receivers; the canonical teaching codebase.
hackathon_notes: Good for learning acquisition and tracking loops on a sample data file.

name: SoftGNSS-python
summary: Python port of the SoftGNSS software-defined GPS receiver toolkit.
why_it_matters: Python version of the textbook receiver; easier for teams without MATLAB.
hackathon_notes: Not updated since 2023 and written for Python 2.7 (README system requirements; installation section says 'Coming soon'). Expect porting work before offline IQ experiments.

name: GPS L1 Direct Position Estimation module
summary: Plug-in module adding Direct Position Estimation (positioning directly in the correlation domain) to MATLAB two-step software receivers such as SoftGNSS.
why_it_matters: DPE is studied for robustness in weak-signal, multipath and interference conditions; this is one of few open implementations.
hackathon_notes: Research code; computationally heavy. Useful as a stretch comparison against conventional tracking.

name: laika
summary: Python GNSS processing library from comma.ai that fetches orbits, clocks and atmospheric corrections automatically and computes corrected pseudoranges and positions from raw measurements.
why_it_matters: Quickest way to go from raw pseudoranges to a corrected fix in Python; it powered openpilot's laikad GNSS localizer until that was removed in October 2023.
hackathon_notes: Install from a clone (`pip install .`); the PyPI 'laika' package is a 2018 0.0.1 stub. Correction downloads need internet, and NASA CDDIS needs an Earthdata login in a .netrc. Good backend for Android raw data experiments.

name: gnss_lib_py
summary: Modular Python library from Stanford NavLab for parsing, analyzing and visualizing GNSS data (Android logs, RINEX, NMEA, SP3/CLK) with baseline positioning algorithms and fault detection examples.
why_it_matters: Strong Python base for smartphone GNSS work and for prototyping integrity/fault detection.
hackathon_notes: pip install gnss-lib-py; tutorials load GSDC data directly. Very good fit for a 24h spoofing-detection or integrity notebook.

name: georinex
summary: Fast Python reader for RINEX 2/3/4 observation and navigation files (plain, gzip/Z/bz2/zip or Hatanaka-compressed) and SP3 orbits into xarray, with batch conversion to NetCDF4/HDF5.
why_it_matters: Makes RINEX data accessible in the scientific Python stack without writing parsers.
hackathon_notes: pip install georinex. Use it to load public CORS/IGS RINEX for analysis or ML features.

name: gnssanalysis
summary: Geoscience Australia Python module of utilities for reading and comparing GNSS products (SP3, CLK, SINEX, Ginan outputs) and computing differences/statistics.
why_it_matters: Companion tooling for evaluating precise orbit/clock products and PPP outputs.
hackathon_notes: Niche; useful if comparing PPP solutions or product quality.

name: PRIDE PPP-AR
summary: Wuhan University's open-source multi-GNSS precise point positioning package with ambiguity resolution, aimed at geodetic-grade post-processing.
why_it_matters: Free PPP-AR gives cm-level positions without a local base station, a key capability where RTK networks are unavailable.
hackathon_notes: Command-line build via install.sh on Linux and macOS, plus a Windows GUI version; needs precise products downloaded. Post-processing only, so plan for hours of data.

name: Ginan
summary: Geoscience Australia's GNSS analysis toolkit for precise orbit determination and real-time/post-processed PPP, producing and consuming correction products.
why_it_matters: Government-backed open PPP and product-generation engine; relevant for sovereign correction services.
hackathon_notes: Heavy build and configuration; Docker images help. Overkill for most 48h builds.

name: GNSSTk
summary: C++ library (successor to GPSTk) from UT Austin ARL for GNSS data formats, time systems, ephemeris handling and positioning algorithms, with Python bindings.
why_it_matters: Long-lived, carefully engineered GNSS core library used in US research and monitoring work.
hackathon_notes: Build is CMake-heavy; use for robust format and time handling rather than quick demos.

name: pyubx2
summary: Python library for parsing and generating u-blox UBX protocol messages, including configuration (CFG-VALSET) and raw measurement (RXM-RAWX) messages.
why_it_matters: Standard way to talk to u-blox receivers from Python: configure, log raw data and read jamming/spoofing status fields (MON-HW, NAV-STATUS).
hackathon_notes: pip install pyubx2. Read MON-RF jamming indicators and NAV-STATUS spoof flags to build a live interference monitor quickly.

name: pyrtcm
summary: Python parser for RTCM 3 messages (MSM observations, station info, ephemerides, SSR).
why_it_matters: Lets teams inspect and manipulate correction streams from NTRIP casters in Python.
hackathon_notes: pip install pyrtcm. Combine with pygnssutils' NTRIP client for live streams.

name: pynmeagps
summary: Python library for parsing and generating NMEA 0183 GNSS sentences, including proprietary variants.
why_it_matters: NMEA is what most autopilots and COTS receivers emit; this is a well-maintained parser/generator.
hackathon_notes: pip install pynmeagps. Can also generate NMEA to feed test positions into a downstream system.

name: PyGPSClient
summary: Cross-platform Python GUI GNSS client that displays and configures receivers over NMEA, UBX, RTCM3 and other protocols, with built-in NTRIP and SPARTN clients.
why_it_matters: Fast visual tool for checking receiver state, satellite C/N0 and corrections during field tests.
hackathon_notes: pip install pygpsclient. Good bench tool to watch C/N0 drop during a jamming test in a shielded setup.

name: pygnssutils
summary: Python CLI and library utilities for reading, parsing and broadcasting GNSS streams, including an NTRIP client and caster/server and a socket server.
why_it_matters: Glue for building correction pipelines and logging tools without writing protocol code.
hackathon_notes: pip install pygnssutils; gnssntripclient gets you RTCM from a caster in one command.

name: pynmea2
summary: Lightweight Python library for parsing NMEA 0183 sentences.
why_it_matters: Widely used minimal NMEA parser.
hackathon_notes: pip install pynmea2; simpler than pynmeagps but less coverage.

name: gpsd
summary: Service daemon that monitors GNSS receivers over serial/USB/network and serves decoded fixes, satellites and timing to client applications via JSON over TCP.
why_it_matters: The standard Linux GNSS middleware; used for timing (with ntpd/chrony and PPS) and for multiplexing receivers to multiple apps.
hackathon_notes: apt install gpsd gpsd-clients; cgps/gpsmon give instant status. Use it for PPS timing demos.

name: ublox ROS driver
summary: ROS driver for u-blox receivers that publishes fixes, raw measurements and receiver status as ROS messages.
why_it_matters: Common bridge from u-blox hardware into ROS-based autonomy stacks.
hackathon_notes: Available as a ROS package; check the branch for ROS 1 vs ROS 2.

name: SparkFun u-blox GNSS v3 Arduino library
summary: Arduino library for u-blox GNSS modules over I2C/SPI/serial, covering configuration, high-precision fixes and RTK correction input.
why_it_matters: Easiest embedded route to an RTK-capable microcontroller node (ESP32 + F9P).
hackathon_notes: Many examples, including NTRIP over Wi-Fi on ESP32. Good for a low-cost rover or base station.

name: ubxlib
summary: u-blox's portable C libraries for building applications on their GNSS and cellular modules across MCU platforms.
why_it_matters: Vendor-maintained abstraction for u-blox hardware on embedded targets.
hackathon_notes: Repository is archived; prefer the SparkFun library or pyubx2.

name: ntripcaster (BKG standard caster)
summary: Maintained mirror of the BKG standard NTRIP broadcaster in C for distributing RTCM correction streams over HTTP.
why_it_matters: Self-hosted correction distribution for a private RTK network, e.g. in a contested area without public casters.
hackathon_notes: Builds with autotools; pair with str2str from RTKLIB as the source.

name: ntripcaster Docker
summary: Dockerfile and instructions to build and run the BKG NTRIP caster in a container.
why_it_matters: Fastest way to stand up your own caster.
hackathon_notes: docker build and go; last updated 2024.

name: go-gnss/ntrip
summary: Go library implementing NTRIP client, server and caster components.
why_it_matters: Modern, embeddable NTRIP implementation for building custom correction services.
hackathon_notes: Use as a library inside a Go backend; smaller community than BKG caster.

name: ROS NTRIP client
summary: ROS/ROS 2 node that connects to an NTRIP caster and publishes RTCM corrections, forwarding NMEA position back to the caster.
why_it_matters: Standard glue to get RTK corrections into a ROS robot.
hackathon_notes: apt-installable ROS package; works with any receiver driver accepting RTCM topics.

name: ntripbrowser
summary: Command-line tool that fetches and displays an NTRIP caster's source table, optionally filtered by distance from a coordinate.
why_it_matters: Quick way to find the nearest public base station mountpoint.
