hackathon_notes: Needs libcurl. pip install ntripbrowser still installs the 2021 release (2.2.3); the repo is at 4.0.0 (2025, Python 3.11+), so install from a clone with make install for current code. Point at rtk2go or a national caster.

name: Node-NTRIP caster
summary: TypeScript/Node.js NTRIP caster library supporting NTRIP v1 and v2.
why_it_matters: JS option for web-stack teams building a correction relay.
hackathon_notes: Last updated 2023; fine for demos.

name: GPS Measurement Tools (incl. GnssLogger)
summary: Google's Android raw GNSS measurement tooling: the GnssLogger app source, MATLAB analysis tools for pseudorange processing (including a RINEX nav reader), and NMEA utilities.
why_it_matters: The canonical way to capture raw pseudoranges and carrier phase from phones, the basis for smartphone spoofing and integrity research.
hackathon_notes: Install GnssLogger from the Play Store and log on any recent Android phone; parse logs with gnss_lib_py.

name: GSDC 2023 solution (taroz)
summary: Code reproducing Taro Suzuki's Google Smartphone Decimeter Challenge 2023 entry (1st on the public leaderboard, 2nd on the private one), using factor graph optimization of smartphone GNSS and IMU in MATLAB.
why_it_matters: Shows what state-of-the-art smartphone positioning looks like on a public benchmark.
hackathon_notes: MATLAB required. Read it for the pipeline design even if you reimplement in Python.

name: GPS-SDR-SIM
summary: Generates GPS L1 C/A baseband IQ sample files for a user-defined static or moving trajectory from a broadcast ephemeris file, for playback through an SDR.
why_it_matters: The standard open test-signal generator for evaluating receiver behavior under simulated or spoofed conditions. Cabled or shielded-enclosure use only: radiating GNSS signals over the air is illegal in most jurisdictions.
hackathon_notes: Generate IQ files and feed GNSS-SDR directly (no RF needed) to test detectors. Repository archived in 2025 but still works. Cabled or shielded-enclosure use only: radiating GNSS signals over the air is illegal in most jurisdictions.

name: bladeGPS
summary: Real-time GPS L1 signal simulator variant of GPS-SDR-SIM for bladeRF hardware.
why_it_matters: Real-time variant for interactive receiver testing. Cabled or shielded-enclosure use only: radiating GNSS signals over the air is illegal in most jurisdictions.
hackathon_notes: Cabled or shielded-enclosure use only: radiating GNSS signals over the air is illegal in most jurisdictions.

name: LimeGPS
summary: Real-time GPS L1 signal simulator variant for LimeSDR.
why_it_matters: Same as bladeGPS for LimeSDR users. Cabled or shielded-enclosure use only: radiating GNSS signals over the air is illegal in most jurisdictions.
hackathon_notes: Cabled or shielded-enclosure use only: radiating GNSS signals over the air is illegal in most jurisdictions.

name: multi-sdr-gps-sim
summary: Maintained derivative of GPS-SDR-SIM that streams GPS L1 baseband on the fly to HackRF or ADALM-Pluto, or to a binary IQ file, with a curses text UI.
why_it_matters: More current option than the archived original for building test rigs. Cabled or shielded-enclosure use only: radiating GNSS signals over the air is illegal in most jurisdictions.
hackathon_notes: Cabled or shielded-enclosure use only: radiating GNSS signals over the air is illegal in most jurisdictions.

name: OSNMA-SDR-SIM
summary: Galileo E1-B/E5b signal simulator with OSNMA authentication data embedded, configurable OSNMA parameters and USRP or file output, tested against GNSS-SDR and OSNMAlib.
why_it_matters: Rare open tool to generate authenticated (and deliberately broken) Galileo signals for testing OSNMA-aware receivers.
hackathon_notes: Use file sink output into GNSS-SDR plus OSNMAlib for a full authenticate-or-alarm pipeline without RF. Cabled or shielded-enclosure use only: radiating GNSS signals over the air is illegal in most jurisdictions.

name: Beidou-SDR-SIM
summary: Open-source generator for BeiDou B1C baseband signals for SDR playback or file output.
why_it_matters: Extends signal simulation testing beyond GPS to BeiDou.
hackathon_notes: Cabled or shielded-enclosure use only: radiating GNSS signals over the air is illegal in most jurisdictions.

name: OSNMAlib
summary: Python implementation of the Galileo OSNMA receiver protocol: verifies TESLA key chains and MACs on navigation data from several input formats (u-blox, Septentrio, GNSS-SDR, files).
why_it_matters: Most practical open tool to add navigation message authentication to a Galileo-capable receiver pipeline.
hackathon_notes: Works live with a u-blox receiver outputting SFRBX; needs the public key and Merkle root from the GSC. Good basis for an 'authenticated position' demo.

name: galileo-osnma (Rust)
summary: Rust implementation of Galileo OSNMA that can run on embedded no_std targets, with examples for live receivers.
why_it_matters: Lightweight, memory-safe OSNMA verifier suitable for embedding in drones or edge devices.
hackathon_notes: Cargo build; includes a u-blox-based example. Embedded angle is a differentiator.

name: FGI-OSNMA
summary: Python OSNMA implementation from the Finnish Geospatial Research Institute designed for flexibility and integration with receivers.
why_it_matters: Second independent Python OSNMA implementation for cross-checking.
hackathon_notes: Not updated since 2023; check against current ICD version.

name: OSNMA_ublox
summary: Jupyter-based real-time OSNMA authentication of u-blox receiver data in Python.
why_it_matters: Small, readable OSNMA example from the test phase.
hackathon_notes: Inactive since 2022, predates OSNMA public service; use for learning only.

name: galmon
summary: Open-source GNSS monitoring network and software that collects navigation data from volunteer receivers worldwide and publishes live health, ephemeris and timing statistics for Galileo, GPS, BeiDou and GLONASS.
why_it_matters: Independent constellation monitoring, valuable for spotting anomalies and checking broadcast data integrity.
hackathon_notes: Run a feeder with a u-blox receiver, or just consume the public galmon.eu data.

name: GPSSpy
summary: Python implementation of GPS jamming detection from receiver signal-to-noise ratio, following a published real-time jamming detection method.
why_it_matters: Simple, explainable C/N0-based jamming detector to start from.
hackathon_notes: Small codebase from 2021; adapt to read C/N0 from pyubx2 or Android logs.

name: Multi-frequency GNSS spoofing raw dataset
summary: Raw GNSS measurement logs from Android phones and smartwatches recorded under spoofing scenarios on L1, L5 and dual-band.
why_it_matters: Labelled smartphone spoofing data is scarce; this enables training and testing detectors without generating signals.
hackathon_notes: Load logs with gnss_lib_py and build a consistency-check or ML detector. Verify labelling and scenario details in the README before trusting results.

name: MAAST for ARAIM
summary: Stanford GPS Lab MATLAB toolset that evaluates Advanced RAIM availability and protection levels over service areas.
why_it_matters: Reference-grade integrity tooling from the lab behind much ARAIM research.
hackathon_notes: MATLAB; heavy on aviation integrity concepts. Use for coverage maps of integrity availability.

name: RAIM (MATLAB)
summary: MATLAB implementation of classic receiver autonomous integrity monitoring (fault detection and exclusion) for GNSS positioning.
why_it_matters: Compact RAIM example to adapt for spoofing/fault detection logic.
hackathon_notes: Small and readable; port the residual test to Python for a quick FDE demo.

name: gtsam_gnss
summary: Custom GTSAM factors and MATLAB wrappers for GNSS factor-graph positioning, including pseudorange, Doppler and carrier-phase factors with ambiguity estimation.
why_it_matters: Factor graphs are a robust way to fuse GNSS with other sensors and reject outliers.
hackathon_notes: Requires the author's GTSAM fork and MATLAB; under active development.

name: GraphGNSSLib
summary: Open-source GNSS positioning and RTK package using factor graph optimization, built on RTKLIB data handling and ROS.
why_it_matters: Shows FGO-based GNSS positioning outperforming filters in urban canyons; good research baseline.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1 + Ceres; uses RTKLIB internals for observation handling.

name: gnss_comm
summary: C++/ROS definitions and utilities for raw GNSS measurement processing (ephemeris, satellite positions, pseudorange models) used by GVINS.
why_it_matters: Reusable raw GNSS building blocks for tightly coupled GNSS-visual-inertial fusion.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1; stable but unmaintained since 2022.

name: UT Starlink signal simulator
summary: MATLAB utility functions from UT Austin's Radionavigation Lab for simulating Starlink Ku-band downlink signals (OFDM frames, PSS/SSS, Doppler and path-loss histories), with MATLAB live-script playground examples.
why_it_matters: Lets teams experiment with Starlink as a signal of opportunity for PNT without capturing real Ku-band data.
hackathon_notes: Small MATLAB codebase, MIT licensed, last commit January 2024 and marked work in progress. The companion paper is Komodromos, Qin and Humphreys, 'Signal Simulator for Starlink Ku-Band Downlink' (ION GNSS+ 2023).

name: RINEX LEO extension proposal
summary: Proposal for RINEX format modifications to carry LEO-PNT observables and ephemeris.
why_it_matters: Shows how LEO-PNT data might be standardized into existing GNSS tooling.
hackathon_notes: Archived; read-only reference.

name: GNSS-Radar
summary: Web application showing current GNSS satellite positions (sky plot) for a location and time across constellations.
why_it_matters: Quick visibility planning tool for field tests.
hackathon_notes: Use the hosted site or run locally for offline sky plots.

name: openpilot
summary: Open driver-assistance robotics stack. Its current locationd fuses IMU and camera odometry in a pose Kalman filter; GNSS is still read and logged (ubloxd, qcomgpsd) but the laika-based GNSS fusion has been removed.
why_it_matters: Real-world example of a production fusion pipeline on consumer hardware, and of a stack that dropped GNSS from its localizer in favour of vision and IMU.
hackathon_notes: Large codebase; study locationd (pose_kf) and the ubloxd GNSS parsing rather than running the full stack. For laika-style GNSS processing, look at the standalone commaai/laika repo or older openpilot releases.

name: GTSAM
summary: Georgia Tech factor-graph library for smoothing and mapping, with incremental solvers (iSAM2) and a full IMU preintegration factor set. Ships Python bindings and navigation examples combining IMU with GPS-style measurements.
why_it_matters: The default backbone for building a custom GNSS/INS or multi-sensor navigation estimator where you add or drop sensor factors as GNSS degrades.
hackathon_notes: pip install gtsam gives Python bindings; start from the ImuFactor examples and add a GNSS position factor. Noise model tuning is where time goes.

name: Ceres Solver
summary: Google's nonlinear least-squares and general optimization library with automatic differentiation and robust loss functions.
why_it_matters: Used as the solver under many VIO and GNSS/INS optimizers (VINS-Fusion, OB_GINS); good for writing your own sliding-window estimator.
hackathon_notes: Solid but you write the residuals yourself. Pair with an existing IMU preintegration residual (e.g. from OB_GINS) rather than deriving from scratch.

name: g2o
summary: General framework for graph optimization, widely used for pose-graph SLAM back ends.
why_it_matters: Lightweight pose-graph back end when you need loop closure or map alignment on top of an inertial front end.
hackathon_notes: Best for pose graphs; IMU factors are less turnkey than in GTSAM.

name: robot_localization
summary: ROS package with EKF and UKF state estimation nodes that fuse any number of odometry, IMU, pose and GNSS inputs, plus a navsat_transform node for GPS-to-map conversion.
why_it_matters: Fastest route to a working fused odometry on a ROS ground robot or drone; the usual baseline before writing a custom filter.
hackathon_notes: apt install on ROS 2; mostly YAML config. Common gotcha: frame conventions (REP-103/105) and double-counting velocities.

name: FilterPy
summary: Python library of Kalman filters (linear, extended, unscented, ensemble), smoothers, particle filtering helpers and related estimators.
why_it_matters: Quick prototyping of filters in notebooks before porting to embedded code.
hackathon_notes: pip install filterpy. Not Lie-group aware, so handle attitude error states manually or use navlie/manif for that.

name: Kalman and Bayesian Filters in Python (book)
summary: Free interactive book of Jupyter notebooks teaching Kalman, EKF, UKF and particle filters with an intuition-first approach.
why_it_matters: Fastest onboarding for team members new to estimation.
hackathon_notes: Run the notebooks locally or in Binder; chapters on UKF and EKF are enough for a hackathon.

name: sfwa UKF
summary: Templated C++ unscented Kalman filter library for state and parameter estimation, including square-root variants, aimed at embedded use.
why_it_matters: Option for an embedded UKF attitude/navigation filter with compile-time state definitions.
hackathon_notes: Heavy template code; worth it only if you specifically need a UKF on a microcontroller-class target.

name: ethzasl_msf (Multi Sensor Fusion)
summary: Modular EKF framework from ETH ASL for fusing IMU propagation with pose, position and other sensor updates, with delayed-measurement handling.
why_it_matters: Classic MAV state estimator that shows how to fuse delayed vision/GPS measurements into an IMU-driven filter.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1 era; building on modern distros takes effort. Read it for the design more than to run it.

name: MaRS (Modular and Robust Sensor-Fusion)
summary: Modular IMU-driven sensor-fusion framework from University of Klagenfurt designed so sensors can be added, removed or fail at runtime without reworking the core filter.
why_it_matters: Directly relevant to graceful degradation when GNSS or another aiding sensor drops out.
hackathon_notes: Core library builds standalone; ROS wrapper exists separately (mars_ros). Good fit for a sensor-dropout demo. Licence is BSD-2-Clause with an added condition that forbids selling the software or services based on it (source-available, no commercial use).

name: KF-GINS
summary: Wuhan University i2Nav reference implementation of loosely coupled GNSS/INS integration with an error-state EKF, with sample data and documentation.
why_it_matters: Clean, readable GNSS/INS baseline in the PSINS/Groves tradition; ideal to adapt for GNSS-outage experiments.
hackathon_notes: Builds with CMake and Eigen; includes demo dataset. Simulate outages by masking GNSS epochs and watch drift.

name: OB_GINS
summary: Optimization-based GNSS/INS integration from Wuhan University i2Nav, using IMU preintegration in a sliding-window factor graph solved with Ceres.
why_it_matters: Shows the optimization alternative to KF-GINS on the same problem, useful for comparing filter vs smoother under outages.
hackathon_notes: Same data formats as KF-GINS, so run both on one dataset for a side-by-side comparison.

name: IC-GVINS
summary: INS-centric GNSS-visual-inertial navigation system from i2Nav, where the precise INS drives the visual front end and GNSS is fused in a factor graph.
why_it_matters: Template for camera-aided INS that keeps working through GNSS denial.
hackathon_notes: ROS-based; heavier setup than KF-GINS. Use their datasets first.

name: LE-VINS
summary: INS-centric visual-inertial navigation with LiDAR depth enhancement for visual features, from i2Nav.
why_it_matters: Shows LiDAR-aided VIO in the same INS-centric architecture as IC-GVINS.
hackathon_notes: Needs camera+LiDAR+IMU data; research code.

name: NaveGo
summary: Open MATLAB/GNU Octave toolbox for simulating and processing integrated INS/GNSS navigation, including IMU error modelling and Allan variance analysis.
why_it_matters: Quick offline analysis and simulation of INS/GNSS without compiling anything.
hackathon_notes: Works in Octave if no MATLAB licence. Last push 2024, so treat as stable rather than evolving.

name: GICI-LIB
summary: GNSS/INS/Camera integrated navigation library supporting a range of GNSS modes (SPP, RTK, PPP and variants) tightly fused with inertial and visual data via factor graph optimization.
why_it_matters: One of the most complete open tightly coupled GNSS/INS/vision stacks; good for showing positioning robustness in degraded GNSS.
hackathon_notes: Large codebase; run on the provided dataset first. Config files are the main interface.

name: GLIO
summary: Tightly coupled GNSS/LiDAR/IMU integration (PolyU) for continuous, drift-free state estimation in urban canyons.
why_it_matters: Shows how raw GNSS measurements can be kept in the loop even when only a few satellites are visible.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1 research code; needs raw GNSS observables in the data.

name: pyins
summary: Python package for modelling and analysing inertial navigation systems: strapdown integration, error models, Kalman-filter aiding and sensor simulation.
why_it_matters: Pure-Python INS/GNSS playground for quick outage and sensor-grade studies.
hackathon_notes: pip install python-ins (the PyPI name; import as pyins), pure Python with numba; docs on readthedocs. Good for scripted what-if plots (tactical vs MEMS IMU drift).

name: strapdown-rs
summary: Rust library and CLI for strapdown INS research under GNSS denial: local-level mechanization, four loosely coupled filters (ESKF, EKF, UKF, Rao-Blackwellized particle filter) and a simulator that removes or corrupts GNSS in recorded or synthetic data from a scenario file.
why_it_matters: Lesser-known, actively developed Rust INS; memory-safe option for embedded or simulation pipelines.
hackathon_notes: cargo build; library crate is strapdown-core (docs.rs) and the CLI is strapdown-sim. Loosely coupled only, no pseudorange or carrier-phase models.

name: ESKF (je310)
summary: Error-state Kalman filter implementation following Sola's quaternion ESKF formulation.
why_it_matters: Compact code reference for Sola's equations when writing your own ESKF.
hackathon_notes: Small codebase, no recent updates; read alongside the Sola report.

name: ESKF ROS (EliaTarasov)
summary: ROS error-state Kalman filter derived from PX4/ecl that fuses IMU with GPS, magnetometer, vision pose and optical flow.
why_it_matters: PX4-style estimator outside the autopilot, easy to feed from a bag.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1, unmaintained since 2019.

name: imu_gps_localization
summary: Error-state Kalman filter fusing IMU and GPS for localization, small and readable.
why_it_matters: Minimal ESKF GNSS/IMU example good for a first hackathon filter.
hackathon_notes: Small ROS project; easy to strip ROS and port.

name: eskf-gps-imu-fusion
summary: ESKF fusing GPS and IMU for improved positioning, with documentation in Chinese.
why_it_matters: Another compact ESKF reference with a worked dataset.
hackathon_notes: Standalone CMake build; docs are in Chinese.

name: imu_x_fusion
summary: Loosely coupled IMU + GNSS / 6-DoF odometry fusion with multiple estimators side by side (ESKF, IEKF, UKF variants, MAP).
why_it_matters: Lets you compare filter variants on the same inputs with little code.
hackathon_notes: ROS package; swap estimator by config to compare behaviour.

name: gps_imu_fusion
summary: GPS/IMU fusion examples derived from zm0612/eskf-gps-imu-fusion, implementing an EKF, the original ESKF and a Sola-style quaternion ESKF, plus an observability analysis; UKF is only listed as TODO. Docs in Chinese.
why_it_matters: Small comparison set of filter types for GNSS/IMU.
hackathon_notes: Inactive since 2022; use as reading material.

name: invariant-ekf (Hartley InEKF)
summary: C++ library implementing the invariant EKF for aided inertial navigation, including contact-aided legged-robot state estimation.
why_it_matters: Reference InEKF implementation; invariant filters behave better than standard EKF under large initial errors.
hackathon_notes: Last push 2019; still compiles with Eigen. Pairs with the Hartley 2019 paper.

name: DRIFT
summary: Symmetry-preserving (invariant) state estimation library from University of Michigan for legged, wheeled and other robots, with real-time ROS support.
why_it_matters: Maintained InEKF stack for proprioceptive dead reckoning when GNSS and vision are unavailable.
hackathon_notes: Has ROS examples; try on a wheeled robot bag for GNSS-free odometry.

name: iekf (contagon)
summary: Invariant Kalman filter implementation on SE(2) and SE(3).
why_it_matters: Small Python-side InEKF example for learning.
hackathon_notes: Small research repo; use for learning the algorithm.

name: gnss-ins-sim
summary: Python GNSS/INS simulator that generates trajectories, IMU/GNSS/magnetometer measurements with configurable error models, and runs navigation algorithms on them.
why_it_matters: Quick way to produce synthetic IMU and GNSS data with known truth to test filters and dead reckoning under GNSS outage.
hackathon_notes: Pure Python; define a motion profile CSV and sensor grade, then plug your filter in as an algorithm.

name: allan_variance_ros
summary: ROS tool (Oxford DRS) that computes Allan deviation plots from an IMU bag and outputs noise parameters in a Kalibr-compatible format.
why_it_matters: Needed to get realistic IMU noise values for any filter or VIO setup.
hackathon_notes: Record a few hours of static IMU data before the event; the analysis itself is quick.

name: imu_utils
summary: ROS package for analysing IMU performance with Allan variance to estimate noise and bias instability.
why_it_matters: Common alternative to allan_variance_ros in VIO workflows.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1, depends on Ceres; needs long static logs.

name: kalibr_allan (archived)
summary: MATLAB scripts producing IMU Allan standard deviation charts and Kalibr-ready noise values.
why_it_matters: Historical reference for IMU noise characterisation.
hackathon_notes: Archived; prefer allan_variance_ros.

name: allan-variance (Python)
summary: Small Python package computing Allan variance and fitting standard noise parameters.
why_it_matters: Quick no-ROS Allan analysis in a notebook.
hackathon_notes: pip install; feed a numpy array of static IMU samples.

name: AV-Matlab-SW
summary: MATLAB scripts (plus a Python port, AV_Python) for Allan variance analysis and Gauss-Markov IMU error modelling, accompanying Farrell et al., 'Inertial measurement unit error modeling tutorial', IEEE Control Systems Magazine 2022 (preprint PDF included).
why_it_matters: Deeper treatment of Allan variance pitfalls than the typical tool.
hackathon_notes: Read with the IEEE CSM tutorial (preprint in the repo). MATLAB for the article scripts; the AV_Python folder has Jupyter demos if you have no MATLAB.

name: Kalibr
summary: ETH ASL calibration toolbox for multi-camera and camera-IMU systems (extrinsics and time offset), plus IMU intrinsics and rolling-shutter calibration.
why_it_matters: Standard way to calibrate a camera-IMU rig before running any VIO.
hackathon_notes: Use the Docker image to avoid ROS 1 build pain; print an AprilGrid target in advance.

name: iKalibr
summary: Continuous-time, targetless multi-sensor calibration framework (IMU, cameras, LiDAR, radar, RGB-D, event cameras) estimating extrinsics and time offsets (IEEE T-RO 2025).
why_it_matters: Calibrate a full heterogeneous rig, including radar, in one tool.
hackathon_notes: ROS-based with many dependencies; budget setup time.

name: imu_tk
summary: Tool for calibrating IMU intrinsics (misalignment, scale factors and biases of accelerometer and gyro) from a sequence of static poses, without a turntable.
why_it_matters: Cheap way to improve MEMS IMU accuracy before deploying a filter.
hackathon_notes: Needs Ceres; collect static poses in many orientations with short rotations between.

name: lidar_imu_calib
summary: Automatic calibration of the extrinsic rotation between a 3D LiDAR and an IMU.
why_it_matters: Quick LiDAR-IMU rotation estimate for LIO setups.
hackathon_notes: Inactive since 2021; rotation only.

name: LI-Calib
summary: Targetless LiDAR-IMU calibration based on continuous-time batch estimation (IROS 2020).
why_it_matters: Full LiDAR-IMU extrinsics without a target.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1; needs a sequence with rich excitation.

name: LiDAR_IMU_Init
summary: Real-time LiDAR-inertial initialization estimating extrinsics, time offset, gravity and IMU bias online (IROS 2022).
why_it_matters: Removes the extrinsic-calibration blocker when bolting a LiDAR and IMU onto a new platform.
hackathon_notes: Builds like FAST_LIO; feed a bag with aggressive motion at start.

name: AHRS (Python)
summary: Python collection of attitude estimation algorithms (Madgwick, Mahony, complementary, EKF, QUEST, TRIAD and more) plus utilities such as the World Magnetic Model and WGS84.
why_it_matters: One import to compare attitude filters on your IMU log.
hackathon_notes: pip install ahrs; numpy arrays in, quaternions out.

name: x-io Fusion
summary: x-io Technologies' C AHRS library (revised Madgwick-style algorithm) with gyro offset correction, acceleration and magnetic disturbance rejection, and Python bindings.
why_it_matters: Production-grade embedded attitude filter with disturbance rejection, from the Madgwick filter's originators.
hackathon_notes: Drop the C files into firmware or pip install imufusion for Python prototyping.

name: MadgwickAHRS (Arduino)
summary: Official Arduino library implementing the Madgwick AHRS filter.
why_it_matters: Fastest hardware demo of attitude estimation on a microcontroller.
hackathon_notes: Install from the Arduino library manager; set sample rate correctly.

name: madgwick_py
summary: Minimal Python implementation of Madgwick's IMU and AHRS algorithms.
why_it_matters: Readable algorithm reference.
hackathon_notes: Tiny, unmaintained; use for reading.

name: imu_tools
summary: ROS tools for IMUs: Madgwick and complementary orientation filters and an RViz IMU visualisation plugin.
why_it_matters: Standard ROS orientation filter feeding robot_localization.
hackathon_notes: apt install on ROS 2.

name: ZUPT-aided INS (OpenShoe MATLAB)
summary: MATLAB implementation of the OpenShoe zero-velocity-aided foot-mounted INS with several zero-velocity detectors (SHOE, acceleration variance and magnitude, angular rate energy).
why_it_matters: Reference for dismounted soldier / first responder navigation without GNSS.
hackathon_notes: Works with any foot-mounted IMU log; sample data included. No updates since 2021.

name: PyShoe
summary: Open Python foot-mounted INS from UTIAS with a public inertial dataset and several zero-velocity detectors, including learned ones.
why_it_matters: Ready-to-run dismounted navigation pipeline with data for evaluation.
hackathon_notes: Python; dataset download needed. Strap an IMU to a boot and compare detectors.

name: RoNIN
summary: Robust Neural Inertial Navigation: smartphone IMU dataset and baseline networks (ResNet, LSTM, TCN) regressing pedestrian velocity from IMU.
why_it_matters: Main benchmark and baselines for learned pedestrian inertial navigation.
hackathon_notes: PyTorch; dataset is large and only about half of it was published (security concerns). Pretrained models give a quick baseline. The RoNIN data and pretrained models are under a custom licence for non-commercial and scientific research use only (code is GPL-3.0).

name: TLIO
summary: Tight Learned Inertial Odometry: a network regresses displacement and uncertainty from IMU windows, fused in a stochastic-cloning EKF.
why_it_matters: Strong blueprint for combining a learned motion prior with a classical filter.
hackathon_notes: Training data is head-mounted; expect domain gap on other platforms. The released dataset is CC BY-NC (non-commercial); the code is BSD-licensed.

name: AI-IMU Dead-Reckoning
summary: Car dead reckoning from IMU only, using an invariant EKF whose noise covariances are adapted by a neural network, evaluated on KITTI.
why_it_matters: Ground vehicle navigation through GNSS outages using only the IMU.
hackathon_notes: PyTorch; KITTI raw data needed. Clear demo of IMU-only drift reduction.

name: Denoise IMU Gyro
summary: CNN that denoises low-cost gyroscope signals to improve attitude estimation.
why_it_matters: Shows learned correction for cheap MEMS gyros.
hackathon_notes: Inactive since 2020; trained on EuRoC/TUM-VI.

name: AirIMU
summary: Learns IMU error correction and uncertainty with a network, combined with differentiable IMU preintegration (CMU AirLab).
why_it_matters: Learned IMU correction that feeds uncertainty into classical estimators.
hackathon_notes: PyTorch and PyPose; pretrained models available.

name: AirIO
summary: Learning-based inertial odometry for UAVs that improves feature observability by changing the IMU data representation (IEEE RA-L 2025).
why_it_matters: Recent IMU-only drone odometry for GNSS-denied flight.
hackathon_notes: PyPose-based research code. EuRoC, Blackbird and a simulated Pegasus split plus pretrained models are on GitHub releases; the EKF also needs the AirIMU results files.

name: EqNIO
summary: Subequivariant neural inertial odometry (ICLR 2025) that canonicalises IMU data so networks generalise across orientations; applied on top of TLIO and RoNIN.
why_it_matters: State of the art learned inertial odometry with released code.
hackathon_notes: Repo vendors modified TLIO (TLIO-master/) and RoNIN code, so no separate setup; get the TLIO dataset (CC BY-NC) or RoNIN data (non-commercial licence) first. No licence file in the repo, so the code is all rights reserved.

name: Learned Inertial Odometry for Drone Racing
summary: UZH RPG code fusing a learned inertial displacement model with an EKF for drone racing state estimation.
why_it_matters: Shows learned IO on aggressive UAV flight.
hackathon_notes: Research code; trained and tested on the MIT Blackbird dataset (converter script, one sample sequence and the trained network are in the repo). Reuses TLIO filter code.

name: manif
summary: Header-only C++11 library for Lie theory (SO2, SE2, SO3, SE3, SE_2(3) and more) with Jacobians, built around Sola's micro Lie theory paper; Python bindings available.
why_it_matters: Correct on-manifold Jacobians for custom ESKF or factor-graph code.
hackathon_notes: Header-only C++; Python bindings (manifpy) via conda install -c conda-forge manifpy or pip install from a clone - there is no PyPI package. Use alongside the micro Lie theory paper.

name: Sophus
summary: C++ Lie group library (SO2, SE2, SO3, SE3, Sim3) built on Eigen, used in many SLAM and VIO systems.
why_it_matters: De facto Lie group dependency in SLAM codebases.
hackathon_notes: Header-mostly; widely packaged. In maintenance mode since June 2024 (bug fixes only); sophus2 and sophus-rs are the successors.

name: liegroups (Python)
summary: Python implementation of SO2, SE2, SO3 and SE3 matrix Lie groups with numpy and PyTorch backends.
why_it_matters: Lie group operations inside PyTorch for learned estimators.
hackathon_notes: pip install from source; small and stable but no longer maintained (README points to PyMLG as the successor).

name: navlie
summary: Python state estimation package on Lie groups (McGill DECAR): EKF, iterated EKF, sigma-point filters, batch estimation, and IMU kinematics models.
why_it_matters: Fastest way to prototype on-manifold INS filters in Python.
hackathon_notes: pip install; has IMU and GNSS-like examples.

name: Nav2 (ROS 2 Navigation)
summary: The standard ROS 2 navigation stack: behavior-tree driven navigator, global planners (NavFn, Smac hybrid-A*/lattice, Theta*), local controllers (DWB, MPPI, Regulated Pure Pursuit), costmaps, recovery behaviors and waypoint following, including GPS waypoints via robot_localization.
why_it_matters: Default autonomy layer for ground robots in ROS 2; the place to plug a GNSS-denied localization source and still get full point-to-point and waypoint missions.
hackathon_notes: apt install ros-<distro>-navigation2 plus nav2_bringup gives a Gazebo TurtleBot demo in under an hour. Swap AMCL for your own localization by publishing map->odom TF. Tuning params YAML is the main time sink.

name: opennav_coverage
summary: Nav2-compatible complete-coverage task server and navigator built on Fields2Cover, with behavior-tree utilities for field/area coverage and row following.
why_it_matters: Gives Nav2 robots area-search and survey patterns (boustrophedon sweeps over a polygon) out of the box, useful for search, mapping and route clearance scenarios.
hackathon_notes: Fields2Cover is apt-installable on Humble, Jazzy and Kilted (ros-<distro>-fields2cover 2.x); only the main branch (Lyrical) builds it from source. Send a polygon in GPS or map frame and get a coverage route. Best for flat open terrain.

name: OMPL - Open Motion Planning Library
summary: Library of sampling-based motion planners (RRT, RRT*, PRM, BIT*, informed variants, kinodynamic planners) with a clean state-space abstraction and Python bindings.
why_it_matters: The reference implementation for sampling-based planning; underpins MoveIt and many UAV/UGV planners, so it is the quickest way to get a correct baseline planner.
hackathon_notes: pip wheels exist for the Python bindings; define a state validity checker against your occupancy grid or DEM and you have a planner in an afternoon.

name: EGO-Planner
summary: ESDF-free gradient-based local planner for quadrotors from ZJU FAST Lab: optimizes B-spline trajectories using collision terms computed only where the trajectory hits obstacles.
why_it_matters: Lightweight onboard replanning for small drones flying through clutter; widely reused baseline for agile UAV navigation in unknown environments.
hackathon_notes: ROS1 (Ubuntu 16.04-20.04) with a bundled simulator; runs on a laptop. A ROS 2 port lives in the ego-planner-swarm ros2_version branch, and upstream recommends EGO-Swarm over this repo; PX4 needs a bridge. Good for a demo of reactive flight in a random forest map.

name: Fast-Planner
summary: HKUST quadrotor planning framework: kinodynamic A* front-end plus B-spline optimization, with a topological-path variant for fast flight in unknown environments. The perception-aware (RAPTOR) planner is listed as 'to appear' and is not in the repo.
why_it_matters: Classic baseline that most later UAV planners compare against; modular enough to reuse its mapping (ESDF) and search components.
hackathon_notes: ROS1 + Gazebo-free lightweight sim; builds in minutes on Ubuntu 20.04. Expect NLopt dependency friction.

name: FUEL - Fast UAV Exploration
summary: Frontier-information-structure based autonomous exploration for quadrotors, combining global tour planning over frontiers with local viewpoint refinement.
why_it_matters: Autonomous mapping of unknown buildings or terrain without GNSS or prior map, a core reconnaissance capability.
hackathon_notes: Bundled sim; pairs naturally with a VIO/LiDAR odometry source from other lanes.

name: RACER - multi-UAV exploration
summary: Rapid collaborative exploration with multiple UAVs: decomposes unknown space and allocates exploration regions between drones with pairwise communication.
why_it_matters: A worked example of multi-robot task allocation for exploration under limited comms.
hackathon_notes: Same toolchain as FUEL; run 2-4 drones in sim and vary comm range.

name: GCOPTER
summary: General-purpose multicopter trajectory optimizer (MINCO) handling safe-corridor constraints and dynamic limits with spatial-temporal deformation.
why_it_matters: Efficient, well-documented trajectory optimizer to turn waypoint paths into flyable minimum-control trajectories.
hackathon_notes: Header-heavy C++ with ROS1 examples; best used as a library behind your own front-end.

name: KR Autonomous Flight
summary: UPenn Kumar Robotics end-to-end autonomy stack for GPS-denied quadrotors: state estimation, mapping, planning and control in one system.
why_it_matters: Full reference stack for flying without GNSS in forests and under canopy, from a lab with many field deployments.
hackathon_notes: Docker images help; large build. Use it to see how estimation and planning are glued, or reuse the planner. Penn Software Licence: non-profit research use only, commercial use needs a licence from Penn. An experimental ROS 2 Jazzy port is on the ros2_dev branch.

name: MADER
summary: MIT ACL decentralized and asynchronous trajectory planner for multiple UAVs in dynamic environments with obstacle and agent avoidance.
why_it_matters: Multi-agent planning without synchronized clocks or central coordination, closer to real comms constraints.
hackathon_notes: No commits since 2022; ROS1. Use for ideas rather than code reuse.

name: PlanSys2
summary: PDDL-based symbolic planning system for ROS 2: domain/problem management, plan generation with off-the-shelf planners and execution via behavior trees.
why_it_matters: Turns high-level mission goals (visit, inspect, deliver) into executable action sequences, the missing layer above Nav2.
hackathon_notes: apt-installable; write a PDDL domain and wrap Nav2 goals as actions. Learning PDDL is the time cost.

name: BehaviorTree.CPP
summary: C++ behavior tree library with XML trees, async actions, logging and the Groot editor; the execution engine inside Nav2 and many mission frameworks.
why_it_matters: Standard way to compose navigation, fallback and recovery logic into readable mission trees.
hackathon_notes: Header-friendly library; Groot2 GUI helps demo mission logic to judges.

name: PythonRobotics
summary: Large collection of readable Python implementations of robotics algorithms: localization (EKF, particle filter), SLAM, path planning (A*, RRT*, D*, state lattice), path tracking and more, with animations.
why_it_matters: Best teaching and prototyping resource; copy a planner or filter into a hackathon prototype in minutes.
hackathon_notes: Pure numpy/matplotlib; no build. Good for a quick 2D planner over a rasterized DEM.

name: Fields2Cover
summary: Modular coverage path planning library: headland generation, swath generation, route ordering (boustrophedon, snake, spiral) and Dubins/Reeds-Shepp path smoothing, with Python bindings.
why_it_matters: Ready coverage planner for area search or survey patterns by ground or air vehicles.
hackathon_notes: Build from source with GDAL dependency; Python bindings let you produce a sweep over a GeoJSON polygon quickly.

name: polygon_coverage_planning
summary: ETH ASL coverage planner for polygons with holes that treats boustrophedon sweep selection as a generalized TSP, aimed at UAV survey.
why_it_matters: Handles no-fly holes inside a survey area, which simple lawnmower generators do not.
hackathon_notes: ROS1 + CGAL; last push 2023. Use as a reference or run offline to produce waypoint lists.

name: grid_map
summary: Universal multi-layer 2.5D grid map library for mobile robots with ROS/ROS 2 integration, filters, iterators and conversion to images, point clouds and costmaps.
why_it_matters: Common data structure for elevation, slope and cost layers - the glue between DEMs and planners.
hackathon_notes: Available as ROS 2 binaries; load a GeoTIFF DEM (via GDAL) into a grid_map layer for terrain-aware costs.

name: Spatio-Temporal Voxel Layer
summary: Nav2 costmap layer using OpenVDB voxel grids with time decay to represent 3D obstacles from depth and LiDAR sensors.
why_it_matters: Better 3D obstacle handling for ground robots in dynamic environments than the default voxel layer.
hackathon_notes: Drop-in Nav2 plugin via apt.

name: CBBA (Python)
summary: Python implementation of the Consensus-Based Bundle Algorithm for decentralized multi-agent task allocation with plotting examples.
why_it_matters: CBBA is the classic decentralized auction for assigning tasks to UAV teams; this is an easy-to-read starting point.
hackathon_notes: numpy + matplotlib only; wrap in a ROS 2 node or call from a mission script to assign search cells to drones.

name: Open-RMF rmf_task
summary: Task allocation library from Open-RMF that assigns tasks to fleets of robots, accounting for battery, travel time and task constraints.
why_it_matters: Production-grade multi-robot task allocation with a fleet-level view, transferable from logistics to multi-vehicle missions.
hackathon_notes: Part of the larger Open-RMF stack; worth it only if you want fleet management, otherwise use CBBA.

name: GDAL
summary: Translator library and CLI tools for raster and vector geospatial formats (GeoTIFF, COG, GeoPackage, Shapefile, KML and hundreds more) with reprojection, warping and DEM utilities.
why_it_matters: Every map, DEM and imagery pipeline goes through GDAL; gdalwarp, gdaldem and gdal_translate cover most reference-map preparation.
hackathon_notes: Use conda or the OSGeo Docker image to avoid version mismatches between GDAL and Python bindings.

name: PROJ
summary: Cartographic projection and coordinate transformation library with datum grids, time-dependent transformations and a pipeline syntax.
why_it_matters: Correct datum and projection handling (WGS84, ITRF, local grids, UTM) is foundational for any nav system that mixes map sources.
hackathon_notes: Bundle the proj-data grids offline if your demo has no internet.

name: pyproj
summary: Python interface to PROJ for CRS definitions, coordinate transformations and geodesic computations.
why_it_matters: Default Python tool for lat/lon <-> UTM/ECEF/local conversions in nav prototypes.
hackathon_notes: pip install pyproj ships PROJ inside the wheel; reuse a Transformer object for speed.

name: Rasterio
summary: Pythonic raster I/O on top of GDAL: read/write GeoTIFF and COG, windowed reads, masks and affine georeferencing.
why_it_matters: Easiest way to sample a DEM or orthophoto at a coordinate for terrain-referenced or visual navigation experiments.
hackathon_notes: pip wheels include GDAL; use windowed reads to crop tiles around a vehicle position.

name: QGIS
summary: Desktop open-source GIS for viewing, editing, analyzing and printing geospatial data, extensible via Python plugins.
why_it_matters: The analyst's workbench for building mission areas, inspecting DEMs and checking flight logs on a map.
hackathon_notes: Install the LTR build; draw AOIs and export GeoJSON for planners. QGIS loads MBTiles/PMTiles for offline basemaps.

name: CesiumJS
summary: WebGL 3D globe and map library with terrain, 3D Tiles, time-dynamic data (CZML) and accurate WGS84 rendering.
why_it_matters: Best open web option for a 3D situational awareness view with terrain and flight paths; widely used in defense demos.
hackathon_notes: npm install cesium. Default imagery/terrain use Cesium ion (token); for offline, serve your own quantized-mesh terrain and tiles.

name: Cesium Terrain Builder
summary: Command-line tools to convert GDAL-readable DEMs into Cesium heightmap terrain tiles; quantized-mesh output needs the ahuarte47 fork, which the tum-gis Docker image packages.
why_it_matters: Turns a Copernicus/SRTM DEM into offline 3D terrain for a CesiumJS display without internet.
hackathon_notes: Unmaintained since 2023; use the tum-gis docker image to avoid build pain.

name: MapLibre GL JS
summary: Open-source WebGL vector tile map renderer (fork of Mapbox GL JS v1) with styles, 3D terrain and globe view.
why_it_matters: Fast, license-clean 2D/2.5D web map for C2 dashboards, works fully offline with your own tiles.
hackathon_notes: Pair with martin or tileserver-gl and a PMTiles extract for an offline basemap.

name: OpenLayers
summary: Feature-rich web mapping library supporting many projections, WMS/WMTS, vector tiles and editing.
why_it_matters: Strong choice when you need non-Web-Mercator projections or OGC services in a C2 web UI.
hackathon_notes: npm install ol; integrates with proj4js for custom CRS.

name: Leaflet
summary: Small, simple JavaScript library for interactive raster/vector maps with a huge plugin ecosystem.
why_it_matters: Quickest route to a working map with markers and tracks in a hackathon UI.
hackathon_notes: Works with milsymbol to render unit icons as markers.

name: deck.gl
summary: GPU-powered large-scale data visualization framework with layers for points, paths, trips, hexbins and 3D tiles, usable over MapLibre or standalone.
why_it_matters: Renders thousands of tracks (ADS-B, AIS, swarm telemetry) smoothly for a common operating picture.
hackathon_notes: Use TripsLayer for animated track histories; integrates with React.

name: OSRM
summary: High-performance road routing engine on OpenStreetMap data using contraction hierarchies or multi-level Dijkstra.
why_it_matters: Offline road routing for ground vehicle convoy and logistics planning.
hackathon_notes: Docker image + a Geofabrik regional extract gives a routing API in under an hour.

name: Valhalla
summary: Tiled OSM routing engine with dynamic costing per request (auto, truck, pedestrian, bicycle), isochrones and map matching.
why_it_matters: Request-time costing makes it easy to avoid areas or prefer terrain types, and its map-matching snaps noisy tracks to roads.
hackathon_notes: Docker images available; build tiles for a region once and run offline. Elevation tiles enable grade-aware costing.

name: GraphHopper
summary: Java OSM routing engine usable as library or server, with custom models for per-request costing and map matching.
why_it_matters: Embeddable routing on the JVM, relevant for dismounted navigation apps; on-device Android routing is no longer officially supported (last Android demo is v1.0).
hackathon_notes: Single jar + OSM pbf; custom model JSON lets you penalize road classes or areas.

name: OSMnx
summary: Download, model and analyze street networks and other OSM features as NetworkX graphs.
why_it_matters: Rapid road/path graph construction for planners and task allocation experiments in Python.
hackathon_notes: pip install osmnx; needs internet for Overpass unless you load a local OSM file.

name: elevation
summary: CLI/Python tool to download, cache and clip global DEMs (SRTM, Copernicus DEM and others) for a bounding box.
why_it_matters: One-command DEM for an AOI, the first input for terrain-referenced navigation and terrain-aware planning.
hackathon_notes: Needs GDAL on PATH; eio clip --bounds ... produces a GeoTIFF.

name: TileServer GL
summary: Vector and raster tile server that serves MBTiles/PMTiles with GL styles and renders raster tiles server-side with MapLibre Native.
why_it_matters: Simplest offline basemap server for field laptops and TAK clients needing raster tiles.
hackathon_notes: docker run maptiler/tileserver-gl with an mbtiles file; also gives WMTS for QGIS.

name: Martin
summary: Fast Rust tile server for PostGIS, MBTiles and PMTiles sources, with tile generation and mbtiles tooling.
why_it_matters: Serves live PostGIS layers (tracks, zones) as vector tiles alongside static basemaps.
hackathon_notes: Single binary or docker; point at a PostGIS table to stream dynamic features.

name: PMTiles
summary: Single-file tile archive format and tooling, served by HTTP range requests from static storage, with JS/Go readers and extraction CLI.
why_it_matters: Ship an entire regional basemap as one file on a USB stick or static server - ideal for disconnected ops.
hackathon_notes: pmtiles extract from a planet build to cut your AOI; load with the MapLibre protocol plugin.

name: Planetiler
summary: Fast vector tile generator that builds OpenMapTiles-compatible tilesets from OSM extracts on a single machine.
why_it_matters: Build your own up-to-date offline basemap for an AOI in minutes.
hackathon_notes: planetiler --download --area=<region> --output=<name>.pmtiles builds mbtiles or pmtiles; the jar needs Java 25+, the Homebrew, single-file and Docker launchers need no Java. The first run downloads about 1 GB of ocean and Natural Earth data.

name: mgrs (Python)
summary: Python library converting between latitude/longitude and MGRS grid references, built on NGA GEOTRANS 3.10 (now a Rust port exposed through a pybind11 extension).
why_it_matters: MGRS is the grid language of military users; needed for any C2 UI or report generator.
hackathon_notes: pip install mgrs; mind the precision argument for 1 m vs 10 m references. Since 1.6.0 inverse conversion returns the grid-cell centre, not the south-west corner.

name: GeographicLib
summary: C++ library for accurate geodesic problems, UTM/UPS/MGRS conversions, geoid heights, gravity and magnetic field models.
why_it_matters: Gold-standard geodesy: geodesic distances, geoid (EGM96/2008) undulation for GNSS height vs DEM height, and MGRS.
hackathon_notes: Python and JS ports exist (geographiclib-python, geographiclib-js); geoid datasets download separately.

name: pymap3d
summary: Pure-Python 3D coordinate conversions: geodetic, ECEF, ENU, NED, AER, ECI, with optional NumPy vectorization.
why_it_matters: The everyday tool for converting GNSS fixes into a local ENU/NED frame for fusion and planning.
hackathon_notes: pip install pymap3d; no compiled deps.

name: sentinelhub-py
summary: Python client for Sentinel Hub and Copernicus Data Space services to search, download and process Sentinel and other satellite imagery.
why_it_matters: Pull recent satellite imagery of an AOI to build reference maps for visual geolocalization.
hackathon_notes: Needs free Copernicus Data Space or Sentinel Hub credentials; set up before the event.

name: pystac-client
summary: Python client for searching STAC APIs (Earth Search, Planetary Computer and others) by area, time and properties.
why_it_matters: Credential-free path to Sentinel-2, Landsat and Copernicus DEM tiles via public STAC catalogs.
hackathon_notes: Search Earth Search (AWS) without a key and read COGs directly with rasterio.

name: odc-stac
summary: Loads STAC items into xarray datasets with reprojection, resampling and mosaicking.
why_it_matters: Turn a STAC search into a ready, aligned raster stack for map-matching experiments.
hackathon_notes: Works with Dask for larger AOIs.

name: OpenDroneMap (ODM)
summary: Photogrammetry toolkit that turns aerial images into orthophotos, point clouds, 3D models and DEMs.
why_it_matters: Build your own up-to-date reference orthophoto and DSM from a survey flight for visual and terrain navigation.
hackathon_notes: docker run opendronemap/odm on a folder of images; WebODM gives a GUI. Processing time scales with image count.

name: TAK Server (open source)
summary: Open-source release of the TAK Server from the TAK Product Center: the federation and message routing server for ATAK/WinTAK/iTAK clients, handling CoT, data packages, missions and video.
why_it_matters: Reference C2 backend used by many government users; integrating with it makes a demo interoperable with fielded TAK clients.
hackathon_notes: Java + PostgreSQL + certificate setup is the main hurdle; use a docker recipe and allow several hours.

name: GoATAK
summary: Go implementation of a simple ATAK-compatible server and a web client, supporting CoT over TCP/UDP/SSL.
why_it_matters: Single static binary TAK server and browser client - minimal footprint for edge devices.
hackathon_notes: go build or release binary; web map client is handy for judges without ATAK installed.

name: CloudTAK
summary: Browser-based TAK-compatible common operating picture with ETL connectors that push external data feeds into TAK.
why_it_matters: Shows how to bridge arbitrary data sources (sensors, APIs) into a TAK network with a web COP.
hackathon_notes: AWS-oriented deployment; locally, reuse its node-CoT library and connector patterns.

name: node-CoT
summary: JavaScript/TypeScript library for parsing, building and converting Cursor-on-Target messages, including GeoJSON conversion and TAK protobuf.
why_it_matters: Quickest way to emit CoT from a Node/web app.
hackathon_notes: npm install @tak-ps/node-cot.

name: takproto
summary: Encode and decode TAK protobuf (TAK Protocol v1) packets, including mesh and stream formats. A GitHub fork of dB-SPL/takprotobuf, now maintained by Sensors & Signals and published on PyPI as takproto.
why_it_matters: Needed when talking to modern TAK clients that prefer protobuf over XML CoT.
hackathon_notes: pip install takproto.

name: cotlib (Go)
summary: Go library for parsing, validating and generating Cursor-on-Target XML with security-focused input limits and optional schema validation.
why_it_matters: Hardened CoT parsing for Go services that accept untrusted network input.
hackathon_notes: Schema validation needs libxml2 and CGO.

name: milsymbol
summary: Pure JavaScript library generating MIL-STD-2525 (B/C/D/E) and APP-6 (B/D/E) military symbols as SVG or canvas.
why_it_matters: Renders correct unit and track symbology on any web map without licensed assets.
hackathon_notes: npm install milsymbol; new ms.Symbol(sidc).asSVG() drops straight into a Leaflet or MapLibre marker.

name: Joint Military Symbology XML
summary: Esri data encapsulation of MIL-STD-2525D and APP-6(D) symbology: symbol IDs, entity tables and SVG assets.
why_it_matters: Machine-readable symbol tables useful for validating SIDCs or building your own renderer.
hackathon_notes: Archived in 2024; data still useful.

name: ASTERIX decoder (Croatia Control)
summary: C/C++ and Python decoder for EUROCONTROL ASTERIX surveillance data from files, stdin or network, with XML category definitions and JSON/XML output.
why_it_matters: ASTERIX is the format real radars and ATC surveillance use; decoding it lets a demo ingest professional air picture feeds.
hackathon_notes: Python module is on PyPI as asterix_decoder; feed it recorded or live UDP ASTERIX and get JSON per record.

name: asterix-specs
summary: EUROCONTROL ASTERIX category specifications in a structured machine-readable format, with generated JSON and docs.
why_it_matters: Authoritative-structured spec source for building ASTERIX encoders/decoders in any language.
hackathon_notes: Companion asterix-libs repo has generated Python libraries.

name: pyModeS
summary: Python decoder for Mode S and ADS-B messages including Comm-B / EHS fields, with live streaming tools.
why_it_matters: Decode raw Mode S yourself, including derived wind and airspeed data; underlies The 1090MHz Riddle book.
hackathon_notes: pip install pyModeS now installs the v3 rewrite (Python 3.11+): a single decode() call plus a stateful PipeDecoder for streams, and a modes CLI. Older tutorials and The 1090MHz Riddle use the v2 pms.adsb.* API; pin pyModeS<3 to follow them. Pairs with a Beast/raw feed from readsb.

name: traffic
summary: Toolbox for processing and analyzing air traffic trajectories: OpenSky access, filtering, resampling, airspace intersection and visualization.
why_it_matters: Analyze flight tracks and airspace structures for airspace awareness or UAV deconfliction studies.
hackathon_notes: pip install traffic; OpenSky historical data needs an account.

name: OpenSky API clients
summary: Python and Java bindings for the OpenSky Network REST API for live and recent aircraft states.
why_it_matters: Free crowd-sourced air picture when no local receiver is available.
hackathon_notes: Anonymous access is rate-limited. Since March 2026 authenticated access uses OAuth2 client credentials (basic auth was dropped); create an API client in your OpenSky account.

name: MassMIND
summary: Long-wave infrared image dataset of a harbour environment with semantic and instance segmentation masks for maritime scene understanding.
why_it_matters: Thermal perception is what keeps an autonomous surface vessel aware of obstacles at night and in haze, when RGB fails.
hackathon_notes: Download the three Google Drive zips in the README (2,916 LWIR images at 640x512, 7 classes, semantic and instance masks); small enough to fine-tune a segmentation net in a few hours. Licence is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 - non-commercial only.

name: LaRS evaluator
summary: Evaluation scripts for LaRS, a panoptic maritime obstacle detection benchmark spanning lakes, rivers and seas.
why_it_matters: Gives a standard scoring harness for USV obstacle detection so a team can compare its model against published baselines.
hackathon_notes: Pair with the LaRS dataset from the project page (4,000+ labelled key frames; test GT is hidden, so score test predictions on macvi.org); use the evaluator to score a YOLO/segmentation baseline. Dataset terms: CC BY-NC 4.0, research access only, no commercial use, no sharing images with third parties. The evaluator repo has no licence file.

name: SubPipe
summary: Underwater dataset recorded by a lightweight AUV inspecting a submarine pipeline: two cameras, side-scan sonar (10,030 images, COCO/YOLO labels), segmentation masks and navigation data, for segmentation, detection and visual-inertial localization.
why_it_matters: One of few open AUV datasets with a pose reference (estimated from the vehicle's own navigation sensors, not an external ground truth), useful for testing underwater VIO where GNSS never reaches.
hackathon_notes: Full set is ~80 GB unzipped on Zenodo; start with SubPipeMini (~12 GB) and run an off-the-shelf VIO to show drift underwater. Data CC BY 4.0, repo code GPL-3.0.

name: CART - Caltech Aerial RGB-Thermal
summary: Aerial RGB plus thermal dataset from natural terrain (rivers, coasts, deserts, forests) with GPS and inertial data, plus benchmarks for segmentation, RGB-to-thermal translation and VIO.
why_it_matters: Thermal-aerial data with GPS/IMU is rare; it supports night-time visual and thermal navigation research without flying your own sensor rig.
hackathon_notes: Use the VIO benchmark to test thermal-inertial odometry, or train RGB-to-thermal translation to build synthetic thermal maps. The labelled subset downloads directly; raw data are ROS1 bags from an S3 bucket. Non-commercial only: data.caltech.edu lists CC BY-NC 4.0 (README says CC BY-SA 4.0, non-commercial).

name: Drone-vs-Bird Detection Challenge
summary: Repository of the long-running Drone-vs-Bird challenge: annotations and instructions for a video dataset of small drones with birds as distractors.
why_it_matters: Telling a distant drone from a bird is the core false-alarm problem in camera-based C-UAS; this is the reference benchmark.
hackathon_notes: Videos only on request (wosdetc@googlegroups.com) after signing a data usage agreement, research use only - allow lead time. Then train a small-object YOLO; the hard part is tiny targets, so tile the frames. Repo not updated since 2022-12 (2023 edition is the last listed).

name: DroneAudioDataset
summary: Indoor recordings of drone propeller noise augmented with noise clips, organised for binary and multiclass audio drone detection.
why_it_matters: A common baseline audio set for acoustic drone detection. Note: its licence explicitly forbids military/defence use, so check fit before building on it.
hackathon_notes: Licence allows educational and non-commercial academic research only, and explicitly bans military, defence, intelligence, security and surveillance use - not usable for a defence entry; pick another acoustic set. The 'Unknown' clips come from ESC-50 and Speech Commands under their own licences.

name: Drone detection dataset (IR, visible, audio)
summary: Multi-sensor dataset from a Swedish thesis: 650 infrared and visible videos (airplane, bird, drone, helicopter; 203k labelled frames) plus 90 audio clips (drone, helicopter, background).
why_it_matters: Lets a team prototype sensor fusion for C-UAS (thermal + RGB + audio) on one consistent set of targets and distractors.
hackathon_notes: Data sits in the repo (~360 MB, no LFS), CC0. Labels are MATLAB groundTruth .mat files that scipy cannot read; use pip install mcos-decoder in Python. Good for a fused IR+audio classifier demo in a weekend.

name: RF-Drone-Detection (Georgia Tech)
summary: Georgia Tech student project on passive RF drone detection: a wifi_monitor.py script that flags DJI MAC OUI prefixes via airodump-ng, plus hackrf_sweep and GNU Radio experiment tools.
why_it_matters: Shows a cheap passive RF detection path for drones that use Wi-Fi links.
hackathon_notes: Needs root and a monitor-mode Wi-Fi adapter (tested on 2.4 GHz only, Ubuntu 18.04). It only matches two DJI OUI prefixes, so it misses non-Wi-Fi links and is trivially spoofed. No licence file.

name: Noisy Drone RF Signal Classification
summary: Loader and inspection scripts for a Kaggle drone RF benchmark: 16,384-sample IQ vectors and spectrograms from 6 drone remote-control transmitters plus a noise class, at SNR -20 to 30 dB in 2 dB steps.
why_it_matters: SNR-labelled RF samples let you measure how a drone RF classifier degrades with distance and noise.
hackathon_notes: Kaggle download is ~26 GB (CC BY 4.0; repo code GPL-3.0). Load dataset.pt with the provided PyTorch dataloader, then train a small CNN.

name: RFClassification
summary: Notebooks that classify drone presence and type from RF using DroneRF and DroneDetect data (PSD+SVM and CNN approaches), aiming at real-time use with GamutRF hardware.
why_it_matters: Ready-made baselines on the two most-cited public drone RF datasets.
hackathon_notes: Fork of the archived IQTLabs/RFClassification; no commits since 2022-09. Includes Raspberry Pi 4 test scripts. Download DroneRF (Mendeley, CC BY 4.0) and DroneDetect (IEEE DataPort, CC BY 4.0, 65.8 GB, needs an IEEE account) separately.

name: Drone Detection and Identification using RF signals
summary: Notebooks and MATLAB feature extractors for drone detection and identification on DroneRF: PSD, MFCC and time-domain features with XGBoost, a 1D-CNN and a CNN+XGBoost hybrid.
why_it_matters: Another reproducible baseline on public drone RF data to compare against.
hackathon_notes: Notebook-based; the processed data is on the Google Drive link in the README, raw DroneRF is CC BY 4.0 on Mendeley. Feature extraction scripts need MATLAB.

name: CNN for drone detection using RF
summary: CNN code for drone detection and identification on RF spectra.
why_it_matters: Simple CNN baseline for RF drone ID.
hackathon_notes: Older code (2020): three Keras scripts that read DroneRF's RF_Data.csv and use the old keras.layers.core API; use as reference only.

name: GNSS jamming/spoofing classification notebooks
summary: Colab notebooks for GNSS jamming-type classification (ML, DL and CV on spectrogram images) from a public raw-IQ jamming set, plus one GPS spoofing ML notebook; companion to arXiv 2501.02352.
why_it_matters: Turnkey starting point for a jamming-type classifier using open data.
hackathon_notes: Open in Colab and download the Zenodo IQ set (1.9 GB, CC BY 4.0). Its signals are simulated in MATLAB: DME, narrowband, AM, chirp, FM and no jamming. The repo has no licence file.

name: Towards Jammer Fingerprinting
summary: LSTM (Bayesian and standard) classifiers that identify individual jammers from IQ recordings, from an ICL-GNSS 2024 paper on how environment and receiver affect classification.
why_it_matters: Fingerprinting which jammer is present is a step toward attribution and targeted mitigation.
hackathon_notes: Needs your own IQ recordings in the expected file layout; reuse the model code on Jammertest data.

name: Sentinel-1 RFI detection
summary: Pipeline that flags radio-frequency interference in Sentinel-1 C-band SAR scenes using temporal z-scores and DEM slope masking, run over Iran, the Persian Gulf and Jammertest 2025.
why_it_matters: Free satellite data as a wide-area RFI sensor, complementing ADS-B based maps - but Sentinel-1 is C-band, and the authors' own Jammertest analysis could not tie detections to L-band GNSS jammers.
hackathon_notes: Needs a free Copernicus Data Space account. Pull Sentinel-1 scenes for a region and produce an RFI heatmap; present it as an RFI map, not a proven jamming map. MIT.

name: foxhunt
summary: Receive-only GNSS interference detection with radio direction finding and triangulation on Raspberry Pi and RTL-SDR.
why_it_matters: Low-cost jammer localization is a practical defensive EW capability.
hackathon_notes: Needs 3+ Raspberry Pi + RTL-SDR nodes with directional antennas; start with foxhunt-sim and --mock-sdr after uv sync. Receive-only, but a live test still needs an authorised interference source. Rotator GPIO driver and PPS wiring are still planned.

name: geoveil-cn0
summary: Rust library with a Python API (pip install geoveil-cn0) that scores GNSS signal quality from RINEX observation files via C/N0 and flags jamming, spoofing and interference across six constellations.
why_it_matters: Drop-in signal-quality monitor for a navigation stack.
hackathon_notes: Input is plain RINEX 2-4 files (decompress Hatanaka first); the spoofing check needs a broadcast nav file. Licence is PolyForm Noncommercial with an attribution term - no commercial use.

name: GNSS multiple jammers dataset
summary: Placeholder repo: its description promises recordings of several simultaneous chirp jammers on GPS L1 for notch-filter (ANF) mitigation studies, but the repo is empty (no commits) as of 2026-11-06.
why_it_matters: Multi-jammer data is rare; useful for testing mitigation filters.
hackathon_notes: No data, README or licence yet - nothing to use. Watch the repo or pick another jamming set.

name: GNSS jamming detection on maritime Antarctica dataset
summary: Thesis code for ML jamming detection and temporal generalisation using real maritime receiver diagnostics (u-blox MON-RF, MON-SPAN, RXM-MEASX) from a public Antarctica voyage dataset.
why_it_matters: Uses receiver-reported diagnostics a cheap u-blox already exposes, so it transfers to real hardware.
hackathon_notes: The Antarctica UBX set is one 45.7 GB zip on Zenodo (CC BY 4.0). Labels are the receiver's own jamming flag and the thesis results are a two-day pilot. Reproduce on your own u-blox logs by enabling the same UBX messages. Repo has no licence file.

name: P-D defense
summary: MATLAB implementation of the power-distortion detector for GNSS spoofing and jamming.
why_it_matters: Classic signal-level spoofing detector from the Humphreys line of work.
hackathon_notes: Inactive since 2020; read alongside the TEXBAT data.

name: Stanford GNSS spoof detection
summary: A single MATLAB script (DoAsimulationStudy.m) simulating direction-of-arrival spoof detection, supporting Rothmaier et al. Stanford GPS Lab papers.
why_it_matters: Reference implementations of spoofing detection tests.
hackathon_notes: Old MATLAB, one simulation script; useful only as an algorithm reference for DoA-based spoof detection.

name: GPS-Spoofing-Detect
summary: MATLAB course project with a write-up that tests GNSS spoofing detection on the TEXBAT DS7 scenario, with its own IQ extraction and least-squares navigation code.
why_it_matters: Small educational example.
hackathon_notes: Reference only. Needs TEXBAT processed data (open index on rnl-data.ae.utexas.edu, no terms stated) and spanikp's GNSS-toolbox. No licence file.

name: NRC UAV vs bird radar tracks
summary: Labelled real-world radar tracks of small UAVs, birds, humans and vehicles from an Echodyne EchoGuard radar over several Canadian field trials.
why_it_matters: Radar track classification (drone vs bird) is central to C-UAS beyond micro-Doppler range; open labelled radar data is scarce.
hackathon_notes: Train a kinematic-feature classifier on the tracks; no RF hardware needed.

name: MMC-UAV dataset
summary: Placeholder for a multimodal low-altitude anti-drone dataset (RGB, infrared, active radar, passive RF); the repo holds only a 3-line README that calls it MMA-UAV.
why_it_matters: Rare dataset with all four C-UAS sensor modalities.
hackathon_notes: No data, download link, paper or licence in the repo - not usable until the authors publish.

name: Audio localization dataset (Crazyflie)
summary: Datasets for acoustic echolocation and sound-source localization recorded on a Crazyflie drone and an e-puck robot.
why_it_matters: Shows acoustic sensing as a localization modality on micro drones.
hackathon_notes: Niche; useful if exploring acoustic self-localization.

name: Batear datasets
summary: Small Git LFS collection of drone and background audio for ESP32-S3 acoustic detection: about 89 WAV clips of DJI Mavic Pro, Mini 4 Pro and 5-inch FPV flights, ambient (urban, rural, fireworks, bat sites) and synthetic sweeps, plus resample and spectrogram tools.
why_it_matters: Targets low-cost acoustic sensor nodes - the cheapest C-UAS tripwire.
hackathon_notes: MIT. Run git lfs pull to get the audio. Pair with the Batear firmware for a microcontroller acoustic sensor demo.

name: drone-acoustic-detection
summary: Open field-test toolkit for acoustic and radar detection of low-signature drones on COTS hardware, aiming at FPV detection baselines.
why_it_matters: FPV-class detection baselines are missing in literature; this gives a reproducible method.
hackathon_notes: MIT, but the README frames it as research and educational use. No field recordings ship in the repo - the experiments run on synthesized signals (--mock) until you record your own. Follow the field protocol to measure your own detection ranges.

name: Game4Loc / GTA-UAV
summary: Benchmark and code for UAV geo-localization trained on synthetic game imagery with partial-match drone-satellite pairs (AAAI 2025).
why_it_matters: Synthetic data generation for geo-localization reduces the need for real flight data.
hackathon_notes: Code Apache-2.0; the HF dataset cards also say Apache-2.0, but the imagery is rendered from GTA V, so check the game's terms before non-research use. LR set 12.8 GB, HR 143.3 GB. Pretrained cross-area and same-area checkpoints on HF; fine-tune on your area's satellite tiles.

name: PiLoT
summary: Neural pixel-to-3D registration for UAV ego-localization and target geo-localization against a geo-referenced 3D map; release uses 3D Gaussian Splatting map backends (CVPR 2026).
why_it_matters: Absolute 6-DoF pose from a 3D map is a strong GNSS-denied fix for low-altitude drones.
hackathon_notes: GPU-heavy (CUDA extension build, CityGaussian conda env); demo data is about 15 GB. Code is MIT, but PiLoT-data on HF is gated: non-commercial research or education only, no redistribution. From NUDT, which is on the US Entity List - check your programme's rules.

name: FSRA
summary: Transformer-based feature segmentation and region alignment for drone-to-satellite geo-localization (TCSVT 2022).
why_it_matters: Widely used baseline on University-1652.
hackathon_notes: No licence file (all rights reserved). Trains on University-1652, which is request-only and research use only. Good comparison baseline.

name: PairUAV
summary: Baseline for last-meter UAV navigation using diffusion-refined aerial visual servoing; serves as the baseline for the ACM MM 2026 UAV workshop challenge.
why_it_matters: Moves geo-localization from retrieval to precise relative positioning for the final approach.
hackathon_notes: No licence on the repo. Training needs University-1652 (request-only, research use only), and the bundled SuperGlue code is Magic Leap's non-commercial research-only code. Competition test set is on HF; official scores only via CodaBench.

name: UAVM 2023 challenge
summary: Page for the ACM MM 2023 drone-satellite matching challenge on University-160k, listing team code repos and the leaderboard.
why_it_matters: Index of open winning-team code for drone-satellite matching.
hackathon_notes: Public entries: MLPN (4th, R@1 92.77), DPN (6th, 90.02) and BingY998 (7th, 85.76); the top two are private, and MBEG's 98.94 was removed for using University-1652 test data. Data is University-1652-derived (request-only, research use).

name: UAVM 2024 challenge
summary: Page for the ACM MM 2024 multi-weather drone-satellite matching challenge, listing team repos.
why_it_matters: Adds weather robustness to cross-view geo-localization.
hackathon_notes: Only two listed entries are public: WAGL (4th, R@1 94.07) and WELN (5th, 85.58). Challenge data (University160k-WX) builds on University-1652 (request-only, research use).

name: MuseNet
summary: Multiple-environment self-adaptive network for aerial-view geo-localization under varied weather (Pattern Recognition 2024).
why_it_matters: Weather robustness for drone-satellite matching.
hackathon_notes: MIT code; needs University-1652 (request-only, research use). Its University-WX weather augmentation matches the UAVM 2024 multi-weather setting, but it is not named as the official challenge baseline.

name: WELN
summary: Siamese-network solution to the ACM MM 2024 multi-environment drone-satellite matching challenge.
why_it_matters: Open challenge entry for weather-robust geo-localization.
hackathon_notes: No licence (all rights reserved). Weights and the University1652-Plus weather set are on Baidu pan only, may be hard to fetch; the data derives from University-1652 (research use). 5th on the public leaderboard (R@1 85.58), 4th after one team was removed.

name: MLPN (UAVM 2023 entry)
summary: Team solution for the ACM MM 2023 drone-satellite matching challenge, 4th on the leaderboard (R@1 92.77).
why_it_matters: Open challenge entry.
hackathon_notes: MIT. Training script with hard-coded paths; needs University-1652 (request-only, research use).

name: DPN (UAVM 2023 entry)
summary: Submission for the ACM MM 2023 drone-satellite matching challenge.
why_it_matters: Open challenge entry.
hackathon_notes: One-line README, no licence (all rights reserved). 6th on the UAVM 2023 leaderboard (R@1 90.02). Needs University-1652 (request-only, research use).

name: MBEG
summary: Modern-backbone efficient geo-localization solution for UAVM 2023 including distillation training.
why_it_matters: Open entry with distillation, useful for edge deployment.
hackathon_notes: MIT. Topped the leaderboard (R@1 98.94) but was removed for using University-1652 test data; the method and distillation code are still useful. Weights on Baidu only; University-1652 is research use only.

name: GSDC 10th place solution
summary: 10th-place solution for the Kaggle Google Smartphone Decimeter Challenge.
why_it_matters: Readable Kaggle-style pipeline for smartphone GNSS post-processing.
hackathon_notes: Apache-2.0 code; GSDC data is under Kaggle competition rules (not checked). Denoises host-baseline positions (STFT + CNN, LightGBM on IMU) and snaps to training ground truth with KNN, so it relies on repeated routes. Private score about 2.61 m.

name: Smartphone Decimeter Challenge MATLAB package
summary: MATLAB package from an ION GNSS+ 2021 decimeter challenge entry.
why_it_matters: MATLAB route for smartphone GNSS positioning.
hackathon_notes: Reference only: the EKF, INS and magnitude submodules are private, so it does not run as cloned. MIT. From an ENAC master's thesis.

name: ML GNSS/IMU integration (GSDC 2022)
summary: GSDC 2022 pipeline: an ML classifier picks the drive environment (highway, tree-lined, downtown) to set rtklib-py PPK options, then a loosely coupled GNSS/IMU Kalman filter refines the result.
why_it_matters: Example of learned GNSS/IMU fusion on phone data.
hackathon_notes: Reference. No licence (all rights reserved).

name: Google SDC corrections (Swift Navigation)
summary: SSR and OSR GNSS correction data for the 2021 Google Smartphone Decimeter Challenge drives, in SBP, JSON, RTCM3 and RINEX.
why_it_matters: Real correction streams aligned to a public phone dataset - good for practising RTK/PPP on phones.
hackathon_notes: No licence; Swift provides it as is. 2020 drives have OSR but no or partial SSR; 2021 drives have both. Pair with GSDC 2021 data and RTKLIB.

name: MAINS
summary: Magnetic-field aided inertial navigation system for indoor positioning, compared against a magnetic EKF.
why_it_matters: Magnetic field anomalies as a GNSS-free position aid indoors.
hackathon_notes: MATLAB with eight recorded datasets in data/. Clone with --recurse-submodules (MAINS is a submodule). MAINS code is GPL-3.0, MAGEKF Apache-2.0. Test on your own magnetometer arrays.

name: Magnetic-field odometry
summary: MATLAB simulation of a tightly-integrated magnetic-field aided INS using a magnetometer array; it generates its own trajectory and sensor data.
why_it_matters: Shows magnetometer arrays as odometry where cameras fail.
hackathon_notes: MATLAB simulation only, no real data. GPL-3.0.

name: ScalLoc
summary: Continuous geo-localization of oblique thermal UAV sequences against a 2D satellite map (VGGT reconstruction + MINIMA-RoMa matching), with the Thermal-Oblique dataset: 216 trajectories, 28,112 frames.
why_it_matters: Night-time thermal geo-localization with oblique cameras, closer to real FPV/ISR views.
hackathon_notes: No code licence yet - the author's notice says it is pending (all rights reserved). Depends on VGGT, whose licence prohibits military and warfare use; the original VGGT-1B checkpoint is non-commercial. Data, map and weights are on HF (gated, Apache-2.0 tag).

name: MBZIRC Maritime Grand Challenge simulator
summary: Simulator (Ignition Fortress + ROS 2) for the MBZIRC Maritime Grand Challenge where UAVs and USVs cooperate in a GNSS-denied environment.
why_it_matters: Ready-made maritime GNSS-denied multi-vehicle scenario.
hackathon_notes: Built for Ubuntu 20.04, ROS 2 Galactic and Ignition Fortress, all now end of life; use the osrf/mbzirc Docker image (needs nvidia-docker2). Apache-2.0.

name: Race Against the Machine dataset
summary: Annotated dataset of fast autonomous and human-piloted quadrotor flight with visual, inertial and mocap data plus labelled racing gates, from TII.
why_it_matters: High-speed VIO and gate-relative state estimation data.
hackathon_notes: Dataset CC BY 4.0, code MIT. 18 autonomous and 18 piloted flights per README, over 21 m/s with mocap ground truth; v3.0.0 (Oct 2025) adds six pro-pilot flights. Use to test VIO at high speed.

name: Swarm in Blocks
summary: Block-programming and web control platform for drone swarms on COEX Clover (ROS, Gazebo); CopterHack 2022 winner by team Atena. The repo now holds Swarm in Blocks 2.0 (CopterHack 2023, 4th).
why_it_matters: Example of a winning open CopterHack project.
hackathon_notes: No licence (all rights reserved). Runs on the Clover Gazebo simulation; the real-swarm mode is barely tested.

name: Clover Rescue Project
summary: Main web server and client (Node.js, Socket.IO) of the Clover Rescue Team's CopterHack 2022 project, 3rd place; the drone-side server is DevMBS/CRTClover.
why_it_matters: Example finalist code.
hackathon_notes: MIT. Reference only.

name: Gazebo Sim (gz-sim)
summary: Current-generation Gazebo robotics simulator with pluggable physics, rendering and a large sensor library (IMU, GPS/NavSat, lidar, cameras, magnetometer, altimeter). Successor to Gazebo Classic.
why_it_matters: The default SITL backend for both PX4 and ArduPilot today; the place to inject sensor noise, GNSS dropouts and degraded conditions into a full autopilot stack.
hackathon_notes: Install a binary release (Harmonic or later) plus ros_gz. Pair with PX4 'make px4_sitl gz_x500' or ardupilot_gazebo. GPU helps for camera sensors; headless server mode works for CI.

name: ros_gz bridge
summary: Bridge packages that relay topics, services and clock between Gazebo Sim transport and ROS 1/ROS 2.
why_it_matters: Needed whenever a ROS 2 navigation or SLAM stack has to consume simulated sensor streams from Gazebo.
hackathon_notes: Use parameter_bridge with a YAML of topic mappings. Match the ros_gz branch to your ROS 2 distro and Gazebo release or builds fail.

name: PX4 Gazebo models
summary: Model and world repository for the new Gazebo, used by PX4 SITL targets such as gz_x500.
