why_it_matters: Shows how PX4 vehicles and sensors are described for gz-sim; the starting point for adding custom sensors to a PX4 airframe.
hackathon_notes: Fetched automatically by PX4 SITL. Fork and edit SDF to add cameras or change sensor noise.

name: jMAVSim
summary: Lightweight Java multirotor simulator that speaks MAVLink to PX4, without a 3D-world physics engine.
why_it_matters: Was the fastest way to get a PX4 SITL quad flying for MAVLink, GCS or mission-logic work when sensors and worlds do not matter; PX4 has since replaced it with SIH.
hackathon_notes: Removed from PX4-Autopilot main in September 2026; 'make px4_sitl jmavsim' only exists up to PX4 v1.17. On current PX4 use 'make px4_sitl_sih sihsim_quadx' with Hawkeye. Needs a JDK. No cameras or lidar, so not for perception work. This repo is PX4's fork of DrTon/jMAVSim.

name: ArduPilot SITL Models
summary: Collection of aircraft and vehicle models and parameter files for ArduPilot SITL, mostly for the RealFlight simulator (planes, quadplanes, tailsitters, helicopters, multicopters) plus a Gazebo package with models and worlds.
why_it_matters: Ready-made airframes (including fixed-wing and VTOL) save hours when a hackathon scenario needs something other than a quadcopter.
hackathon_notes: No top-level README. RealFlight is a paid commercial simulator; without it, only the Gazebo folder is usable. RealFlight model folders each have their own README.

name: AirSim
summary: Unreal Engine based simulator for drones and cars with camera, depth, lidar, IMU, GPS, barometer and magnetometer models and a Python/C++ API. Microsoft wound down development and pointed users to Project AirSim.
why_it_matters: Still the most widely used photorealistic drone sim in research papers; many visual-nav and geolocalization datasets were rendered with it.
hackathon_notes: Prebuilt binary environments are the quickest path. Building from source requires a matching old Unreal version. For new work prefer Colosseum or Project AirSim.

name: Colosseum (AirSim fork)
summary: Community fork of AirSim that moved it to newer Unreal Engine 5 releases. The GitHub repository is now marked archived.
why_it_matters: Was the main path to run AirSim on UE5; useful as a reference port even though it is no longer maintained.
hackathon_notes: Archived on GitHub, so expect unanswered issues. Use only if you need its UE5 changes specifically.

name: Project AirSim
summary: Open-source release of Project AirSim, the rewrite and successor of AirSim, for building and testing autonomous aerial systems in high-fidelity Unreal environments.
why_it_matters: The actively developed line of the AirSim family, relevant for photorealistic aerial perception and autonomy testing.
hackathon_notes: Check its docs for supported Unreal version and OS. Heavier setup than AirSim binaries; budget several hours.

name: FlightGoggles
summary: Unity3D and ROS framework from MIT for photorealistic camera rendering with real or simulated vehicle dynamics in the loop.
why_it_matters: Pioneered vehicle-in-the-loop rendering: fly a real drone in a mocap room while feeding it synthetic imagery.
hackathon_notes: Not actively maintained since 2024; ROS1. Mostly of interest as a reference or alongside the Blackbird dataset.

name: Pegasus Simulator
summary: Framework on top of NVIDIA Isaac Sim for simulating multirotors with PX4 in the loop and Python-defined vehicles and sensors.
why_it_matters: Gives PX4 users photorealistic, GPU-accelerated Omniverse rendering while keeping the real autopilot stack.
hackathon_notes: Needs an RTX GPU and an Isaac Sim install; match Pegasus release to the Isaac Sim version listed in its docs.

name: NVIDIA Isaac Sim
summary: NVIDIA's Omniverse-based robot simulator, now open source, with RTX sensor simulation (cameras, lidar, IMU) and ROS 2 bridges.
why_it_matters: Base layer for Pegasus, OmniDrones and Isaac Lab; strong for synthetic data generation for perception models.
hackathon_notes: RTX GPU and a lot of disk required. Use the prebuilt container or pip install rather than building from source in a hackathon.

name: Isaac Lab
summary: Robot-learning framework on Isaac Sim for massively parallel RL and imitation learning, with navigation and locomotion task examples.
why_it_matters: Fast route to training learned navigation or locomotion policies with thousands of parallel simulated robots.
hackathon_notes: Install via pip on a supported Isaac Sim version. Start from an existing nav task config rather than writing environments from scratch.

name: CARLA
summary: Open-source autonomous-driving simulator on Unreal with camera, lidar, radar, GNSS and IMU sensors, traffic and weather control.
why_it_matters: Standard ground-vehicle testbed for localization and planning under weather, night and sensor-degradation conditions.
hackathon_notes: Use packaged releases and the Python client; the ROS 2 bridge is separate. A decent GPU is required.

name: RotorS
summary: Gazebo Classic MAV simulator from ETH ASL with multirotor models, IMU and odometry sensor plugins and example controllers.
why_it_matters: Classic reference for MAV sim used in many VIO and planning papers; its IMU noise models are still frequently copied.
hackathon_notes: ROS1 and Gazebo Classic only; use for reproducing older papers rather than new builds.

name: Aerial Gym Simulator
summary: GPU-parallel aerial-robot simulator from NTNU ARL built on NVIDIA Isaac Gym, with depth/range sensors and RL navigation examples.
why_it_matters: Train learned obstacle avoidance and navigation for drones at scale with simulated depth cameras and lidar.
hackathon_notes: Needs NVIDIA GPU and Isaac Gym preview (a legacy package); check README for current install path.

name: gym-pybullet-drones
summary: Gymnasium environments on PyBullet for single and multi-agent quadcopter control and RL (formerly under utiasDSL).
why_it_matters: Lowest-friction multi-drone RL sandbox: pure Python, CPU-only, quick to modify.
hackathon_notes: pip install in a venv and run examples within minutes. No photorealistic sensors; good for control, swarming and planning logic.

name: OmniDrones
summary: GPU-parallel drone simulation and RL platform built on Isaac Sim.
why_it_matters: Supports multi-drone and transport tasks with vectorized environments for learning-based autonomy.
hackathon_notes: Pinned to specific Isaac Sim versions (README badge: 4.1.0) and Linux only. The author states at the top of the README that this version is hard to maintain and will not be updated further; treat it as frozen.

name: RotorPy
summary: Python multirotor simulator with aerodynamic effects (drag, wind) for education and research.
why_it_matters: Good for studying estimator and controller behaviour under wind and disturbances without a game engine.
hackathon_notes: pip installable, runs on a laptop. Has IMU and mocap-style sensor models; add your own estimator in Python.

name: Webots
summary: General-purpose open-source robot simulator with many robot models and sensors including GPS, compass, IMU, lidar and radar.
why_it_matters: Cross-platform and easy to install; good for ground and multi-robot nav demos with ROS 2 integration.
hackathon_notes: Installers for Windows, macOS and Linux. webots_ros2 package for ROS 2. Less common in aerial autonomy.

name: HoloOcean (documentation)
summary: Documentation repository for HoloOcean, BYU's Unreal-based underwater simulator with sonar, DVL, IMU, depth and camera sensors and multi-agent support. The simulator code itself is not hosted in this repo.
why_it_matters: Photorealistic underwater sim aimed at marine navigation and SLAM research, including acoustic modems for multi-agent setups.
hackathon_notes: Follow the installation page of the docs; Python package plus downloadable worlds. Heavy GPU load for sonar rendering.

name: GRID playground (AirGen)
summary: Notes and examples for the GRID platform from General Robotics (formerly Scaled Foundations), which pairs the AirSim-derived AirGen simulator with foundation-model perception and LLM-driven robot control.
why_it_matters: Shows a sim plus foundation-model workflow for aerial autonomy, close to 'LLM in the loop' hackathon ideas.
hackathon_notes: Uses the hosted GRID platform for the sim side; check account requirements before relying on it.

name: JSBSim
summary: Open-source flight dynamics model library for fixed-wing and other aircraft, used by FlightGear and as an ArduPilot SITL backend.
why_it_matters: Credible fixed-wing dynamics for testing navigation filters on aircraft profiles rather than quadcopters.
hackathon_notes: Python bindings via pip. Combine with ArduPilot SITL for an autopilot loop.

name: MARSIM
summary: Lightweight point-realistic lidar simulator for UAVs from HKU MaRS, supporting rotating and solid-state lidar patterns.
why_it_matters: Fast way to test lidar-based UAV navigation and planning without a full game-engine sim.
hackathon_notes: ROS based; runs on CPU or modest GPU. Pairs well with FAST-LIO-style stacks.

name: ESIM
summary: Event camera simulator from UZH RPG that renders event streams from simulated scenes.
why_it_matters: Generates event-camera data for high-speed or low-light VIO research without hardware.
hackathon_notes: ROS1 and older build tooling. For converting existing video to events, rpg_vid2e is easier.

name: evo
summary: Python package and CLI for evaluating odometry and SLAM trajectories (ATE/RPE, alignment, plotting) in TUM, KITTI, EuRoC and ROS bag formats.
why_it_matters: The default way to score a nav or SLAM result against ground truth; essential for any demo that claims accuracy.
hackathon_notes: pip install evo. Run evo_ape with alignment flags; it reads most dataset ground-truth formats directly.

name: rpg_trajectory_evaluation
summary: Toolbox for quantitative trajectory evaluation of VO/VIO, implementing the alignment and relative-error protocol from Zhang & Scaramuzza (IROS 2018).
why_it_matters: Implements the alignment conventions used in many VIO benchmarks; good for apples-to-apples comparisons.
hackathon_notes: Old Python 2 era code, ROS optional. evo is easier for quick use.

name: pykitti
summary: Python loaders for the KITTI raw and odometry datasets.
why_it_matters: Removes boilerplate when using KITTI's GPS/IMU, lidar and stereo data for localization experiments.
hackathon_notes: pip install pykitti and point it at the dataset folders.

name: UZH-FPV dataset tools
summary: Companion repo for the UZH-FPV drone racing dataset with scripts and info.
why_it_matters: Aggressive high-speed drone sequences stress VIO well beyond EuRoC.
hackathon_notes: Inactive since 2020; dataset itself is on the UZH site under CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (non-commercial). The repo code is GPL-3.0.

name: Hilti SLAM Challenge 2022
summary: Repository for the 2022 Hilti SLAM Challenge with dataset info and evaluation tooling.
why_it_matters: Construction-site sequences with accurate ground truth; a strong test of lidar/visual-inertial SLAM in GNSS-denied indoor spaces.
hackathon_notes: Bags are on the challenge site and Hugging Face (Hilti-Research/hilti-slam-challenge-2022); ground truth and evaluation scripts are in the repo. Data licence is CC BY-NC-SA 3.0: non-commercial use only.

name: Hilti SLAM Challenge 2023
summary: Repository for the 2023 Hilti SLAM Challenge, including multi-session sequences.
why_it_matters: Multi-session data is useful for map reuse and relocalization experiments.
hackathon_notes: Same workflow as 2022; bags on the challenge site and Hugging Face. Data licence is CC BY-NC-SA 3.0: non-commercial use only.

name: MCD: Multi-Campus Dataset
summary: Site repo for MCD, a multi-campus dataset across Asia and Europe with spinning and non-repetitive lidar, stereo cameras, IMUs, UWB ranging, survey-grade prior maps and continuous-time ground truth.
why_it_matters: Covers localization against prior maps and UWB-aided fusion in large outdoor areas.
hackathon_notes: Data downloads and tutorials are linked from the site. Licensed CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, intended for non-commercial academic use.

name: NTU VIRAL dataset
summary: Site repo for NTU VIRAL, an aerial dataset with lidars, cameras, IMU and UWB ranging from a drone.
why_it_matters: Rare UWB-equipped drone dataset for range-aided fusion experiments.
hackathon_notes: ROS bags; download links on the site. Licensed CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 for non-commercial academic use; commercial use needs contact with the authors.

name: M2DGR
summary: Multi-modal, multi-scenario ground robot dataset from SJTU with cameras, lidar, IMU, GNSS and more, indoor and outdoor.
why_it_matters: Indoor/outdoor transitions with GNSS make it useful for testing GNSS-loss handling in fusion.
hackathon_notes: ROS bags; check repo for download mirrors. Repo says MIT but the dataset is 'provided for academic purpose'; commercial use requires contacting the authors.

name: GVINS dataset
summary: Dataset with synchronized visual, inertial and raw GNSS measurements released with GVINS.
why_it_matters: One of few datasets with raw GNSS pseudoranges plus camera and IMU, needed for tightly coupled GNSS-VIO.
hackathon_notes: ROS bags with custom GNSS message types; install the gnss_comm package. Dataset licence is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (non-commercial).

name: UrbanNav
summary: Open multisensor urban positioning dataset from PolyU IPNL with GNSS, IMU, lidar and camera in deep urban canyons.
why_it_matters: Benchmark for GNSS multipath and NLOS mitigation in cities.
hackathon_notes: Pick one Hong Kong sequence and run an RTKLIB plus loosely coupled baseline to show urban degradation.

name: ALTO
summary: Placeholder repo for ALTO, an aerial-view, large-scale, terrain-oriented dataset for UAV place recognition and localization. It holds only a README with Dropbox links to the ICRA 2022 GPR Competition rounds; the full dataset is still marked 'Coming soon'.
why_it_matters: Directly targets UAV localization over terrain when GNSS is unavailable.
hackathon_notes: Inactive since 2022; only the competition subsets are downloadable (Dropbox), so check the links still work before planning around it. The BSD-3 licence covers the repo; no data terms are stated.

name: VPAIR
summary: Repo for VPAIR, an aerial visual place recognition dataset matching low-altitude flight imagery to reference orthophotos.
why_it_matters: Benchmark for UAV visual geolocalization against georeferenced maps.
hackathon_notes: Academic use only, commercial use prohibited (README). Full set is 20.5 GB (2,706 query/reference pairs plus 10,000 distractors); a 0.86 GB sample is on Zenodo. The repo itself holds only the README and images. Evaluate with VPR-methods-evaluation.

name: AerialVL
summary: Visual geo-localization dataset and code designed for aerial vehicles.
why_it_matters: Another aerial-to-map benchmark with sequential flights, useful for testing filtering over VPR outputs.
hackathon_notes: Check README for map tile download steps.

name: Mapillary SLS
summary: Tools for the Mapillary Street-level Sequences dataset for lifelong visual place recognition.
why_it_matters: Large, diverse street-level VPR benchmark used to train many current VPR models.
hackathon_notes: Dataset download needs registration on Mapillary.

name: VPR-Bench
summary: Open-source visual place recognition evaluation framework from the IJCV paper, with many datasets and techniques integrated.
why_it_matters: Ready harness to compare VPR methods across conditions and viewpoints.
hackathon_notes: Older dependencies; consider VPR-methods-evaluation for modern models. Bundled datasets and techniques keep their own licences (see each folder); the MIT licence covers the framework code only.

name: tartanairpy
summary: Python package for downloading, customizing and iterating the TartanAir-V2 synthetic dataset.
why_it_matters: TartanAir's photorealistic scenes with weather and lighting variety stress-test SLAM and VO.
hackathon_notes: Download only the environments and modalities you need - full set is very large.

name: pyboreas
summary: Devkit for the Boreas multi-season driving dataset with radar, lidar, camera and GNSS/INS ground truth.
why_it_matters: Radar plus lidar over seasons and snow suits all-weather localization work.
hackathon_notes: Data is hosted on S3; download selected sequences.

name: Oxford RobotCar SDK
summary: SDK for the Oxford RobotCar dataset with loaders and projection tools.
why_it_matters: Long-term, all-condition driving data is a staple for localization and place recognition research.
hackathon_notes: Inactive since 2022; Python and MATLAB helpers still work. The dataset itself is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, for non-commercial academic use only.

name: Blackbird dataset
summary: MIT dataset of aggressive indoor quadrotor flights with real IMU and motor data and rendered camera imagery.
why_it_matters: Combines real flight dynamics with synthetic vision, good for VIO under aggressive motion.
hackathon_notes: Inactive since 2022; download scripts may need adaptation.

name: ORB-SLAM2
summary: Feature-based SLAM for monocular, stereo and RGB-D cameras using ORB features, with loop closing and relocalization against a reusable map.
why_it_matters: The reference visual SLAM baseline most papers compare against; cheap camera-only localization when GNSS is denied.
hackathon_notes: Superseded by ORB-SLAM3 and no longer developed; builds need patching on modern OpenCV/Eigen. Use only to reproduce old baselines.

name: ORB-SLAM3
summary: Visual, visual-inertial and multi-map SLAM supporting monocular, stereo and RGB-D cameras with pinhole and fisheye models, using a map atlas to survive tracking loss.
why_it_matters: Still the most cited open VI-SLAM system; a solid GNSS-denied drift baseline for drones and ground robots.
hackathon_notes: Build against Pangolin, OpenCV and Eigen; expect a few compile fixes. Run on EuRoC or TUM-VI first, then your own camera after Kalibr calibration. Upstream sees little activity.

name: ORB_SLAM3_ROS2
summary: ROS 2 wrapper package that exposes ORB-SLAM3 as nodes for monocular, stereo and RGB-D input.
why_it_matters: Shortest path to running ORB-SLAM3 inside a ROS 2 robot stack.
hackathon_notes: Needs a working ORB-SLAM3 build first; check the README for the ROS 2 distro it targets before choosing your Docker base image.

name: VINS-Mono
summary: Optimization-based monocular visual-inertial estimator with sliding-window bundle adjustment, online initialization, loop closure and pose-graph reuse.
why_it_matters: The canonical one-camera-plus-IMU estimator; works on light UAV payloads where stereo or LiDAR is too heavy.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1 only and no longer maintained; the README targets Ubuntu 16.04 / ROS Kinetic with Ceres 1.14, and the bundled Docker image is ROS Kinetic. Sensitive to time sync and initialization motion.

name: VINS-Fusion
summary: Extension of VINS-Mono supporting mono+IMU, stereo, and stereo+IMU, with optional loose fusion of global sensors such as GPS.
why_it_matters: Shows how to plug intermittent GNSS into a VIO estimator, which is the core pattern for degraded-PNT navigation.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1; use a Docker image. The global-fusion node is a good template for injecting GNSS when it is trusted and dropping it when jammed.

name: OpenVINS
summary: MSCKF-based visual-inertial navigation platform with online calibration, a simulator, and extensive documentation for research use.
why_it_matters: Probably the best-documented VIO codebase; filter-based, light enough for embedded boards.
hackathon_notes: Supports ROS 1 and ROS 2. Its built-in simulator lets you test without hardware on day one. Docs site explains every estimator component.

name: MINS
summary: Multi-sensor aided inertial navigation that fuses IMU with camera, LiDAR, GNSS and wheel odometry, including online spatial/temporal calibration and a multi-sensor simulator.
why_it_matters: Directly relevant to assured PNT: one estimator that degrades gracefully as individual sensors (including GNSS) drop out.
hackathon_notes: Start with the provided simulated data to see each sensor's contribution, then disable GNSS mid-run to demo a jamming scenario.

name: Kimera-VIO
summary: Stereo visual-inertial odometry with a factor-graph backend, robust loop closure and real-time 3D mesh generation; the odometry core of the Kimera stack.
why_it_matters: Gives both a pose and a lightweight 3D mesh, useful for situational-awareness displays.
hackathon_notes: Heavier build (GTSAM, OpenGV, DBoW2); use the Docker setup. The ROS wrapper lives in a separate repo.

name: Kimera-RPGO
summary: Robust pose-graph optimization that rejects bad loop closures via pairwise consistency maximization on top of GTSAM.
why_it_matters: Outlier-robust loop closure is what keeps a long GNSS-denied mission from corrupting its map; reusable outside Kimera.
hackathon_notes: Small library; feed it any odometry + loop closure edges. Good drop-in back end for a custom front end.

name: Basalt
summary: GitHub mirror of Basalt, a visual-inertial odometry and mapping system built around non-linear factor recovery, with calibration tools; primary development is on GitLab.
why_it_matters: Fast, accurate stereo VIO that runs well on CPUs; also ships camera-IMU calibration.
hackathon_notes: Submit issues upstream on GitLab. Install from GitLab release binaries (Ubuntu 22.04+ amd64, macOS arm64) or build from source with CMake presets + vcpkg; ROS integration is via community wrappers.

name: SVO Pro
summary: Open release of SVO Pro: semi-direct visual(-inertial) odometry with fisheye/omni camera support, optional global map and loop closure.
why_it_matters: Very low-latency front end suited to fast agile flight on compute-limited drones.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1 / catkin build; dormant since 2024. Good when CPU budget is tight.

name: DSO (Direct Sparse Odometry)
summary: Direct monocular visual odometry that optimizes photometric error over a sparse set of pixels with joint photometric calibration.
why_it_matters: Works in low-texture scenes where feature-based methods fail; the basis for DM-VIO and many direct methods.
hackathon_notes: No IMU, no loop closure, scale-ambiguous; mostly useful as a building block or comparison.

name: DM-VIO
summary: Monocular visual-inertial odometry built on DSO using delayed marginalization and pose-graph bundle adjustment for IMU initialization.
why_it_matters: Strong monocular VIO accuracy; good for single-camera drones.
hackathon_notes: Standalone build with an optional ROS wrapper repo. Expects photometrically calibrated input for best results.

name: ROVIO
summary: Robust visual-inertial odometry using an iterated EKF directly on image-patch photometric errors.
why_it_matters: Long a go-to VIO on PX4/MAV research platforms because it is cheap to run.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1 / catkin. Lightweight; tuning of patch and feature counts matters.

name: MSCKF_VIO
summary: Stereo multi-state constraint Kalman filter VIO designed for fast autonomous flight.
why_it_matters: Lean filter-based stereo VIO that runs comfortably on embedded CPUs.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1; unmaintained. Tested heavily on EuRoC; good comparison point to OpenVINS. Licence: Penn Software License - non-profit research use only, no redistribution without Penn's approval; commercial use needs a separate licence.

name: OKVIS2
summary: Keyframe-based visual-inertial SLAM with loop closure and a realtime scalable factor-graph design; second generation of OKVIS.
why_it_matters: Mature research VI-SLAM from the ETH/TUM lineage with active maintenance.
hackathon_notes: CMake build; check the README for ROS integration and the camera/IMU config format for your sensor.

name: OKVIS2-X
summary: Extension of OKVIS2 that can additionally use dense depth or LiDAR and fuse GNSS.
why_it_matters: Recent (2025-2026) multi-sensor VI-SLAM that includes GNSS fusion, matching assured-PNT architectures.
hackathon_notes: New codebase; expect some setup friction. Good showcase for switching GNSS on/off.

name: AirSLAM
summary: Point-and-line visual(-inertial) SLAM using learned features, designed for illumination-robust operation, with TensorRT acceleration; successor to AirVO.
why_it_matters: Targets lighting changes (dawn/dusk/night), a common failure mode for camera navigation.
hackathon_notes: Needs an NVIDIA GPU (TensorRT). Docker recommended.

name: maplab
summary: Modular multi-session, multi-modal mapping framework with map merging, optimization and localization against saved maps.
why_it_matters: Build a map once, then localize repeatedly against it; supports multi-robot and multi-session merges.
hackathon_notes: Large ROS 1 codebase; only worth it if you need persistent map management.

name: RTAB-Map
summary: Graph-based SLAM library and app supporting RGB-D, stereo and LiDAR, with memory management for large-scale loop closure and map reuse.
why_it_matters: Practical all-rounder with GUI, database and localization modes; easiest way to get a working 3D map on a ground robot.
hackathon_notes: Install via apt binaries (ROS) or the standalone app. Supports phone/iPad LiDAR capture. Save a map, then switch to localization mode.

name: rtabmap_ros
summary: ROS and ROS 2 integration for RTAB-Map, exposing SLAM, localization and odometry nodes.
why_it_matters: Drop-in SLAM for ROS 2 Nav2 stacks.
hackathon_notes: apt-installable for supported distros; launch examples cover common sensors.

name: DROID-SLAM
summary: Deep visual SLAM that iterates dense bundle adjustment through a recurrent update operator, for monocular, stereo and RGB-D input.
why_it_matters: Much more robust than classic pipelines on hard sequences; strong learned baseline.
hackathon_notes: Needs a large-memory NVIDIA GPU; not real-time on embedded. Pretrained weights available.

name: DPVO / DPV-SLAM
summary: Deep Patch Visual Odometry: learned sparse patch tracking for VO, plus DPV-SLAM with loop closure.
why_it_matters: Lighter learned VO than DROID-SLAM, closer to real-time on a desktop GPU.
hackathon_notes: CUDA build of custom kernels; follow the conda instructions.

name: MASt3R-SLAM
summary: Real-time dense monocular SLAM built on the MASt3R two-view 3D reconstruction prior, needing no fixed camera model (CVPR 2025).
why_it_matters: Works with uncalibrated cameras, useful for opportunistic imagery from unknown cameras.
hackathon_notes: Requires a capable NVIDIA GPU and model checkpoint downloads. Great demo value on handheld video. Licence: the code is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and the MASt3R checkpoints are also non-commercial - research and demo use only.

name: VGGT
summary: Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer: a feed-forward network predicting camera poses, depth and point maps from one or many images (CVPR 2025 best paper).
why_it_matters: Instant pose and geometry from a handful of frames; a building block for learned relocalization and mapping.
hackathon_notes: GPU inference via PyTorch; Hugging Face demo for quick tests. Not a full SLAM system by itself. Licence: LICENSE.txt prohibits military, warfare and ITAR-controlled uses; the default VGGT-1B checkpoint is non-commercial and only the gated VGGT-1B-Commercial checkpoint allows commercial use.

name: MonoGS (Gaussian Splatting SLAM)
summary: Gaussian-splatting SLAM for monocular, stereo and RGB-D cameras that tracks and maps directly against a 3D Gaussian representation.
why_it_matters: Produces photorealistic maps useful for operator situational awareness and later simulation.
hackathon_notes: Needs a strong GPU; not real-time on embedded hardware. Best as an offline mapping demo. Licence: Imperial College MonoGS licence - non-commercial, internal or academic research use only.

name: SplaTAM
summary: Dense RGB-D SLAM that tracks and maps using 3D Gaussians and differentiable rendering (CVPR 2024).
why_it_matters: Reference Gaussian-splatting SLAM for RGB-D sensors.
hackathon_notes: GPU-heavy and slower than real time; good for offline indoor captures. The repo is BSD-3, but it depends on diff-gaussian-rasterization-w-depth, which carries the Inria Gaussian-Splatting licence (non-commercial research use only).

name: Photo-SLAM
summary: Couples ORB-SLAM3-style geometric tracking with a photorealistic Gaussian map for monocular, stereo and RGB-D cameras (CVPR 2024).
why_it_matters: Classic robust tracking plus a nice-looking map, closer to real time than pure splatting SLAM.
hackathon_notes: LibTorch + CUDA build; check version pins carefully. Licence: GPL-3.0 overall, but the repo also ships the Inria Gaussian-Splatting licence (LICENSE.md), which limits that code to non-commercial research use.

name: ESVO
summary: Event-based stereo visual odometry using spatio-temporal consistency of two event cameras for mapping and tracking.
why_it_matters: Event cameras keep working under high dynamic range and fast motion, where frame cameras blur or saturate.
hackathon_notes: Needs stereo event cameras or recorded datasets; ROS 1.

name: Ultimate SLAM
summary: Open-source release of Ultimate SLAM, combining events, standard frames and IMU for VIO in HDR and high-speed scenarios (RA-L 2018).
why_it_matters: Template for fusing event cameras with frames and IMU for robust flight state estimation.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1 / catkin; test on event datasets before buying hardware.

name: Event-based Vision Resources
summary: Community-curated list of event-camera papers, datasets, drivers, simulators and code.
why_it_matters: Fastest way to find event-camera datasets and odometry code.
hackathon_notes: Use as a discovery index; not runnable code.

name: HKU Event-based VO/VIO/SLAM
summary: Dataset and index of event-based VO, VIO and SLAM work from HKU ArcLab, including stereo event sequences.
why_it_matters: Ready-made event data for testing event odometry without hardware.
hackathon_notes: Download sequences as rosbags from OneDrive or Baidu Disk. The README warns that ESVO, EVO and Ultimate SLAM fail on most of the stereo sequences, so expect a hard benchmark. Licence: MIT, but the README says the data is provided for academic purposes and commercial use needs contact with the lab.

name: ROVTIO
summary: Visual-thermal-inertial odometry extending ROVIO to fuse asynchronous thermal and visual images with IMU, switching to whichever camera is informative.
why_it_matters: Thermal keeps odometry alive in darkness and smoke; NTNU ARL targets subterranean and degraded environments.
hackathon_notes: Needs a thermal camera synced to IMU (or their datasets). Thermal calibration targets need a heated pattern.

name: ETIO
summary: Edge-based monocular thermal-inertial odometry that tracks thermal edges for visually degraded environments.
why_it_matters: Low-cost night/smoke navigation from a single thermal camera plus IMU.
hackathon_notes: Code released with the paper; try on public thermal datasets first.

name: RRxIO
summary: Radar visual/thermal inertial odometry fusing 4D mmWave radar with a visual or thermal camera and IMU for degraded visual conditions.
why_it_matters: Radar plus thermal is a strong combination for fog, smoke and darkness.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1; datasets released by the author. Good for a degraded-visibility demo.

name: RIO
summary: EKF-based radar-inertial odometry using 4D mmWave radar ego-velocity measurements.
why_it_matters: Cheap automotive radars give velocity in fog/smoke/darkness; a minimal radar odometry template.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1; uses the author's radar ego-velocity estimator. Works with TI mmWave-class sensors.

name: 4DRadarSLAM
summary: 4D radar SLAM with scan-to-scan registration, loop closure and pose-graph optimization, released with an NTU 4D radar dataset.
why_it_matters: One of the few full SLAM pipelines for 4D imaging radar, the all-weather sensor for ground vehicles.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1; structured like hdl_graph_slam. Test on their dataset first.

name: CFEAR Radarodometry
summary: Landing page for CFEAR, learning-free spinning-radar odometry that filters returns to sparse oriented surface points and registers against keyframes. This repo holds only a README and LICENSE; the code is in dan11003/CFEAR_Radarodometry_code_public.
why_it_matters: Strong baseline for spinning (Navtech-style) radar odometry; robust in weather that defeats LiDAR.
hackathon_notes: Clone CFEAR_Radarodometry_code_public for the ROS 1 code (Melodic or later; Oxford Radar RobotCar demo bag provided). Benchmarked on Oxford Radar RobotCar and Boreas. GPL-3.0.

name: Go-RIO
summary: Ground-optimized 4D radar-inertial odometry integrating continuous velocity via Gaussian processes (ICRA 2025 best paper finalist).
why_it_matters: Recent state of the art for 4D radar odometry on ground vehicles.
hackathon_notes: Recent code; check sensor assumptions against your radar.

name: Gaussian-RIO
summary: 4D radar-inertial odometry using Gaussian modeling of radar points and multi-hypothesis scan matching.
why_it_matters: Another recent open 4D radar odometry baseline, useful for comparison.
hackathon_notes: Small research codebase; read the paper before integrating.

name: LIO-SAM
summary: Tightly coupled LiDAR-inertial odometry via factor-graph smoothing, with optional GPS factors and loop closure.
why_it_matters: Popular LIO with built-in GNSS factors; the template for LiDAR+INS+intermittent GNSS.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1 main branch, community ROS 2 branch. Needs a 9-axis IMU and careful extrinsics.

name: FAST-LIO / FAST-LIO2
summary: Computationally efficient LiDAR-inertial odometry using an iterated error-state Kalman filter and incremental k-d tree map, mapping raw points directly.
why_it_matters: The default LIO in many field robots; runs on ARM boards and supports solid-state and spinning LiDARs.
hackathon_notes: Easiest LIO to get running; Livox drivers supported. No loop closure; pair with a localization or loop-closure add-on.

name: Point-LIO
summary: High-bandwidth LiDAR-inertial odometry that updates the state point by point, tolerating aggressive motion and IMU saturation.
why_it_matters: Handles violent motion (agile drones, vibration) where frame-based LIO breaks.
hackathon_notes: Same ecosystem as FAST-LIO; try when FAST-LIO diverges on aggressive motion.

name: FAST-LIVO2
summary: Direct LiDAR-inertial-visual odometry fusing LiDAR, camera and IMU in a sequential ESIKF update with a unified voxel map.
why_it_matters: High-accuracy colored mapping that stays robust when either LiDAR or camera degrades.
hackathon_notes: Needs hardware-synced LiDAR+camera; datasets available.

name: R3LIVE
summary: Tightly coupled LiDAR-inertial-visual estimation and RGB-colored mapping package.
why_it_matters: Produces dense colored maps useful for operator displays and mapping.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1, heavy on dependencies; FAST-LIVO2 is the newer alternative. Licence: GPLv2 but the README allows it free only for personal and academic use; commercial use needs a separately negotiated licence.

name: KISS-ICP
summary: Minimal LiDAR odometry based on point-to-point ICP with adaptive thresholding, working across sensors with few parameters.
why_it_matters: Works out of the box on almost any LiDAR without IMU; ideal hackathon starting point.
hackathon_notes: `pip install kiss-icp` and run on a rosbag or KITTI folder in minutes. Add KISS-SLAM for loop closure.

name: KISS-SLAM
summary: LiDAR SLAM that adds loop closure and pose-graph optimization on top of KISS-ICP odometry.
why_it_matters: Full LiDAR SLAM with the same low-configuration philosophy.
hackathon_notes: Pip-installable; quick to demo on outdoor bags.

name: MapClosures
summary: Loop-closure detection using bird's-eye-view density images of local LiDAR maps.
why_it_matters: Sensor-agnostic loop closure that plugs into any LiDAR odometry.
hackathon_notes: Python bindings via pip.

name: RKO-LIO
summary: LiDAR-inertial odometry aiming to work without sensor-specific modelling or heavy tuning.
why_it_matters: Recent (2025-2026) LIO from the KISS-ICP group; good for unknown hardware.
hackathon_notes: `pip install "rko_lio[all]"` then `rko_lio -v /path/to/bags` runs on ROS 1 or ROS 2 bags with a rerun viewer; a ROS 2 node is also available. You must supply IMU and LiDAR extrinsics if the bag's TF tree lacks them. No loop closure - see rko_slam for that.

name: LeGO-LOAM
summary: Lightweight ground-optimized LiDAR odometry and mapping that segments ground to speed up feature extraction on UGVs.
why_it_matters: Classic UGV LiDAR SLAM for rough terrain on modest compute.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1 only, unmaintained, tuned for Velodyne VLP-16. Use LIO-SAM or KISS-ICP instead unless reproducing baselines.

name: Cartographer
summary: Real-time 2D and 3D SLAM with submaps and branch-and-bound loop closure across many sensor configurations.
why_it_matters: Widely deployed 2D LiDAR SLAM for indoor and warehouse robots.
hackathon_notes: Project is in maintenance mode with little activity. Still available via ROS packages and works for 2D indoor mapping.

name: GLIM
summary: Versatile point-cloud localization and mapping framework with GPU-accelerated factor graphs, supporting many range sensors and optional IMU.
why_it_matters: Modern, maintained 3D mapping with GPU speedups and an extensible module system.
hackathon_notes: Prebuilt packages exist for ROS 2; GPU optional but recommended.

name: fast_gicp
summary: Collection of fast GICP and VGICP point-cloud registration implementations, multithreaded and CUDA.
why_it_matters: Fast scan registration building block used by many LiDAR and radar SLAM systems.
hackathon_notes: Successor library small_gicp is more actively maintained.

name: small_gicp
summary: Efficient, parallel point-cloud registration library (GICP, ICP variants) with C++ and Python APIs.
why_it_matters: Pip-installable registration to build your own LiDAR odometry or map-based relocalization fast.
hackathon_notes: `pip install small_gicp`; good for scan-to-map localization prototypes.

name: Faster-LIO
summary: Lightweight tightly coupled LiDAR-inertial odometry using parallel sparse incremental voxels instead of a k-d tree.
why_it_matters: Faster variant of the FAST-LIO design for constrained compute.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1; same config style as FAST-LIO.

name: DLIO
summary: Lightweight LiDAR-inertial odometry with coarse-to-fine continuous-time motion correction (ICRA 2023).
why_it_matters: Accurate and compute-light LIO for aerial and ground robots.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1 on master; ROS 2 is supported on the repo's feature/ros2 branch.

name: FAST_LIO_LOCALIZATION
summary: Relocalization in a prebuilt map using FAST-LIO odometry plus global scan-to-map registration.
why_it_matters: Localize in a map you surveyed earlier, the standard pattern for GNSS-denied ground ops in known areas.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1; build a map with FAST-LIO first, then localize. Needs a rough initial pose (RViz or another sensor). The global-localization node needs Python 2.7 and Open3D 0.9, so plan for a Melodic-era environment or a container.

name: Scan Context
summary: LiDAR global place descriptor for loop detection and relocalization (backup of the original IRAP KAIST repo).
why_it_matters: Simple, widely used LiDAR loop-closure descriptor; plugs into most LiDAR SLAM.
hackathon_notes: Header-only style C++; SC-LIO-SAM shows integration.

name: SC-LIO-SAM
summary: LIO-SAM combined with Scan Context loop closure for more reliable large-scale LiDAR-inertial SLAM.
why_it_matters: Practical recipe for adding a global descriptor to an existing LIO.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1; same setup as LIO-SAM.

name: STD
summary: Stable Triangle Descriptor for 3D point-cloud place recognition and loop closure.
why_it_matters: Works with solid-state LiDARs and small fields of view where Scan Context struggles.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1 demos; integrates with FAST-LIO. Licence: GPLv2 but the README allows it free only for personal and academic use; commercial use needs a separate licence.

name: TEASER++
summary: Certifiable, outlier-robust point-cloud registration library with C++, Python and MATLAB bindings.
why_it_matters: Global registration that tolerates extreme outlier rates, useful for map-to-map alignment and relocalization.
hackathon_notes: Needs correspondences (e.g. FPFH) as input; Python bindings make it quick to prototype.

name: Quatro
summary: Fast, robust global registration for terrestrial robots that assumes near-planar motion to cut degrees of freedom.
why_it_matters: Faster global relocalization for ground vehicles.
hackathon_notes: Smaller research codebase; pair with KISS-ICP.

name: MIMOSA
summary: Tightly coupled sliding-window factor-graph fusion of IMU with LiDAR (geometric and photometric), radar radial-speed factors and external odometry such as VIO.
why_it_matters: From the group behind DARPA SubT field robots; relevant to smoke/dark/dust scenarios.
hackathon_notes: ROS Noetic; publishes nav_msgs/Odometry. Radar factor lets you keep velocity constraints when LiDAR is blinded by dust or smoke.

name: livox_ros_driver2
summary: ROS 1/ROS 2 driver for Livox LiDARs such as Mid-360 and HAP.
why_it_matters: Mid-360 is a common cheap LiDAR for drones; you need this driver to feed FAST-LIO and friends.
hackathon_notes: Build with the Livox SDK2; set the custom message format expected by FAST-LIO.

name: hdl_graph_slam
summary: 3D LiDAR graph SLAM with NDT/GICP scan matching odometry, loop detection and optional GPS, IMU and floor-plane constraints.
why_it_matters: Simple, hackable graph SLAM that 4DRadarSLAM and others build on; GPS constraints make it handy for mixed GNSS/denied runs.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1; GLIM is the author's newer framework.

name: Kimera-Distributed
summary: Distributed front end of Kimera-Multi: handles the inter-robot communication protocol and pose-graph coarsening; the robust distributed optimization back end is DPGO.
why_it_matters: Reusable distributed SLAM back end.
hackathon_notes: Used through Kimera-Multi.

name: DPGO
summary: Distributed pose-graph optimization library with certifiably correct solutions for multi-robot SLAM.
why_it_matters: Solver core for decentralized multi-robot SLAM.
hackathon_notes: Library only; feed it pose graphs from each robot.

name: Swarm-SLAM
summary: ROS 2 decentralized collaborative SLAM supporting LiDAR, stereo and RGB-D, with sparse inter-robot communication.
why_it_matters: Designed for bandwidth-limited swarms, a realistic constraint under jamming.
hackathon_notes: This repo is only the core cslam ROS 2 package (loop closure detection front end and pose-graph back end); setup, launch files and docs live in the main MISTLab/Swarm-SLAM repo. Experiments run on recorded multi-robot datasets. Pick one sensor type to start.

name: COVINS / COVINS-G
summary: Centralized collaborative visual-inertial SLAM where agents run VIO and a server merges maps; COVINS-G is VIO-front-end agnostic.
why_it_matters: Pattern for drones sharing maps through a ground station.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1 + Docker; COVINS-G can take poses from any VIO such as OpenVINS.

name: 14 Lectures on Visual SLAM (English)
summary: English edition of Gao Xiang's open textbook on visual SLAM, from geometry and Lie groups to back-end optimization.
why_it_matters: Best free practical intro for a team ramping up on SLAM in a weekend.
hackathon_notes: PDF and code exercises (slambook2 repo).

name: White Rabbit PTP Core software (wrpc-sw)
summary: Software for the White Rabbit PTP Core (WRPC): a bare-metal PTP daemon (PPSi) and drivers for the WRPC HDL that runs on a soft CPU inside the FPGA, giving a node sub-ns sync over fibre.
why_it_matters: The node side of White Rabbit: if a team has a WR-capable FPGA board, this is what turns it into a synchronised timing endpoint.
hackathon_notes: Needs WR hardware (e.g. SPEC board + WR switch) and the wr-cores gateware. Not a 48 h starting point without the kit on the table; useful as reference for how WR extends PTP with phase tracking and link calibration.

name: White Rabbit (OHWR project hub)
summary: Umbrella OHWR project for White Rabbit, the deterministic Ethernet extension of PTP; the wiki collects specs, hardware lists, user stories and links to all WR sub-projects.
why_it_matters: Starting point to find which WR hardware, gateware and calibration notes exist before committing to WR in a timing demo.
hackathon_notes: Read the wiki, not the code. Use it to pick hardware and to cite WR accuracy from the project's own docs.

name: White Rabbit calibration
summary: Procedures and notes for calibrating White Rabbit equipment: fixed hardware delays and fibre asymmetry that must be measured for absolute time accuracy.
why_it_matters: Calibration is where path asymmetry gets removed in practice; the same A/2 error modelled in sample:timing-network-holdover.
hackathon_notes: Reference reading for explaining why uncalibrated asymmetry biases two-way time transfer.

name: Roughenough
summary: Rust Roughtime (RFC 10049) server and client with a batching UDP server, optional malfeasance reporting and several key-protection backends (KMS, PKCS#11, SSH agent).
why_it_matters: Quickest way to stand up an authenticated rough-time source and a client that checks several servers against each other.
hackathon_notes: cargo build needs a recent Rust (README states MSRV 1.94.1). Run a local server plus public servers; show the client flagging a server whose time you skew.

name: pyroughtime
summary: Python Roughtime library and CLI implementing RFC 10049; validates signatures against server long-term keys, queries several servers to catch a misbehaving one, and includes a small test server.
why_it_matters: Python is the fastest route to put Roughtime into a hackathon notebook or detector.
hackathon_notes: pip install pycryptodome in the venv. Query several servers, then run the bundled test server with a wrong clock to show detection.

name: ntpperf
summary: Load generator for NTP servers and PTP masters by chrony's author: simulates many clients with raw Ethernet frames via libpcap and reports responses, losses and, with a known direct link, how transmit timestamp accuracy degrades with rate.
why_it_matters: Tests whether a time server stays accurate under request floods - a denial-of-service angle on timing infrastructure.
hackathon_notes: Needs a dedicated link and routing so responses come back to the test host. Lab tool, not demo material.

name: flashptpd
summary: Experimental C++17 client/server style PTP from Meinberg: the client sends Sync with a request TLV and the server answers, so no BMCA or master announce is needed. Archived.
why_it_matters: Shows a unicast request/response PTP variant close to NTP in shape; useful when thinking about how a client chooses among several servers.
hackathon_notes: Archived; read for the protocol idea, do not build on it.

name: ptp-book
summary: Open book on PTP (IEEE 1588 / gPTP) in Chinese with an English translation: BMCA, the four-timestamp maths, transparent clocks, hardware timestamping, security, a walk through linuxptp source, and a ~1000-line ptp-lite implementation.
why_it_matters: Fast self-study path for a team member who has to explain or modify PTP during the event.
hackathon_notes: Read the English chapters for BMCA and the servo; ptp-lite is small enough to instrument for a delay-attack demo.

name: LibPTP
summary: OMNeT++/INET library for simulating IEEE 1588-2008 networks: ordinary, boundary and transparent clocks, E2E and P2P delay, a PI servo with pluggable servos and filters, and power-law clock noise via LibPLN.
why_it_matters: A packet-level PTP network simulator if a stdlib model is too coarse.
hackathon_notes: OMNeT++ setup is heavy and the repo was last pushed in 2021. Prefer sample:timing-network-holdover or clknetsim unless packet-level detail is required.

name: flexPTP
summary: PTP (IEEE 1588, also 802.1AS) for Cortex-M4/M7 microcontrollers: master and slave ordinary clock, E2E and P2P, L2 and L4 transports, one- and two-step. MIT licence, with a journal paper.
why_it_matters: Puts PTP on the MCU next to a sensor, so each sensor node timestamps in a shared timebase.
hackathon_notes: Needs an MCU with an Ethernet MAC that supports PTP timestamps (STM32F7/H7 class). Good fit for a sensor-network TDOA demo if the boards are at hand.

name: Wi-PTP
summary: PTP over Wi-Fi: a patched ath9k driver (Linux 4.19) that timestamps in the Wi-Fi hardware path plus an adjusted linuxptp.
why_it_matters: Time sync between drones or ground nodes over Wi-Fi instead of cable.
hackathon_notes: Needs Atheros ath9k cards and a kernel rebuild on an old kernel. Cite the idea; do not plan on building it in 48 h.

name: linuxptp-daemon (OpenShift)
summary: Kubernetes DaemonSet that manages ptp4l, phc2sys, ts2phc and timemaster per node, parses their logs into clock-state events, and for u-blox GNSS grandmasters treats a UBX-NAV-STATUS spoofing flag as GNSS loss.
why_it_matters: Production code that already wires GNSS spoofing detection into PTP grandmaster state - a concrete reference for clock-state handling and holdover.
hackathon_notes: Read pkg/parser and the ts2phc monitoring code for log parsing and state machines; reuse the regexes to parse your own ptp4l logs. Running it needs OpenShift and E810-class NICs.

name: time-transfer-tools
summary: MATLAB classes to read CGGTTS (V1, V2E) and RINEX 2/3 observation files, match observations between two stations and compute averaged differences - the GNSS common-view time transfer workflow.
why_it_matters: Lets a team compare two GNSS-timed sites the way timing labs do.
hackathon_notes: Needs MATLAB. Useful only if CGGTTS files are available (e.g. from a timing lab).

name: gr-allan
summary: GNU Radio sink block that wraps allantools to plot Allan deviation in real time from a stream.
why_it_matters: Live ADEV of an SDR-measured frequency or phase offset during a demo.
hackathon_notes: Tested by the author on GNU Radio 3.10.5; needs allantools installed. Build with cmake.

name: GNSSTimeServer
summary: ESP8266/ESP32 stratum-1 time server fed by a GNSS module and a TCXO-backed RTC, serving NTP and RDATE over WiFi or W5500 Ethernet, with a PTPv2 master edition, web dashboard and battery backup.
why_it_matters: Cheapest portable GNSS-fed time source for a field demo network.
hackathon_notes: Bill of materials and firmware in the repo; an ESP32 plus GNSS module with PPS. Accuracy is MCU-class, not NIC hardware timestamping.

name: MMCM_GPSDO
summary: All-digital GPSDO in VHDL for a Basys3 FPGA board: steers the clock with MMCM phase shifts from a GPS 1PPS, showing frequency error on LEDs. Author describes the loop as simple and constants as empirical.
why_it_matters: Minimal FPGA disciplining loop to read or extend with holdover logic.
hackathon_notes: Needs a Basys3 (Artix-7) and a GPS with PPS. No licence file per GitHub metadata - read, do not copy.

name: linuxptp
summary: The standard Linux implementation of IEEE 1588 PTP: ptp4l (boundary/ordinary/transparent clock), phc2sys (sync system clock to a NIC hardware clock), ts2phc (discipline a PHC from 1PPS + NMEA), pmc for management queries, and timemaster. richardcochran/linuxptp on GitHub carries the same tree.
why_it_matters: If a hackathon build needs sub-microsecond time across several computers (sensor nodes, TDOA receivers, a radar array), this is the off-the-shelf way to get it on Linux with hardware timestamping.
hackathon_notes: apt install linuxptp. Needs NICs with hardware timestamping (check `ethtool -T`); Raspberry Pi CM4/CM5 and Intel i210/i225 work. Use ts2phc with a GNSS 1PPS to build a grandmaster, ptp4l -S for software timestamping in a demo. Log `pmc` offsets to show holdover and attack behaviour.

name: chrony
summary: NTP client and server that also disciplines the system clock from reference clocks (1PPS, gpsd shared memory, PHC). Supports NTS, hardware timestamping on NTP packets, and source selection with outlier rejection. GitHub mirror: mlichvar/chrony.
why_it_matters: The default Linux time daemon on most distributions; combining a GNSS refclock with several NTS servers is the quickest way to get a clock that notices when one source lies.
hackathon_notes: Configure `refclock PPS /dev/pps0 lock NMEA` plus `refclock SHM 0` from gpsd, add `server ... nts` lines, then `chronyc sources -v` and `chronyc tracking` show offset, frequency and which sources are rejected. Good live demo of source selection when one GNSS source is walked off.

name: NTPsec
summary: A security-focused refactor of the reference NTP implementation with much of the legacy code removed, NTS support and the classic refclock drivers. GitHub mirror: ntpsec/ntpsec.
why_it_matters: Keeps the reference-implementation refclock drivers (useful for odd timing receivers) while dropping much of the attack surface of classic ntpd.
hackathon_notes: Use when a specific refclock driver is needed that chrony lacks; otherwise chrony is easier. ntpviz plots offsets and frequency from its logs.

name: NTP reference implementation (ntpd)
summary: The Network Time Foundation's reference implementation of NTPv4 (ntpd, ntpq, ntpdate and refclock drivers).
why_it_matters: The baseline that NTP attack papers were written against; useful to reproduce published time-shifting attacks in a lab.
hackathon_notes: Mostly a reference for behaviour comparisons; prefer chrony or ntpd-rs for new builds.

name: ntpd-rs
summary: A memory-safe NTP client and server in Rust with NTS support, from the Pendulum project (Trifecta Tech Foundation).
why_it_matters: NTS-authenticated time from a small Rust daemon: a reasonable second time source to cross-check GNSS time on an edge box.
hackathon_notes: Packages and a container exist; configure NTS sources and read offsets via ntp-ctl. Its source-selection behaviour is a useful comparison with chrony.

name: Statime
summary: A PTP (IEEE 1588-2019) implementation in Rust: a platform-agnostic library with a Linux daemon and an STM32 example for embedded targets.
why_it_matters: A second PTP stack to compare against linuxptp, and a route to PTP on embedded targets.
hackathon_notes: Try the Linux daemon against a linuxptp grandmaster; library use needs more effort.

name: NTS pool
summary: Server side for a pool of NTS time servers: a key-exchange front end that hands clients to member servers while keeping authentication end to end.
why_it_matters: Authenticated public time at pool scale is a prerequisite for using network time as an anti-spoofing cross-check.
hackathon_notes: Background reading for the authenticated-time story; not needed to build a demo.

name: Meta Time libraries
summary: Meta's Go libraries and tools for NTP and PTP: protocol implementations, PTP hardware clock and timestamping helpers, a PTP server (ptp4u), the simple-PTP client sptp, ptpcheck/ntpcheck diagnostics, a Calnex API client, leap-second utilities and the oscillatord monitoring protocol. Formerly facebook/time.
why_it_matters: Production code from a large-scale PTP deployment, including tools to inspect PTP clients and to monitor time cards.
hackathon_notes: Go build; `ptpcheck` and `ntpcheck` are the quickest wins for diagnosing a lab setup.

name: OCP Time Card
summary: Open Compute Project Time Appliance Project hardware: a PCIe card with a GNSS receiver and an atomic or OCXO holdover oscillator that turns a server into a PTP grandmaster, plus specs and drivers.
why_it_matters: An open reference design for exactly the GNSS + holdover-oscillator architecture resilient timing guidance recommends.
hackathon_notes: Hardware, not a 48 h build; read the architecture and holdover sections for design ideas.

name: Open Time Server spec
summary: OCP specification for an open time server: COTS server, a NIC with hardware timestamps and PPS in/out, and the Time Card as the GNSS/oscillator source.
why_it_matters: A concise architecture document for a GNSS-backed time server with holdover; useful as a slide template for a resilient-timing pitch.
hackathon_notes: Read-only spec. Use the block diagram and responsibilities split when designing your own time node.

name: oscillatord
summary: Daemon that disciplines the oscillator on the Orolia (Safran) Atomic Reference Time Card from a PPS reference and exposes monitoring.
why_it_matters: Real disciplining code for a miniature atomic clock on a time card, to compare with toy GPSDO loops.
hackathon_notes: Needs the hardware; read the disciplining code for the loop design.

name: Roughtime (Cloudflare)
summary: Go implementation of Roughtime, a protocol that returns signed coarse timestamps so a client can prove a server lied and can combine several servers.
why_it_matters: Gives a cryptographically checkable, coarse sanity bound on time, useful to catch large GNSS or NTP time shifts at boot.
hackathon_notes: Query several public Roughtime servers at startup; reject GNSS time if it is outside their bound. Accuracy is seconds-level by design, not a fine timing source.

name: cfnts
summary: Cloudflare's Rust implementation of Network Time Security (NTS) key exchange and NTP server/client. Archived.
why_it_matters: Readable NTS reference code; for running NTS use chrony, ntpd-rs or NTPsec.
hackathon_notes: Archived; read only.

name: allantools
summary: Python library for time and frequency stability statistics: Allan, modified Allan, overlapping, Hadamard and time deviation, plus confidence intervals and power-law noise generators.
why_it_matters: The tool to turn a logged clock offset series into an ADEV/TDEV plot and to read holdover performance off it.
hackathon_notes: pip install allantools; feed phase data from chronyc tracking logs, ptp4l offsets or a TICC. Plot ADEV per oscillator and compare with datasheet curves.

name: TAPR TICC
summary: Firmware and design files for TAPR's Arduino-based sub-nanosecond time interval counter, used to compare 1PPS outputs.
why_it_matters: Cheap way to measure a GPSDO or GNSS receiver PPS against a reference and get the phase data ADEV tools need.
hackathon_notes: Needs the board; output is a text stream of timestamps that pipes into allantools.

name: STM32 GPSDO
summary: Experimental GPS-disciplined oscillator: STM32 Black Pill, u-blox NEO-M8, a DAC and a used 10 MHz OCXO, with Arduino-framework firmware counting the OCXO against the 1PPS.
why_it_matters: Low-cost build that shows the full GPSDO loop on hobby parts; a starting point for adding holdover and spoof-detection logic.
hackathon_notes: Parts are cheap and available; the loop is frequency-counting with long averaging, so expect hours to settle. felixd/STM32-GPSDO is a fork.

name: Lars DIY GPSDO (original files)
summary: Archive of Lars Walenius' Arduino GPSDO from the EEVblog forum: a PI loop with a simple 1 ns resolution time-interval phase detector between the GPS 1PPS and the divided OCXO.
why_it_matters: The design many hobby GPSDOs copy; its loop and time-interval counter trick are a compact reference.
hackathon_notes: Reference files only; derivatives such as paulvee/Lars-GPSDO-V4.2 and W3AXL/Simple-GPSDO are maintained builds.

name: gpsdo-fw (BH3SAP alternative firmware)
summary: Replacement firmware for a widely sold BH3SAP GPSDO module, with menus for PPB trend, PWM value storage and PPS resync.
why_it_matters: Turns a cheap off-the-shelf GPSDO into something whose discipline and holdover behaviour you can read and modify.
hackathon_notes: Buy the module, flash over SWD. fredzo/gpsdo-fw is an active fork.

name: PicoGPSDO
summary: RP2040-based GPS-disciplined OCXO: firmware steers the OCXO via PWM from u-blox UBX timing messages (coarse from clock bias, fine from TIM-TP quantization error) and a Flask dashboard plots telemetry.
why_it_matters: A modern open GPSDO that uses the receiver's quantization-error correction, the step most hobby designs skip.
hackathon_notes: Needs Pico SDK and the board; the web dashboard is a good pattern for a demo.

name: Arduino SI5351 GPSDO
summary: Minimal GPSDO: Arduino Nano steers an SI5351 synthesizer from the GPS 1PPS, with measurement time scaled to the observed stability and an optional phase detector.
why_it_matters: Shows that a usable disciplined reference needs only a PPS and a few dollars of parts, and why the crystal's temperature sensitivity dominates.
hackathon_notes: Fast to build; replace the SI5351 crystal with a TCXO as the README advises.

name: GPSDO PTP Master
summary: A GPS-disciplined PTP grandmaster on a TI MSP432E4 MCU: u-blox receiver, software-disciplined crystal, PPS output, and NTP, PTP and SNMP servers on PoE with battery backup.
why_it_matters: A single-board GNSS time server for a sensor network, the kind of node a distributed-sensing build needs.
hackathon_notes: Hardware specific; read for architecture of a small grandmaster.

name: lbgpsdo
summary: Command-line utilities to read and write the configuration of Leo Bodnar GPSDO devices over USB HID.
why_it_matters: Leo Bodnar units are a common lab GPS reference; scripting them helps a team set up repeatable reference outputs.
hackathon_notes: Only useful if you own the hardware.

name: SatPulse
summary: Software for using a GNSS receiver on a computer for precise time: stratum-1 NTP with chrony, ntpd-rs or NTPsec, a PTP grandmaster on Raspberry Pi CM4/CM5 or Intel NICs via linuxptp, RTK base/rover, and a web GUI to configure and monitor receivers.
why_it_matters: The shortest path from a GNSS timing receiver to a working NTP/PTP time server with monitoring, on cheap hardware.
hackathon_notes: Install on a Pi CM4/CM5 with a u-blox timing receiver; follow satpulse.net. The GUI makes receiver state visible during a jamming or spoofing demo.

name: Time Pi
summary: Configuration for a Raspberry Pi stratum-1 PTP and NTP time server built from a GNSS module with PPS.
why_it_matters: A documented recipe a team can reproduce in hours for a local GNSS time reference.
hackathon_notes: Ansible-driven; budget an afternoon including GNSS antenna placement.

name: pps-tools
summary: User-space tools and headers for the Linux PPS API (ppstest, ppsctl, ppswatch).
why_it_matters: First thing to run when wiring a GNSS 1PPS into a Linux box: confirms pulses arrive and shows their jitter.
hackathon_notes: apt install pps-tools; `ppstest /dev/pps0`.

name: PTPd
summary: Older open-source PTPv2 daemon; the repository has been inactive since 2022.
why_it_matters: Sometimes the only option on platforms without linuxptp hardware support; also appears in older PTP security papers.
hackathon_notes: Prefer linuxptp or statime.

name: PTPsec
summary: Research implementation, based on linuxptp 3.1.1, that detects and mitigates PTP time-delay attacks by checking path asymmetry around cyclic redundant paths; includes a DPDK man-in-the-middle delay attacker for testing.
why_it_matters: Shows how to defend the network time path, the part a GNSS-vs-PTP cross-check silently trusts.
hackathon_notes: Needs two NICs with hardware timestamping per node and DPDK for the attacker; plan a day of setup. The detection idea can be reproduced in software on logged offsets.

name: NMEAdesync
summary: Proof-of-concept that feeds crafted NMEA sentences to a GPS-referenced NTP server to move its time; a red-team tool, inactive since 2017.
why_it_matters: A ready-made test input for a time-spoofing detector: it reproduces the 'trusted serial GNSS time' weakness without RF.
hackathon_notes: Only for a closed lab against your own time server; no RF needed. Use it to show the detector alarm, not to attack anything.

name: clknetsim
summary: Clock and network simulator from the chrony author: runs real NTP/PTP daemons against simulated clocks and network delays to test synchronization behaviour. Mirror of gitlab.com/chrony/clknetsim.
why_it_matters: Lets a team test a time daemon's reaction to delay changes, steps or a lying server without hardware.
hackathon_notes: Linux only (LD_PRELOAD); the chrony test suite shows usage patterns.

name: chrony_exporter
summary: Prometheus exporter for chrony tracking, sources and server statistics.
why_it_matters: Puts clock offset, frequency and source health on a dashboard: the monitoring half of a timing-resilience demo.
hackathon_notes: Run next to chronyd, scrape with Prometheus, chart in Grafana; enable the sources collector to see each reference.

name: White Rabbit cores (wr-cores)
summary: CERN Open Hardware Repository HDL cores for White Rabbit nodes and switches, including the White Rabbit PTP Core that gives sub-nanosecond synchronization over fibre Ethernet.
why_it_matters: White Rabbit is the open route to sub-ns time across a distributed array (radio telescopes, accelerators) and an alternative to GNSS time inside a facility.
hackathon_notes: FPGA work; buy WR nodes/switches if you need it in a build.

name: PPSi
summary: Portable PTP stack ('PTP Ported to Silicon') used in White Rabbit nodes and switches; one source tree builds for bare metal and Linux.
why_it_matters: A PTP stack that runs on soft-core CPUs, with the White Rabbit extension.
hackathon_notes: Read for embedded PTP design.

name: White Rabbit switch software
summary: Embedded Linux software for the White Rabbit switch, including the PTP daemon integration and management.
why_it_matters: Completes the White Rabbit picture for teams evaluating it as a distribution network.
hackathon_notes: Hardware specific.

name: gr_DCF77_Receiver
summary: GNU Radio receiver and live decoder for the DCF77 77.5 kHz time signal, covering both the OOK and phase-modulated channels, with a simulated transmitter and channel for testing without hardware.
why_it_matters: Time from a terrestrial LF signal of opportunity, independent of GNSS; the simulator lets a team test without an LF front end.
hackathon_notes: Needs an SDR that reaches 77.5 kHz (e.g. Airspy HF+, or an upconverter). Docker CI image exists. Outside Europe swap to WWVB/MSF.

name: DCF77Decode
summary: C library that decodes the DCF77 time code bitstream (from a cheap AM receiver module) covering most of the public standard.
why_it_matters: A tiny GNSS-independent coarse time source for a microcontroller.
hackathon_notes: Pair with a DCF77 receiver module; accuracy is limited by the AM envelope.

name: SDRangel
summary: General SDR receive/transmit application with many demodulator plugins; its Radio Clock plugin decodes LF time broadcasts including MSF, DCF77, TDF, WWVB, JJY and RBU.
why_it_matters: One GUI that decodes several LF time broadcasts and many other signals, useful for a signals-of-opportunity timing demo.
hackathon_notes: Install packages or the Docker image; add the Radio Clock channel.

name: TDOA evaluation with RTL-SDRs
summary: MATLAB scripts that localize a transmitter by TDOA from three RTL-SDR receivers, synchronizing them on a known reference transmitter instead of GNSS time.
why_it_matters: Shows that distributed RF sensing needs nanosecond-level relative timing and one way to get it without GNSS disciplining.
hackathon_notes: Three Pis with RTL-SDRs plus the modified librtlsdr; MATLAB or port to Octave/NumPy.

name: librtlsdr-2freq
summary: Modified librtlsdr that switches between two frequencies during one recording without losing samples, so a reference transmitter and the target land in the same stream.
why_it_matters: The trick that makes reference-transmitter synchronization of cheap TDOA receivers work.
hackathon_notes: Build on the Pi receivers; see the companion evaluation scripts.

name: kiwiclient
summary: Python clients for KiwiSDR receivers, including recorders that save IQ with GNSS timestamps from the receiver.
why_it_matters: GNSS-timestamped IQ from a public network of receivers is the input for HF TDOA; it also shows what breaks when the receivers' GNSS time is denied.
hackathon_notes: Pure Python; record from public KiwiSDRs. Timestamps are only as good as each receiver's GNSS.

name: cuckoo_time_translator
summary: ROS algorithms that translate a sensor's own hardware timestamps into host system time from one-way timing, estimating skew and offset.
why_it_matters: Multi-sensor fusion (camera, IMU, LiDAR) breaks quietly when timestamps are off; this is the lightweight fix when PTP is not available on the sensor.
hackathon_notes: ROS1 catkin package; inactive since 2022, port the algorithm if on ROS 2.

name: KROT (Где мы, Бариста?) - terrain correlation from radar altimeter
summary: Team 'Где мы, Бариста?' solution to the 2026 'Полёт вслепую' (Blind flight) hackathon case: 'КРОТ' (Корреляционный Рельефный Определитель Траектории) turns a radar-altimeter NMEA-0183 log flown at a constant 1500 m MSL into a terrain profile, correlates it against a Copernicus GLO-30 GeoTIFF, and outputs map position, WGS-84 coordinates, ground speed, azimuth and match-quality metrics. React/Three.js operator panel plus separate C++ and Rust compute cores. README in Russian also records what the organisers' technical expert clarified (no IMU/camera, final-day validation log, bonus for speed and noise robustness).
why_it_matters: The most complete public write-up of the TERCOM-style hackathon problem: input format, organiser constraints and a quality/confidence readout, which is exactly what a judge asks for.
hackathon_notes: Read the README section on expert clarifications first: it is the closest thing to a published spec of the case. The C++/Rust cores are the parts to lift; the web UI is a demo shell. Works offline against a GeoTIFF, no flight hardware needed.

name: Gagarin - TERCOM for UAVs without GNSS
summary: Python TERCOM pipeline from the June 2026 'Полёт вслепую' hackathon, continued into July: correlates radar-altimeter profiles with a DEM using a coarse-to-fine 360-degree search, a hybrid MAD+NCC metric, minima-ratio discrimination, pre-rejection gates and an error-state Kalman filter with dead-reckoning fallback. Adds pre-flight terrain-informativeness analysis along a route, flags false-correlation risk segments, and tabulates expected search time on companion computers (RPi, Jetson, Orange Pi). README (Russian) reports per-region errors honestly, including failures where the azimuth was wrong.
why_it_matters: Shows the failure modes of altimeter TERCOM in practice (wrong-azimuth peaks, flat terrain) and the engineering answers: quality grading, ambiguity detection and pre-flight route fingerprinting.
hackathon_notes: Best starting point if the brief is altimeter + DEM: the NCC/MAD search, quality gates and pre-flight terrain analyzer are separable. Performance table gives realistic onboard budgets. Self-reported errors are 50 m to 1.5 km depending on region, so treat as a baseline, not a result to quote.

name: Полёт вслепую - GCS with terrain-referenced navigation
summary: Another team's take on the 2026 'Полёт вслепую' case, built as a ground control station for a UAV swarm: a Go telemetry ingestion gateway feeds RabbitMQ, a Python worker runs a particle-filter terrain-referenced navigation core on a DEM (rasterio) with Qdrant used for relocalisation, and MAVSDK-Python bridges to MAVLink vehicles. Full Docker Compose stack with PostgreSQL, Redis, Prometheus/Grafana/Loki.
why_it_matters: An architecture reference for putting a TRN estimator behind a real telemetry pipeline and operator panel rather than in a notebook.
hackathon_notes: docker compose up brings the whole stack; heavy for a 24-48h build. Useful mainly for the particle-filter TRN module and the MAVSDK bridge pattern. Docs in docs/ (domain.md covers TRN).

name: HackatonCODEreal - altimeter/DEM autonomous flight (SKB 'FIZ-TECH')
summary: Hackathon code from team SKB 'ФИЗ-ТЕХ' for the June 2026 blind-flight case: takes NMEA, sample rate, barometric altitude and a height map, and estimates track by profile correlation. Post-processing is the stable mode (multithreaded, vectorised); a sliding-window real-time mode adds Kalman filtering. Outputs include true vs estimated tracks over the map, profile comparisons and speed/azimuth correlation heatmaps; a Webots simulation was used to generate test data.
why_it_matters: A compact Python baseline with heatmaps over speed and azimuth, handy for visualising why altimeter matching is ambiguous.
hackathon_notes: Run gui.py. README says post-processing is more stable than real time and that a 10 m altimeter error was tested. Demo videos are on Yandex Disk links.

name: Terrain-Relative Navigation (particle filter on DEM)
summary: Personal Python prototype of terrain-relative navigation: matches a height profile along the route against a DEM and estimates position with a particle filter from an imprecise start. Simulates altimeter noise, bias and outliers, and was exercised on synthetic maps and Copernicus GLO-30 tiles for three Bulgarian areas from flat to mountainous. README in Russian.
why_it_matters: Clean, self-contained particle-filter TRN with a noise model, a good teaching companion to the hackathon correlation solutions.
hackathon_notes: Laptop-only; load a GeoTIFF or generate a synthetic DEM. Swap its measurement model for real radar-altimeter logs to compare against NCC-based TERCOM.

name: Radio Altimeter A-053 simulator (MCU part)
summary: C firmware for a microcontroller-based simulator of the A-053 aircraft radio altimeter; part 1 of 2, with PC software as the second part. README is a one-line Russian description.
why_it_matters: Niche, but relevant to TERCOM work: hardware-in-the-loop testing needs something that emits realistic altimeter output.
hackathon_notes: Little documentation; read the source to see the output interface before planning HIL use. Last push 2022.

name: aerial-nav - GPS-denied navigation via Siamese network
summary: Matches onboard camera frames to a pre-built satellite map of the route: a ResNet-18 Siamese network with SAFA spatial aggregation ranks map tiles indexed at 13 altitude levels (0-1200 m), then SuperPoint/LightGlue with RANSAC homography refines position and heading. README in Russian.
why_it_matters: A full coarse-retrieval plus fine-registration VPS pipeline, the same structure fielded visual positioning products describe.
hackathon_notes: Good template for a two-stage VPS demo: retrieval narrows the search, LightGlue gives the fix. Check what weights and data are shipped before relying on it.

name: drone_navigation - ROS 2 + PX4 + RTAB-Map diploma
summary: Diploma project: autonomous quadcopter navigation in PX4 SITL + Gazebo with ROS 2, RTAB-Map visual SLAM for mapping and localisation, A* global planning, VFH plus a custom 3D manoeuvre for obstacle avoidance, and YOLO person detection. README in Russian.
why_it_matters: An integrated sim stack that wires SLAM, planning and avoidance to PX4, which is the glue most teams lose time on.
hackathon_notes: Needs a working ROS 2 + PX4 SITL + Gazebo setup (hours, not minutes). Reuse the node layout and the SLAM-to-planner wiring.

name: MVIO - monocular visual-inertial odometry in C++
summary: C++ monocular VIO: ORB features tracked with Lucas-Kanade flow, parallax-based keyframes, essential-matrix initialisation then PnP, IMU preintegration, least-squares scale and gravity estimation, and a 15-state error-state Kalman filter. Built on OpenCV 4.6 and Eigen 3.4. Companion to a Russian Habr article.
why_it_matters: A small, readable VIO you can actually step through, unlike the large research systems.
hackathon_notes: CMake build; configs in configs/. Calibrate your own camera (camera.yaml) as the article insists. No accuracy numbers are published.

name: Visual-Odometry-VIO- (VO + IMU EKF)
summary: Minimal Python project: essential-matrix visual odometry fused with IMU in an EKF to estimate position without GPS. README is two lines in Russian.
why_it_matters: Smallest possible VO+IMU EKF skeleton, useful as a starting file rather than a system.
hackathon_notes: Read the code directly; there is no documentation of inputs or datasets.

name: ViNet_AirSim_drone - learned VIO in AirSim
summary: PyTorch CNN+RNN network that predicts relative pose between frames from a monocular camera and 6-axis IMU, trained on data collected in Microsoft AirSim with ground-truth poses and a composite loss to limit drift. README in Russian.
why_it_matters: A learned-VIO baseline with a simulator data loop, relevant if the team wants to compare deep and geometric odometry.
hackathon_notes: Needs AirSim to regenerate data; notebooks otherwise. Expect sim-to-real gaps.

name: GNSS-AK_model - GNSS + astro-corrector model
summary: Diploma C++ code modelling a moving user, GNSS operation and an astro-corrector (star-tracker style celestial correction), with integrator and linear-algebra helpers. No README; description in Russian.
why_it_matters: Rare open code pairing GNSS with celestial correction, the classic long-range fallback when GNSS is degraded.
hackathon_notes: Undocumented; useful only as a reference for structuring a GNSS + celestial simulation.

name: V-NAV (CopterHack 2022) - visual navigation for Clover
summary: Archived fork of the Clover framework holding team V-NAV's CopterHack 2022 entry (article in docs/ru/v-nav.md on branch v-nav_article): a multi-camera plus IMU optical navigation module using graph-based SLAM with CNN-extracted features, aimed at indoor and GNSS-denied industrial-site flights, with a companion Pixhawk FMUv6U + CM4 + Coral board concept.
why_it_matters: Shows how a Russian student team scoped GNSS-free navigation on the Clover/PX4 stack; a design reference more than working code.
hackathon_notes: Read the article on the v-nav_article branch; the fork itself is mostly upstream Clover.

name: TPU_2 (CopterHack 2023) - flight through forest
summary: Fork of Clover with Tomsk Polytechnic team TPU_2's CopterHack 2023 entry (docs/ru/tpu_2.md on branch tpu_2): an algorithm for autonomous flight through dense forest using empirical search plus classic planners such as Dijkstra and RRT.
why_it_matters: Under-canopy flight is a GNSS-degraded case; the article frames planning in clutter on an educational stack.
hackathon_notes: Article-level material; check the branch for code before planning around it.

name: CRTClover - Clover Rescue Team backend
summary: Drone-side backend of the Clover Rescue project (CopterHack 2022, third place), which the team describes as returning the Clover to the user or takeoff point with one click when radio contact is lost.
why_it_matters: Lost-link return-home is the same behaviour EW-resilience work needs; this is a small worked example on Clover.
hackathon_notes: Pair with DevMBS/CRTClient. Old (2022) and tied to the Clover image.

name: Приемники ГНСС - GNSS receiver design handbook (MPEI)
summary: Source of a Russian-language textbook for the MPEI course on satellite navigation user equipment by I. Korogodin (NavSysLab): signals, acquisition, tracking loops, positioning and practical receiver design.
why_it_matters: One of the few open, maintained Russian-language GNSS receiver textbooks; useful to understand why jamming and spoofing break tracking loops.
hackathon_notes: Reading material, not code. Pair with gnss-sdr for hands-on work.

name: gnssrecbasics2020 - GNSS receiver course labs (MPEI)
summary: Assignments and lab reports for the first semester of the MPEI navigation receivers course (2020): signal model, statistical correlator equivalent, positioning accuracy and further labs. Russian.
why_it_matters: Structured exercises for building intuition about correlators and positioning accuracy.
hackathon_notes: Good pre-hackathon homework for whoever owns the GNSS side.

name: glnephexercise - GLONASS satellite position exercise
summary: MPEI student project template for computing GLONASS satellite positions from broadcast ephemerides. Russian.
why_it_matters: GLONASS ephemerides use a different (numerical integration) model than GPS; this is a compact way to learn it.
hackathon_notes: Pair with the GPS twin exercise (Korogodin/gpsephexercise).
