EXIF GPS is a consumer-grade fix, not survey truth

title: NASA SkyView virtual observatory
summary: A NASA service that cuts FITS images with a reference WCS from many all-sky surveys at any position, scale and projection. The celestial star-tracker sample pulls cutouts of the Mellinger optical all-sky mosaic to score plate-solving accuracy against a known attitude.
key_takeaways: Free reference star fields with known pointing for testing lost-in-space star trackers
Under load it can answer with an HTML 'Too Many Processes' page instead of FITS; retry and validate
Survey mosaics are not camera frames: no lens distortion, noise or stray light of a real sensor

title: JPL DE421 planetary ephemeris (NAIF SPK kernel)
authors: NASA JPL Solar System Dynamics / NAIF
summary: The DE421 planetary and lunar ephemeris as a NAIF SPK binary kernel (de421.bsp, about 16 MB), an older but compact JPL Development Ephemeris commonly loaded with Skyfield. Celestial navigation code needs it to place the Sun, Moon and planets and to compute observer geometry.
key_takeaways: Small, offline ephemeris adequate for celestial fixes; newer DE files exist under the same NAIF tree
Load with Skyfield; no account needed
Kept under a_old_versions on the NAIF server

title: Natural Earth vector data
summary: Public-domain world vector layers (land, coastline, countries) at 1:10m, 1:50m and 1:110m scales. Samples use the 10 m land polygon as an 'is this position on land' mask for AIS plausibility checks and the 50 m country borders as a basemap for interference maps.
key_takeaways: Public domain, small downloads, no login
At 1:10m, canals, fjord heads and harbours are drawn as land: most 'on land' AIS alerts in the sample were coastline resolution
Use a large-scale water mask for harbour-level checks

title: OpenStreetMap data via the Overpass API
summary: A read-only query API over the OpenStreetMap database that returns features (coastlines, bridges, wind turbines, buoys) inside a bounding box. The USV GNSS-denied sample builds its radar chart and landmark set from Overpass queries; OSM data is under ODbL with attribution.
key_takeaways: Quick way to build a real chart or landmark map for any region
Public endpoints rate-limit; keep fallbacks and cache results
If the simulated sensor sees the same OSM map the matcher uses, error numbers are optimistic

title: GPS Spoofing WorkGroup 2024 - Final Report
summary: Crowd-sourced industry report from a six-week OPSGROUP workgroup of pilots, controllers, regulators and manufacturers on GPS spoofing hitting civil flights, mainly near Middle East and Black Sea / Baltic conflict areas. Comes with crew guidance and a technical guide.
key_takeaways: Spoofing degrades terrain-warning (EGPWS) functions, which may stay wrong after GPS returns
No quick fix: mitigation is crew awareness, procedures and keeping ground navaids
Strong evidence that integrity monitoring and 'is my position plausible?' checks matter more than raw accuracy
Spoofing can leave systems like terrain warning degraded after GPS returns
Receivers may retain corrupted data after an event
Argues for retaining ground-based navaids

title: EASA SIB 2022-02R3: Global Navigation Satellite System Outage and Alterations Leading to Communication / Navigation / Surveillance Degradation
summary: EASA's safety information bulletin on GNSS jamming and spoofing affecting aircraft, revised repeatedly since 2022 as interference spread around conflict zones. Lists symptoms and recommendations for authorities, ANSPs, operators and manufacturers; later revisions (R4) followed.
key_takeaways: Spoofing is harder for crews to detect than jamming and so the bigger safety risk
Recommends cross-checking with non-GNSS navaids and reporting events
Affected flight information regions are tracked on EASA's GNSS page

title: EASA - Global Navigation Satellite System outages and alterations
summary: EASA's landing page for GNSS interference: current SIB revision, affected regions and related guidance and workshops.
key_takeaways: Single place to check the current bulletin revision
Links civil-aviation guidance to the interference geography

title: EASA and IATA comprehensive plan to mitigate the risks of GNSS interference
summary: Joint plan from a May 2025 EASA/IATA workshop setting out actions on reporting and monitoring, prevention and mitigation, airspace/infrastructure (backup navaids) and civil-military coordination against GNSS interference.
key_takeaways: Four pillars: reporting, prevention, infrastructure, coordination
Retaining conventional navaids is explicitly part of resilience
Calls for better civil-military sharing of interference data
Standard radio calls and NOTAM Q-codes for interference
Tighter controls on jammer sales
Keep a minimum network of conventional navaids as backup

title: FAA SAFO 24002: Recognizing and Mitigating GPS/GNSS Disruptions
summary: FAA Safety Alert for Operators describing jamming vs spoofing effects on aircraft systems, typical locations near conflict and counter-UAS areas, and recommended crew and operator actions.
key_takeaways: Hybrid GPS/inertial solutions can also be corrupted by spoofing
Revert to conventional procedures and report to ATC
Disruptions cluster around conflict zones and C-UAS protection areas

title: SKYbrary - GNSS Jamming and Spoofing
summary: Aviation safety wiki article explaining jamming vs spoofing, their effects on aircraft systems and the regulatory material around them, with links to bulletins and incident reports.
key_takeaways: Good primer on how interference propagates through avionics
Collects links to EASA, FAA and ICAO material
Plain-language intro to the aviation impact
Links to EASA/FAA/ICAO references

title: Above Us Only Stars: Exposing GPS Spoofing in Russia and Syria
summary: Open-source investigation using AIS ship tracks, public records and ISS-based measurements to map thousands of GNSS spoofing events around Russia, Crimea and Syria, many linked to protection of VIPs and bases.
key_takeaways: Shows how public data (AIS) reveals spoofing via impossible tracks
Spoofing used for airspace denial around military facilities
A model for OSINT-style interference detection projects
AIS position anomalies reveal spoofing at scale
Methodology is reproducible with public data

title: GPSJam - daily GPS interference map
summary: Daily world map of likely GPS interference derived from ADS-B navigation-integrity reports (NIC/NACp) aggregated into hexagons from community flight-tracking data. The FAQ documents the method and its blind spots.
key_takeaways: Interference is inferred from aircraft self-reported integrity, not measured RF
Empty cells mean no data, not no jamming
Easy to reproduce with your own ADS-B receiver
Derived from ADS-B NIC/NACp degradation
Hex-binned daily snapshots
Shows persistent interference zones (Baltic, Middle East, Black Sea)
Method is indirect: inferred from aircraft-reported accuracy

title: Bellingcat OSINT Toolkit - GPSJam
summary: Bellingcat's toolkit entry on using GPSJam for open-source investigations, with notes on limitations and interpretation.
key_takeaways: Frames interference maps as OSINT evidence with caveats
Useful for teams building verification workflows

title: ADS-B Data Analysis for GNSS Interference Mapping
summary: Trade-press article on using ADS-B integrity data to detect and map GNSS interference regions.
key_takeaways: ADS-B is an existing, free sensor network for interference awareness
Method details help design your own detector

title: GNSS interference report: Russia 2024/2025 - Part 1: Kaliningrad and the Baltic Sea
summary: Spire analysis using satellite-received ADS-B integrity metrics and RF data to characterize persistent interference around Kaliningrad and over the Baltic.
key_takeaways: Satellite ADS-B extends interference monitoring over sea areas
Kaliningrad is a persistent Baltic interference zone

title: Researchers home in on origins of Russia's Baltic GPS jamming
summary: Reporting on Gdynia Maritime University research tracing Baltic jamming to Russian sites such as Baltiysk in Kaliningrad, DLR comment on how cheap and mobile jammers are, and an analyst's heatmap of likely jammer locations built from aircraft ADS-B integrity data.
key_takeaways: Emitter localization from distributed monitors plus ADS-B is feasible
Baltic interference has shifted to include spoofing
Emitter localization from distributed measurements
Shows the Baltic as a persistent interference zone

title: Spoofing now affecting commercial flights
summary: Post from Todd Humphreys' lab on spoofing incidents hitting commercial aircraft and what they show about receiver and avionics vulnerability.
key_takeaways: Academic view on why civil receivers accept spoofed signals
Points toward authentication and cross-checks as defenses

title: GPS Spoofing in the Civil Aviation Sector (RIN 2024)
summary: Royal Institute of Navigation event microsite gathering expert talks on spoofing affecting airlines and possible mitigations.
key_takeaways: UK navigation-community perspective
Covers detection, operations and policy angles

title: 2025 Was a Stress Test & Maritime AI™ Is the Only Way to Pass
summary: Windward's quarter-by-quarter review of 2025 maritime risk: sanctions, dark fleet growth, flag-registry fraud and GNSS interference. Reports GPS jamming affecting more than 24,000 vessels across Q1-Q3, with hotspots in the Arabian Gulf, Mediterranean and Baltic, and false port calls near Iranian terminals during the Iran conflict.
key_takeaways: GPS jamming affected more than 24,000 vessels in Q1-Q3 2025, over 13,000 in Q2 alone
AIS anomalies are the main public signal of GNSS manipulation at sea

title: Meatgrinder: Russian Tactics in the Second Year of Its Invasion of Ukraine
summary: RUSI special report on Russian battlefield adaptation, including the density of Russian electronic warfare and its heavy effect on Ukrainian UAVs, with a widely cited estimate of around 10,000 drone losses per month.
key_takeaways: Dense EW coverage along the front is weighted toward defeating UAVs
Loss figures came from interviews and are contested
Explains why EW-resilient navigation became a top Ukrainian requirement
Describes dense, layered Russian EW deployment
Drone attrition to EW drives demand for non-GNSS navigation

title: Space Threat Assessment 2025
summary: Annual CSIS Aerospace Security Project review of counterspace capabilities, with sections on GPS jamming and spoofing in Eastern Europe and the Middle East.
key_takeaways: Puts terrestrial GNSS jamming in the wider counterspace picture
Useful citation for problem framing in pitches
Country-by-country counterspace inventory
Tracks GNSS electronic attack incidents year over year

title: The Invisible War: Inside the electronic warfare arms race that could shape course of war in Ukraine
summary: Long-form reporting on the EW and counter-EW cycle in Ukraine, covering jamming of drones and navigation and the rapid iteration of countermeasures.
key_takeaways: GPS-guided Excalibur shells and JDAM bombs lost accuracy to Russian jamming within months to a year of delivery
Ukraine's Pokrova system jams and spoofs satellite navigation; officials claim it cut the accuracy of spoofed missiles by 40%

title: Ukrainian military's anti-drone GPS spoofing spills into civilians' phones
summary: Report on Ukraine's nationwide defensive spoofing against incoming drones and missiles, and its side effects on civilian devices' location and time.
key_takeaways: Defensive spoofing has collateral effects on civil PNT and timing
Any consumer-grade nav stack must tolerate wrong GNSS

title: NATO DIANA unveils 10 new challenges to accelerate dual-use technology breakthroughs
summary: Announcement of DIANA's 2026 challenge programme topics, including operating in contested electromagnetic environments, with problem statements that describe what NATO wants solved.
key_takeaways: Problem statements stress dual-use and resilience in contested spectrum
Good template for writing a hackathon pitch in NATO language

title: NATO DIANA's breakthrough solutions for secure communication and navigation
summary: DIANA feature on cohort companies working on resilient navigation and secure communications, illustrating which approaches made it through selection.
key_takeaways: Shows the spread of selected approaches: magnetic, quantum, LEO PNT, vision
Selection favors deployable, testable dual-use products

title: Ukraine's Brave1, NATO Launch €10M Competition for Counter-Drone Technology
summary: Coverage of a Brave1-NATO competition funding counter-drone technology and navigation that works under electronic warfare.
key_takeaways: Brave1 frames navigation under EW as a top battlefield need
Competitions emphasize rapid field testing

title: В Україні провели хакатон зі створення антидронових рішень (Anti-drone hackathon held in Ukraine)
summary: Ukrainian-language report on a defense hackathon focused on counter-drone solutions.
key_takeaways: Ukrainian hackathons are short, problem-driven and tied to frontline users
Detection and EW-resilience recur as tracks

title: DIU launches new emerging tech portfolio, solicits industry for quantum sensing capabilities
summary: Coverage of DIU's Transition of Quantum Sensing call seeking quantum inertial sensors and magnetometers to extend navigation holdover when GPS is unavailable.
key_takeaways: DIU's stated value: reduced drift means longer holdover without GPS
Lines of effort: inertial, magnetometers, technology insertion
Magnetic anomaly navigation is a funded transition path

title: DARPA eyeing new quantum sensing program
summary: Report on DARPA's RoQS program to make quantum sensors robust to platform interference so they can support navigation without GPS on real vehicles.
key_takeaways: Platform noise, not lab sensitivity, is the barrier DARPA targets
Context for why classical magnetic compensation still matters

title: DARPA Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (PNT) Technology and their Impacts on GPS users
summary: DARPA slide deck summarizing its PNT portfolio, including All Source Positioning and Navigation (ASPN), a plug-and-play architecture for fusing non-traditional sensors when GPS is denied.
key_takeaways: ASPN pushes sensor-agnostic, plug-and-play fusion
Shows the long-running DoD interest in all-source navigation

title: EDF-2024-LS-RA-CHALLENGE-SENS-RADNP: Multi-sensor integration for robust autonomous drone navigation
summary: European Defence Fund technological-challenge topic on multi-sensor integration for autonomous drone navigation in GNSS-denied or contested environments, run as an organized competition with evaluation campaigns. Listing via an aggregator; confirm details on the EU Funding and Tenders portal.
key_takeaways: EU frames GNSS-denied drone navigation as a benchmarked challenge
Multi-sensor fusion, not a single sensor, is the ask

title: EDF 2021 NAVGUARD project factsheet
summary: Factsheet for an EDF-funded project developing ground and space-based detection of illegitimate activity in GNSS bands.
key_takeaways: Interference detection and monitoring is a funded European priority
Pairs well with ADS-B/SDR monitoring hackathon ideas

title: Advanced Radio Frequency Sensing, Integrated Effects and PNT
summary: UK DASA themed competition (for the Bright Corvus project) seeking RF sensing and resilient PNT innovations.
key_takeaways: UK MOD treats RF sensing and PNT as one problem space
Example of UK-style challenge framing

title: Positioning, Navigation and Timing Growth: government response
authors: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
summary: UK government response on growing the resilient PNT sector, following its national PNT framework work.
key_takeaways: UK policy treats resilient PNT as both security and export opportunity
Useful framing for dual-use pitches

title: Resilient PNT Conformance Framework
summary: Defines four cumulative resilience levels for PNT user equipment based on prevent, respond and recover behaviours, so buyers and vendors can describe how a receiver behaves under jamming or spoofing.
key_takeaways: Gives vocabulary to grade your solution: prevent, respond, recover
Solution-agnostic, so it fits any sensor mix
Later versions and an IEEE standards effort followed
Levels escalate from basic recovery to full prevention and response
Scope is PNT-producing equipment, not downstream consumers
A later v2.0 was reported in 2022 with evaluation guidance

title: NISTIR 8323: Foundational PNT Profile - Applying the Cybersecurity Framework for the Responsible Use of PNT Services
summary: Maps the NIST Cybersecurity Framework onto systems that consume PNT, giving identify/protect/detect/respond/recover practices for GNSS dependence.
key_takeaways: Treats GNSS as an untrusted external input
Detection and recovery practices map directly to hackathon features

title: HACKtheMACHINE Unmanned (ONR / NavalX)
summary: US Navy prize challenge on unmanned and autonomous systems with tracks on securing a simulated autopilot, separating benign from malicious data, and model-based mission requirements.
key_takeaways: Navy judges reward working prototypes on realistic simulated systems
Cyber-resilience of autopilots is treated as part of autonomy

title: Space Security Challenge 2022: Hack-A-Sat 3
summary: AFRL/Space Force capture-the-flag on satellite and ground-segment security; challenge code from several editions has been released publicly.
key_takeaways: Space-segment security is part of assured PNT
Released challenges are good training material

title: DARPA Subterranean (SubT) Challenge
summary: DARPA's 2018-2021 challenge for autonomous robot teams mapping and searching tunnels, urban underground and caves with no GNSS and degraded comms; systems and virtual tracks.
key_takeaways: Scoring rewarded accurate localization of reported artifacts, not just coverage
Heterogeneous teams (legged + aerial) won
Communication-denied autonomy was decisive

title: DARPA Triage Challenge
summary: DARPA challenge for autonomous systems that find and assess casualties in mass-casualty scenes, combining drones and ground robots navigating degraded, GNSS-unreliable environments.
key_takeaways: Humanitarian defense use-case with navigation plus perception
Team directory helps find open contributions

title: A Multi-Robot Platform for Robotic Triage Combining Onboard Sensing and Foundation Models
summary: Technical report from a DARPA Triage Challenge team describing a multi-robot system and fine-tuned open vision-language models for injury identification.
key_takeaways: Shows how a challenge team integrates navigation, perception and VLMs
Open-model fine-tuning is viable under challenge time budgets

title: DAF-MIT AIA Open Flight Data for Magnetic Navigation Research
summary: Zenodo record of airborne magnetometer, INS and GNSS flight data with datasheets, collected for the MagNav challenge.
key_takeaways: Real flight lines with multiple magnetometers
Ground truth from GNSS for evaluating nav error

title: Team CERBERUS Wins the DARPA Subterranean Challenge: Technical Overview and Lessons Learned
authors: Team CERBERUS (NTNU, ETH Zurich, UNR, Oxford, et al.)
summary: Winning team's description of its legged-plus-aerial system: multi-modal perception, robust localization and mapping, exploration planning and artifact detection, with lessons from the final.
key_takeaways: Robust multi-sensor odometry and exploration were key
Field-hardening and operator workflow mattered as much as algorithms

title: CERBERUS: Autonomous Legged and Aerial Robotic Exploration in the Tunnel and Urban Circuits of the DARPA Subterranean Challenge
summary: Field Robotics paper covering CERBERUS' systems and results in the earlier SubT circuits, including perception, planning and artifact reporting.
key_takeaways: Documents the iteration path to the winning system

title: NeBula: Quest for Robotic Autonomy in Challenging Environments; TEAM CoSTAR at the DARPA Subterranean Challenge
summary: Describes the NeBula belief-space autonomy stack: multi-modal positioning, mapping, traversability, risk-aware mission planning and multi-robot reasoning; CoSTAR won the Urban circuit.
key_takeaways: Reasoning over uncertainty in localization improves mission decisions
Redundant odometry sources were essential underground

title: AlphaPilot: Autonomous Drone Racing
summary: UZH's second-place AlphaPilot system: learned gate detection, nonlinear filtering of visual-inertial state and time-optimal trajectory planning for GPS-free racing.
key_takeaways: Vision-inertial state estimation, not GNSS, drove the race
Splitting perception and planning made it robust

title: MAVLab wins the AlphaPilot AI challenge
summary: TU Delft MAVLab's account of winning the 2019 Lockheed Martin AlphaPilot / AIRR autonomous drone race.
key_takeaways: Lightweight onboard estimation can beat heavier stacks
Same lab later won A2RL 2025

title: Champion-level drone racing using deep reinforcement learning
summary: Swift, a quadrotor using only onboard camera and IMU with an RL-trained policy, beat human world-champion pilots in head-to-head races.
key_takeaways: Onboard VIO plus learned control reached human-champion level
Sim-to-real with residual models from real data

title: 2025 Abu Dhabi Autonomous Racing League
summary: Summary of the A2RL x DCL autonomous drone championship, won by TU Delft MAVLab ahead of TII Racing and KAIST, including races against human pilots.
key_takeaways: Standardized drone and camera-only sensing put the focus on estimation and control
University labs still beat well-funded teams

title: Satellite Pose Estimation Challenge: Dataset, Competition Design and Results
summary: ESA Kelvins / Stanford competition on monocular spacecraft pose estimation, analyzing 48 entries.
key_takeaways: Keypoint detection plus PnP beat direct pose regression
Shows how ESA designs and scores a navigation competition

title: ESA Kelvins Satellite Pose Estimation Competition 2021 (SPEED+)
summary: Follow-up Kelvins challenge focused on bridging the domain gap: train on synthetic images, test on hardware-in-the-loop lightbox and sunlamp images.
key_takeaways: Sim-to-real gap is the core difficulty judges scored
Kelvins pages document rules and metrics

title: Stone Soup documentation and tutorials
summary: Official docs for the Stone Soup tracking framework with step-by-step tutorials from a single-target Kalman filter through data association (PDA, JPDA), multi-hypothesis tracking, GM-PHD, track initiation/deletion, sensor management and performance metrics.
key_takeaways: Tutorial path from single-target Kalman to multi-target
Metrics module helps score your fusion objectively
Tutorials double as a self-paced multi-target tracking course
Metrics module (OSPA, SIAP) gives defensible evaluation numbers
Sensor and simulator components let you test without real radar

title: Drone Security and the Mysterious Case of DJI's DroneID
summary: Security analysis of DJI drones that reverse-engineers the DroneID broadcast and shows it is unencrypted, with an open receiver released.
key_takeaways: Passive decoding enables detection and localization of DJI drones
Security analysis of drone firmware and protocols
DroneID leaks drone and pilot position in the clear
Decoding needs SDR captures at high sample rates

title: FAA - Remote Identification of Drones
summary: FAA guidance on the Remote ID rule: what drones must broadcast, standard vs broadcast-module compliance and operator obligations.
key_takeaways: Remote ID gives a lawful, cooperative signal for drone awareness
Defines what fields you can expect to decode
Standard Remote ID broadcasts drone and control station location
Non-compliant drones need non-cooperative detection

title: The EAR and Open Source Software
summary: Practical guide to how US Export Administration Regulations treat published open-source code, including the separate notification step for encryption.
key_takeaways: Code published without restriction is generally outside the EAR
Encryption source has an extra BIS/NSA notification step
Private repos shared with foreign nationals can count as exports

title: 15 CFR 734.7 - Published (Export Administration Regulations)
authors: US Bureau of Industry and Security
summary: The regulation text defining when information and software count as 'published' and therefore not subject to the EAR.
key_takeaways: Primary source to cite in an export-control slide
Read with 734.3(b)(3) and 742.15(b)

title: U.S. Export Controls and "Published" Encryption Source Code Explained
summary: EFF explainer on the 2016-era EAR changes for published encryption source and when email notification is still needed.
key_takeaways: Relevant if your PNT code includes signal authentication crypto

title: Overview of Regulatory Definitions of Publicly Available, Public Domain, and Published
summary: University compliance guide comparing ITAR public-domain (22 CFR 120.34) and EAR published definitions and the fundamental-research exclusion.
key_takeaways: ITAR-controlled data cannot simply be put in the public domain by an individual
Fundamental-research protection can be lost via publication restrictions
Military GNSS items (e.g. M-code receivers, some anti-jam antenna tech) may be ITAR or EAR controlled - keep hackathon code on public civil signals and published methods

title: DOD adopts 5 principles of artificial intelligence ethics
summary: Announcement of the DoD's AI ethical principles - responsible, equitable, traceable, reliable, governable - recommended by the Defense Innovation Board.
key_takeaways: Traceable and governable map to logging and safe fallback in nav autonomy
Judges increasingly ask how an AI component can be disengaged

title: Summary of the NATO Artificial Intelligence Strategy
summary: NATO's 2021 AI strategy summary setting six principles of responsible use: lawfulness, responsibility and accountability, explainability and traceability, reliability, governability, bias mitigation.
key_takeaways: Applies across the whole AI lifecycle
Expect a NATO-flavored jury to probe reliability and governability

title: DoD Directive 3000.09: Autonomy in Weapon Systems (2023 reissue)
summary: DoD policy governing development and use of autonomous and semi-autonomous weapon systems, reissued January 2023. Cited here as the boundary marker: navigation and awareness tools are outside its scope, weapon autonomy is not.
key_takeaways: Clear line between navigation/autonomy for mobility and weapon autonomy
Keep hackathon scope on the navigation and awareness side

title: Regulation (EU) 2021/821 - Dual-use export control regime
summary: The EU's recast dual-use export control regulation covering items, software and technology including navigation and avionics categories, with public-domain and basic-research de-control notes.
key_takeaways: Category 7 covers navigation and avionics items
Public-domain and basic scientific research notes protect open publication

title: Commission Recommendation (EU) 2021/1700 on internal compliance programmes for controls of research involving dual-use items
summary: Non-binding guidance helping universities and researchers spot and manage dual-use export risks, with scenarios, red flags and FAQs.
key_takeaways: Practical red-flag checklist for collaborative or international teams
Contact national authority when control status is unclear

title: IS-GPS-200N: NAVSTAR GPS Space Segment / Navigation User Segment Interfaces
summary: The master interface specification for the legacy GPS L1 C/A and L2C (and P(Y) at the public level) signals: code generation, signal structure, and the full LNAV/CNAV navigation message bit layouts. Every GPS receiver, simulator and spoofing detector ultimately decodes against this document.
key_takeaways: Defines LNAV subframe and CNAV message formats bit-for-bit
Ephemeris, clock and ionosphere parameter algorithms live here
Revisions are managed through the public ICWG process
Authoritative source for ephemeris and clock equations
Defines L1 C/A and L2C signal structure
Needed to build or audit any navigation message decoder

title: IS-GPS-705J: NAVSTAR GPS Space Segment / User Segment L5 Interfaces
summary: Interface specification for the GPS L5 safety-of-life band signal: I5/Q5 codes, the L5 CNAV message, and signal characteristics. L5's higher chipping rate and wider band make it more robust to narrowband interference than L1 C/A.
key_takeaways: Defines the L5 dataless pilot (Q5) and data (I5) channels
CNAV message types shared with L2C
Draft uprevisions were discussed at the 2025 public ICWG

title: IS-GPS-800J: NAVSTAR GPS Space Segment / User Segment L1C Interfaces
summary: Interface specification for the modernized L1C civil signal designed for interoperability with Galileo E1 and other GNSS: BOC/TMBOC modulation, Weil-code ranging codes, and the CNAV-2 message.
key_takeaways: L1C uses a pilot plus data component, like Galileo E1
CNAV-2 adds FEC-coded subframes
Key reference for multi-GNSS L1 receiver design

title: GPS Interface Control Documents (ICWG index)
summary: Index page for the public GPS ICDs and ISs (200, 705, 800, 870 etc.), change notices and public ICWG meeting material. Useful to find the current revision and pending changes such as integrity support message formats.
key_takeaways: Single place to check which revision is in force
Hosts proposed change notices and meeting redlines
Single entry point for all GPS signal ICDs
Historic versions also linked
Archive site, frozen since February 2025 per its own banner

title: GPS Standard Positioning Service (SPS) Performance Standard, 5th Edition
summary: The formal commitment the US government makes about civil GPS signal-in-space accuracy, availability, continuity and integrity. It is the baseline to compare against when judging whether a receiver anomaly is the signal or interference.
key_takeaways: States guaranteed SIS user range error and availability levels
Defines what counts as a major service failure
Basis for RAIM and integrity assumptions in aviation

title: Galileo Open Service Signal-In-Space Interface Control Document (OS SIS ICD) Issue 2.1
summary: Specification of the Galileo open service signals (E1, E5a, E5b, E6 at the structure level) and the F/NAV and I/NAV navigation messages. Needed for any multi-constellation receiver or Galileo decoder.
key_takeaways: Defines I/NAV and F/NAV page layouts
Ranging code and modulation details for E1 and E5
Newer issues are listed in the GSC reference documents library
Required for decoding Galileo navigation data
I/NAV is the carrier for OSNMA bits

title: Galileo OSNMA Signal-In-Space Interface Control Document Issue 1.1
summary: Defines Open Service Navigation Message Authentication: how TESLA-chain MACs and keys are embedded in spare I/NAV bits so a receiver can cryptographically verify that navigation data came from Galileo. It is the first civil GNSS data-authentication service in operation.
key_takeaways: Uses a TESLA key chain with delayed key disclosure
Authenticates navigation data, not the ranging signal itself
Requires loose time sync and a public key obtained out of band
Civil signal authentication is available today on Galileo E1-B
Receivers need loose time synchronization to verify TESLA keys
Defines what an authenticated vs unauthenticated navigation message means

title: Galileo OSNMA Receiver Guidelines Issue 1.3
summary: Companion to the OSNMA ICD describing how a receiver should process OSNMA: time-sync requirements, key and Merkle-tree handling, verification procedures and how to report authentication status to the user.
key_takeaways: Spells out the receiver time-sync assumption that OSNMA security depends on
Covers cold start, key renewal and chain transitions
Practical checklist for implementing OSNMA in software
Explains which attacks OSNMA does and does not stop (e.g. replay/meaconing limits)
Covers key renewal and alert handling

title: Galileo Open Service Navigation Message Authentication (OSNMA) - service page
summary: Official landing page for the OSNMA service with status, public key and Merkle tree downloads, and links to the ICD and guidelines.
key_takeaways: Where to get the current OSNMA public key and Merkle root
Links to service notices and documentation
Where to download the cryptographic material receivers need

title: Galileo High Accuracy Service Signal-In-Space ICD (HAS SIS ICD) Issue 1.0
summary: Defines the free Galileo High Accuracy Service: PPP orbit, clock and bias corrections broadcast on E6-B (and via internet), including message structure and Reed-Solomon encoding.
key_takeaways: Free PPP corrections broadcast from the satellites themselves
Enables decimetre-level PPP without a ground subscription
E6-B message decoding details for receiver builders

title: European GNSS Service Centre - Programme Reference Documents
summary: Library of current Galileo ICDs, service definition documents and receiver guidelines (OS, HAS, OSNMA, SAR). Check here for the latest issue numbers before implementing.
key_takeaways: Authoritative versions of all public Galileo specs
Includes service definition documents with committed performance
Includes the HAS (High Accuracy Service) ICD for free PPP corrections

title: BeiDou Navigation Satellite System Signal-In-Space ICDs (B1I, B3I, B1C, B2a, B2b)
summary: Official English-language ICD library for BeiDou open service signals, including the BDS-3 B1C and B2a signals that are interoperable with GPS L1C/L5 and Galileo E1/E5a, plus PPP-B2b.
key_takeaways: BDS-3 B1C and B2a are designed for multi-GNSS interoperability
PPP-B2b carries free regional precise corrections
The BeiDou site is the official distribution channel

title: QZSS Performance Standards and Interface Specifications (IS-QZSS)
summary: Japan's QZSS interface specifications covering GPS-compatible signals, the L6 CLAS centimetre-level augmentation and MADOCA PPP services.
key_takeaways: QZSS signals are GPS-interoperable and improve urban-canyon availability in Asia-Oceania
CLAS and MADOCA give free precise positioning corrections
Specs are published openly by the Cabinet Office

title: RTCM 10403.x Differential GNSS (DGNSS) Services - Version 3
summary: The paid-access RTCM v3 standard that defines the binary messages used to stream GNSS corrections and observations (legacy RTK 1001-1012, MSM 1-7 per constellation, ephemerides, SSR). Practically every NTRIP caster and RTK base station speaks it.
key_takeaways: MSM messages replaced legacy observation messages and align with RINEX 3
MSM4/MSM7 are the common choices for RTK
Standard itself is purchased; open parsers document much of it

title: Navipedia: RTK Standards
summary: Free encyclopedia overview of the RTCM correction message families and transport (NTRIP) used for real-time kinematic positioning. A good orientation before buying or parsing the RTCM standard.
key_takeaways: Explains the role of RTCM 2.x vs 3.x messages
Covers NTRIP for internet transport

title: NMEA 0183 Interface Standard
summary: The ASCII serial sentence standard (GGA, RMC, GSA, GSV, VTG...) used by nearly all GNSS receivers and marine electronics. The official standard is sold; open references cover the common sentences.
key_takeaways: Talker IDs distinguish GPS, GLONASS, Galileo, BeiDou and multi-GNSS output
Checksummed ASCII over serial, easy to parse and to fake
Still the lowest-common-denominator GNSS output

title: NMEA 2000 Standard (CAN-based marine network)
summary: CAN bus based marine network standard that carries position, heading, AIS and engine data as PGNs between devices. Paid standard; the community has reverse-documented many PGNs.
key_takeaways: PGNs carry GNSS position, COG/SOG, heading and AIS
Plug-and-play backbone on modern vessels
Unauthenticated bus, relevant to maritime spoofing resilience

title: NMEA Revealed (gpsd project)
summary: A free, detailed field-by-field reference to NMEA 0183 sentences as actually emitted by real receivers, including vendor quirks and version differences. The practical substitute for the paywalled standard.
key_takeaways: Documents real-world deviations from the standard
Covers talker IDs for multi-GNSS output
Written by gpsd maintainers who parse these daily

title: MAVLink Developer Guide
summary: Official documentation for the MAVLink micro air vehicle messaging protocol: message definitions, microservices (mission, parameters, camera, FTP), dialects and code generators.
key_takeaways: Lightweight binary protocol between autopilots, GCS and companion computers
Microservices define stateful exchanges like mission upload
Generators produce bindings for C, Python, Rust and more

title: MAVLink Common Message Set (common.xml)
summary: Reference of all messages and commands in the common dialect, including GPS_RAW_INT, GPS_INPUT for injecting external position, ODOMETRY and VISION_POSITION_ESTIMATE for non-GNSS navigation sources.
key_takeaways: GPS_INPUT and VISION_POSITION_ESTIMATE are the hooks for feeding alternative PNT into an autopilot
ODOMETRY carries full pose plus covariance
Enumerations document EKF and GPS fix status flags

title: MAVLink 2 and Message Signing
summary: Describes MAVLink 2 packet signing: a shared-secret SHA-256 based signature and timestamp appended to frames to authenticate the link and resist replay.
key_takeaways: Signing authenticates but does not encrypt traffic
Key distribution is left to the integrator
Relevant for hardening drone C2 links against injection

title: MAVLink Mission Protocol
summary: The microservice used to upload, download and clear waypoint missions, geofences and rally points between a GCS and an autopilot, with its handshake and retry rules.
key_takeaways: Defines MISSION_COUNT / MISSION_ITEM_INT handshake
Same protocol carries geofence and rally point plans

title: Cursor on Target (NDIA briefing)
summary: Briefing introducing the Cursor on Target XML event schema: the minimal event/point/detail model for exchanging what-when-where of tracked entities between C2 systems.
key_takeaways: Base schema is tiny: event, point, detail
Type strings follow a hierarchical a-f-G-... code derived from symbology
Extensibility lives in the detail element

title: TAK Protocol (takproto) - protobuf encoding of CoT
summary: Documentation of the TAK protocol used by ATAK and TAK Server: how CoT events are framed and carried as protocol buffers over mesh (UDP multicast) and streaming (TCP/TLS) transports, alongside legacy XML.
key_takeaways: Explains version negotiation between XML and protobuf CoT
Mesh vs streaming framing headers
Essential to get a custom app talking to ATAK

title: STANAG 4586 - Standard Interfaces of UAV Control System (UCS) for NATO UAV Interoperability
summary: Public overview of NATO's UAS interoperability standard, which defines a core UCS, a vehicle-specific module and five levels of interoperability from receiving payload data up to full flight control including launch and recovery.
key_takeaways: LOI 1-3 cover payload data and control; LOI 4-5 cover flight control
Vehicle Specific Module isolates proprietary air vehicle interfaces
Full text distributed via NATO / national channels

title: NATO Standardization (topic page)
summary: NATO's public explanation of how STANAGs and Allied publications are produced and ratified, and how interoperability standards flow into national forces. Starting point for locating public STANAG/AP summaries.
key_takeaways: STANAGs record national agreement to implement an Allied publication
Most full texts are restricted; summaries and some APs are public

title: NATO Joint Military Symbology (APP-6) - overview
summary: Overview of APP-6, the NATO standard for map symbols of units, equipment and tactical graphics, now at edition E and aligned with the US MIL-STD-2525 family. Explains frames, affiliation colours and the symbol identification code.
key_takeaways: Affiliation (friend/hostile/neutral/unknown) is encoded by frame shape and colour
APP-6 and MIL-STD-2525 share a common symbol code structure
Open renderers implement it for COP displays

title: MIL-STD-2525 Joint Military Symbology - overview
summary: Summary of the US military symbology standard and its revisions (2525B through E), including the SIDC code formats that symbol renderers and CoT type strings map onto.
key_takeaways: 2525D/E moved to a numeric 20/30-digit SIDC
Basis for symbology in TAK and many C2 tools

title: Executive Order 13905: Strengthening National Resilience Through Responsible Use of PNT Services
summary: US executive order that defines 'responsible use of PNT' and tasks Commerce/NIST, DHS and others to produce PNT profiles, identify critical infrastructure dependencies and pilot-test resilience. It is the root of NIST IR 8323 and the DHS conformance framework.
key_takeaways: Treats PNT disruption as a critical infrastructure risk
Directs creation of voluntary PNT profiles
Calls for testing PNT resilience in federal contracts

title: NIST IR 8323r1: Foundational PNT Profile - Applying the Cybersecurity Framework for the Responsible Use of PNT Services
summary: Maps the NIST Cybersecurity Framework functions (identify, protect, detect, respond, recover) onto systems that produce or consume PNT data. A checklist-style profile for building resilient PNT into an architecture.
key_takeaways: Revision 1 supersedes the 2021 original
Organized around CSF functions, applicable to both GNSS and non-GNSS sources
NIST has signalled alignment with CSF 2.0

title: Resilient PNT Reference Architecture
summary: Companion to the conformance framework describing architectural patterns (source diversity, integrity checking, holdover) that map to its resilience levels.
key_takeaways: Architectural guidance for multi-source PNT
Mapped to conformance framework levels

title: DHS S&T Positioning, Navigation, and Timing Program
summary: Program hub for DHS PNT work: conformance framework, reference architecture, timing guidance and test events for critical infrastructure.
key_takeaways: Links all DHS resilient PNT publications
Shows the civil critical-infrastructure angle of PNT resilience

title: DoD Directive 4650.05: Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (PNT)
summary: DoD policy directive governing the department's PNT enterprise, including the PNT Oversight Council and responsibilities for assured PNT and navigation warfare. Change 3 (2023) updated the oversight structure.
key_takeaways: Establishes the DoD PNT Oversight Council
Assigns responsibilities for PNT and navigation warfare

title: GAO-21-320SP: Defense Navigation Capabilities - DOD Is Developing Positioning, Navigation, and Timing Technologies to Complement GPS
summary: Technology assessment of DoD's alternative PNT efforts (inertial, vision, celestial, magnetic, signals of opportunity, clocks), with maturity status and challenges. A concise government map of the alt-PNT landscape.
key_takeaways: DOD keeps GPS at the core and adds complements
Reviews maturity of many alt-PNT technology families
Flags integration and testing as recurring challenges

title: National Positioning, Navigation, and Timing Resilience R&D Plan
authors: US National Science and Technology Council
summary: Federal R&D plan responding to EO 13905, laying out research priorities for resilient PNT: threat detection, alternative sources, timing distribution and integrity.
key_takeaways: Identifies federal R&D priorities for PNT resilience
Ties research areas back to EO 13905

title: DOT Complementary PNT Action Plan
authors: US Department of Transportation / Volpe Center
summary: US DOT plan to drive adoption of complementary PNT for transportation and critical infrastructure via stakeholder engagement, specifications, field trials and test ranges.
key_takeaways: Five lines of effort starting with engagement and standards
Leads to field testing of commercial CPNT technologies

title: Analyzing a More Resilient National Positioning, Navigation, and Timing Capability (RR-2970)
summary: DHS-sponsored RAND study of civil US PNT dependence that argues GPS is not the only PNT source in practice and that no single system is a perfect backup. It is a deliberately contrarian counterweight to the 'GPS loss is catastrophic' framing.
key_takeaways: Realistic adaptation lowers estimated economic cost of GPS loss
High bar for a large government-funded GPS backup
Recommends modest investment in threat detection

title: Assessing Alternative Positioning, Navigation and Timing Technologies for Potential Deployment in the EU
summary: JRC test campaign at Ispra of commercial alternative PNT systems (terrestrial beacons, LEO, eLoran-like, fibre timing and others) for DG DEFIS. One of the few side-by-side public evaluations of A-PNT products.
key_takeaways: Mature commercial A-PNT already exists for positioning or timing
Recommends a system-of-systems approach
Warns the diverse tests do not allow a fair head-to-head ranking

title: JRC Complementary Position, Navigation and Timing
summary: JRC activity page hosting the A-PNT assessment report with per-vendor appendices and related EU complementary PNT work.
key_takeaways: Official host for the report and vendor appendices

title: International Committee on GNSS (ICG)
authors: UN Office for Outer Space Affairs
summary: UN forum where GNSS providers coordinate compatibility, interoperability and spectrum protection, including interference detection and mitigation work.
key_takeaways: Venue for multi-GNSS interoperability agreements
Hosts work on interference detection and mitigation

title: EASA Safety Information Bulletin 2022-02R4: GNSS Outage and Alterations Leading to Communication / Navigation / Surveillance Degradation
summary: EASA's running bulletin on GNSS jamming and spoofing affecting aviation since February 2022, with recommendations for authorities, ANSPs, operators and manufacturers. Revision 4 is the current issue.
key_takeaways: Spoofing is treated as the harder-to-detect, higher-risk threat
Recommendations are informational, not mandatory
Affected FIRs are tracked on the EASA website

title: FAA GPS/GNSS Interference Reports and Anomaly Reporting
summary: FAA page for reporting and reviewing GPS anomalies and interference events, with links to notices about planned GPS interference testing and operator guidance.
key_takeaways: Where US pilots file post-flight interference reports
Links to GPS test NOTAM information

title: FAA SAFO 24002: Recognizing and Mitigating GPS/GNSS Disruptions
summary: Safety alert for operators describing how jamming and spoofing manifest in the cockpit and what crews should do: revert to conventional procedures, report to ATC, and file written reports.
key_takeaways: Describes cockpit symptoms of jamming vs spoofing
Advises readiness to use conventional navaids
Later FAA guidance revisions followed in 2026

title: GNSS interference (ICAO WRC-27 Preparatory Workshop presentation)
summary: French DGAC presentation at an ICAO WRC-27 preparatory workshop on GNSS RFI: definitions of RFI, jamming and spoofing, the problems they cause in flight (with OPSGROUP 2024 spoofing data), where interference happens, and the ICAO position and actions.
key_takeaways: Summarizes operational impacts on avionics
Frames the ICAO-level mitigation agenda

title: DARPA Robust Optical Clock Network (ROCkN)
summary: Program to field low-SWaP optical atomic clocks with timing holdover beyond GPS satellite clocks, in a portable airborne variant and a transportable land/sea variant, to keep precise time without GNSS.
key_takeaways: Two technical areas: portable and transportable clocks
Two two-year phases from physics package to operational clock

title: DARPA's ROCkN Program Targets GNSS-Free Precision Timing in Contested Environments
summary: Progress report on ROCkN field tests, including optical clock hardware flown on aircraft and deployed aboard a ship.
key_takeaways: Reports field synchronization and platform trials
Shows optical clocks leaving the lab

title: MagNav Challenge Problem (DAF-MIT AI Accelerator)
summary: Challenge site for airborne magnetic anomaly navigation: compensate the aircraft's own magnetic field out of magnetometer data so the remaining crustal anomaly can be map-matched for GPS-free navigation. Challenge is closed but data and code remain.
key_takeaways: Scored against a professionally compensated tail-stinger magnetometer
Real flight data from survey aircraft
Directly reusable as a hackathon benchmark
Sensors: scalar and vector magnetometers, INS, GPS truth
Domain: airborne
Code: MagNav.jl
Terms: Air Force data sharing agreement, non-profit research, education or US government use only, one-year licence

title: MagNav Challenge flight dataset (Zenodo)
summary: Zenodo record holding the MagNav challenge flight data: magnetometer, INS, GPS truth and map data from survey flights.
key_takeaways: HDF5 flight lines with truth position
Paired with MagNav.jl loaders

title: Developing a Series of AI Challenges for the United States Department of the Air Force
summary: Describes the Air Force AI challenge series including MagNav, covering both the compensation stage and a navigation stage that turns cleaned readings into position estimates.
key_takeaways: MagNav split into compensation and navigation sub-challenges
Context on how DAF releases open benchmarks

title: NovAtel GAJT-410ML Anti-Jam Antenna Product Sheet
summary: Datasheet for a compact CRPA anti-jam antenna that combines an antenna array and null-forming electronics for land vehicles and small platforms, protecting GPS and Galileo bands and supporting M-code.
key_takeaways: Null-steering CRPA as a drop-in in front of an existing receiver
Shows typical number of nulls and suppression claims for this class

title: NovAtel GAJT-710ML anti-jam antenna
summary: Product page for the larger 7-element GAJT CRPA unit in a hardened enclosure for land vehicles and fixed sites.
key_takeaways: More elements give more simultaneous nulls
Typical military vehicle CRPA form factor

title: Septentrio AIM+ GNSS jamming and spoofing protection
summary: Vendor explanation of AIM+ interference monitoring and mitigation: narrowband and wideband (chirp) jamming suppression in the receiver's signal processing plus layered spoofing detection including Galileo OSNMA.
key_takeaways: Single-antenna, in-receiver mitigation rather than CRPA
Tiered feature levels
OSNMA is one of the anti-spoofing layers

title: Most resilient GNSS receiver: results from Jammertest in Norway
summary: Vendor write-up of its receivers' behaviour during the Jammertest live jamming and spoofing campaign in Norway. Read as a vendor claim, but useful for the scenario descriptions.
key_takeaways: Describes live jamming and spoofing scenarios
Vendor-authored results, not independent

title: The looming threat of GPS jamming and spoofing (u-blox insights)
summary: u-blox explainer on how jamming and spoofing affect mass-market receivers and which receiver-side defences (multi-band, multi-constellation, signal monitoring) help.
key_takeaways: Spoofing many signals consistently is harder with multi-GNSS
Mass-market receivers expose jamming/spoofing indicators that apps can read

title: White Paper: Protecting GNSS Against Intentional Interference
summary: Open white paper summarizing the threat of jamming and spoofing to civil GNSS and the countermeasure landscape (signal authentication, antenna arrays, consistency checks, regulation).
key_takeaways: Taxonomy of intentional interference
Argues for layered defence and authentication

title: Navipedia - ESA GNSS encyclopedia
summary: ESA's free wiki covering GNSS fundamentals, systems, signals, receivers, augmentation and applications. The fastest authoritative lookup for any GNSS term.
key_takeaways: Peer-reviewed style articles maintained by ESA
Covers GPS, Galileo, GLONASS, BeiDou, SBAS
Best free reference for GNSS concepts
Good RAIM and error-model explanations
Reliable quick reference for GNSS equations
Covers Galileo signal and service details

title: Navipedia: Galileo Open Service Navigation Message Authentication
summary: Navipedia article explaining OSNMA's design and status in plain terms before you tackle the ICD.
key_takeaways: Gentle introduction to TESLA-based navigation message authentication

title: GNSS Data Processing, Vol. I: Fundamentals and Algorithms (ESA TM-23)
authors: J. Sanz Subirana, J.M. Juan Zornoza, M. Hernandez-Pajares (ESA)
summary: Free ESA textbook covering GNSS measurement modelling, SPP, differential positioning and PPP algorithms with full equations. Pairs with the gLAB tool.
key_takeaways: Complete measurement model incl. clocks, troposphere, ionosphere
SPP through PPP derivations
Designed to accompany gLAB exercises

title: GNSS Data Processing, Vol. II: Laboratory Exercises (ESA TM-23)
authors: J. Sanz Subirana, J.M. Juan Zornoza, M. Hernandez-Pajares (ESA)
summary: Hands-on lab volume with step-by-step exercises on real data using the gLAB software, from SPP to carrier-phase PPP.
key_takeaways: Ready-made labs usable as a GNSS bootcamp
Real RINEX data throughout

title: A Software-Defined GPS and Galileo Receiver: A Single-Frequency Approach
authors: K. Borre, D. Akos, N. Bertelsen, P. Rinder, S.H. Jensen
summary: Classic textbook that walks through a complete MATLAB GPS software receiver: acquisition, code/carrier tracking, navigation decoding and positioning. The linked University of Colorado page is the official support site for the book's code.
key_takeaways: The canonical entry point to SDR GNSS receivers
MATLAB code makes every loop inspectable
Foundation for many later open SDR receivers
Teaches acquisition and tracking loops by code
Still the standard SDR GNSS teaching text

title: Stanford Center for Position, Navigation and Time (SCPNT) / GPS Lab
summary: Home of the Stanford GPS Lab and the annual PNT symposium; hosts papers and presentations on integrity, interference monitoring, spoofing and alternative PNT.
key_takeaways: Annual symposium talks are a good snapshot of the field
Lab papers on aviation integrity and RFI localization

title: Stanford GPS Laboratory
summary: Research group site with publications and theses on GNSS integrity, interference detection and localization, and navigation for aviation.
key_takeaways: Thesis archive is a deep free resource
Publications on GNSS RFI detection and localization

title: Stanford NAV Lab (Grace Gao)
summary: Grace Gao's lab working on robust navigation for autonomous systems: GNSS in urban environments, sensor fusion, integrity and lunar PNT. Course and paper material is linked from here.
key_takeaways: Research on GNSS+vision/lidar fusion and integrity
Home of AA272-related teaching on smartphone GNSS

title: Real-World Spoofing Detection and Characterization Using Low-Cost Receivers
summary: Analyses a real spoofing event in the Mediterranean recorded on low-cost u-blox F9P receivers and evaluates detection approaches on that live data rather than a simulator.
key_takeaways: Real spoofing captured on commodity hardware
Shows which detection cues actually fire in the wild

title: Recent Advances on Jamming and Spoofing Detection in GNSS
summary: Open-access Sensors review of GNSS jamming and spoofing detection methods, finding machine learning is now the dominant approach, and covering combined jamming-plus-spoofing scenarios.
key_takeaways: ML-based detection dominates recent work
Separates jamming-only, spoofing-only and combined attacks

title: Detecting and Mitigating Attacks on GPS Devices
authors: J. Burbank, T. Greene, N. Kaabouch
summary: Open-access review of GPS attack detection and mitigation focused on the GPS-denied case, including the alternative sensors and methods used to keep navigating.
key_takeaways: Covers both detection and what to fall back on
Does not cover timing-only alternatives

title: Overview of satellite nav spoofing and anti-spoofing techniques
summary: Open-access Frontiers in Physics overview grouping anti-spoofing countermeasures into detection, identification, suppression and localization of the spoofer.
key_takeaways: Four-stage countermeasure taxonomy
Contrasts spoofing with suppression jamming

title: Survey on positioning technology based on signal of opportunity from low earth orbit
summary: Open-access survey of LEO signals-of-opportunity positioning: Doppler methods, error sources, and extracting observables from signals never designed for navigation (unknown codes, poor onboard clocks).
key_takeaways: Doppler positioning is the workhorse for LEO SoOP
Unknown modulation and clock quality are the core difficulties

title: Enter LEO on the GNSS Stage: Navigation with Starlink Satellites
authors: Z. Kassas, M. Neinavaie, et al.
summary: Opportunistic navigation using Starlink downlink signals without cooperation from the operator, describing two ways to extract navigation observables from unknown signals.
key_takeaways: Starlink is usable for navigation without operator support
Signal structure must be partly estimated blind

title: Navigation with Multi-Constellation LEO Satellite Signals of Opportunity: Starlink, OneWeb, Orbcomm, and Iridium
summary: Experimental multi-constellation LEO SoOP navigation combining four commercial constellations, using the simultaneous tracking and navigation (STAN) framework.
key_takeaways: Combining constellations improves geometry and accuracy
STAN estimates satellite states and receiver state together

title: Preliminary Lessons in Conventional Warfighting from Russia's Invasion of Ukraine: February-July 2022
summary: RUSI analysis of the first months of the war, including the scale of Russian electronic warfare and its effect on Ukrainian UAV survival and GNSS-dependent systems.
key_takeaways: EW is a dominant factor in small-UAV attrition
Lessons for resilience of navigation and C2 links

title: Space Threat Assessment 2024
summary: Previous edition of the CSIS counterspace assessment; useful to see how GNSS interference reporting escalated between years.
key_takeaways: Baseline for year-over-year comparison

title: Jammertest - open GNSS jamming and spoofing test event (Andoya, Norway)
authors: Norwegian Communications Authority, FFI, NPRA and partners
Norwegian public authorities (NPRA, Nkom, FFI and others)
summary: Annual open field event where Norwegian agencies transmit real jamming, spoofing and meaconing so vendors and researchers can test PNT equipment. The public test catalogue and community datasets make it the best source of real interference recordings.
key_takeaways: Real over-the-air jamming and spoofing in a controlled area
Published test catalogue and plan
Participants release datasets on GitHub
Real jamming/spoofing scenarios documented in the public test plan
Use the catalog to design realistic sim scenarios

title: Stone Soup: No Longer Just an Appetiser
summary: FUSION 2023 paper announcing Stone Soup version 1.0, describing the framework's stable architecture and its use across the tracking community.
key_takeaways: Marks the stable 1.0 API
Background on why defence labs backed an open tracking testbed

title: MIT 2.680 Unmanned Marine Vehicle Autonomy, Sensing and Communications
summary: MIT course site with lectures and hands-on labs built on MOOS-IvP, covering behaviour-based autonomy, multi-vehicle coordination, collision avoidance and marine sensing.
key_takeaways: Lab sequence is a ready MOOS-IvP onboarding path
Includes COLREGs-style collision avoidance behaviours

title: MOOS-IvP documentation wiki
summary: Documentation hub for MOOS-IvP with install guides, the IvP Helm manual, behaviour and app references and example missions.
key_takeaways: Helm manual explains multi-objective behaviour arbitration
Mission files are simple text, quick to adapt

title: COLREGs - Convention on the International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea, 1972
summary: IMO page for the collision regulations that define give-way and stand-on duties, lights and signals; the rule set autonomous surface vessels must encode.
key_takeaways: Rules 13-17 (overtaking, head-on, crossing) drive most USV avoidance logic
Rules are written for human judgement, which makes formalization hard

title: ITU-R M.1371-6 - Technical characteristics for VHF automatic identification system using time division multiple access in the maritime mobile service
summary: The ITU recommendation defining AIS radio, TDMA access and message formats that decoders such as pyais implement.
key_takeaways: Defines message types 1-27 decoded by pyais and AIS-catcher
AIS is unauthenticated, so spoofing detection is an open problem

title: Signal K Specification
summary: Published Signal K specification describing the JSON data model, REST and streaming APIs for marine data.
key_takeaways: Defines navigation.* paths for position, attitude and speed
WebSocket delta stream is easy to consume from any language

title: ArduSub documentation
summary: User and developer documentation for ArduSub, covering ROV configuration, sensors, and integration of external positioning such as DVL and USBL via MAVLink.
key_takeaways: Explains how external position sources feed the EKF on a sub
Good companion to BlueOS extensions

title: Water Linked documentation (DVL and Underwater GPS)
summary: Vendor documentation for Water Linked DVLs and Underwater GPS (USBL-style) systems, including the JSON-over-TCP and serial protocols.
key_takeaways: DVL reports velocity and dead-reckoning over JSON/TCP
Check firmware version against protocol version

title: Autoware documentation
summary: Official Autoware documentation with architecture, installation, tutorials and design notes for localization, perception and planning components.
key_takeaways: Localization design docs explain NDT plus EKF fusion
Planning simulator tutorial runs without hardware

title: RELLIS-3D Dataset: Data, Benchmarks and Analysis
summary: Paper introducing the RELLIS-3D multimodal off-road dataset with annotated lidar and images and baseline results.
key_takeaways: Off-road semantics differ sharply from urban datasets
Includes GNSS/IMU for localization work

title: Wild Visual Navigation: Fast Traversability Learning via Pre-Trained Models and Online Self-Supervision
authors: Mattamala, Frey et al., ETH Zurich / Oxford
summary: Describes learning visual traversability online from pre-trained features and robot experience, adapting within minutes in forests and grassland.
key_takeaways: Self-supervision removes manual traversability labels
Pre-trained vision features make online learning feasible

title: Loco Positioning System documentation
summary: Bitcraze documentation for its UWB positioning system covering anchor placement, two-way ranging versus TDoA modes and configuration with Crazyflies.
key_takeaways: TDoA scales to many tags, TWR is simpler
Anchor geometry dominates accuracy

title: UTIL: An Ultra-wideband Time-difference-of-arrival Indoor Localization Dataset
summary: Project page for a UWB TDoA dataset collected with Loco Positioning hardware, with ground truth for evaluating indoor UWB localization. No licence file in the learnsyslab/util-uwb-dataset GitHub repo, so reuse terms are unstated (all rights reserved by default).
key_takeaways: Real UWB data including non-line-of-sight effects
Useful to benchmark estimators before buying hardware

title: Crazyswarm2 documentation
summary: Docs for Crazyswarm2 with installation, simulation backends, swarm configuration and tutorials.
key_takeaways: Simulation mode lets you prototype swarm logic on a laptop

title: Onboard Ranging-based Relative Localization and Stability for Lightweight Aerial Swarms
authors: Shushuai Li et al. (TU Delft MAVLab)
summary: Presents onboard UWB ranging with an EKF for relative localization among small quadrotors, with a stability analysis of formation control built on those estimates.
key_takeaways: Relative localization needs no anchors
Observability depends on relative motion between agents

title: Swarm-SLAM: Sparse Decentralized Collaborative Simultaneous Localization and Mapping Framework for Multi-Robot Systems
summary: Decentralized collaborative SLAM aimed at swarms, prioritizing which inter-robot loop closures to compute and share to limit communication.
key_takeaways: Budgeted loop-closure exchange keeps bandwidth low
Works across lidar, stereo and RGB-D
Communication budget is a first-class design constraint
Supports LiDAR, stereo and RGB-D

title: DCL-SLAM: A Distributed Collaborative LiDAR SLAM Framework for a Robotic Swarm
summary: Describes a fully distributed lidar C-SLAM using compact descriptors for inter-robot place recognition.
key_takeaways: Compact LiDAR-Iris descriptors reduce data exchange

title: Anti-UAV: A Large Multi-Modal Benchmark for UAV Tracking
summary: Introduces the Anti-UAV RGB and thermal infrared video benchmark for UAV tracking and an evaluation protocol.
key_takeaways: Thermal IR matters for night and small-target tracking
Targets frequently disappear, so trackers must handle absence

title: Anti-UAV Challenge
summary: Site for the recurring Anti-UAV workshop and challenge with tracks for single and multiple UAV tracking in infrared video.
key_takeaways: Leaderboards give a reference point for hackathon results

title: Enabling Novel Mission Operations and Interactions with ROSA: The Robot Operating System Agent
summary: Describes ROSA, an LLM agent that lets operators inspect and command ROS systems in natural language through a curated tool set, and discusses safety and operational considerations.
key_takeaways: Tool-based LLM access keeps robot actions auditable
Targets operators, not only developers

title: OpenFly: A Comprehensive Platform for Aerial Vision-Language Navigation
summary: Presents a multi-engine aerial VLN platform with automated data generation, a large outdoor benchmark and a keyframe-aware VLN model.
key_takeaways: Automated toolchain scales aerial VLN data
Multiple rendering engines reduce sim bias

title: AerialVLN: Vision-and-Language Navigation for UAVs
summary: ICCV 2023 paper introducing a city-scale UAV vision-and-language navigation task, simulator and baselines.
key_takeaways: Aerial VLN is much harder than indoor VLN
Long trajectories and 3D actions

title: CityNav: A Large-Scale Dataset for Real-World Aerial Navigation
summary: Introduces a language-goal aerial navigation dataset built on real-city 3D data with geographic metadata, and baselines using map-based grounding.
key_takeaways: Geographic map priors improve aerial language navigation
Human demonstrations from a web simulator

title: ViNT: A Foundation Model for Visual Navigation
summary: Trains a transformer navigation policy across many robot datasets and shows it adapts to new robots and tasks with little data.
key_takeaways: Cross-embodiment pretraining works for navigation
Image-goal policy plus topological graph

title: NoMaD: Goal Masked Diffusion Policies for Navigation and Exploration
summary: Single diffusion policy that handles both goal-directed navigation and undirected exploration by masking the goal.
key_takeaways: One model for explore and goal-reach
Runs on small robots

title: Visual Language Maps for Robot Navigation
summary: Fuses visual-language features into 3D maps so robots can localize landmarks named in open-vocabulary language and navigate to them.
key_takeaways: Language-indexed spatial maps
Enables spatial instructions like 'between X and Y'

title: LM-Nav: Robotic Navigation with Large Pre-Trained Models of Language, Vision, and Action
summary: Combines an LLM for landmark extraction, CLIP for grounding and a visual navigation model to follow long route instructions outdoors.
key_takeaways: No language-annotated robot data needed
Modular pretrained composition

title: TypeFly: Flying Drones with Large Language Model
summary: Proposes a compact drone programming language for LLM output, cutting token count and latency while keeping plans checkable.
key_takeaways: Constrain LLM output to a small DSL
Latency matters for flight

title: ChatGPT for Robotics: Design Principles and Model Abilities
summary: Early study of prompting strategies and API design for using ChatGPT to generate robot and drone control code, with AirSim demos.
key_takeaways: Expose a high-level function library to the LLM
Keep a human in the loop to review code

title: ConceptGraphs: Open-Vocabulary 3D Scene Graphs for Perception and Planning
summary: Builds object-centric 3D scene graphs with open-vocabulary labels from RGB-D and uses an LLM to plan over them.
key_takeaways: Compact object-level maps for LLM planning
Uses 2D foundation models

title: NaVid: Video-based VLM Plans the Next Step for Vision-and-Language Navigation
summary: Video-based VLM that plans navigation actions from monocular RGB history without maps, odometry or depth.
key_takeaways: Map-free language navigation
Sim-to-real transfer

title: Model Context Protocol specification
summary: The specification for MCP, the protocol LLM clients use to call tools and read resources from servers; the basis of the ROS, MAVLink and QGIS MCP servers.
key_takeaways: Tools, resources and prompts as server primitives
Transport and authorization rules

title: OpenShoe: open source embedded foot-mounted INS
summary: Project site (offline since 2026; archived copy) for OpenShoe, an open hardware and software ZUPT-aided foot-mounted INS module, described in the PLANS 2012 paper 'Foot-mounted INS for Everybody' and follow-up IPIN 2014 work.
key_takeaways: Open hardware + firmware for ZUPT-aided INS
Module reports per-step displacement and heading change

title: Deep Event Visual Odometry
summary: Learned event-only monocular VO trained on simulated events that generalizes to real event datasets.
key_takeaways: Event-only VO without frames
Simulation-trained, real-world tested

title: cuVSLAM: CUDA accelerated visual odometry and mapping
summary: Describes NVIDIA's GPU-accelerated VO/SLAM supporting from one to many cameras with optional IMU, designed for real-time edge deployment.
key_takeaways: Multi-camera rigs supported
Runs in real time on Jetson

title: R-Mode Baltic and R-Mode Baltic 2
authors: DLR Institute of Communications and Navigation
summary: DLR project page for R-Mode Baltic, which built a Baltic Sea testbed adding ranging signals to existing maritime radio beacons and AIS base stations as a terrestrial backup to GNSS, continued by R-Mode Baltic 2 and ORMOBASS.
key_takeaways: Reuses existing MF beacons and VHF AIS for ranging
Moving toward IALA standardisation

title: The Global Loran / eLoran Infrastructure Evolution: A Robust and Resilient PNT Backup for GNSS
summary: Briefing by the FAA's chief navigation systems engineer to the US Space-Based PNT Advisory Board (3 June 2014) on the history of Loran/eLoran and the findings of the 2006-2008 Independent Assessment Team, which judged eLoran a viable independent backup to GPS.
key_takeaways: eLoran has different physical failure modes than GNSS
IAT found eLoran meets non-precision approach (RNP 0.3), harbor entrance (10-20 m) and Stratum 1 timing needs

title: NVIDIA Jetson AI Lab
summary: Tutorial hub for running generative AI, VLMs and robotics models on Jetson devices, built around jetson-containers.
key_takeaways: Step-by-step onboard LLM/VLM deployment
Covers ROS and robotics integrations

title: EUSPA GNSS Market and User Technology Reports
summary: Download page for EUSPA's market reports and GNSS User Technology Reports, which survey receiver, antenna and resilience technology trends.
key_takeaways: User Technology Report covers anti-jamming, authentication and multi-constellation trends
Useful for framing a pitch

title: Flightradar24 GPS jamming map
summary: Flightradar24's map of GNSS interference, computed from navigation integrity category values broadcast by aircraft over its receiver network.
key_takeaways: Grey areas mean insufficient flights or receivers, not absence of jamming
Covers all GNSS, not just GPS

title: Assessing the Spoofing Threat: Development of a Portable GPS Civilian Spoofer
summary: Landmark ION GNSS 2008 paper that built a receiver-based civil GPS spoofer and analysed how hard it is to detect, kicking off modern civil spoofing defense research.
key_takeaways: Receiver-based spoofers can align with authentic signals and drag the victim smoothly
Simple checks are insufficient against a sophisticated spoofer
Motivates cryptographic and signal-level defenses

title: GNSS Spoofing and Detection
summary: Proceedings of the IEEE survey of spoofing attack types and detection/mitigation techniques, from navigation-data checks to signal distortion monitoring and multi-antenna methods.
key_takeaways: Taxonomy of defenses: cryptographic, signal-processing, geometric
Multi-antenna angle-of-arrival checks are powerful
Combining several weak tests beats any single test

title: Texas Spoofing Test Battery (TEXBAT)
summary: Public set of recorded high-rate IQ files of GPS L1 spoofing scenarios (static and dynamic, time and position push) used as a standard benchmark for spoofing detection.
key_takeaways: De facto benchmark for signal-level spoofing detectors
Recordings are large IQ files suitable for GNSS-SDR
Terms: research use only, (c) University of Texas; users asked not to redistribute the data

title: Signal Structure of the Starlink Ku-Band Downlink
summary: Reverse-engineers the Starlink Ku-band downlink as OFDM and identifies synchronization sequences usable for opportunistic ranging and positioning.
key_takeaways: Starlink frames contain known sequences usable as pilots
Enables LEO signals-of-opportunity PNT without operator cooperation

title: The First Carrier Phase Tracking and Positioning Results With Starlink LEO Satellite Signals
summary: IEEE TAES letter showing carrier-phase tracking of Starlink signals with unknown structure and positioning from several satellites.
key_takeaways: Positioning from Starlink is feasible without knowing the signal format
Six satellites tracked; 7.7 m horizontal error with known receiver altitude

title: Google Smartphone Decimeter Challenge 2023-2024
summary: Kaggle competition with raw GNSS and IMU logs from Android phones in cars, scored on positioning accuracy against high-grade truth.
key_takeaways: Large public smartphone GNSS dataset with truth
Winning solutions used factor graphs and carrier phase
Data also on IEEE DataPort under CC BY; Kaggle competition rules not verified
Sensors: phone raw GNSS, IMU
Size class: medium
Kaggle account required

title: Google Smartphone Decimeter Challenge 2022
summary: Earlier edition of the smartphone GNSS positioning competition with Android raw measurement logs and ground truth.
key_takeaways: Good secondary dataset for testing detectors on diverse phones
Sensors: phone raw GNSS, IMU
Kaggle account required

title: Android Raw GNSS Measurement Datasets for Precise Positioning
summary: ION GNSS+ 2020 paper releasing the first public Android raw GNSS datasets with corrections and ground truth, the origin of the GSDC series.
key_takeaways: Describes data collection and ground truth
Basis for all later GSDC editions

title: Raw GNSS Measurements
summary: Android documentation on the GnssMeasurement API: which phones expose pseudorange, carrier phase and AGC, and how to log them.
key_takeaways: AGC and C/N0 fields support jamming detection on phones
Duty cycling must be disabled for continuous carrier phase

title: NTRIP: Networked Transport of RTCM via Internet Protocol (BKG)
summary: BKG's overview of the NTRIP protocol for streaming GNSS corrections, with links to its caster, client and server software.
key_takeaways: NTRIP is HTTP-based streaming of RTCM
BKG maintains the reference caster

title: BKG Ntrip Client - BNC
summary: Page for BNC, BKG's multi-stream NTRIP client that records, decodes, converts to RINEX, monitors and can compute real-time PPP from correction streams.
key_takeaways: Swiss-army tool for real-time correction streams
Can monitor stream latency and outages

title: GNSS-SDR documentation
summary: Tutorials and reference for configuring the GNSS-SDR receiver, including signal processing blocks, front-end setup and monitoring outputs.
key_takeaways: Step-by-step first-fix tutorials with sample files
Explains each receiver block for modification

title: rtklibexplorer blog
summary: Long-running practitioner blog on getting centimetre-level RTK/PPK from low-cost u-blox receivers with the demo5 RTKLIB fork, with configuration walk-throughs and data analysis.
key_takeaways: Configuration recipes that save hours
Honest comparisons of receivers and settings
Practical RTK tuning tips you will not find in papers
Maintainer of the demo5 RTKLIB fork

title: IGS products
summary: Catalog of International GNSS Service precise orbits, clocks, biases and atmospheric products used by PPP and precise processing.
key_takeaways: Precise products are free
Product latency ranges from real-time to final

title: Quaternion kinematics for the error-state Kalman filter
summary: Long tutorial report covering quaternion conventions, rotation perturbations and their derivatives, and a full derivation of an IMU-driven error-state Kalman filter including the reset step.
key_takeaways: Pins down Hamilton vs JPL quaternion conventions
Step-by-step ESKF prediction, correction and reset
Global vs local error definitions
Standard reference for implementing an INS/ESKF
Covers local vs global perturbation conventions

title: A micro Lie theory for state estimation in robotics
summary: Tutorial paper giving just enough Lie theory (groups, exponential map, adjoint, Jacobians, uncertainty on manifolds) to write correct estimators for 3D pose; it is the basis of Solà's 'Lie theory for the roboticist' course and the manif library.
key_takeaways: Unified plus/minus notation for manifold states
Ready-to-use Jacobians for SO(3), SE(3) and others
Ready-to-use Jacobians for SO(3)/SE(3)
Fixes the most common EKF-on-rotations mistakes

title: Principles of GNSS, Inertial, and Multisensor Integrated Navigation Systems, Second Edition
summary: Standard reference on satellite, inertial and terrestrial radio navigation and their integration, including INS/GNSS integration architectures, dead reckoning, feature matching and integrity monitoring.
key_takeaways: Loose, tight and deep INS/GNSS coupling explained
Covers fault detection and integrity
Companion MATLAB simulation software for buyers

title: Strapdown Inertial Navigation Technology, 2nd Edition
summary: Classic IET text on strapdown inertial navigation: sensor technologies, mechanisation, error propagation and compensation, and aided navigation.
key_takeaways: Physical principles and error growth of INS
Sensor technology from mechanical gyros to MEMS

title: State Estimation for Robotics (Second Edition)
summary: Textbook on probabilistic estimation for robotics, from linear-Gaussian filtering and batch estimation to matrix Lie groups for 3D pose; the second edition adds variational inference and inertial navigation material. Author hosts a PDF; print edition from Cambridge University Press.
key_takeaways: Batch vs recursive estimation from first principles
Matrix Lie groups for pose and uncertainty
New inertial navigation section in 2nd edition
Rigorous treatment of SE(3) uncertainty
Bridges filtering and batch optimization

title: Factor Graphs for Robot Perception
summary: Foundations and Trends monograph (free author PDF) explaining SLAM and sensor fusion as inference on factor graphs, with incremental smoothing (iSAM) and the reasoning behind the GTSAM library.
key_takeaways: Why sparsity makes smoothing tractable
From batch to incremental (iSAM) inference
Why smoothing beats filtering for multi-sensor nav
Direct conceptual guide to GTSAM
