title: iSAM2: Incremental Smoothing and Mapping Using the Bayes Tree
summary: Introduces the Bayes tree and the iSAM2 algorithm for incremental nonlinear smoothing with fluid relinearization, the engine behind GTSAM's online estimators.
key_takeaways: Incremental updates without periodic batch steps
Bayes tree data structure

title: On-Manifold Preintegration for Real-Time Visual-Inertial Odometry
summary: Derives IMU preintegration on the SO(3) manifold with bias-correction Jacobians, enabling IMU factors between keyframes in factor-graph optimization.
key_takeaways: Summarise many IMU samples into one relative-motion factor
First-order bias correction avoids re-integration

title: The invariant extended Kalman filter as a stable observer
summary: Foundational paper showing that for group-affine systems the invariant EKF has error dynamics independent of the trajectory, giving stability guarantees standard EKFs lack.
key_takeaways: Error defined on the Lie group, not in vector space
Better consistency under large initial errors

title: Contact-Aided Invariant Extended Kalman Filtering for Robot State Estimation
summary: Applies the invariant EKF to legged robots, fusing IMU with leg contact kinematics, and evaluates it against a quaternion EKF.
key_takeaways: Contact points as extra states in the group
Faster convergence than quaternion EKF

title: AI-IMU Dead-Reckoning
summary: Car localisation from IMU alone by combining an invariant EKF with a neural network that adapts measurement noise covariances (pseudo-measurements), evaluated on KITTI.
key_takeaways: Learned covariances, classical filter structure
IMU-only ground vehicle dead reckoning

title: TLIO: Tight Learned Inertial Odometry
summary: Combines a network that predicts displacement and uncertainty from IMU data with an EKF, for pedestrian inertial odometry.
key_takeaways: Learned measurement plus learned uncertainty in a filter

title: RoNIN: Robust Neural Inertial Navigation in the Wild: Benchmark, Evaluations, and New Methods
summary: Introduces a large smartphone IMU dataset with ground truth and benchmarks neural architectures for pedestrian velocity regression.
key_takeaways: Benchmark dataset for learned pedestrian navigation
Body-frame heading-agnostic representation

title: AirIO: Learning Inertial Odometry with Enhanced IMU Feature Observability
summary: UAV-focused learned inertial odometry that changes how IMU data are represented to the network to make motion features more observable.
key_takeaways: IMU-only odometry for drones
Representation choice matters for UAV learned IO

title: Kalibr wiki: IMU Noise Model
summary: Practical explanation of white noise and random-walk bias parameters for IMUs, how to convert datasheet values to continuous/discrete form and how to inflate them for real use.
key_takeaways: Continuous vs discrete noise density conversion
Inflate Allan-derived noise for real-world use

title: Factor Graphs and GTSAM: A Hands-on Introduction
summary: Hands-on introduction to the GTSAM library: modelling robot odometry, landmark and pose-graph SLAM as factor graphs, solving with Levenberg-Marquardt or iSAM2, and reading marginal covariances, with C++ and MATLAB snippets.
key_takeaways: Best first hour with GTSAM
Shortest path to a working pose-graph (C++ or MATLAB examples)
Pattern reusable for GNSS/INS/visual factor fusion

title: An efficient orientation filter for inertial and inertial/magnetic sensor arrays
summary: Internal report introducing the gradient-descent orientation filter now known as the Madgwick filter, for IMU and MARG sensors.
key_takeaways: Low computational cost attitude filter
Single tuning parameter

title: Auterion Skynode S and Auterion Visual Navigation
summary: Auterion sells PX4-derived AuterionOS plus Skynode flight/mission computers. Skynode S (2024) is a small integrated autopilot/mission computer marketed for operation when GNSS and links are jammed; Auterion Visual Navigation is the company's camera-based position source, named in its 2025 DIU Artemis completion announcement.
key_takeaways: Vendor claim: AuterionOS detects GNSS jamming/spoofing and stops trusting GNSS (Jan 2024 announcement)
Vendor/press claim: used in Ukraine; no public accuracy figures found
Open-source base is PX4; the visual navigation layer is proprietary

title: Shield AI Hivemind autonomy stack
summary: Hivemind is Shield AI's onboard autonomy software, flown on its V-BAT and on partner aircraft. In an interview the CTO describes a state-estimation framework fusing visual, EO/IR and inertial observations so the aircraft keeps operating without GNSS or comms.
key_takeaways: Vendor description: multi-sensor state estimation for GNSS-denied and comms-denied flight
No published accuracy numbers found
ViDAR (acquired with Sentient Vision, 2024) is an EO/IR detection product, not a navigation source

title: Helsing HX-2 - map/landmark-based GNSS-denied navigation (navigation aspect only)
summary: Helsing's HX-2 is a loitering UAS supplied to Ukraine. Indexed here only for its navigation approach: press reporting says an onboard computer with stored map data lets it navigate by recognising landmarks when satellite navigation is denied. Helsing navigation job postings mention vision-aided, terrain-relative, celestial and signals-of-opportunity methods.
key_takeaways: Press/vendor claim: landmark recognition against stored maps; no public accuracy data
Shows the European market expects map-based visual nav as a baseline feature

title: Q-CTRL Ironstone Opal quantum-assured magnetic navigation
summary: Q-CTRL's navigation product pairs quantum magnetometers with its software to match measured crustal magnetic anomalies against maps (MagNav). The company reports flight, ground and maritime trials and positions it as a GNSS backup for aviation, including work with Airbus.
key_takeaways: Vendor claims (not independent): RNP 0.3 met in flight (error under 0.3 nm for 95% of a flight); the linked case study claims 50x lower positioning uncertainty than an INS over a ~500 km flight and at least 11x with the sensor inside the cabin; other Q-CTRL materials give different multipliers
Vendor claim: RTCA DO-160 environmental qualification - not an airworthiness or RNP operational approval
Underlying method is the same map-matching problem as the open AFRL/MIT MagNav challenge

title: SandboxAQ AQNav geomagnetic navigation
summary: AQNav is SandboxAQ's magnetic anomaly navigation system: magnetometers plus learned compensation, matched against magnetic anomaly maps. Flight-tested with Acubed (Airbus) on a Beechcraft Baron using public maps, and, per later SandboxAQ announcements, with the USAF on C-17/C-130J and in 2026 on a Northrop Grumman Lumberjack drone.
key_takeaways: Vendor claims (July 2025 Acubed campaign, 150+ flight hours on a Beechcraft Baron 58 with the public NAMAM map): within RNP 2 100% of the time and RNP 1 95%; outperformed INS without GNSS on every flight over 2 h
Sept 2026 drone test announcement gave no error figures (noted by press)
Accepted into the 2025 NATO DIANA cohort (vendor/press)

title: Xona Space Systems Pulsar LEO PNT constellation
summary: Xona is building Pulsar, a commercial LEO constellation broadcasting dedicated L-band navigation signals with authentication. Pulsar-0 launched in June/July 2025 as an in-orbit demonstrator; production satellites and initial service were planned for 2026-2027 per later reporting, and the FCC granted conditional approval in August 2026 (initially 16 satellites, more after a debris review).
key_takeaways: LEO PNT signals are stronger at the ground than MEO GNSS, which is the anti-jam argument
Service is not yet generally available; dates in press reports conflict
Open work in this space uses existing LEO signals of opportunity (Starlink, Iridium Doppler) instead

title: TrustPoint - C-band LEO PNT
summary: TrustPoint is developing a commercial C-band LEO navigation constellation. Its third demonstration satellite (Time Flies) launched in June 2025 carrying a C-band payload for testing partner receivers.
key_takeaways: Vendor claim: commercial GPS alternative from LEO; no independent performance reports found
C-band choice moves PNT away from crowded and jammed L-band

title: Iridium PNT (Satellite Time and Location) and Iridium PNT ASIC
summary: Iridium broadcasts a high-power LEO timing and location signal (STL, from the Satelles acquisition) usable as a GNSS backup and cross-check. A dedicated PNT ASIC was unveiled in October 2025 and announced commercially available in July 2026; integrators include Solace and Skyband, and VectorNav/NAL Research announced STL-aided INS work in 2025.
key_takeaways: Positioning is coarse compared to GNSS; main value is timing and an independent plausibility check
Vendor claim on ASIC size: 8 x 8 mm, under 0.2 g (Iridium fact sheet, Oct 2025)
Open LEO Doppler code in the index can use Iridium signals of opportunity without a subscription

title: Honeywell Vision Aided Navigation (Alternative Navigation Suite)
summary: Honeywell's VAN correlates live visible or IR imagery against onboard reference maps for an absolute fix, paired with its inertial units. It sits in an Alternative Navigation Suite with magnetic-anomaly and celestial modules.
key_takeaways: Vendor description: passive, sensor-agnostic image-to-map correlation
Press claim: 'GPS-like' performance on Embraer E170 and AW139 tests; no numbers published
Same problem as open UAV absolute visual localization benchmarks

title: Honeywell HGuide o480 single-card INS and HGuide i700 IMU
summary: HGuide o480 (May 2025) is a single-card INS for small UAVs and ground robots that accepts velocity aiding (e.g. Honeywell radar velocity sensor) and embeds a Septentrio receiver with AIM+ anti-jam/anti-spoof. The HGuide i700 IMU is marketed as near navigation grade with a no-license-required export classification.
key_takeaways: Shows the commodity pattern: tactical IMU + velocity aid + hardened GNSS in one card
Export classification is a selling point, which matters for team hardware choices

title: Advanced Navigation Boreas FOG INS with LVS laser velocity sensor
summary: Advanced Navigation's Boreas fibre-optic-gyro INS line, fused with its LVS laser velocity sensor or wheel odometry, is marketed for long GNSS-denied ground and maritime runs; reported trials include a US Army testbed and an underground mine.
key_takeaways: Vendor/press claims: 11.7 m error over 65 km with GNSS jammed (wheel-encoder config, US Army testbed, linked article); better than 0.1% of distance travelled in BHP's Callio mine trial (Advanced Navigation case study)
Strategy is inertial-centric dead reckoning with velocity aiding, not vision

title: Inertial Labs VINS visual-aided INS (with Maxar Raptor)
summary: Launched June 2025, VINS combines an Inertial Labs INS with Maxar Raptor software that matches camera frames to Maxar Precision3D satellite-derived 3D maps for absolute position on long-range UAV flights.
key_takeaways: Vendor claims: about 35 m horizontal / 5 m vertical without GNSS
Options for Iridium-based PNT and M-code receivers
Commercial map product (Precision3D) is the moat; open teams use free orthophotos and DEMs

title: Safran VersaPNT and Geonyx resilient PNT units
summary: Safran's defense PNT range includes VersaPNT (GNSS receiver + IMU + disciplined oscillator with jamming/spoofing detection and NTP/PTP time serving) and the Geonyx HRG-based INS; GPS World reports a NAVKITE kit combining Geonyx M with VersaSync for French Navy commandos.
key_takeaways: Combined position + timing holdover in one box is the standard defense product shape
Detection flags and holdover timing are reproducible in open stacks at lower grade

title: SBG Systems Ellipse INS - 2025 GNSS-denied firmware
summary: A March 2025 free firmware update for SBG's Ellipse (v3 hardware) adds jamming/spoofing detection flags and lets users reject or re-enable GNSS and other aiding sensors without resetting the filter.
key_takeaways: Vendor claim: improved accuracy in GNSS-denied and magnetically disturbed conditions
Integrity flags plus manual sensor rejection is now an expected feature even in small INS

title: VectorNav - Iridium STL-aided INS collaboration with NAL Research
summary: VectorNav makes small tactical-grade IMU/GNSS-INS units widely used on research drones (PX4 has a driver). In April 2025 it announced work with NAL Research on Iridium STL-aided INS for GNSS-denied operation.
key_takeaways: Collaboration announcement, not a shipped product feature
VN-series units are a common drop-in for PX4 testbeds

title: Spirent GSS7000 and PNT X GNSS/PNT simulators
summary: Spirent's lab simulators generate multi-GNSS RF with controllable interference and spoofing (meaconing, trajectory spoofing, nav data spoofing) for hardware-in-the-loop receiver testing; PNT X extends this to combined PNT/sensor simulation.
key_takeaways: Lab-grade, export-controlled tooling; judges from industry will know it
Open alternatives are SDR-based signal simulators - legal only into a cable or shielded enclosure

title: Safran Skydel simulation engine / GSG-8 GNSS simulator (ex-Orolia)
summary: Skydel is the SDR/GPU-based simulation engine behind Safran's GSG-8 simulators, with built-in jamming and spoofing scenarios, CRPA wavefront variants and LEO PNT signal options; Safran offers it to universities through an academic programme.
key_takeaways: Vendor datasheet: jamming and spoofing generated without extra hardware
Spoofing workflows run a 'truth' and a 'spoofer' instance - a useful mental model for test design

title: infiniDome GPSdome / GPSdome 2 small-UAS anti-jam module
summary: infiniDome sells retrofit anti-jam modules that sit between antenna elements and a commercial GNSS receiver on small drones and vehicles; GPSdome 2 is dual-band with up to four elements for nulling several jammer directions.
key_takeaways: Vendor claim: CRPA-like protection without CRPA cost or export restrictions
Weight figures differ across press releases (500 g in the linked GPS World piece, 350 g elsewhere)

title: Twist Robotics OSCAR visual navigation module (Ukraine)
summary: Ukrainian company Twist Robotics announced OSCAR in January 2026: a camera-based module that recognises landmarks, matches them to a map and feeds coordinates to the UAV autopilot when GNSS is jammed.
key_takeaways: Vendor claim: platforms with the module have flown more than 500,000 km
Architecture (camera => map match => coordinates into autopilot) is the same one open repos implement

title: Blue Arrow - Ukrainian visual navigation for drones (Brave1 cluster)
summary: Brave1 cluster member Blue Arrow was presented by Ukraine's minister Fedorov in 2025 as having an autonomous visual navigation system that lets drones fly without GNSS under jamming and spoofing.
key_takeaways: Claim relayed from a ministerial post; no technical detail or numbers published
One of many Ukrainian vendors in this niche (others named by Brave1: Norda Dynamics, The Fourth Law, ZIR)

title: Theseus Visual Navigation System (YC launch)
summary: US startup whose founders started at the February 2024 El Segundo Defense Tech Hackathon (Aviation Week coverage). Its VNS uses a camera, an IMU and pre-loaded satellite imagery to estimate position and feeds the drone a substitute GPS signal.
key_takeaways: Vendor claims: six months from hackathon to a SOCOM sale (YC launch post); integration under 30 minutes (company statement relayed by press)
Direct precedent that a hackathon visual-nav demo can become a product - and that judges have seen this pitch

title: Spleenlab VISIONAIRY perception and GNSS-free navigation software
summary: German company Spleenlab sells VISIONAIRY, an AI perception suite for drones (vendor description: VIO, map-based relocalization, EO/IR and LiDAR SLAM) that joined the Auterion ecosystem in 2022 and integrates with PX4/Auterion and ROS. Quantum Systems later acquired Spleenlab and uses it for GNSS-denied navigation (press).
key_takeaways: Vendor description only; no published accuracy
Module list mirrors what open VIO + VPR repos offer

title: UAVOS NavAI vision-based navigation module
summary: UAVOS markets NavAI as an add-on vision-based navigation module for UAS in GNSS-degraded conditions (GPS World product announcement).
key_takeaways: Product announcement; performance figures not verified here

title: DARPA Robust Quantum Sensors (RoQS) - Phase 1
summary: RoQS (solicitation DARPA-PS-25-11) aims to make quantum sensors robust to platform vibration and motion so they work on real vehicles; Phase 1 launched August 2025 with compact sensors to be tested on a government helicopter plus platform integration studies.
key_takeaways: Problem statement: quantum sensors lose their advantage on moving platforms
Signals where defense money is going for GNSS-independent inertial/magnetic sensing

title: DIU Transition of Quantum Sensing (TQS)
summary: DIU programme fielding quantum sensors for PNT: lines of effort cover quantum inertial sensors, gravimeters for gravity-aided naval navigation, quantum magnetic sensing, magnetic navigation and component insertion, with more than 10 field tests planned in the first ~12 months (announced March 2025).
key_takeaways: 18 named performers including Honeywell, Lockheed Martin, Q-CTRL, AOSense, Anduril, Northrop Grumman, Vector Atomic
Honeywell flew a quantum MagNav test on an Embraer 170 under TQS (press)

title: DAF-MIT AI Accelerator MagNav real-time C-17 demonstration (2023)
summary: In May 2023 the Air Force and MIT flew a real-time MagNav demo on a C-17A during exercise Golden Phoenix, training the compensation network in flight on a laptop. Follows the open MagNav challenge problem and dataset.
key_takeaways: No accuracy figure is public: the linked article and the official releases defer it to a government technical report. The value shown is RF independence
Public dataset and Julia/Python code make this the most reproducible alt-PNT track for a hackathon

title: UK quantum navigation flight trials (Infleqtion, BAE Systems, QinetiQ)
summary: In May 2024 an optical atomic clock and a cold-atom sensor flew on QinetiQ's RJ100 testbed from Boscombe Down, toward a quantum inertial navigation system concept. Linked to the UK National Quantum Strategy mission of quantum navigation on aircraft by 2030.
key_takeaways: Government claim: first publicly acknowledged in-flight tests of this kind
Government funding stated as nearly GBP 8 million

title: UK DASA Early Market Engagement: PNT problem statement for uncrewed systems
summary: Published September 2024. Asks for assured PNT for small UAS: low-cost, low-SWaP CRPA (multi-frequency, SDR-based), SDR/GPU GNSS receivers, AI for spoofing detection and multi-source fusion, as plug-in replacements for COTS GNSS.
key_takeaways: Explicit platform example: under 1.5 m wingspan
Unit cost must suit mass use - cost is a first-class requirement

title: UK national eLoran, Timing Centre and GNSS warning investment (2025)
summary: November 2025 UK announcement of about GBP 155M for a national timing centre, a sovereign eLoran system and GNSS interference warning; a Find a Tender notice targets eLoran IOC by 2028 and FOC by 2030.
key_takeaways: Terrestrial backup and GNSS warning, not only alt-nav on the vehicle

title: ESA NAVISP (Navigation Innovation and Support Programme)
summary: ESA's PNT R&D programme funding industry projects including GNSS-independent PNT; 2025 examples include ALL.SPACE (EUR 950k per the October 2025 ALL.SPACE announcement, signals of opportunity from a multi-orbit terminal, with GMV NSL) and maritime alt-PNT via VDES and R-Mode.
key_takeaways: Permanent open call route for European companies
Shows European emphasis on SoOP and terrestrial backups

title: European Defence Fund 2025 calls
summary: EDF 2025 work programme (EUR 1.065B) closed 16 October 2025 with 410 proposals; results expected April 2026. Indexed as the current EDF cycle; the explicit drone-navigation challenge topic in the index is from EDF 2024.
key_takeaways: No 2025 topic explicitly on GNSS-denied navigation confirmed in this pass
EDF 2024 challenge (multi-sensor drone navigation) is the best-matched prior topic

title: UNITE - Brave NATO: Brave1 and NATO Innovation HQ joint competition (2026)
summary: March 2026 programme pairing Ukrainian and NATO-country companies on joint solutions: first round EUR 10M, up to EUR 1M per project split between partners. Focus areas are counter-UAS and navigation where EW disrupts positioning; NATO-side funding limited to non-lethal categories.
key_takeaways: Ministerial framing: 'robust navigation in GPS-denied environments' as a critical field

title: EUDIS Defence Hackathon, 5th edition (Oct 2026) - GNSS-denied navigation challenge
summary: EU-funded 48-hour hackathon held 15-17 October 2026 at eight sites under the theme 'Autonomy on the Battlefield'. Common challenges were GNSS-denied navigation and swarm coordination, plus one local challenge per host (e.g. counter-UAS in Cyprus).
key_takeaways: Most direct precedent for this hackathon's likely problem statement
Eligibility: EU, Norway, Ukraine citizens aged 18+

title: European Defense Tech Hackathon series (Paris, London, Sheffield, Prague...)
summary: Independent recurring European defense hackathon series. The December 2024 Paris edition had a second-place magnetic navigation entry for underwater drones; 2025 London and Sheffield editions listed GNSS-denied navigation tracks.
key_takeaways: Navigation tracks recur; winners skew toward working demos with real data

title: El Segundo Defense Tech Hackathon (Feb 2024) - origin of Theseus GPS-denied drone
summary: Aviation Week story (March 2024) on three non-defense engineers who built a GPS-denied drone for under USD 500 at a 24-hour defense tech hackathon; the team became Theseus.
key_takeaways: Cheap visual nav prototypes are a known hackathon genre in the US

title: Online Training: Mobile Robotics (Basics + Robotics blocks)
summary: A curated self-study path of short recorded lectures from Bonn's Photogrammetry & Robotics lab, going from linear algebra, rotations and least squares through Bayes filters, EKF localization, particle filters, ICP, RANSAC and graph-based SLAM. Each topic pairs a '5 Minutes with Cyrill' teaser with a full-length lecture.
key_takeaways: Fastest structured on-ramp to probabilistic state estimation
Covers EKF/MCL localization and pose-graph SLAM end to end
Links the older full SLAM course playlist

title: SLAM Course (2013)
summary: Full semester recording of the Freiburg Robot Mapping course: EKF-SLAM, sparse extended information filters, FastSLAM, grid-based mapping, least-squares and graph-based SLAM, and front-end/back-end design. Still one of the most-cited free SLAM courses.
key_takeaways: Classic derivations of EKF-SLAM and FastSLAM
Graph-SLAM via least squares, robust kernels
Slides and Octave exercises on the course page

title: Robot Mapping - WS 2013/14 course page (slides, exercises)
summary: Course page that accompanies the Robot Mapping lecture videos, with lecture slides and programming exercises (EKF-SLAM, UKF, FastSLAM, least-squares calibration, graph-SLAM) in Octave/Matlab.
key_takeaways: Hands-on exercises missing from the video playlist
Good template for a 1-day SLAM crash course

title: Photogrammetry I & II
summary: Recorded two-semester photogrammetry course (2015/16 playlist): camera models, direct linear transform, projective geometry, epipolar geometry, bundle adjustment, and image-based 3D reconstruction. The geometric backbone for visual navigation and map-matching against imagery.
key_takeaways: Camera calibration and orientation from first principles
Bundle adjustment as used in VIO and visual geolocalization
Useful before attempting aerial image-to-map registration

title: Cyrill Stachniss YouTube channel (incl. '5 Minutes with Cyrill')
summary: Channel hosting Stachniss's full lecture courses plus the '5 Minutes with Cyrill' series of short explainers on single concepts (Kalman filter, factor graphs, ICP, RANSAC, SIFT, occupancy grids).
key_takeaways: Short explainers ideal for onboarding teammates during a hackathon
Also hosts newer courses on LiDAR and photogrammetric vision

title: Vision Algorithms for Mobile Robotics (UZH/ETH)
summary: Graduate course building a monocular visual odometry pipeline step by step: image formation, calibration, feature detection, two-view geometry, P3P+RANSAC, bundle adjustment, KLT tracking, place recognition, visual-inertial fusion and event cameras. Slides and Matlab/Python exercises with solutions are public; recordings go to the UZH platform.
key_takeaways: Exercises culminate in a working mini VO pipeline
Covers place recognition and VIO fusion
Python templates available alongside Matlab

title: Visual Odometry: Part I - The First 30 Years and Fundamentals / Part II - Matching, Robustness, Optimization, and Applications
summary: Two-part IEEE Robotics & Automation Magazine tutorial (Part II at rpg.ifi.uzh.ch/docs/VO_Part_II_Scaramuzza.pdf). Explains the VO problem formulation, 2D-2D/3D-2D motion estimation, feature matching, outlier rejection and local optimization in a compact, readable form.
key_takeaways: Best single-read primer on VO design choices
Part II covers RANSAC and windowed bundle adjustment

title: MIT 16.485 Visual Navigation for Autonomous Vehicles (VNAV)
summary: MIT graduate course on the math and software of visual navigation: 3D geometry, Lie groups, quadrotor modelling and control, trajectory optimization, feature tracking, two-view geometry, nonlinear optimization, VIO and SLAM. Lecture slides/notes and ROS 2 based lab handouts are public, with lab code on GitHub.
key_takeaways: Labs walk from ROS basics to a quadrotor VIO stack
Strong on certifiable/robust estimation
Lecture notes downloadable per topic

title: Visual Navigation for Flying Robots (TUM, 2013)
summary: Award-winning TUM lecture on making quadrotors navigate with cameras: 3D geometry, sensors, state estimation, visual motion estimation, SLAM, dense reconstruction, planning and exploration. Each lecture has slides and a recorded video.
key_takeaways: Compact quadrotor-centric syllabus
Bridges control, estimation and visual SLAM

title: Autonomous Navigation for Flying Robots (TUM edX, AUTONAVx)
summary: MOOC version of the TUM flying-robots lecture with lecture videos and browser-based Python exercises on quadrotor state estimation, Kalman filtering, control and visual navigation.
key_takeaways: Lighter-weight than the full lecture
Python exercise format is easy to adapt

title: Kalman and Bayesian Filters in Python
summary: Free interactive book as Jupyter notebooks: g-h filters, discrete Bayes, univariate and multivariate Kalman filters, EKF, UKF, particle filters and smoothers, all with runnable code built on the companion FilterPy library.
key_takeaways: Intuition-first, code-first; ideal for teammates new to filtering
Notebooks run in Binder or locally
FilterPy gives drop-in KF/EKF/UKF classes for prototypes

title: Kalman Filter Explained Through Examples
summary: Free web tutorial deriving the Kalman filter through worked numerical examples (alpha-beta filter, 1D and multidimensional KF, EKF, UKF), written for engineers who want the equations without heavy theory.
key_takeaways: Numeric step-by-step examples you can check by hand
Good companion to Labbe for tracking problems

title: SLAM Handbook: From Localization and Mapping to Spatial Intelligence
summary: Community-written handbook released in three parts (Part 1 November 2024, Part 2 March 2025, Part 3 May 2025), to be published by Cambridge University Press; the free PDF (main.pdf) and LaTeX sources are in the GitHub release repo. Covers factor graphs, Lie groups, robust estimation, certifiable methods, visual/LiDAR/radar/event-based SLAM, and learned spatial representations.
key_takeaways: Most current one-stop reference on SLAM (2025)
Chapters on non-visual sensors such as radar
Free PDF; GitHub repo tracks newest release
Single up-to-date reference spanning classic estimation and learned methods
Free chapter PDFs on GitHub

title: SLAM toolbox for Matlab (EKF-SLAM teaching code)
summary: Solà's Matlab EKF-SLAM toolbox, used as teaching material for his SLAM courses: modular robots, sensors, landmark parameterizations (including inverse-depth points and lines) and graph-SLAM variants. Old but clear code for learning.
key_takeaways: Readable reference implementation of EKF-SLAM
Shows landmark parameterization trade-offs

title: 14 Lectures on Visual SLAM: From Theory to Practice
summary: English translation of the popular Chinese visual SLAM textbook, from rigid-body motion and Lie algebra through camera models, nonlinear optimization, feature/direct VO, backend optimization, loop closure and dense mapping, each with C++ examples.
key_takeaways: Code-heavy: every chapter compiles
Good bridge from theory to ORB-SLAM-style systems

title: State Estimation and Localization for Self-Driving Cars (Coursera)
summary: Course 2 of the UofT Self-Driving Cars specialization: least squares, KF/EKF/ES-EKF/UKF, IMU and GNSS sensor models, LiDAR scan matching with ICP, culminating in an error-state EKF that fuses IMU, GNSS and LiDAR on CARLA data.
key_takeaways: Final project is a ready template for GNSS/IMU/LiDAR fusion
Explicit error-state EKF derivation
Free to audit

title: Self-Driving Cars Specialization (University of Toronto)
summary: Four-course specialization covering vehicle dynamics and control, state estimation and localization, visual perception, and motion planning, using the CARLA simulator for assignments.
key_takeaways: End-to-end autonomy pipeline in one program
CARLA-based assignments transfer to hackathon sims

title: GPS: An Introduction to Satellite Navigation, with an interactive Worldwide Laboratory using Smartphones
summary: Stanford MOOC (originally on Coursera) now freely available as a long video series: how GPS works, pseudoranges, orbits and signals, receiver design, assisted GPS and the future of GNSS, with smartphone-based labs.
key_takeaways: Best intro to pseudoranges and receiver basics
Smartphone labs pair with Android raw GNSS measurements

title: Sensor Fusion and Non-linear Filtering for Automotive Systems (edX)
summary: Self-paced edX course on Bayesian filtering: state-space and motion/measurement models, Kalman filter, EKF/UKF/CKF, and particle filters, with Matlab assignments building a personal filtering toolbox.
key_takeaways: Rigorous but practical nonlinear filtering
Pairs with Chalmers' multi-object tracking course

title: Multi-Object Tracking for Automotive Systems (edX)
summary: edX course on single- and multi-object tracking: data association, GNN/JPDA/MHT, random finite sets and PMBM filters, with Matlab assignments. Relevant for situational awareness and C-UAS track management.
key_takeaways: Modern RFS/PMBM trackers explained
Direct use for radar/EO track fusion

title: Artificial Intelligence for Robotics (Udacity CS373)
summary: Free classic course by Sebastian Thrun programming robot localization (histogram filter, Kalman filter, particle filter), search/planning, PID control and GraphSLAM in Python. The original Udacity course page now redirects to Udacity's paid AI catalogue; the link points to a 2023 archive copy.
key_takeaways: Gentle, code-along intro to localization filters
Particle-filter lesson is a 1-hour hackathon primer

title: Understanding Sensor Fusion and Tracking (MATLAB Tech Talks)
summary: Short video series on sensor fusion for autonomous systems: what sensor fusion is, IMU/magnetometer orientation estimation, fusing GPS and IMU for pose with an asynchronous EKF, single- and multi-object tracking, and track-level fusion.
key_takeaways: Clear 10-15 minute visual explanations
GPS+IMU episode maps directly to a nav-filter build

title: Stanford PNT Symposium 2025 (19th annual)
authors: Stanford Center for Position, Navigation and Time
summary: Annual Stanford SCPNT symposium page (8-9 October 2025) with the agenda and links to recorded student talks (Day 1) and invited speaker talks (Day 2), plus downloadable slides for many presentations.
key_takeaways: Current state of GNSS integrity, resilience and alt-PNT from leading labs
Student talks are a good source of fresh project ideas

title: 2025 PNT Symposium - Day 2 Invited Speaker Presentation Videos
summary: Video album of invited speaker talks from the 2025 Stanford PNT Symposium, featuring speakers such as Brad Parkinson and Jade Morton.
key_takeaways: Primary-source talks on the direction of GPS and resilient PNT

title: Stanford PNT Symposium 2024 (18th annual)
summary: Page for the 28-29 October 2024 symposium with agenda, student and invited-speaker video albums, and slides; topics span GNSS, inertial sensing, timing and alternative navigation.
key_takeaways: Year-over-year view of resilient PNT research
Slides downloadable for many talks

title: SCPNT Photo and Video Gallery (PNT Symposium recordings archive)
summary: Archive index of Stanford PNT Symposium recordings going back to 2007, organised by year into student and invited-speaker albums.
key_takeaways: Deep back-catalogue of GNSS and PNT talks

title: ION GNSS+ Tutorials
summary: Pre-conference tutorial programme of ION GNSS+, the main annual GNSS technical meeting: full-day course series taught by field experts (2026: Survey of GNSS Systems, Advanced Algorithms for Navigation, Space and Spacecraft Navigation), with a one-time on-demand recording for registered students.
key_takeaways: Expert-taught deep dives; topics change yearly
Paid add-on to conference registration

title: ION GNSS+ Short Courses - Taught by ION Masters
summary: Masters short course programme at ION GNSS+, complimentary for paid conference attendees: 50-minute lectures by ION Master Instructors. The 2026 line-up includes Space Applications of GNSS (Penny Axelrad), GNSS Modernization (Christopher Hegarty), LEO PNT with mega-constellations (Zak Kassas), quantum navigation (Allison Kealy, Andrew Greentree) and the first public GPS spoofer (Todd Humphreys).
key_takeaways: Short expert lectures on GNSS, LEO PNT, spoofing and quantum navigation for ION GNSS+ attendees

title: ION Online Tutorial: The Basics of Satellite Navigation
summary: ION recorded online tutorial by Per Enge in four parts: Fundamentals of Satellite Navigation (45 min, viewable after ION sign-in), plus Applications, Mathematics, and Performance & Future of Satellite Navigation ($50 members / $100 non-members each). The tutorial page now redirects to the ION publications store, which sells the three paid parts.
key_takeaways: Short, authoritative intro by Per Enge; only the Fundamentals part is free (sign-in)

title: ION Webinar Series (archive and YouTube recordings)
summary: Running ION webinar programme with summary pages per talk and a YouTube playlist of past recordings (youtube.com/playlist?list=PLPiP0PPIY2x4k1OemLZH8_OJPyLjGLYFY). Topics include GNSS spoofing and jamming, LEO PNT, signals of opportunity, quantum sensors and GNSS-denied robotics.
key_takeaways: Hour-long talks from active researchers, free
Strong coverage of spoofing detection and LEO PNT

title: First results from three years of GNSS interference monitoring from low Earth orbit
summary: UT Radionavigation Lab results from detecting and geolocating terrestrial GNSS jammers using receivers on LEO satellites, revealing persistent interference hotspots in conflict regions.
key_takeaways: Space-based RFI monitoring is practical
Maps of jamming hotspots tied to conflict zones

title: Unveiling Starlink for PNT
summary: Presents work on exploiting Starlink downlink signals for opportunistic positioning, including signal structure discovery and Doppler/pseudorange-based navigation results.
key_takeaways: Starlink can serve as an alt-PNT source without operator cooperation

title: Navigation using carrier Doppler shift from a LEO constellation: TRANSIT on steroids
summary: Analysis of Doppler-only positioning from large LEO constellations, revisiting the TRANSIT concept with modern megaconstellations and quantifying achievable accuracy.
key_takeaways: Doppler positioning theory for LEO PNT

title: Implementation and Accuracy of Doppler Navigation with LEO Satellites
summary: Talk on navigation with carrier Doppler-shift measurements from LEO satellite signals of opportunity: analytically derived Jacobian formulas for the navigation solution and a GNSS-like dilution-of-precision metric to assess accuracy, with preliminary numerical results. The paper is free in NAVIGATION (ION journal).
key_takeaways: DOP-style accuracy metric for LEO Doppler nav

title: Detecting GNSS Jamming and Spoofing on Android Devices
summary: Shows how Android raw GNSS measurements (AGC, C/N0, pseudoranges) can flag jamming and spoofing on commodity phones.
key_takeaways: Phones can be cheap distributed interference sensors

title: Results on GNSS Spoofing Mitigation Using Multiple Receivers
summary: Spoofing detection and mitigation using several spatially separated receivers, exploiting the fact that a single spoofer produces geometrically inconsistent measurements.
key_takeaways: Multi-antenna/multi-receiver consistency checks

title: GNSS Spoofing Detection through Spatial Processing
summary: Stanford work on detecting spoofing from spatial signal characteristics (angle-of-arrival consistency) using antenna motion or arrays.
key_takeaways: Direction-of-arrival is a strong spoofing discriminator

title: Robust Interference Mitigation in GNSS Snapshot Receivers
summary: Interference mitigation techniques adapted to snapshot (short-capture) GNSS receivers used in low-power and IoT devices.
key_takeaways: Snapshot receivers need different mitigation than tracking receivers

title: A Robust Approach to Vision-Based Terrain-Aided Localization
summary: Vision-based terrain-aided localization for aircraft, matching onboard imagery against terrain/map references as a GNSS-independent position source.
key_takeaways: Map-matching as a GNSS-denied position fix

title: Cooperative Localization for GNSS-Denied Subterranean Navigation: A UAV-UGV Team Approach
summary: West Virginia University work on UAV and UGV teams sharing ranging and odometry to localize jointly in GNSS-denied underground environments.
key_takeaways: Cooperative ranging reduces drift in heterogeneous teams

title: Relative navigation of fixed-wing aircraft in GPS-denied environments
summary: AFRL perspective on relative navigation for fixed-wing aircraft without GPS, keeping estimation consistent by working in a relative frame with periodic global updates.
key_takeaways: Relative navigation frames tame unobservable global drift

title: Quantum Sensors for Navigation - From Physics to Field Deployment
summary: Overview of quantum sensing for navigation (atom interferometers, quantum magnetometers, clocks) and what it takes to move them from lab to field.
key_takeaways: Realistic timeline for quantum inertial and magnetic nav

title: Should It Be TPN? Prioritizing Timing in Positioning and Navigation
summary: Webinar arguing for timing as the foundation of resilient PNT, covering precision terrestrial time distribution and timing/positioning from current and future LEO constellations.
key_takeaways: Timing resilience underpins telecom and power grid
LEO as a timing source

title: LTE Receiver Design and Multipath Analysis for Navigation in Urban Environments
summary: Design of a software receiver that extracts navigation observables from cellular LTE signals and analysis of multipath effects in urban settings.
key_takeaways: Cellular signals of opportunity are viable in cities

title: Resilience Monitoring for Multi-Filter All-Source Navigation Framework With Assurance
summary: AFIT research on all-source navigation that runs multiple filters and monitors sensor integrity to detect and isolate faulty or spoofed inputs.
key_takeaways: Plug-and-play all-source nav with integrity monitoring

title: When GNSS fails, what will you do? MarRINav!
summary: UK maritime resilient navigation study (MarRINav) on backups for GNSS at sea, including eLoran and R-Mode style terrestrial systems; co-sponsored by the RNT Foundation.
key_takeaways: Maritime PNT backup architecture options

title: How to fool a GPS (TEDxAustin)
summary: Accessible TEDx talk from the head of UT Austin's Radionavigation Lab on GPS jamming and spoofing and why civil GPS is trivially counterfeitable, given around the time of his lab's drone and yacht spoofing demonstrations.
key_takeaways: Why unauthenticated civil GNSS is a systemic risk
Good opener for a resilient-PNT pitch

title: UT Austin Radionavigation Laboratory (talks, papers, news)
summary: Lab site of Todd Humphreys' group, indexing talks, briefings and papers on GNSS spoofing detection, LEO interference monitoring, Starlink-based PNT and precise automotive positioning.
key_takeaways: Hub for Humphreys' talks on spoofing and LEO PNT
Papers on spoofing detection are linked from here

title: Ad Astra: Navigation with Megaconstellation LEO Satellites (GRASP on Robotics)
summary: UPenn GRASP seminar by Zak Kassas on opportunistic PNT from Starlink, OneWeb and other LEO megaconstellations, addressing unknown signal structure, poor ephemerides and clock instability with his STAN (simultaneous tracking and navigation) framework validated on ground and aerial vehicles.
key_takeaways: LEO signals of opportunity as a GNSS backup
Covers SDR receiver design to navigation filter

title: Low-cost GPS simulator: GPS spoofing by SDR (DEF CON 23)
summary: DEF CON 23 talk showing that open-source tools and cheap SDRs can generate counterfeit GPS L1 signals that fool phones and a consumer drone; the speakers end with defensive advice such as multi-constellation positioning and spoofing detection in chipsets.
key_takeaways: Shows how low the barrier to civil GPS spoofing is
Motivates detection and multi-source fusion in any drone build

title: Who cares about the Baltic Jammer? Terrestrial Navigation in the Baltic Sea Region (39C3)
summary: 39th Chaos Communication Congress talk from DLR researchers on R-Mode, a terrestrial maritime navigation backup built on existing radio beacons and coastal infrastructure, tested in the heavily jammed Baltic. Covers real-world jamming impacts, transmitter/receiver build-out and the path from research to critical infrastructure.
key_takeaways: Concrete view of Baltic jamming/spoofing effects on ships, aircraft, timing
Terrestrial backups as an alternative to space-based ones

title: Detect GNSS jamming and spoofing (Android developer guide)
summary: Android developer documentation on the platform APIs and signals that apps can use to detect GNSS jamming and spoofing on phones.
key_takeaways: Phone-based interference sensing for a hackathon prototype
No custom hardware needed

title: Results Jammertest 2025 - Resilient GNSS in an Era of Rising Jamming & Spoofing (webinar)
summary: On-demand vendor webinar reviewing receiver behaviour during the high-power interference trials of Jammertest 2025 in Norway, with speakers from Septentrio, the GPS Innovation Alliance and drone maker UVify.
key_takeaways: Field results under interference levels like Baltic/Eastern Europe
Vendor view; treat claims accordingly

title: The Future of Secure Positioning and Timing: Insights from Jammertest 2025
summary: u-blox webinar (25 November 2025) on Jammertest 2025 results: what multi-band receiver testing revealed about positioning continuity under interference, meaconing defence and hybrid spoofing detection with authentication. The page offers the slide deck for download rather than a recording.
key_takeaways: Multi-band receivers and spoofing detection in mass-market chips

title: Podcast: the vulnerable state of global navigation satellite systems (PolicyTracker Spectrum Podcast)
summary: Spectrum-policy podcast episode with PNT consultant Logan Scott on GNSS jamming, spoofing, adjacent-band interference and mitigations, and the global rise in spoofing incidents affecting aviation.
key_takeaways: Policy and spectrum angle on GNSS interference

title: What Happens When GPS Goes Dark? (From the Crows' Nest)
summary: Episode of the Association of Old Crows electronic warfare podcast in which RNT Foundation president Dana Goward discusses threats to GPS and the case for terrestrial and other backups.
key_takeaways: EW-community framing of PNT resilience

title: Dana A. Goward on Geospatial FM podcast (RNT Foundation)
summary: RNT Foundation post linking Dana Goward's Geospatial FM podcast appearance on GPS vulnerability and national PNT resilience policy.
key_takeaways: Advocacy perspective on eLoran and PNT backups

title: EUDIS Defence Hackathon, 3rd edition (with BraveTech EU)
summary: EU defence hackathon (17-19 October 2025, eight locations) with challenges on protecting space assets, space for defence (including navigation and coordination) and sovereign aerospace including drone countermeasures; a recorded pre-hackathon webinar is on YouTube (watch?v=gLrCkk6XEuY).
key_takeaways: Shows how EU frames navigation and C-UAS challenge statements
Pre-hackathon webinar recording available

title: Ukraine's DefTech at the End of 2025: From Drone Mass to Systems Warfare
summary: Analysis of Ukraine's defence-tech ecosystem at the end of 2025, noting that GNSS-denied operation is now the norm and expecting broad adoption of radio-beacon, visual and fused alternative navigation in 2026.
key_takeaways: GNSS denial is a baseline requirement in current conflict
Context for prioritising alt-nav in hackathon scope

title: Navigating Using GPS Localization (Nav2 tutorial)
summary: Nav2 tutorial on outdoor navigation with GPS: fusing GNSS, IMU and odometry with robot_localization's navsat_transform, configuring Nav2 for GPS waypoints, and demonstrating it in Gazebo.
key_takeaways: Shortest working path to GPS waypoint following on a ROS 2 robot
Shows datum and frame setup that trips people up

title: ROSCon UK 2025 - State Estimation for Mobile Robotics Workshop

title: From Sea to Space: Advancing Perception in Harsh Domains (ICRA 2026 workshop)

Speaker list points to active groups

title: Nav2 ROSCon Talks (index)

Built on AirSim

summary: Large synthetic dataset rendered in AirSim/Unreal environments with challenging lighting, weather and motion, with perfect ground truth for many modalities.

GNSS-denied underground

summary: Urban driving in dense city areas with lidar, stereo and navigation sensors where GNSS is degraded.

summary: Driving data from Hong Kong and California urban canyons with a full sensor suite, targeted at GNSS outliers and degraded localization.

Focus: dense urban GNSS failure
Licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, non-commercial academic use

summary: Segway robot sessions over many months on one campus with lidar, omnidirectional camera, GPS, IMU and odometry.
key_takeaways: Sensors: Velodyne HDL-32E, Ladybug3, GPS/RTK, IMU
Long-term change over seasons

summary: Multi-campus sequences in Asia and Europe across seasons with two lidar types, stereo, IMUs, UWB and survey-grade prior maps.
key_takeaways: Sensors: lidar, stereo, IMU, UWB
Ground truth: continuous-time with prior maps
Licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, non-commercial academic use

summary: Hardware-synchronized event stereo, regular stereo, RGB-D, lidar and IMU across different motion and lighting, with 6-DoF ground truth.
key_takeaways: Sensors: event stereo, stereo, RGB-D, lidar, IMU

title: DSEC: A Stereo Event Camera Dataset for Driving Scenarios
summary: Stereo event and frame cameras plus lidar and RTK GNSS on a car, including night and challenging illumination.
key_takeaways: Sensors: stereo event, stereo RGB, lidar, RTK GNSS
Good for low-light perception

title: The Multi Vehicle Stereo Event Camera Dataset (MVSEC)
summary: Stereo event cameras with IMU, lidar and ground truth on several platforms including a hexacopter and a car.
key_takeaways: Sensors: stereo event, IMU, lidar, GPS
Platforms: drone, car, motorcycle, handheld

title: MARS-LVIG Dataset: A multi-sensor aerial robots SLAM dataset for LiDAR-visual-inertial-GNSS fusion
summary: Aerial robot SLAM dataset for lidar-visual-inertial-GNSS fusion, including sequences with raw GNSS measurements under different lighting.
key_takeaways: Sensors: lidar, camera, IMU, GNSS (incl. raw)
Domain: aerial over large outdoor areas
Licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, academic use only

title: SITL Simulator (Software in the Loop)
summary: Developer docs for running ArduPilot vehicles in SITL, connecting GCS and external simulators.
key_takeaways: sim_vehicle.py workflow
Lists supported external simulators

title: HoloOcean Documentation
summary: Install guide, sensor reference (sonar, DVL, IMU, depth) and examples for the HoloOcean underwater simulator.
key_takeaways: Covers sonar and DVL sensor configs
Multi-agent and acoustic comms examples

title: AirSim Documentation
summary: Docs for AirSim covering setup, APIs, sensor configuration and PX4/ArduPilot integration.
key_takeaways: Sensor settings via settings.json
Notes on the project's end of active development

title: Past, Present, and Future of Simultaneous Localization And Mapping: Towards the Robust-Perception Age
summary: Landmark survey that frames modern SLAM as factor-graph MAP estimation and discusses robustness, scalability, representations and open problems.
key_takeaways: Standard framing of front end vs back end
Robustness to outliers and long-term operation remain the hard problems

title: Visual-Inertial Navigation: A Concise Review
summary: Compact review of visual-inertial navigation: filtering vs optimization, observability, calibration and representative systems.
key_takeaways: Explains why MSCKF-style filters and sliding-window optimizers coexist
Observability and consistency drive estimator design

title: ORB-SLAM3: An Accurate Open-Source Library for Visual, Visual-Inertial and Multi-Map SLAM
summary: Describes ORB-SLAM3's tightly integrated visual-inertial SLAM, MAP-based IMU initialization and the multi-map Atlas that recovers from tracking loss.
key_takeaways: Multi-map atlas lets the system restart and later merge maps
Supports pinhole and fisheye models

title: VINS-Mono: A Robust and Versatile Monocular Visual-Inertial State Estimator
summary: Presents the VINS-Mono estimator: IMU preintegration, robust initialization, tightly coupled sliding-window optimization, relocalization and global pose graph.
key_takeaways: Monocular camera + IMU recovers metric scale
Initialization is a key practical component

title: FAST-LIO2: Fast Direct LiDAR-inertial Odometry
summary: Introduces direct registration of raw LiDAR points in an iterated Kalman filter with an incremental k-d tree map, avoiding hand-crafted feature extraction.
key_takeaways: Raw-point registration generalizes across LiDAR types
ikd-Tree enables efficient incremental mapping

title: LIO-SAM: Tightly-coupled Lidar Inertial Odometry via Smoothing and Mapping
summary: Formulates LiDAR-inertial odometry as factor-graph smoothing with IMU preintegration, LiDAR odometry, GPS and loop-closure factors.
key_takeaways: Factor graphs make it straightforward to add or drop GNSS
Keyframe-local scan matching keeps it real time

title: KISS-ICP: In Defense of Point-to-Point ICP -- Simple, Accurate, and Robust Registration If Done the Right Way
summary: Argues that a carefully engineered point-to-point ICP with motion compensation and adaptive thresholds matches far more complex LiDAR odometry across platforms.
key_takeaways: Few parameters, works across sensors and platforms
Strong baseline before reaching for complex pipelines

title: FAST-LIVO2: Fast, Direct LiDAR-Inertial-Visual Odometry
summary: Presents an error-state iterated Kalman filter that sequentially fuses LiDAR and image measurements against a shared voxel map, with exposure and plane-prior handling.
key_takeaways: Sequential updates handle LiDAR/camera dimension mismatch
Robust when one modality degrades

title: DROID-SLAM: Deep Visual SLAM for Monocular, Stereo, and RGB-D Cameras
summary: Learned SLAM that iteratively refines poses and depth through a differentiable dense bundle adjustment layer.
key_takeaways: Big robustness gains on hard sequences
GPU-heavy

title: MASt3R-SLAM: Real-Time Dense SLAM with 3D Reconstruction Priors
summary: Builds a real-time dense monocular SLAM system on the MASt3R two-view reconstruction prior, without assuming a fixed parametric camera model.
key_takeaways: 3D foundation models can serve as SLAM front ends
Works with uncalibrated video

title: Kimera: an Open-Source Library for Real-Time Metric-Semantic Localization and Mapping
summary: Describes the Kimera stack: VIO, robust pose-graph optimization, mesh reconstruction and semantic mapping in one open library.
key_takeaways: Metric-semantic maps on CPU in real time
Modular: VIO, RPGO, mesher, semantics

title: Kimera-Multi: Robust, Distributed, Dense Metric-Semantic SLAM for Multi-Robot Systems
summary: Distributed multi-robot SLAM where robots exchange compact information peer to peer and jointly optimize with outlier-robust distributed pose-graph optimization.
key_takeaways: Peer-to-peer, no central server
Robust to bad inter-robot loop closures

title: Event-based Vision: A Survey
summary: Comprehensive survey of event cameras: sensing principle, algorithms (feature tracking, optical flow, VO/SLAM) and applications.
key_takeaways: Microsecond latency and high dynamic range
Algorithms must be redesigned for asynchronous data

title: How NeRFs and 3D Gaussian Splatting are Reshaping SLAM: a Survey
summary: Survey of SLAM methods that use neural radiance fields or 3D Gaussian splatting as the map representation, organized by sensor and technique.
key_takeaways: Radiance-field maps trade compute for photorealism
Most methods are GPU-bound and not yet embedded-ready

title: Gaussian Splatting SLAM
summary: Monocular and RGB-D SLAM that tracks and maps directly against 3D Gaussians using analytic Jacobians for camera pose optimization.
key_takeaways: Single representation for tracking, mapping and rendering

title: LiDAR Odometry Survey: Recent Advancements and Remaining Challenges
summary: Survey of LiDAR-only, LiDAR-inertial and multi-sensor LiDAR odometry, with discussion of datasets, evaluation and open challenges such as degeneracy.
key_takeaways: Taxonomy of LiDAR, LiDAR-inertial and LiDAR-plus-other fusion
Geometric degeneracy (tunnels, open fields) is a key open issue

title: 4D Millimeter-Wave Radar in Autonomous Driving: A Survey
summary: Survey of 4D imaging radar: signal processing, datasets, calibration, perception and SLAM/odometry uses.
key_takeaways: 4D radar adds elevation and works in adverse weather
Sparse, noisy point clouds need radar-specific methods

title: CFEAR Radarodometry - Conservative Filtering for Efficient and Accurate Radar Odometry
summary: Learning-free spinning-radar odometry that keeps the strongest returns per azimuth, builds oriented surface points and registers against a keyframe history (IROS 2021).
key_takeaways: Simple filtering beats heavier radar pipelines
Runs fast on a single CPU thread per the authors

title: Edge-based Monocular Thermal-Inertial Odometry in Visually Degraded Environments
summary: Thermal-inertial odometry that tracks thermal image edges instead of corner features, targeting darkness and smoke where visible cameras fail.
key_takeaways: Thermal edges are more stable than corners in low-contrast IR
Relevant for night and obscurant operations

title: ITU-T G.8275.1: Precision time protocol telecom profile for phase/time synchronization with full timing support from the network
summary: The telecom PTP profile for networks where every node is a boundary or transparent clock (full on-path support), using Ethernet transport. Current in-force edition per the ITU page is 02/2026 with Amendment 1 (08/2026); the first edition was 2014.
key_takeaways: The profile a 5G fronthaul / TDD backhaul uses to deliver phase from a PRTC
Assumes every hop timestamps; pairs with G.8273.2 clock limits and the G.8271.1 network budget
linuxptp ships configs/G.8275.1.cfg

title: ITU-T G.8275.2: Precision time protocol telecom profile for phase/time synchronization with partial timing support from the network
summary: Telecom PTP profile for networks where some nodes do not support PTP (partial timing support), carried over IPv4/IPv6 unicast. Intended for assisted partial timing support, e.g. a local GNSS receiver with PTP as backup during GNSS outage. In-force edition 02/2026 plus Amendment 1 (08/2026) per the ITU page.
key_takeaways: Unicast PTP over IP through non-PTP-aware routers: asymmetry and packet delay variation are not removed hop by hop
The APTS case (GNSS primary, PTP as holdover aid) is the closest standard to a GNSS-denied timing fallback
linuxptp ships configs/G.8275.2.cfg

title: ITU-T G.8273.2: Timing characteristics of telecom boundary clocks and telecom time synchronous clocks for use with full timing support from the network
summary: Performance limits for telecom boundary clocks (T-BC) and telecom time slave clocks (T-TSC): constant and dynamic time error, noise generation, tolerance and transfer, by clock class. In-force edition 06/2023 with amendments 08/2024 and 11/2025 per the ITU page.
key_takeaways: Defines the clock classes (A/B/C/D) whose per-hop time error sums into the G.8271.1 budget
Gives the vocabulary for reporting a PTP chain: cTE, dTE, max|TE|
Use it to set honest per-hop error assumptions in a simulation

title: 3GPP TS 38.133 (ETSI TS 138 133): NR; Requirements for support of radio resource management - clause 7.4 Cell phase synchronization accuracy
summary: Clause 7.4 defines cell phase synchronization accuracy for TDD as the maximum absolute deviation in frame start timing between any pair of same-frequency cells with overlapping coverage, and requires it to be better than 3 us at the BS antenna connectors (read in V15.2.0, 2018-07). Commonly translated into roughly +-1.5 us per cell against a common reference. The ETSI server lists releases up to V19.6.0; only V15.2.0 was read here.
key_takeaways: 5G TDD needs cells within 3 us of each other => roughly +-1.5 us to UTC per cell
GNSS loss at a TDD site becomes a holdover problem measured against this number
Linked PDF is the 2018 Release 15 edition; check the current release before quoting clause numbers

title: RFC 10049: Roughtime: A Protocol for Rough Time Synchronization
summary: The published RFC version of Roughtime: signed, rough (seconds-level) time from several servers, with a chained-nonce scheme so a client can prove a server lied. The hub already indexes the IETF draft; this is the final RFC that current implementations (roughenough, pyroughtime) cite.
key_takeaways: Authenticated time to bootstrap certificate checks or detect a grossly wrong clock, not to discipline an oscillator
Querying several servers gives cryptographic evidence of misbehaviour

title: PTPsec: Securing the Precision Time Protocol Against Time Delay Attacks Using Cyclic Path Asymmetry Analysis
summary: Detects PTP time delay attacks by measuring round-trip times over redundant network paths and comparing their asymmetry, with a new measurement message on top of IEEE 1588-2019. Evaluated on a hardware testbed; code at tum-esi/ptpsec. Detection relies on at least one redundant path staying symmetric.
key_takeaways: A delay attack is a path asymmetry change - encryption and authentication alone do not stop it
Cyclic path measurements catch static and incremental delay attacks if one path is clean
Same idea as the cross-node consistency check in sample:timing-network-holdover

title: Securing the Precision Time Protocol with SDN-enabled Cyclic Path Asymmetry Analysis
summary: Follow-up to PTPsec that uses software-defined networking to find redundant paths dynamically in arbitrary topologies and then runs the cyclic path asymmetry check against delay attacks. Open-access PDF on Zenodo (CC BY 4.0).
key_takeaways: Removes PTPsec's need for hand-configured redundant paths
Useful reference for a delay-attack detection demo on a small switched testbed

title: Enhanced Loran (eLoran) Definition Document
summary: High-level definition of eLoran for policy makers, service providers and users: what distinguishes it from Loran-C (UTC-synchronised transmitters, a data channel, differential corrections) and the positioning and timing services it is meant to provide. The linked copy is version 0.1 issued for consultation in January 2007.
key_takeaways: eLoran transmissions are tied to UTC, which is what makes it a GNSS-independent timing source
Draft for consultation - check later ILA material before quoting requirement numbers

title: Chronos Technology Tests eLoran Timing Provision in the UK
summary: Report on the ESA-funded UTC Time Distribution (UTD) project led by Chronos Technology: caesium clocks replaced at the Anthorn eLoran transmitter, and prototype receivers producing UTC-aligned 1PPS from eLoran alone in timing mode. Accuracy is described by the company as comparable to good GNSS timing receivers; no measurement report is linked.
key_takeaways: Current UK evidence that eLoran is being used as a timing (not positioning) backup
Press account - treat the accuracy statement as a vendor claim

title: Data for "PTP over wide area networks with offset measurement outlier filtering"
summary: University of Granada measurements of ptp4l and chrony time transfer over about 200 km of research network between ROA (Spanish UTC lab) and Granada, plus Calnex Paragon-X network emulation runs and free-running NIC stability against a passive hydrogen maser. CSVs give ptp4l offset_raw, offset_sw, delay, frequency adjustment and a hardware 1PPS time error from a frequency counter, and GNSS common-view one-way delays. Zenodo marks the files as restricted (access on request), CC BY 4.0.
key_takeaways: The only dataset found with both ptp4l's own offset estimate and an independent 1PPS truth - exactly what a replay needs
One-way delays each direction give the real path asymmetry, not an assumed one
Files are restricted on Zenodo: request access early, it is not a same-day download

title: Clock Synchronization Accuracy over Mobile Networks
summary: PTPv2 (PTPd) time synchronization between two hosts across mobile networks including a private 5G SA network, with the slave's PTPd 'offset from master' log values and an independent PPS-vs-PPS offset measured with an Analog Discovery 2 between the two NICs. Setup schematics included. Single zip, about 60 MB, open, CC BY 4.0. One folder is described in 'Clock Synchronization and Network Delay Evaluation over a Private 5G Standalone Network' (Kalnins, Rusins, Elsts).
key_takeaways: Real asymmetric, high-jitter packet path - a stress case for a PTP servo or for path-asymmetry detection
PPS truth lets you compare what PTP thinks against what the clocks actually did
PTPd, not ptp4l; the README warns the logged offset is the servo's view, not true offset

title: IEC61850 SV and PTP traffic under GNSS time synchronization attacks
summary: Pseudonymised pcap captures of IEC 61850 Sampled Values and IEEE 1588 PTP traffic from the KIT KASTEL energy security lab while the substation's GNSS-fed time server is spoofed. About 592 GB tar on KIT RADAR, CC BY-NC 4.0. Companion of the jamming dataset; related publication 'Compromising Synchrophasor Data by Attacking Time Synchronization: A Hardware-Lab Study' (2026). The landing page does not list devices or derived offset series.
key_takeaways: Real PTP grandmaster behaviour while its GNSS input is attacked - announce/clockClass changes and timestamps are in the pcaps
Very large: plan a partial download and a pcap-to-offset extraction step
Non-commercial licence

title: IEC61850 SV and PTP traffic under GNSS jamming
summary: Jamming half of the KIT KASTEL captures: IEC 61850 Sampled Values and PTP traffic while the substation time server's GNSS is jammed, about 594 GB pcap tar on KIT RADAR, CC BY-NC 4.0, identifiers pseudonymised.
key_takeaways: Shows how a real grandmaster announces loss of GNSS and enters holdover on the wire
Pair with the spoofing half to contrast detectable loss vs silent drift

title: MIKES NorduNET NTS White Rabbit link data (UTC(MIKE) - WR(RISE))
summary: Public HDF5 files from the White Rabbit link between RISE (Stockholm) and MIKES (Espoo): time-interval counter readings of UTC(MIKE) against the WR-delivered RISE time every 10 minutes (valid from about 2026-05-23), plus WR switch telemetry (round-trip time in ps for boundary clocks at SUNET, CSC and MIKES) via SNMP. Updated about daily per the readme; an example plotting script sits in the same folder.
key_takeaways: A real long-haul WR time-transfer series against a national UTC realisation - good for Allan deviation and drift plots
RTT telemetry lets you look for path changes
Live folder, no DOI or licence stated - cite the URL and date of download

title: BIPM Circular T
summary: Monthly BIPM publication of UTC - UTC(k) for the national timing labs contributing to UTC, with uncertainties, plus related TAI data on the BIPM FTP server. The canonical public record of how well real national clock ensembles track UTC.
key_takeaways: Real clock-ensemble offsets to feed allantools or to sanity-check the scale of ensemble numbers
5-day sampling, published monthly: long-term behaviour only, not holdover over minutes

title: Time Guidance for Network Operators, Chief Information Officers, and Chief Information Security Officers
summary: CISA guidance on making enterprise time resilient and secure: know where time comes from, use several independent sources, detect anomalies in timing sources, and test. The 2022 update added network considerations from a tabletop pilot plus self-assessment questions and a test plan.
key_takeaways: Inventory every time dependency and its upstream source
Use multiple, diverse time sources and compare them
Detect and handle anomalies in time sources; test the response

title: Technical-Level Resilient Timing Overview (CISA fact sheet)
summary: Short fact sheet that frames time as an invisible utility, lists sectors that depend on it, and summarizes technical measures for resilient timing.
key_takeaways: Many organizations do not know where their time comes from
Short entry point before the longer CISA time guidance

title: Best Practices for Improved Robustness of Time and Frequency Sources in Fixed Locations
summary: Best-practice guide for people who install and maintain time and frequency sources at fixed infrastructure sites, where GPS receivers are the usual source of time and time interval.
key_takeaways: Written for fixed sites that take time from GPS receivers
Covers installation and operating practice rather than protocol design

title: Best Practices for Resilient Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (PNT) Supporting Critical Infrastructure
summary: DHS S&T guide released in February 2025 under EO 13905 to help providers, owners and operators use PNT responsibly. It gives general best practices with GPS/GNSS examples and use cases including stationary timing and moving platforms, applied through risk assessment.
key_takeaways: Includes a stationary-timing use case
Risk-based: assess, then choose resilience measures

title: Handbook of Frequency Stability Analysis (NIST SP 1065)
summary: NIST tutorial and reference on characterizing clocks and oscillators: Allan, modified Allan, Hadamard and time deviation, power-law noise types, drift removal and confidence intervals.
key_takeaways: Identify the noise type from the ADEV slope before extrapolating
Remove drift separately; ADEV alone does not show aging
TDEV is the time-domain statistic for time error over an interval

title: Fundamentals of Time and Frequency
summary: Handbook chapter introducing accuracy vs stability, quartz, rubidium and cesium standards, and time and frequency transfer by radio and satellite signals.
key_takeaways: Accuracy and stability are different properties
Overview of oscillator families and time-transfer signals

title: The Use of GPS Disciplined Oscillators as Primary Frequency Standards for Calibration and Metrology Laboratories
summary: Explains how GPSDOs work, why they are attractive as self-calibrating references, and where they fall short of a cesium standard, including behaviour when the GPS signal is lost.
key_takeaways: A GPSDO is only as good as its local oscillator once GNSS is gone
Discusses traceability and verification of GPSDO outputs

title: Introduction to Quartz Frequency Standards - Oscillator Comparison and Selection
authors: J. R. Vig (US Army Research Laboratory)
summary: Section of Vig's introduction to quartz frequency standards comparing TCXO, MCXO, OCXO, rubidium, RbXO and cesium on accuracy, aging, temperature stability, short-term stability, size, warm-up, power and price (table 1). Hosted on a mirror; the original is an Army technical report.
key_takeaways: One table with aging/year, temperature stability and ADEV at 1 s per oscillator class
OCXO beats rubidium at 1 s; rubidium wins on aging
Used as the parameter source for samples/timing-holdover

title: Microchip SA65 Chip Scale Atomic Clock datasheet (DS00003478F)
summary: Datasheet for the SA65 CSAC: ADEV 3e-10 at 1 s, typical aging below 9e-10 per month, +/-3e-10 frequency change over -40 to +80 C, under 120 mW, with 1PPS input for discipline to GNSS. Third-party mirror of the 9/25 revision.
key_takeaways: Low power atomic holdover for portable and battery systems
1PPS input to discipline it from a GNSS receiver

title: RFC 5905: Network Time Protocol Version 4: Protocol and Algorithms Specification
summary: The NTPv4 specification: on-wire protocol, clock filter, selection and clustering algorithms, and the clock discipline loop.
key_takeaways: Selection and clustering reject falsetickers when several servers are used
The discipline algorithm is a hybrid phase/frequency loop

title: RFC 8915: Network Time Security for the Network Time Protocol
summary: Specifies NTS: a TLS-based key exchange followed by authenticated NTP packets, protecting clients from on-path spoofing of time responses.
key_takeaways: Authenticates the server; does not stop delay attacks
Supported by chrony, ntpd-rs and NTPsec

title: RFC 7384: Security Requirements of Time Protocols in Packet Switched Networks
summary: Threat model and security requirements for NTP and PTP: packet manipulation, spoofing, replay, rogue master, delay attacks, cryptographic attacks and DoS.
key_takeaways: Delay attacks cannot be stopped by cryptography alone
Useful checklist for a timing threat model slide

title: RFC 9523: A Secure Selection and Filtering Mechanism for the Network Time Protocol with Khronos
summary: Informational RFC describing Khronos: an NTP client watchdog that samples many servers and uses trimming to bound how far a man-in-the-middle controlling some of them can shift time.
key_takeaways: Sample many servers, trim outliers, bound the shift
Grew out of the Chronos NDSS 2018 work

title: Roughtime (draft-ietf-ntp-roughtime)
summary: IETF draft specifying Roughtime: signed coarse time responses that let clients chain queries across servers and prove misbehaviour.
key_takeaways: Coarse but cryptographically accountable time
Good boot-time sanity bound for GNSS time

title: IEEE 1588-2019: IEEE Standard for a Precision Clock Synchronization Protocol for Networked Measurement and Control Systems
summary: The PTP standard (version 2.1), approved November 2019 and published June 2020. Defines ordinary, boundary and transparent clocks, profiles and an optional security mechanism.
key_takeaways: PTP accuracy depends on hardware timestamping and symmetric paths
The 2019 edition adds optional security mechanisms

title: ITU-T G.8271: Time and phase synchronization aspects of telecommunication networks
summary: Telecom recommendation that sets time and phase synchronization requirements and network limits for packet networks (2020 base text with a 2024 amendment).
key_takeaways: Source of the telecom time-error budgets that PRTC/T-BC specs feed into

title: ITU-T G.8272: Timing characteristics of primary reference time clocks
summary: Defines the primary reference time clock (PRTC), the GNSS-fed time source at the top of a telecom timing chain, and its output limits.
key_takeaways: PRTC = the 'grandmaster from GNSS' in telecom vocabulary

title: ITU-T G.8272.1: Timing characteristics of enhanced primary reference time clocks
summary: Defines the enhanced PRTC: GNSS plus an autonomous primary reference (in practice cesium or equivalent) to hold time through long GNSS outages. Secondary summaries describe about 30 ns to UTC when locked and around 100 ns over multi-week holdover; read the Recommendation for normative values.
key_takeaways: Holdover is specified as a bound over days, not seconds
The 2024 edition adds parametric holdover

title: ITU-T G.8272.1 (ePRTC) One-Page Summary
summary: Vendor one-page summary of the ePRTC: within 30 ns of UTC when locked to GNSS and within 100 ns of UTC for up to 40 days in holdover, depending on the locked period.
key_takeaways: Quick numbers for a pitch; check against the ITU text

title: How Precision Time Protocol is being deployed at Meta
summary: Meta's PTP architecture: Time Appliance racks, unicast PTP through transparent clocks, and clients that report a window of uncertainty instead of a single time. When an appliance enters holdover its uncertainty grows with oscillator stability and clients are steered away by clock class.
key_takeaways: Publish an uncertainty bound with time, not just time
Holdover is signalled to clients through clockClass

title: Open-sourcing a more precise time appliance
summary: Introduces the Time Card (GNSS receiver, miniature atomic clock, FPGA time engine on PCIe) and the OCP Time Appliance Project. States a holdover target of within 1 microsecond over 24 hours and reports a 24-hour test with PPS drift within 300 ns.
key_takeaways: Atomic holdover target: 1 us per 24 h
Time Card driver is in Linux 5.15+

title: White Rabbit (CERN project page)
summary: Project page for White Rabbit, the CERN-led extension of PTP and synchronous Ethernet that distributes sub-nanosecond time over fibre; links to specs, hardware and users.
key_takeaways: Sub-ns time distribution inside a facility without GNSS at each node
Open hardware and HDL on the Open Hardware Repository

title: Attacking the Network Time Protocol
summary: NDSS 2016 paper showing on-path time shifting of NTP clients, an off-path single-packet denial of service against NTP synchronization, and related attacks that exploit unauthenticated NTP.
key_takeaways: Unauthenticated NTP can be shifted by an on-path attacker
Some attacks work off-path

title: Preventing (Network) Time Travel with Chronos
summary: NDSS 2018 paper proposing Chronos, an NTP client that queries many servers and discards outliers to bound time-shifting by a man in the middle; basis of the later Khronos RFC.
key_takeaways: Many servers plus trimming bounds an attacker's shift

title: Evaluation of the vulnerability of phasor measurement units to GPS spoofing attacks
summary: International Journal of Critical Infrastructure Protection paper that spoofed the GPS timing receivers of power-grid phasor measurement units and showed their timestamps could be shifted.
key_takeaways: Classic demonstration of GNSS time-push spoofing on infrastructure

title: Global GPS time anomaly on Tue, Jan 26th (2016)
summary: Vendor note on the January 2016 event in which GPS receivers worldwide, including all of Meinberg's own, showed time jumps of about 13 microseconds; later analyses traced it to faulty UTC correction parameters uploaded to some satellites.
key_takeaways: A non-adversarial GNSS time fault hit many receivers at once
Argues for holdover and cross-checks even without an attacker

title: GPS Experiences UTC Timing, IIF Satellite Launcher Problems
summary: News report on the January 2016 GPS UTC timing error of about 13 microseconds, attributed by the US Air Force to an erroneous ground software upload during the retirement of SVN 23.
key_takeaways: Navigation was fine; only time was wrong

title: PTB: DCF77
summary: PTB's page on the DCF77 77.5 kHz longwave time signal: transmitter, time code and how legal time is disseminated in Germany.
key_takeaways: Terrestrial time source independent of GNSS over much of Europe

title: NIST Radio Station WWVB
summary: NIST page for WWVB, the 60 kHz time signal from Fort Collins, Colorado, with its time code formats including the phase-modulated code.
key_takeaways: US terrestrial time signal; phase modulation improves reception

title: NIST Authenticated NTP Service
summary: NIST's authenticated NTP service for registered users, using symmetric keys so clients can verify that time came from NIST.
key_takeaways: An authenticated public reference for cross-checking GNSS time

title: Comparison of NTP implementations (chrony)
summary: Feature table comparing chrony, ntpd, NTPsec, OpenNTPD and others on NTS, hardware timestamping, reference clocks and other features.
key_takeaways: Fast way to pick an NTP daemon for a build

title: LeapSecond.com (Tom Van Baak time and frequency pages)
summary: Long-running personal site with measurements of oscillators, GPSDOs and atomic clocks, Allan deviation tutorials and experiments.
key_takeaways: Real ADEV plots of hobby and surplus oscillators
Practical measurement setups

title: Хакатон: трек «Робототехника и сенсорика», кейс «Полёт вслепую»
summary: English: 'Hackathon: Robotics and sensing track, case Blind flight'. Problem-statement page of the 48-hour hackathon held 26-28 June 2026 in Krasnodar. A commercial operator of light unmanned and optionally piloted aircraft delivering cargo to taiga, Arctic and mountain sites asks teams to build a prototype that determines coordinates, speed and heading from onboard data when GNSS degrades (high latitudes, narrow sky in gorges, jamming/spoofing near industrial zones, storms). The page itself does not name the sensors; public team repos show the case data were a radar-altimeter log (NMEA-0183 or TXT), a constant 1500 m MSL altitude and a DEM (Copernicus GLO-30 / GeoTIFF).
key_takeaways: Civil framing: cargo delivery to remote areas, GNSS loss from geometry, latitude and interference
Input data (radar altimeter + DEM) are documented in team READMEs, not on the page
Prize fund listed as 250k/150k/100k RUB; scoring criteria not published
At least six public solution repos exist; compare them before designing a TERCOM entry

title: Cистема визуально-инерциальной навигации для дрона на C++
summary: English: 'A visual-inertial navigation system for a drone in C++'. Walks through a monocular VIO built with OpenCV and Eigen: per-camera intrinsic calibration, ORB detection with Lucas-Kanade tracking at 30 Hz (SIFT judged too slow on a Raspberry Pi), parallax-based keyframes, essential-matrix initialisation then PnP, IMU preintegration, QR least-squares for scale and gravity with sanity bounds, and a 15-state ESKF. Includes a demo GIF; no quantitative accuracy is reported.
key_takeaways: Track with optical flow, detect with ORB: descriptor matching every frame is too slow on small boards
Accept scale/gravity solutions only inside physical bounds (gravity near 9.81)
ESKF states: position, velocity, attitude error, accel and gyro biases
Code: RusaUB/mvio

title: NextVision HackLab 2026: «Виявити. Супроводити. Перемогти.»
authors: Kharkiv National University of Radio Electronics (NURE)
