summary: English: 'NextVision HackLab 2026: Detect. Track. Win.' Flyer for a student hackathon on drone detection held 22-24 April 2026 at NURE in Kharkiv. Teams of three build prototypes that detect and track small, fast objects including UAVs using optical, thermal, acoustic, radar or hybrid sensing, with requirements on range, day/night and all-weather operation, and trajectory tracking. Judged on accuracy with few false alarms, noise and interference robustness, novelty and practical value.
key_takeaways: Defensive C-UAS detection and tracking, not interception
Explicit criteria: low false-alarm rate and robustness to noise
Deliverable can be a working prototype or a conceptual model with simulation or video
Useful template for scoping a 48h C-UAS detection entry

title: Аналіз методів автономної навігації БПЛА в умовах відсутності GPS-сигналу
summary: English: 'Analysis of autonomous UAV navigation methods in GPS-denied environments' (Technical Engineering, No. 1(95), 2025). Survey comparing optical flow, visual odometry, visual SLAM, IMU, lidar SLAM, radar SLAM, RF (Wi-Fi/UWB/BLE) and multi-sensor fusion on accuracy, latency, compute and power, with a summary table and a power-draw chart for small UAVs. Concludes no single method fits all conditions and names gaps: no unified test methodology, power cost, lack of realistic datasets and integration into flight controllers.
key_takeaways: Rule-of-thumb drift figures per method (e.g. optical flow ~5% of distance, VO ~2%, VSLAM <1% with loop closure) are the authors' rough comparisons, not measurements
Recommends optical flow for small drones' stabilisation, fusion with SLAM for long missions, radar for bad weather, UWB/visual indoors
Flags the dataset gap for degraded and emergency conditions
Funded under Horizon Europe WIDE AcrossEU

title: Способи навігації БПЛА у складних умовах зовнішнього середовища
summary: English: 'UAV navigation methods in complex environmental conditions' (Mechanics of Gyroscopic Systems, No. 49, 2025). Reviews GNSS/IMU integration, lidar navigation, geomagnetic navigation and computer-vision methods (SLAM, visual odometry) for GPS-denied flight, listing each one's weaknesses: jamming and spoofing, lidar processing load, magnetometer calibration, and visual dependence on light and texture. Concludes that a condition-specific multi-sensor combination is needed.
key_takeaways: KPI gyroscopic-systems department perspective: inertial core plus aiding sources
Geomagnetic navigation is included alongside vision and lidar
No single technology is universal; pick sensors per operating conditions

title: Програмна реалізація алгоритмів навігації БПЛА із використанням систем обробки телеметрії
summary: English: 'Software implementation of UAV navigation algorithms using telemetry processing systems'. Master's thesis that fuses GPS, IMU, barometer and optical-camera telemetry with an EKF, a complementary filter and ML-based correction, then tests three scenarios: EKF vs IMU-only, GPS+IMU+barometer fusion, and map-matching with trajectory correction under simulated GPS jamming. Implemented in Python with NumPy, OpenCV and Matplotlib.
key_takeaways: Includes a simulated-jamming experiment measuring recovery after GPS loss
Compares EKF and complementary filter on the same telemetry
Student work; results are self-reported

title: Анализ проблемных направлений автономной навигации беспилотных летательных аппаратов
summary: English: 'Analysis of problem areas in autonomous UAV navigation' (MLSD-2025 conference, ICS RAS). Reviews GNSS jamming and spoofing threats to small UAVs and three families of countermeasures: neural matching of camera imagery to a geo-referenced map or terrain model, lidar or stereo SLAM combined with neural models, and other options such as radar methods and RSSI trilateration from relay UAVs. Notes the common practical stack of ArduPilot or INAV plus a companion computer and lists observed problems, such as the volume of map tiles to store onboard and the cost and weight of 3D lidars.
key_takeaways: Map-tile storage on board is a real constraint for VPS
Relay-UAV RSSI trilateration is mentioned as an emerging option
Author affiliation is a Russian defence test centre; content is navigation-only

title: Разработка метода навигации беспилотных летательных аппаратов по изображению подстилающей поверхности в условиях отсутствия сигналов внешних навигационных систем
summary: English: 'A method for UAV navigation by images of the underlying surface without external navigation signals'. Short ITMO young-scientists congress abstract (file dated January 2025): keypoint detection, FLANN matching and a transformation matrix against a reference map of the underlying surface give the UAV's local position. Tested only in Gazebo, where coordinates were fed to the flight controller and the authors report accuracy to about 2 m.
key_takeaways: Classic keypoints + FLANN + homography, not deep features
Simulation-only result (Gazebo), about 2 m self-reported
Reviews image-matching families: correlation-extremal, keypoints, neural

title: Беспилотники научили видеть дорогу без GPS и ГЛОНАСС: «умную» навигацию создали в МФТИ
summary: English: 'Drones taught to see the road without GPS and GLONASS: MIPT built smart navigation'. News on 'Фасетка' from MIPT's robotics R&D centre (NTI Foundation support): it matches temporally stable landmarks (roads, buildings, river channels, power-line pylons) to an onboard satellite map, using thermal and radar imagery for seasonal robustness, and tolerates camera tilt up to 45 degrees thanks to training on synthesised viewpoints. Claims about 6 m accuracy at 1000 m altitude in helicopter and drone tests.
key_takeaways: Pick landmarks that change little over time
Off-nadir tolerance (45 degrees) via synthetic-view training is the stated novelty
Accuracy is a press claim, no paper cited

title: Разработана система автономной визуальной навигации роя дронов
summary: English: 'A system for autonomous visual navigation of a drone swarm has been developed' (press release, 25 April 2025). SPC RAS describes a software prototype that navigates a UAV swarm from camera data under jamming or without satellite navigation, needing only ordinary satellite imagery (no height maps or geophysical fields) and no hardware beyond a video camera. Quotes postgraduate K. Konovalov.
key_takeaways: Same author line as the NSTU route-planning-over-landmarks paper
Claims plain satellite imagery suffices as the reference
Press release; no accuracy data

title: Систему для полёта дронов в «серой» зоне без GPS создали в России
summary: English: 'A system for drone flight in the grey zone without GPS was created in Russia'. Kazan engineers, funded through the NTI Foundation, describe an adaptive wireless mesh of ground base stations and onboard modules in several frequency bands that provides positioning and control without GNSS. Claimed: up to 10 m positioning accuracy and 10-15 km range in open terrain; field trials with four base stations and two UAVs planned for end of 2026.
key_takeaways: Terrestrial radio positioning plus comms in one mesh
Numbers are announced targets; trials not yet done at publication
Positioning algorithm not described

title: «Очікую прориву в українській ракетній програмі». Прогнози українського deftech на 2026
summary: English: 'Ukrainian deftech forecasts for 2026'. Industry round-up (25 Dec 2025). Navigation-relevant views: Vyriy expects mass adoption of GPS-free navigation based on radio beacons; Athlon Avia's CTO names the lack of a compact, reliable optical system that fully replaces GNSS as the year's main disappointment; Swarmer says visual SLAM, visual navigation and optic flow fused with inertial sensors passed field tests and that GPS-denied is now a baseline condition. EW vendors discuss CRPA-equipped threats and mesh-networked drones.
key_takeaways: Practitioners report optical navigation as still not a full GNSS replacement
Beacon navigation expected to scale in 2026
Operators value stable links and predictable behaviour under EW over range
Strike-related forecasts in the article are out of scope here

title: В Україні створили модернізовану версію РЕБ Lima для придушення новітніх CRPA-антен - командир «Нічної варти»
summary: English: 'Ukraine built an upgraded Lima EW system to suppress the newest CRPA antennas'. Interview-based news (July 2026) on a counter-drone EW system: the original Lima layered navigation-antenna suppression, GNSS spoofing and anti-spoofing bypass; the Quant version is claimed to defeat multi-element CRPAs regardless of element count by exploiting that a CRPA cannot locate the source of a high-energy signal. All claims come from the unit commander; no test data.
key_takeaways: Defensive counter-UAS view of the CRPA race: element count alone is not a guarantee
Claims are unverified interview statements
Context for why receivers need spoofing and jamming detection, not just null steering

title: Українська «КОРТ» розробила нову 8-канальну CRPA-антену
summary: English: 'Ukrainian KORT developed a new 8-channel CRPA antenna'. September 2026 news on Orion 8, an adaptive 8-channel CRPA that KORT integrates with Septentrio GNSS receivers and tests on its own fixed-wing drones supplied to Ukraine's Defence Forces, against various jamming types; shown at MSPO in Poland.
key_takeaways: Domestic Ukrainian CRPA paired with a commercial high-end receiver
In final testing at publication, no performance figures
Continues the CRPA lab and element-count thread from round 1

title: 28 із 37 деталей - зі США: ГУР МО розкрило склад іноземних компонентів у російських «Кометах»
summary: English: '28 of 37 parts from the US: HUR disclosed foreign components in Russian Kometa modules'. Teardown-level description of the Kometa CRPA: a patch-element array plus a processing module built around an Altera Cyclone FPGA; 16-element versions widely fielded, 20-element in preparation, and 32-element arrays documented on downed drones. Lists the origin of 37 foreign components.
key_takeaways: CRPA = antenna array + FPGA beamforming; spatial rejection grows with element count
Gives a concrete architecture for anyone modelling anti-jam receivers
No RF front-end or channel specs disclosed

title: Що це за українська система Sky Map яку поспіхом ставлять американці на своїх базах, щоб захиститись від «Шахедів»
summary: English: 'What is the Ukrainian Sky Map system that Americans are rushing to install at their bases against Shaheds'. April 2026 article on Sky Fortress's command-and-control layer that fuses air-target data from radars and a network of more than 14,000 low-cost acoustic sensors (direction finding and triangulation) into one picture on tablets for mobile fire groups and interceptor operators. Reports, citing Reuters, US deployment in the Middle East.
key_takeaways: Low-cost distributed acoustic sensing + fusion is a proven C-UAS situational-awareness pattern
Per-sensor cost quoted at roughly 400-1000 USD
Tracking algorithms are not described

title: Автономний БпЛА без GPS та GNSS з візуальною навігаційною системою
authors: Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine (Warchangers)
summary: English: 'Autonomous UAV without GPS and GNSS with a visual navigation system'. Short Warchangers interview (Dec 2024) with the AI4UAV developers: a visual navigation system positioned as a GPS/GNSS alternative that works day and night, with or without maps. Chapters cover the idea, development problems, pilot training time, Brave1 support and optimisation plans. Summary from the video description.
key_takeaways: Ukrainian VPS vendor perspective, Brave1-backed
Claims map-free and map-based modes; no figures in the description
Good for problem framing, not technical depth

title: Введение в визуальную одометрию
authors: E. Kozlovskikh (SPbETU LETI, MO EVM dept.)
summary: English: 'Introduction to visual odometry'. Department seminar covering the main VO problem classes and methods, results on public test datasets, and the main limitations of VO. Summary from the video description.
key_takeaways: Russian-language entry point to VO concepts
Covers limitations explicitly, useful before choosing VO vs VPS

title: Аэрофотосъемка без ГНСС!?
summary: English: 'Aerial photography without GNSS!?' Talk at the XVII 'Geodesy. Mine surveying. Aerial survey. Navigation' conference (13 Feb 2026) on doing UAV aerial survey when GNSS is unavailable. Only the title and venue are confirmed from the description; technical content not verified.
key_takeaways: Survey-industry angle: georeferencing imagery when GNSS is denied
Description gives no method details; watch before citing

title: Как работать без ГНСС?! Системы лазерного сканирования
summary: English: 'How to work without GNSS?! Laser scanning systems'. Talk at the XV 'Geodesy. Mine surveying. Aerial survey. Navigation' conference (15 Feb 2024) on lidar scanning workflows without GNSS. Summary from title and description only.
key_takeaways: Lidar/SLAM scanning as a GNSS-free mapping workflow in the survey industry
Content not verified beyond the description

title: Дроны: Автономные беспилотные воздушные системы
summary: English: 'Drones: autonomous unmanned aerial systems'. Free self-paced Russian online course built on Geoscan competition experience: drone basics, simple programming including indoor and outdoor navigation systems, companion-computer interaction (Python, Raspberry Pi, autopilot protocol, mapping), computer vision with marker recognition and vision-based navigation, and swarm control with ROS. Lesson videos (e.g. ultrasonic local navigation, vision system) were published on YouTube in Dec 2022.
key_takeaways: Beginner path from flight basics to vision-based navigation and swarms
Uses the Geoscan Pioneer ecosystem
Free, including certificate

title: Разработка алгоритмов навигации БПЛА
summary: English: 'Development of UAV navigation algorithms'. Diploma defence slides from Belarusian State University: goal is to use the drone camera for positioning without GPS; compares SIFT, SURF and ORB, reviews SLAM and SfM 3D terrain mapping, and demonstrates SLAM + ROS + webcam + SfM localisation on a 3D map.
key_takeaways: Student-level overview of feature choice and SLAM/SfM for GPS-free localisation
Slides only

title: Аналіз ефективності використання візуальної одометрії для навігації мобільної платформи у невизначеному середовищі
summary: English: 'Analysis of the effectiveness of visual odometry for mobile platform navigation in an uncertain environment'. Short NURE conference paper weighing wheel odometry, laser/ultrasonic odometry, GNSS, INS and visual odometry for robot localisation in industrial interiors, arguing VO gives reliable localisation from the camera stream alone.
key_takeaways: Ground-robot framing; complements the UAV papers
Brief; conceptual rather than experimental

title: Датчик оптического потока -MTF02
summary: English: 'MTF02 optical flow sensor'. August 2025 Habr review of the MicoAir MTF02 module, which combines an optical flow camera with a ToF rangefinder and talks MAVLink to ArduPilot and PX4, for position hold and motion sensing without GPS.
key_takeaways: Cheap off-the-shelf flow + range module for GNSS-free hover
Integrates as a MAVLink sensor in ArduPilot/PX4

title: В поисках автономного полета
summary: English: 'In search of autonomous flight' (15 Dec 2025). Practitioner comparison of GNSS, ultrasonic indoor positioning (Geoscan Pioneer 'Locus' as example) and optical flow plus laser rangefinder for agricultural, warehouse and indoor drones. The author picks optical flow + rangefinder on ArduPilot, mentions Holybro H-Flow and MTF-01 modules, and reports an OpenMV camera + TFMini Plus build that held autonomous hover up to 10 m.
key_takeaways: Optical flow + rangefinder judged the most universal low-cost option
Ultrasonic systems are sensitive to beacon calibration (1 cm offsets matter)
Civil use cases only

title: Локализовать нельзя ошибиться. Как работает локализация в автономном транспорте и почему это - самая сложная задача. 2/2
summary: English: 'How localization works in autonomous transport and why it is the hardest task, part 2/2' (June 2026). Evocargo, a Russian autonomous-truck company, walks through GNSS/RTK, cameras against HD maps, lidar scan-to-map matching, IMU (bias growth example), wheel odometry and auxiliary RF sources, fused with Kalman or particle filters plus integrity monitoring and spoofing detection. Lists failure modes such as snow, featureless yards, tunnels and truck jammers near toll sites, and argues localization cannot be bought off the shelf.
key_takeaways: Localization is interpretation of conflicting data, not measurement
Truck-mounted jammers near toll sites are a real ground GNSS threat
Autoware, Apollo and robot_localization need heavy adaptation

title: Как фильтровать GPS-треки от ложных точек: спуфинг, заморозка координат, подмена времени
summary: English: 'How to filter GPS tracks for false points: spoofing, frozen coordinates, time spoofing' (July 2026). A fleet-telematics backend developer's rule set: a reachability envelope instead of a fixed speed cutoff, altitude-gradient checks against a terrain database, teleport-segment boundaries, frozen-series detection, a longest-non-decreasing-odometer filter against timestamp spoofing, GPS-path vs odometer ratio with hysteresis, and cell-tower fallback. Trust order: CAN, then cell, then GPS.
key_takeaways: Use an independent odometer to expose spoofed GPS (honest path/odometer ratio ~1.6-1.8x, a spoofed track hit 3.3x)
Judge frozen coordinates as series, not points
Store raw, filter at read time, regression-test on clean days

title: Как джамминг и спуфинг GPS мешают мирному населению
summary: English: 'How GPS jamming and spoofing affect civilians' (August 2024). Explainer opening with a regional GPS interference map and covering why weak GNSS signals are easy to jam and spoof, and the spill-over onto aviation and everyday users.
key_takeaways: Civil-impact framing with interference-map examples
Background reading, not technical depth

title: Формування вирішальної функції кореляційно-екстремальних систем навігації за критерієм максимуму узагальненого коефіцієнта взаємної кореляції
summary: English: 'Forming the decision function of correlation-extremal navigation systems by the maximum generalised cross-correlation criterion' (Bulletin of NTU KhPI, No. 50, 2016). Studies how viewing geometry, mainly perspective distortion, degrades the decision function when onboard images are matched to stored references, and proposes adapting the references: per resolution element take the peak cross-correlation and combine into a generalised correlation function. Keywords cite UAVs.
key_takeaways: 'Correlation-extremal navigation' (КЕНС) is the Soviet/Ukrainian term for map-matching navigation
Perspective distortion dominates the geometric error in image matching
Background theory for TERCOM/scene-matching style entries

title: An analysis of approaches to determining the type of reference image for correlation-extreme aircraft navigation systems
summary: Ukrainian journal paper (Data Recording, Storage and Processing, IPRI NAS of Ukraine, 2025) on how to form reference images for correlation-extremal aircraft navigation. Argues that selective images of the Earth's surface are possible, and often preferable, as references instead of direct sighting images. Metadata from the NAS harvester record; full text not read.
key_takeaways: Reference-map design matters as much as the matcher
Selective (feature-reduced) references proposed over raw imagery
Same research line as the 2016 generalised CENS model by these authors

title: В Україні представили візуальний навігаційний модуль OSCAR, що забезпечує стійкість дронів до РЕБ
summary: English: 'Ukraine unveils the OSCAR visual navigation module that makes drones resilient to EW'. Twist Robotics' OSCAR (Optical System of Coordinates with Automatic Relocalization) recognises terrain landmarks in camera frames, matches them to a map, computes coordinates and passes them to the autopilot. Vendor claims: up to 20 m accuracy, day and night, over 500,000 km flown in 24 months, development aided by an in-house combat simulator ('Obrii').
key_takeaways: Map-matching visual positioning is fielded as an autopilot position source, not as a research demo
Vendor accuracy claim is ~20 m, which sets a realistic bar for hackathon VPS demos
Simulation of combat conditions is part of the development loop
Interfaces, weight and supported autopilots are not stated

title: Компанія, що постачає CRPA-антени для російських дронів, показала нову 32-елементну модель
summary: English: 'Company supplying CRPA antennas for Russian drones shows a new 32-element model'. Explains CRPA (controlled reception pattern antenna) as a multi-element array with digital beamforming that nulls interference directions while keeping satellite signals, and lists vendor specs of a 32-element Harxon unit shown at DWC2026 (up to 31 simultaneous interferers, under 6.5 kg, up to 90 W).
key_takeaways: CRPA element count is escalating (4 => 16 => 24 => 32) as an arms race against jamming
An N-element array can null up to N-1 interference sources
Size, weight and power of high-element CRPAs limit them to larger airframes
Explains why broadband jamming alone is losing effectiveness against long-range UAVs

title: Brave1 запускає лабораторію для тестування CRPA-антен
summary: English: 'Brave1 launches a lab for testing CRPA antennas'. Ukraine's defense-tech cluster opened a lab with EW equipment where domestic developers can test anti-jam GNSS antenna prototypes against jamming and get feedback before fielding. Test procedures are not described.
key_takeaways: Ukraine treats anti-jam GNSS antennas as a domestic product category with a dedicated test facility
Testing against real EW emitters is the gate before field use
Shows the government-cluster model (Brave1) for EW-resilience hardware

title: «Інколи від РЕБ очікують більше, ніж вона може». Як радіоелектронна боротьба працює проти FPV і «Шахедів»
summary: English: 'Sometimes more is expected from EW than it can deliver. How electronic warfare works against FPVs and Shaheds'. Explainer for engineers on defensive EW: control uplink, video downlink and GNSS as separate attack surfaces, why radio reconnaissance must precede jamming, why spoofing is weaker against drones with CRPA antennas and position-jump filters, and why fiber-optic and vision-autonomous drones bypass RF EW.
key_takeaways: Detection/RF reconnaissance comes before any effective jamming; protocols and frequencies shift often
Plausibility filters on position jumps plus CRPA blunt GNSS spoofing
Fiber-optic and onboard-vision drones remove the RF link entirely, so layered defense (EW + interceptors + fire) is the field answer
Friendly-fire on own drones is a real cost of EW

title: Як модернізуються «Шахеди» і чи є там штучний інтелект. Розбір DOU
summary: English: 'How Shaheds are being upgraded and whether there is AI inside. DOU breakdown'. Threat-side view of a long-range one-way UAV's navigation stack, useful for defenders: satellite navigation plus INS on pre-planned routes, 16-element CRPA antennas for jam/spoof resistance, and cellular modems used as trackers rather than as a navigation link.
key_takeaways: Upgraded long-range UAVs combine GNSS, INS and CRPA, which reduces the value of GNSS jamming as a defense
Cellular modems are telemetry/tracking aids, not navigation
Defensive conclusion in the article: interceptors outperform EW against these threats

title: «Ми почали будувати захищену екосистему для всіх військових застосунків». Архітектор DELTA - про розвиток системи
summary: English: 'We started building a secure ecosystem for all military applications. DELTA's architect on the system's development'. Interview on Ukraine's DELTA situational-awareness system: a shared core fed by aerial recon, satellites, drones and radars; a map as one view; a synchronization matrix linking drone missions to map objects; streaming, chat with zone alerts, mobile app, AI video detection; security built on NIST 800-53 and FIDO2.
key_takeaways: SA systems in Ukraine evolved from a single map into a product ecosystem on a common data core
Contrasted with the NATO model of separate systems joined by custom integration
Security baseline cited: NIST 800-53 and FIDO2 phishing-resistant auth
Offline/edge operation is not discussed

title: Шукають РЕБ/РЕР рішення для боротьби з ворожими дронами. Деталі про Jammer Hackathon
summary: English: 'EW/ELINT solutions against enemy drones wanted: Jammer Hackathon details'. Problem statement of the Brave1 + D3 Jammer Hackathon (29 Nov - 1 Dec 2024, $100k pool). Tracks: disrupting commercial-class drones via their control protocols, and automatic drone detection and tracking.
key_takeaways: Counter-UAS detection and tracking was an explicit hackathon track
Organisers named concrete commercial reference drones, so problem statements are platform-specific
Shows the typical Brave1 hackathon format: short sprint, jury pitch, follow-on funding

title: Завершився Jammer Hackathon, де шукали РЕБ/РЕР рішення для фронту. Які проєкти перемогли
summary: English: 'Jammer Hackathon is over: which EW/ELINT projects won'. Results page: winners include a reactive EW system, an FPV video-signal detector, and a radio-monitoring / direction-finding decision-support system (SPRMT); prizes $20k/$10k/$7k with a further $50k for one-month progress.
key_takeaways: Winning themes cluster around detection, direction finding and decision support, not only jamming
Short one-line descriptions only; no technical depth published
Follow-on prize for progress after a month is part of the format

title: У 17 років створив навігацію для дронів, яку не глушить РЕБ. Історія киянина, який переміг на «Олімпіаді геніїв» у США
summary: English: 'Built EW-proof drone navigation at 17: the story of a Kyiv student who won the Genius Olympiad in the USA'. Describes an urban GNSS-free concept: an IMU dead-reckons, side-looking rangefinders measure distances to buildings at roughly 7th-floor height, and the ranges are matched to OpenStreetMap building geometry about once per second. Simulation in C#/MonoGame; hardware tests on a Betaflight FPV were at bench stage.
key_takeaways: Rangefinder-to-building matching against OSM is a cheap urban alternative to camera VPS
Correction at ~1 Hz bounds IMU drift
Status at publication: simulation plus bench tests, not flight-proven

title: Vyriy створила маякову навігацію для дронів, яка працює без GPS і зв’язку
summary: English: 'Vyriy built beacon navigation for drones that works without GPS or a data link'. Ground radio beacons placed along a route in advance; an onboard board ranges to several beacons by delay or signal strength and trilaterates, like a local terrestrial GNSS. Frequencies, range and accuracy are not disclosed.
key_takeaways: Local terrestrial ranging beacons are a fielded GNSS substitute in Ukraine
Works without any link to the operator once the route is confirmed
No performance numbers published

title: Троє 20-річних хлопців за 24 години створили дрон, якому не потрібен GPS
summary: English: 'Three 20-year-olds built a drone that needs no GPS in 24 hours'. Ukrainian retelling (citing Defense One) of a US hackathon-born build motivated by Ukrainian front-line feedback: downward camera frames matched to stored imagery, ~256 GB of compressed map tiles covering 10,000+ sq km on an SD card, under $500 of hardware.
key_takeaways: Hackathon-scale VPS is feasible with commodity compute and pre-loaded tiles
Map storage and preloading time are the practical bottlenecks
Body text says several days of work, not 24 hours; open problems are altitude and speed envelope

title: 12 переможців і призовий фонд у 120 000 доларів: результати Хакатону «Наступ машин»
summary: English: '12 winners and a $120,000 prize pool: results of the Onslaught of Machines hackathon'. Official MoD results page: 2,000+ applications, 450 participants, 12 winners at $10k each. Winning-idea areas include advanced navigation systems, resilient communications, real-time recon data transfer, coordination of unmanned systems and network integration of heterogeneous unmanned systems.
key_takeaways: Navigation and resilient comms were named winning areas at a state-run drone hackathon
Judging criteria: deployment readiness, scalability, timeline
Winners are not named on the page

title: European Defense Tech Hackathon: Як стартапи в Мюнхені вирішують проблеми оборони України
summary: English: 'European Defense Tech Hackathon: how startups in Munich tackle Ukraine's defense problems'. Report from the Feb 2025 Munich edition (48 h, 200+ participants). Tracks included machine vision for counter-drone use, autonomous underwater navigation and improved radio reconnaissance. Brave1's stated expectation: integrable components, not finished systems.
key_takeaways: Hackathon outputs are valued as quickly integrable components
Underwater navigation appeared as a track
Teams, networks and investor access are the main realistic outcomes of 48 h

title: Боротьба за координати. Глобальні навігаційні системи та їх значення у сучасних військових конфліктах
summary: English: 'The fight for coordinates. GNSS and its role in modern military conflicts'. Pre-invasion (Jan 2022) Ukrainian overview of GNSS dependence, documented Russian interference during exercises in the Nordics/Baltics and Crimea, and responses: multi-constellation receivers, modernised GPS signals, quantum navigation research.
key_takeaways: Baseline for how the GNSS-interference picture looked just before 2022
Multi-constellation use is the first-line civilian mitigation
Good intro context for non-specialists

title: Алгоритм оптичної навігації дрона
summary: English: 'Drone optical navigation algorithm'. Master's defense slides (Kyiv-Mohyla Academy): a GeoTIFF map is cut into field-of-view tiles with precomputed keypoints; each drone frame is matched (ORB vs SuperPoint+SuperGlue) against tiles near the current estimate, a homography gives position, and fallback strategies handle lost or repeating fixes. Reported on 930 tiles: SuperPoint+SuperGlue reached the goal in fewer steps with more matches but ~631 s run time vs ~26 s for ORB; goal reached in 30/30 runs.
key_takeaways: Tile pre-indexing plus local search around the last fix is the practical VPS structure
Learned matchers win on match count but cost ~25x run time in this setup
Explicit fallback behaviours (repeat detection, default heading) matter as much as the matcher
Motivation cites both EW and fiber-optic range limits

title: Метод навігації БПЛА в умовах відсутності GPS-сигналу на основі візуальної одометрії
summary: English: 'UAV navigation method in GPS-denied conditions based on visual odometry'. Short Ukrainian conference paper: ORB features, a modified RANSAC and Kalman refinement for frame-to-frame VO, targeting +/-5 m and 10 Hz. Authors report 4.8 m position error (33% better than their baseline) and 42 ms per frame on a 10,000-frame closed-loop flight set.
key_takeaways: Sets a concrete target spec (+/-5 m, +/-2 deg, >=10 Hz) typical of Ukrainian academic work
Classic ORB + RANSAC + KF pipeline, not learned features
Results are the authors'; dataset not published

title: Інтелектуальна кіберфізична система для навігації БПЛА в умовах дії засобів РЕБ противника
summary: English: 'Intelligent cyber-physical system for UAV navigation under enemy EW'. Journal article fusing IMU data with optical-flow cameras via an EKF to hold position without any external radio signal, with a comparison of sparse (Lucas-Kanade), dense (Farneback) and learned (RAFT) optical flow.
key_takeaways: Side-by-side of LK, Farneback and RAFT for UAV flow is a handy reference
EKF remains the default fusion choice in Ukrainian applied work
Framed explicitly around full loss of external RF

title: Система управління та навігації БПЛА
summary: English: 'UAV control and navigation system'. KPI authors describe an ArduPilot-based control and navigation architecture intended to keep working under EW: protected GPS module, inertial navigation, backup channels, and ArduPilot code modifications including pseudo-random frequency reassignment for the link.
key_takeaways: Ukrainian practice modifies ArduPilot rather than writing autopilots from scratch
Link resilience (frequency agility) is treated together with navigation resilience
System-level description; limited quantitative evaluation

title: Комбіноване керування безпілотними літальними апаратами в умовах радіоелектронної боротьби
summary: English: 'Combined UAV control under electronic warfare'. Lviv Polytechnic article proposing a fiber-optic outbound leg plus anti-jam radio return leg, EO/IR fusion, and GNSS-free navigation with visual-inertial and lidar odometry corrected by baro and magnetometer, switched by a deterministic state machine. Reports prototype results over a 40 km mission (author figures: drift under 0.7%, 96% success over 50 runs).
key_takeaways: Mixed fiber + radio links appear as an EW-resilience pattern in Ukrainian research
Deterministic mode switching between nav sources is emphasised
Numbers are self-reported prototype results

title: Шляхи підвищення стійкості управління безпілотним літальним апаратом у завадовій обстановці
summary: English: 'Ways to increase UAV control resilience in a jamming environment'. Survey-style article from the National Guard Academy: optical/landmark navigation, hybrid GPS+optics, lidar, wideband data links, swarm concepts and adaptive signal processing as resilience levers.
key_takeaways: Readable Ukrainian-language map of the resilience options considered by practitioners
Lists landmark-based optical navigation systems as a key direction
Survey, not new results

title: Помехи в глобальных навигационных спутниковых системах
summary: English: 'Interference in global navigation satellite systems'. Habr article by a developer of interference-resistant receivers: why GNSS is below the noise floor, receiver structure (front end, 1-2 bit sampling, per-satellite correlator channels), narrowband vs wideband jamming and spoofing, and their effect on code/carrier tracking loops.
key_takeaways: Clear receiver-level explanation of how jamming breaks tracking loops
Low-bit quantization trades SNR for simpler correlators, which matters under jamming
Anti-jam methods were deferred to a part 2

title: GPS: глушилки, спуфинг и уязвимости
summary: English: 'GPS: jammers, spoofing and vulnerabilities'. Early Russian-language overview: how spoofing gradually walks a receiver off, the 2013 UT Austin yacht demonstration, consumer jammers sold in Russia, lab results on car jammers, and proposed defenses. The comment thread adds practitioner views (TERCOM as a GPS backup, antenna shielding limits).
key_takeaways: Gradual pull-off is the core spoofing technique
Cheap personal jammers were already widespread years before 2022
Comments are a source of practitioner folklore, not verified data

title: SDR приемник GPS на микроконтроллере
summary: English: 'SDR GPS receiver on a microcontroller'. Builds a real-time software GPS receiver on an STM32F4 (later ESP32) fed with 1-bit samples from a MAX2769 front end: XOR-based correlation, table bit-sums, four time-multiplexed channels with DLL/PLL, navigation decoding, RTCM 3 pseudorange output and on-chip RTKLIB positioning (author reports ~80 m indoors).
key_takeaways: A GPS receiver can run on a commodity MCU without FPGA
Exposes the tracking loops that interference attacks
Good hands-on companion to receiver-theory articles

title: Высокоточная навигация GNSS RTK
summary: English: 'High-precision GNSS RTK navigation'. Hands-on review of the u-blox ZED-F9P: tracing letters and spinning the antenna on a carousel to visualise RTK Fixed track quality. Comments add practical limits (lower RTK rate with more constellations, LoRa correction links, urban canyon dropouts).
key_takeaways: Simple visual tests (carousel, letters) expose RTK fix quality without survey gear
RTK output rate drops with the number of constellations
Comment thread has DIY base-station experience

title: RTKLib - Сантиметровая точность GPS/ГЛОНАСС в пост-обработке
summary: English: 'RTKLIB: centimeter-level GPS/GLONASS accuracy in post-processing'. Step-by-step base (rooftop) + rover logging with two raw-capable receivers and processing with STRSVR, RTKCONV and RTKPOST in kinematic mode; author reports fixed solutions for 97.3% of epochs.
key_takeaways: Complete RTKLIB post-processing walk-through in Russian
GLONASS enabled alongside GPS
Useful for building ground truth for nav experiments

title: Как я научил квадрокоптер возвращаться домой без GPS: алгоритм «верёвочной лестницы»
authors: Habr author (name not verified; companion repo by VohminV)
summary: English: 'How I taught a quadcopter to return home without GPS: the rope-ladder algorithm'. Explains why integrating optical flow velocity drifts so that the drone ends up offset after return, and replaces it with stored keyframe 'rungs' matched on the way back. Habr blocked automated fetch, so author and date are not verified (year inferred from the companion repo, created July 2025); content summarised from search snippets and the repo README.
key_takeaways: Flow integration error accumulates; keyframe matching bounds it for return-home
Teach-and-repeat is a pragmatic answer when only the way back matters

title: Уловки, подсмотренные у медоносных пчёл, помогают дронам возвращаться домой без GPS
summary: English: 'Tricks borrowed from honeybees help drones return home without GPS'. Russian translation of a New Atlas piece on TU Delft's Bee-Nav: after a short exploratory flight capturing panoramas, a tiny network (3.4 KB indoors, 42 KB outdoors) estimates direction and distance home. Reported outdoor runs exceeded 600 m, with ~70% success in wind.
key_takeaways: Homing can be learned with kilobyte-size models
Wind tilt degrades panoramic matching
Shows Russian tech media tracking GNSS-free homing closely

title: Навигация без GPS, которая уже работает
summary: English: 'Navigation without GPS that already works'. Overview of deployed or demonstrated non-GNSS methods: accelerometer-based subway positioning, a star-tracker drone prototype (Raspberry Pi 5, night only, ~4 km accuracy), quantum-magnetometer map matching (AQNav), quantum accelerometers, and barometric tunnel detection.
key_takeaways: Broad menu of alternative PNT methods with honest limits (night-only, km-level)
Magnetic anomaly navigation is presented as the most mature quantum-sensing use

title: Навигация квадрокоптера с использованием монокулярного зрения
summary: English: 'Quadcopter navigation using monocular vision'. Walk-through of monocular navigation on a Parrot AR.Drone: building an obstacle map from a single camera and correcting the trajectory.
key_takeaways: Early Russian-language introduction to monocular VO/SLAM on a toy platform
Scale ambiguity and obstacle mapping are the central difficulties

title: Технология коррекции навигационных параметров БПЛА в условиях отсутствия сигналов спутниковой навигации с использованием методов оптической одометрии
summary: English: 'Technology for correcting UAV navigation parameters without satellite signals using optical odometry'. Short competition paper from Russia's state aviation systems institute on correcting micro-multicopter navigation with optical odometry when GNSS is absent, framed by autonomy-level roadmaps.
key_takeaways: Shows GNSS-denied optical odometry was an institutional priority in Russia by 2016
Framed around small multicopters

title: Навигация по снимкам местности на основе сопоставления глубоких признаков и визуальной одометрии
summary: English: 'Terrain relative navigation based on deep feature template matching and visual odometry'. Belarusian journal article: self-supervised (triplet-loss) deep features for matching UAV views to satellite patches across season, weather and lighting; visual odometry bridges featureless forest/field areas; an entropy filter plus path planning steers flights over feature-rich terrain.
key_takeaways: Plan the route over informative terrain instead of only improving the matcher
Self-supervised features avoid labelled cross-season data
VO bridges texture-poor segments between absolute fixes

title: Разработка алгоритма абсолютной визуально-инерциальной навигации беспилотных воздушных судов
summary: English: 'Development of an absolute visual-inertial navigation algorithm for unmanned aircraft'. Russian preprint comparing absolute navigation methods against preloaded satellite maps and proposing a season-invariant SIFT keypoint matching approach corrected by INS, optimised for real time and evaluated on real flight data against GNSS reference. Year inferred from the PDF (references run to 2025).
key_takeaways: Absolute map-based fixes + INS is the mainstream Russian approach too
Seasonal invariance is the named key problem
Evaluated against GNSS reference on real flights

title: Алгоритм планирования маршрута БПЛА в условиях недостатка визуальных ориентиров
summary: English: 'UAV route planning algorithm under a shortage of visual landmarks'. Journal article (Analysis and Data Processing Systems, vol. 94 no. 2) on planning routes so a video-navigation system keeps seeing enough landmarks when satellite navigation is unavailable.
key_takeaways: Navigation-aware path planning: route choice is a resilience lever
Pairs naturally with map-matching VPS that fails over texture-poor areas

title: GPS complex interference models and the possible antispoofing protective measures
summary: Belarusian conference paper (BSUIR, 'Information radiosystems and radiotechnologies 2022'; English title, Russian-language repository) on GPS interference models and possible anti-spoofing protections. Only the metadata was checked; conclusions not verified.
key_takeaways: Example of the Belarusian academic literature on spoofing defences
Metadata only verified

title: Неоднозначный сигнал
summary: English: 'An ambiguous signal'. Russian-language independent journalism on GNSS interference over Europe: cites an EU states' report to ICAO (about 123k affected flights in Jan-Apr 2025), Estonian, Lithuanian and Polish statistics, jamming vs spoofing mechanics, and trackers such as gpsjam.org and gpswise.aero.
key_takeaways: Interference has spilled far beyond the front line into civil aviation
Spoofing shows up as position jumps of hundreds of km and inconsistent instrument readings
Public trackers are the main open data sources cited

title: Навигация по Optical Flow · Clover
summary: English: 'Optical Flow navigation - Clover docs'. Russian-language official documentation for enabling downward-camera optical flow on the Clover quadcopter (requires a laser rangefinder), the ROS topics involved and the PX4 EKF2/flow parameters to set, plus tuning advice. Year approximate (docs are continuously updated).
key_takeaways: Concrete parameter list for optical-flow-only position hold in PX4
Rangefinder is mandatory for metric flow
Max horizontal speed is limited in flow mode

title: Навигация по карте маркеров · Clover
summary: English: 'Navigation by marker map - Clover docs'. Russian documentation for flying with a map of ArUco markers (floor or ceiling), publishing the resulting pose to the flight controller as a vision position estimate, and commanding flights in the marker-map frame. Year approximate.
key_takeaways: Fiducial maps are the fastest way to get GNSS-free indoor positioning for a demo
Shows the generic pattern: external pose => VPE => autopilot EKF

title: CopterHack 2023
summary: Russian-language page of COEX's international open-source flying-robotics contest built on the Clover platform: format (teams develop open-source projects over months with expert feedback), final standings and links to projects, including a radio-navigation system entry.
key_takeaways: Open-source requirement makes finalist repos reusable
Long-format contest, unlike 48 h hackathons
Navigation and swarm entries recur across editions

title: Integrity monitoring for alt-PNT: solution-separation FDE, protection levels and a Stanford diagram
summary: A stdlib-only simulated UAV flight with INS, VIO-like velocity, intermittent visual-geolocalization fixes (repetitive-texture outliers, map-misregistration bias, dropouts over water), optional coarse MagNav-like fixes and a GNSS that is jammed and then spoofed. An 8-state EKF with chi-square innovation gating feeds a solution-separation bank that detects, excludes or (with only two sources) alerts and resolves by dead-reckoning consistency, computes horizontal protection levels against an alert limit, and reports MI/HMI, availability, time-to-alert and an ASCII/SVG Stanford diagram. A monitor-off negative control shows the misleading-information events the monitor removes. v2 (altpnt_v2.py, calibration.py) extracts measured error models from sibling samples (OpenVINS / KISS-ICP / nadir-VO heading and scale, real visual-geoloc availability, bias and residuals, TRN confidence-vs-error), adds heading and scale states, a DeCleene/Rife-style Gaussian overbound with a bias term, per-source fault priors and TRN measurement covariance from particle spread, and shows that v1's zero-MI result fails under measured models (MI* 0 => 8901 of 12000 epochs) while v2 restores zero MI at 13-26 % availability instead of 41.7 %.
verified: ran with python3.14.7 stdlib on 2026-11-06: default run, --magnav, --no-gnss, --al-sweep, 20-seed Monte Carlo for 8 configurations, CSV and SVG writers (SVG rendered with macOS qlmanage and inspected); 15 unit tests pass (python3 -m unittest), and the detection tests were confirmed to fail with detection disabled. Synthetic data only; no real flight log or indexed repo was run. v2: ran with python3.14.7 and 3.12.14 stdlib on 2026-11-06: calibration.py --check reproduces calibration.json from the committed sibling results; 20-seed Monte Carlo over 29 world/filter rows (182 s), v1 rows identical to the v1 table; 10 v2 unit tests pass. Error models are measured on short real runs (27-197 s) and replayed over a synthetic 600 s flight; correlation times and fault-rate priors for GNSS are assumptions.
group: Integrity and GNSS-loss response on a vehicle
shows: Stdlib EKF (INS + VIO + visual geoloc + jammed then spoofed GNSS) with solution-separation FDE, protection level, MI/HMI, Stanford diagram; v2 recalibrates every error model on measured sibling-sample data
runtime: v1 ~20 s (20 seeds); v2 Monte Carlo ~3 min
key_result: [v2, 20 seeds, AL 50 m](README.md#3-monte-carlo-python3-altpnt_v2py---runs-20-182-s-resultsv2_mcjson): with error models measured on real runs, the v1 monitor goes from 0 to 8901 of 12 000 MI* epochs; v2 (heading/scale states + measured R) gets back to 0 MI* at 13-26 % availability (34-41 % at AL 100 m). v1's 0 MI at 41.7 % holds only under its own assumed noise ([why](README.md#4-what-changed-vs-v1-honestly))

title: ArduPilot EKF3 source-set switch under GPS denial
summary: Flies ArduCopter SITL on GPS, switches EKF3 to an external-nav source set (SITL vicon) with MAV_CMD_SET_EKF_SOURCE_SET, cuts simulated GPS, flies a 15 m leg, then restores it. A --no-switch contrast run shows the EKF losing position and the EKF failsafe landing the copter. EKF_STATUS_REPORT, GPS fix and local position are logged throughout; the flag decoder is stdlib with unit tests.
verified: Ran on 2026-11-06 against ArduCopter Copter-4.6.3 SITL in Docker (samples/sitl-docker, linux/arm64) with pymavlink 2.4.50 on python3.12: source switch accepted, EKF kept POS_HORIZ_ABS with GPS fix_type 1 for 30 s and flew the 15 m leg; --no-switch lost position after ~6 s and triggered 'EKF Failsafe: changed to LAND Mode'. Output in README. ekf_flags.py tests (6) pass on python3.14.7. --switch-via rc not run.
first_command: python3 source_switch.py --connect tcp:127.0.0.1:5762 --setup && python3 source_switch.py --connect tcp:127.0.0.1:5762
group: Integrity and GNSS-loss response on a vehicle
shows: EKF3 source-set switch to ExternalNav (SITL vicon) around a GPS cut, plus a no-switch contrast run
key_result: [With switch](README.md#run-the-sitl-flight-ran-2026-11-06): POS_HORIZ_ABS kept 30 s without GPS; [without](README.md#contrast-run-gps-cut-without-the-source-switch): ~6 s coast, then EKF failsafe LAND

title: Anti-spoof autopilot configurations tested in SITL: 13 PX4 EKF2 / ArduPilot EKF3 configs (EV velocity + EKF2_GPS_MODE 1, aux global position, EK3 source sets, fuse-all-velocities, EK3_GLITCH_RAD 0, dual GPS affinity / blending, a Lua GPS-vs-ExternalNav source-switch applet, companion monitor) x coherent drag 0.3/1/3 m/s + clean, 3 seeds, 156 flights, ranked recipe table
summary: Builds on samples/autopilot-spoof-response (both EKFs believe a coherent GNSS drag) and looks for configurations that keep each autopilot flying. Reuses the golden-demo / golden-demo-px4 companions and spoof_fly.py unchanged, adds committed parameter files per config, a second unspoofed GPS_INPUT receiver, and an ArduPilot Lua applet (scripts/gnss_extnav_switch.lua) that dead-reckons with ExternalNav velocity recovered from EKF3 innovations and switches to source set 2 on a GPS position or velocity disagreement. 156 flights on PX4 v1.17.0 SIH and ArduCopter 4.6.3 SITL in Docker; metrics per flight: max EKF error and cross-track deviation, time GNSS stopped being used (source switch or EKF2 cs_gnss_pos sampled from the PX4 shell), false alarms on clean flights, failsafes. Best onboard recipes: ArduPilot Lua switch (6/6 safe at 1 and 3 m/s, switch 2.3-3.5 s), PX4 EKF2_EV_CTRL 4 + EKF2_GPS_MODE 1 + gates 3 (6/6 safe at 1 and 3 m/s, GNSS out 8-15 s); nothing onboard caught 0.3 m/s, the external companion monitor did.
verified: Ran 2026-11-06 on Apple Silicon (linux/arm64 Docker): 156 flights (13 configs x coherent drag 0.3/1/3 m/s + clean x seeds 1-3), PX4 v1.17.0 SIH (nav-sitl-px4:v1.17.0, companion in nav-sitl-client:latest) and ArduCopter 4.6.3 SITL (nav-sitl-ardupilot:copter-4.6.3, companion on the host, Python 3.12 + pymavlink 2.4.50), every parameter override echoed by PARAM_VALUE. title: How PX4 EKF2 and ArduPilot EKF3 handle a spoofed GNSS: source walk-through plus a 45-flight SITL sweep (drag rate 0.1-5 m/s, step offsets, default vs tightened gates, PX4 EKF2_GPS_MODE)
summary: Explains from source (PX4 v1.17.0, ArduPilot Copter-4.6.3) why both EKFs end up on a spoofed position even after flagging a GNSS glitch: innovation gates reject the GNSS, then a fixed timeout (EKF2 reset_timeout_max 7 s, EKF3 posRetryTimeUseVel_ms 10 s) resets position onto the GNSS when no other position source is fused; a coherent drag inside the gate is simply fused. Measures it with the golden-demo companions in shadow mode on PX4 SIH and ArduCopter SITL in Docker: coherent drag 0.1/0.5/1/2/3/5 m/s, position-only drag 3 m/s, 20 m and 100 m steps, PX4 default / gates 3 / EKF2_GPS_MODE 1 and ArduPilot default / gates 300. Reports flag times, reset jumps (cross-checked with EKF2 ODOMETRY.reset_counter), share of the spoof believed, path deviation and failsafes; docs/autopilot-gnss-fault-handling.md turns it into parameter and monitor guidance.
verified: Ran 2026-11-06 on Apple Silicon (linux/arm64 Docker): 45 flights, seed 7, one per cell, PX4 v1.17.0 SIH (nav-sitl-px4:v1.17.0, companion in nav-sitl-client:latest) and ArduCopter 4.6.3 SITL (nav-sitl-ardupilot:copter-4.6.3, companion on the host with Python 3.12 + pymavlink), all parameter overrides echoed by PARAM_VALUE. Steps 20/100 m: PX4 rejected (GPS_GLITCH 0.2-7.2 s) then reset onto the full offset at 7.3 s; ArduPilot flagged 1.1-20.1 s and reset at 10.1 s; gates 3 / 300 identical. Position drag 3 m/s: PX4 5 resets of 24-28 m every ~10 s, ArduPilot 3 of 29-41 m every ~19 s, both ended 150 m off (spoof cap). Coherent 0.1-5 m/s: every config believed 96-110 % of the offset; no flag at <= 1 m/s with default gates. Tighter gates added LAND failsafes (PX4 coherent 2 m/s, ArduPilot coherent 3 m/s) without reducing capture. PX4 EKF2_GPS_MODE 1 refused steps and position drags (EKF error <= 5 m) and blind-landed after 12-14 s. Wall 1812 s for 43 flights in 3+2 lanes plus 287 s for 2. Source line citations at PX4 v1.17.0 (d6f12ad) and Copter-4.6.3 (92b0cd7) in docs/autopilot-gnss-fault-handling.md. Unit tests: 11 run, plain python3 9 pass / 2 skip (pymavlink, matplotlib); venv 11 pass. Not tested: EK3_GLITCH_RAD, EKF3 affinity with 2 receivers, EKF2_GPS_MODE 1 with a second aiding source, real receivers with spoof flags, hardware.

title: Blind-flight bench: radar altimeter + Copernicus GLO-30 TRN, six navigators on one harness
summary: Benchmark harness that reproduces the 2026 'Polyot vslepuyu' (Blind flight) hackathon case on four real GLO-30 windows (Khibiny mountains, Middle Urals, Yenisei taiga, the flat Moscow-region map area): 20 km simulated flights at a constant 1500 m baro level, a leading-edge radar altimeter with a 40 deg beam footprint, range noise, dropouts, outliers, baro bias and drift, map error and canopy, delivered as checksummed $GPGGA lines. Scores dead reckoning on the hints, our TERCOM baseline (core.tercom_fix from terrain-heightmap-pf) and our particle filter, each also against a precomputed beam-aware reference map, plus clean-room re-implementations (from README text only) of the GORIZONT multi-hypothesis tracker and the Gagarin MAD/NCC gated pipeline. Leaderboard of median/p95 error at 5/10/20 km, divergence rate, CPU and worst-step latency, and a one-impairment-at-a-time ablation.
verified: ran 2026-11-06 with CPython 3.13.15 + numpy 2.5.4 / scipy 1.18.1 / rasterio 1.5.2 on an Apple M2 Max: regions.py fetched the four GLO-30 windows over public HTTPS through terrain-heightmap-pf/fetch_dem.py; run_bench.py produced out/results.json and the leaderboard (80 flights x 10 navigators, 349 s wall) and --ablation produced out/ablation.md (144 flights x 6 navigators); two full runs gave identical error numbers for unchanged navigators. unittest: 10 passed in the venv; with plain python3 and no third-party packages 3 metric tests pass and 7 skip. Mutating error_at_distances (bisect_left => bisect_right) or the sign of the TERCOM correction makes a test fail. Flights, altimeter, baro error, map error and canopy are simulated with assumed parameters; the GORIZONT and Gagarin navigators are our re-implementations from their README text, not their code, and no team code was run.

title: Celestial fix: cedar-solve plate solving on real star images, then position from star elevations above an IMU vertical
summary: Runs cedar-solve (tetra3 API, v0.6.0 on NumPy 2) lost-in-space on 40 real SkyView Mellinger cutouts with a known WCS (12 and 20 deg FOV, random pointing and roll) and on the 20 real camera frames shipped with cedar-solve, reporting solve rate, pointing/roll error against the WCS and runtime on an M2 Max. A stdlib Marcq St Hilaire least-squares solver turns star elevations above the gravity vertical into latitude/longitude; a Skyfield-truth Monte Carlo sweeps level bias, vibration, accelerometer bias, clock error, refraction and FOV, and confirms 1 arcmin of level error = about 1.85 km. The 8 ESA tetra3 frames (mount alt/az in the file names) give a crude real-data fix.
verified: ran on 2026-11-06 with Python 3.12.14 (numpy 2.5.4, cedar-solve git tag v0.6.0 installed --no-deps, skyfield 1.55, astropy 8.0.2) on an Apple M2 Max: plate_solve_eval.py with and without --fov-hint, esa_mount_fix.py, position_fix_sim.py --runs 200; outputs in results/ and quoted in the README. Plate solving uses real images (SkyView Mellinger mosaic cutouts, reference = requested WCS; cedar-solve test frames, no reference). The position-fix budget is simulation with Skyfield truth; centroid noise, vibration and bias levels are stated assumptions. The ESA-frame position has no ground truth (capture site undocumented). 11 unittest tests pass in the venv; with plain Homebrew python3 10 pass and the Skyfield test skips. A planted Jacobian sign flip fails 4 tests. No real IMU, moving camera, lens distortion, ESA tetra3, Cedar-Detect or database generation was run.

title: C-UAS classifiers on public data: radar tracks (UAV vs bird) and DroneRF spectra
summary: Two defensive drone-detection baselines on openly licensed recordings. Radar detections can be emitted as unknown-affiliation rotor-UAS Cursor-on-Target via the mavlink-to-tak-cot builder.

title: Dismounted foot-mounted INS: stdlib 15-state ZUPT EKF on the real pyshoe hallway data, cross-checked against pyshoe, with corridor heading, UWB and TAK output

title: GNSS interference monitor from u-blox telemetry and ADS-B NACp
summary: A stdlib heuristic scorer turns per-epoch receiver telemetry (C/N0 across SVs, AGC, CW jamming indicator, clock, position and velocity, receiver spoofing/jamming flags, and the navigation data the receiver decoded) into jamming and spoofing scores. Instantaneous rules are joined by power CUSUMs on the median per-SV C/N0 deviation and on AGC that catch staircase power changes, by position consistency against the best reference available (IMU/odometry/static velocity, else the receiver's own reported velocity integrated over a 10 s window so normal driving stays consistent, else a constant-velocity prior), Doppler velocity and clock-rate CUSUMs, a velocity-jump bound, and lost fix as its own alert class. Each reference learns only while its own detector is quiet; the per-SV C/N0 baseline is robust (clipped innovations), keeps learning through spoofing sub-alerts so a recovered sky is re-learned, and can drift at a bounded rate while frozen. An ephemeris module decodes GPS LNAV subframes from UBX-RXM-SFRBX and flags SVs whose decoded orbit/clock disagrees with an independent IGS broadcast file. Alerts latch until explicit clear conditions hold and every alert carries value, threshold, unit and evidence. A pyubx2 adapter feeds it from UBX NAV-PVT/SAT/STATUS/CLOCK, MON-RF and SEC-SIG; eval_real.py scores it per slot and detector on the real Jammertest 2024 VAARA logs with a tune/holdout split. A second module applies the GPSJam percentage method to readsb aircraft.json NACp for area-level maps.
verified: Ran 2026-11-06. Tests: 53 (30 scorer, 12 real-data defect regressions, 6 ephemeris, 6 area map, 1 UBX replay) OK on /opt/homebrew/bin/python3 3.14.7 without packages (1 skipped: pyubx2) and OK with pyubx2 1.4.1 on Python 3.13.15. The defect regressions fail on the previous scorer (git dae8229) for driving, position pull, velocity jump, step drop after recovery, C/N0 and AGC staircase and spoofed ephemeris. Mutation check: 10 of 12 single mutations of the new logic fail 1-3 tests; references frozen by any alarm and the power term of the clear rule are not covered. Real data: eval_real.py on the 7 VAARA u-blox logs (13 h, 20 attack slots + 1 quiet), 4 parameters chosen on 3 tuning logs, reported on all 7 with a 4-log holdout: the quiet slot went from 98 % alerting (constant-velocity pos_drift) to 0 %, pos_drift false-alert epochs 10220 => 275, driving alarm time 86 % => 28 %, and every attack slot is detected by a C/N0 detector (before, without the latched pos_drift, 4 slots incl. the 2.4.3 staircase were missed). The ephemeris check, against IGS BRDC from the BKG mirror, decoded 267 GPS sets with 0 parity failures and flagged spoofer ephemerides (276 km to 53 000 km off) in 7 of the 8 spoofing slots, never on the jamming-only days. Synthetic: 20 h soak per reference mode 0 / 0 / 17 alert epochs (cv-prior / doppler / external static); a drag that moves position and Doppler together is not detected without an external reference (by design, drag table in README). gnss-signal-chain GNSS-SDR epochs rescored: clean 0 alerts, overpower/jam-then-spoof alert at attack onset (power CUSUM), drag-off alerts at +6 s on its power step but pos_drift only with --ref-vel 0,0. Not verified: live u-blox receiver, AGC/MON-RF on real data (VAARA has none), Galileo/GLONASS/BeiDou ephemeris checking, real readsb feed, any OSNMA processing.

title: File-based GNSS signal chain: gps-sdr-sim => GNSS-SDR => spoofing/jamming scorer
summary: A Docker (arm64/amd64) testbed that never transmits: gps-sdr-sim synthesizes GPS L1 C/A IQ for a static receiver from the shipped 2022-01-01 broadcast ephemeris, a numpy mixer adds noise, a second spoofer stream (power offset, time offset, ramp) and/or a jamming burst, GNSS-SDR 0.0.19 processes each file into PVT, RINEX and a PVT dump, and an adapter feeds 1 Hz epochs (position, Doppler velocity, HDOP, clock, per-SV C/N0, plus no-fix epochs when PVT stops) into the gnss-interference-monitor scorer, with and without a static velocity reference, and reports time-to-detect, silent windows and false alarms. Four scenarios: clean, unaligned overpower, jam-then-spoof, and a code/carrier-aligned drag-off that walks the fix 978 m away.
verified: Ran end to end twice on 2026-11-06 with Docker arm64 on Apple Silicon (second run: image rebuilt, ./run.sh 319 s): gps-sdr-sim commit 28ca29a, GNSS-SDR 0.0.19 (Ubuntu 24.04 package), RTKLIB demo5 v2.5.1 rnx2rtkp. Real outputs of the second run are in out/ and quoted in the README. Clean: median horizontal error 2.9 m, 0 alarm epochs in both reference modes. Drag-off: PVT captured to 977.8 m off truth; the old scorer alerted at t=138 (run 1: t=67 with a 43 s silent stretch), the new scorer at t=89 (constant-velocity prior) / t=86 (static reference), 9 / 6 s after the drag began, with no silent epoch after the first alert. Unaligned overpower and jam-then-spoof caused a GNSS-SDR PVT outage, not a capture; the old scorer gave 1 and 0 alert epochs, the new one latched a lost-fix alarm at t=81 and t=76 and held it to the end. GNSS-SDR runs are not bit-identical. Not validated against a hardware receiver; the AGC input is a file-power proxy; the static velocity reference is ideal.

title: Low-cost GNSS jammer sensor network: u-blox telemetry => localization => TAK and dashboard
summary: End-to-end stdlib pipeline for the 'cheap receivers detect and localize a GNSS jammer and put it on a COP' problem. Simulated u-blox-class nodes (static surveyed sites plus vehicles that lose GNSS and fall back to dead reckoning) report the fields pyubx2 exposes (NAV-PVT fix, per-SV C/N0 drop, MON-RF agcCnt / jamInd / jammingState) as compact JSON on an MQTT-shaped topic schema. The aggregator inverts the C/N0 drop with the standard effective-C/N0 relation (J = Q Rc N0 (10^(D/10) - 1), SV-independent) and the AGC reduction into jammer power at each node, with censored 'clear' and 'all SVs lost' observations. Three localizers: weighted centroid, multistart Levenberg-Marquardt RSS least squares with unknown power (and a BIC test for two jammers), and a grid likelihood over position and power with Bayesian update over time, motion diffusion for a moving jammer, and bookkeeping that counts static-node evidence once. DF bearings from the KrakenSDR sample are triangulated with its own code and optionally fused into the grid. Propagation truth is log-distance path loss with 4-D correlated link shadowing and optional building blockage. Outputs: CoT point + 95% ellipse via tak_out.py / cot.py, sensor-node CoT, and navdash/1 tracks + zones (ellipse, model fix-loss radius, nodes) for templates/demo-dashboard. Includes a Monte Carlo of error vs node count, density and shadowing sigma, and a hardware section limited to documented u-blox monitoring fields.
verified: Ran 2026-11-06 on Python 3.14.7, stdlib only: 16 unittest cases OK (physics inversions and SV-independence, shadow field statistics, building clip, protocol validation incl. 8 malformed cases and topic mismatch, censored measurement kinds, noiseless LS / grid / centroid, k=2 selected only when two sources exist, no estimate without a jammer, motion diffusion, HTTP round trip with a bad line returning 207, CoT and zones from the server, ellipse ring geometry); 6 hand mutations (censor sign, Q in the inversion, BIC always/never k=2, lower censor off, LS ignoring censoring) each fail 1-5 tests. demo.py ran all three scenarios plus a buildings variant; HTTP path gives identical results to in-process; stdin path ran on 2548 dumped messages. evaluate.py ran 40 trials per configuration (~2 min). All data synthetic: no real receiver, no real jammer, no MQTT broker, no TAK client rendering of the ellipse. Model constants (noise figure, tracking threshold, AGC counts per dB, path-loss exponent) are assumptions stated in jsn_model.py.

title: GNSS spoofing signatures in real AIS tracks: detectors, injected ground truth, GeoJSON and CoT
summary: Shore-side detection of GNSS spoofing from the AIS picture, on real Danish Maritime Authority AIS (partial HTTP-range download of a daily file, ~4.4 h, 1.7 M fixes, 2.5-3 k vessels). Offset, drift, single-circle and group crop-circle episodes are injected into real tracks to measure recall and time-to-detect (offsets >= 2 km and circles ~0.9-1.0 recall, median TTD 5-17 s; slow 1-2 m/s drift ~0.1). Alerts on unaltered data are broken down by hand (coastline artifacts, a real MMSI conflict, an inland Class B report). pyais handles raw NMEA decode and an encode/decode round trip; flagged vessels export as GeoJSON and Cursor-on-Target via the mavlink-to-tak-cot builder. title: Multi-source fault detection and exclusion on one real flight: ARAIM-style subset exclusion across GNSS, visual fixes and two TRNs (VPAIR)
summary: Extends two-source-integrity-vpair from detection to exclusion. One altpnt v2 EKF per subset of the absolute sources (16 filters: simulated GNSS, real visual fixes, LiDAR-heightmap TRN and GLO-30 TRN simulated over real terrain at the real VPAIR poses) runs on real nadir VO. A stdlib decision layer detects by solution separation, excludes only when exactly one candidate subset passes its own consistency test, declares unavailable when two or more do (or none), computes the PL from per-hypothesis priors and readmits after hold and probation. Seven scenarios over 10 seeds (GNSS drag-off spoof, visual misregistration, visual wrong-place lock, TRN secondary-peak ambiguity, two double faults) compare detection-only, single- and dual-fault subset FDE, and altpnt's largest-separation exclusion, which two-source reused. Reports detection latency, correct, partial and wrong exclusions, missed detections, HMI/MI and availability at AL 25/50/100 before and after exclusion.

Reproduces two-source's GNSS-denied three-source numbers with the reused max-separation monitor (84.7 % available at AL 50 nominal, 19 HMI at AL 50 under TRN ambiguity). Subset FDE: 0 HMI and 0 MI in every run at AL 25/50/100. GNSS 2 m/s drag-off: detected in 5-8 s, GNSS excluded 10/10, availability at AL 50 after onset 18.8 % detection-only => 83.8 %, error max 279 m => 21 m. Wrong exclusions: single-fault FDE 1 of 60 (a double fault, stayed unavailable, no HMI), dual-fault FDE 0 of 60, GNSS denied 0 of 30 with 7 runs unavailable instead; max-separation 27 of 60 and 25 of 30. Dual-fault monitoring drops GNSS-denied nominal availability at AL 50 from 84.7 % to 5.0 %. Tests: venv 17 pass; plain /opt/homebrew/bin/python3 3.14.7 14 pass, 3 skip. GNSS and TRN sensors simulated, faults injected, visual fixes and VO real.

title: Galileo OSNMA authentication as a spoofing defence: real recording, file-level attacks, scorer adapter
summary: Runs unmodified OSNMAlib on the real Galileo I/NAV recording bundled with it (Septentrio SBF, 2025-12-12, 76 min) clean and under 10 file-level manipulations: replay without an independent clock, meaconing at 3 s, replay at 60 s and 1 h with an independent clock, forged ephemeris from cold start and after authentication, a spoofer with random keys and tags, OSNMA stripping, a GST shift and a Merkle-only cold start. Shows which attacks OSNMA catches (forged data, keyless spoofing, GST shift, replay beyond the time bound with an independent clock) and which it misses (replay with no independent clock, meaconing inside the bound, ranging attacks with genuine data, and a same-IOD forgery after authentication that OSNMAlib keeps reporting as authenticated). A stdlib adapter subclasses the gnss-interference-monitor scorer and adds six OSNMA detectors with not-measured handling. Includes a Docker recipe for GNSS-SDR 0.0.20 decoding an OSNMA-SDR-SIM IQ file, and operational requirements (time sync, cold/warm start, u-blox and Septentrio support). File-based only, no RF.
verified: Ran 2026-11-06. OSNMAlib (commit 25aa61de, Python 3.12.14) on its bundled real SBF recording: full 76 min clean = 56 KROOT, 962 TESLA keys, 4711 tags authenticated, 0 failures; 11 scenarios on 20 min: replay with no independent clock and 3 s meaconing authenticate normally; 60 s replay leaves only ADKD12; 1 h replay authenticates nothing without any failure; forged OMEGA_0 bit = 277 tag failures; random keys/tags = 97 key-chain failures; stripping = silent loss; 120 s GST shift = 590 rejected pages + 73 key failures; Merkle-only cold start never authenticates (no DSM-PKR in 76 min); a same-IOD forgery after authentication stayed 'authenticated' for 10 min (OSNMAlib freezes the authenticated stream). 15 tests pass with OSNMAlib, 14 + 1 skipped stdlib-only on Python 3.14.7; mutating each OSNMA detector or the weak-signal guard fails 1-2 tests. GNSS-SDR 0.0.20 (Debian trixie) in Docker on OSNMA-SDR-SIM E1 files (600 s, 6.2 GB): fixes computed, strict mode rejects the replayed file on time; with cross_auth_mode=1 KROOT signature and 6 TESLA keys verified but no tag or nav data authenticated (cause not found); fix lands ~3000 km from the configured sim location (not investigated). Not verified: GNSS-SDR tag/data authentication, re-tagging with disclosed keys, live receivers (u-blox/Septentrio support is from vendor and third-party pages), hot-start TTFAF.

title: Real attack replay: Jammertest 2024 u-blox logs through the GNSS interference monitor, with RTKLIB SPP
summary: Replays 7 public u-blox logs from Jammertest 2024 (University of Vaasa VAARA dataset, about 13 h, 21 labelled test slots: drive-by and convoy jamming, motorcade spoofing, time-offset and pseudorange-ramp spoofing at Bleik, jamming-then-spoofing) through the unmodified gnss-interference-monitor scorer. A stdlib adapter frames mixed UBX + NMEA (the logs have no UBX NAV messages and break pyubx2), builds epochs from GGA/RMC/GSV with L1-band C/N0 only, and reconstructs a monotonic time axis so receiver time jumps reach clock_jump. Labels come from the VAARA field log plus two tests recovered from the 2024 NPRA plan shifted by the observed 50 min offset. Reports per test detected / time to detect / detector, alarm time in quiet and unlogged spans, for the shipped scorer and four variants, and RTKLIB SPP error (Docker) with logged vs IGS broadcast ephemerides. Findings with the scorer at git dae8229 (the first three were fixed in the scorer afterwards and the replay re-run): the constant-velocity pos_drift latches on a driving car; a cn0_rise sub-alert freezes the C/N0 baseline for good and hides later drops; staircase power evades cn0_drop; spoofing mostly appeared as a C/N0 drop while the receiver kept its true fix; spoofer ephemerides poison post-processing with the logged nav file.
verified: Ran 2026-11-06. replay.py (Python 3.14.7, stdlib) on 7 VAARA u-blox logs downloaded by fetch_data.sh (64 MB .xz): 21 labelled slots (20 attack, 1 quiet), shipped scorer and variants B/C/D/F; result JSON in results/. RTKLIB demo5 v2.5.1 SPP in the rtklib-demo5 Docker image (built from samples/gnss-rinex-processing/docker, 91 s) on 3 logs with logged nav and with IGS BRDC from the BKG mirror; spp_eval.py numbers in results/. 13 tests on a synthetic VAARA-shaped stream: OK (1 skipped) on /opt/homebrew/bin/python3 3.14.7 without packages, OK with pyubx2 1.4.1 on Python 3.13.15; 4 single mutations each fail 1-3 tests. Not verified: test windows beyond the VAARA field log (2.4.2/2.4.3 are plan-shifted guesses), receiver truth beyond self-referenced medians, phone logs, MON-SPAN, OSNMA on the logged Galileo data. Re-run on 2026-11-06 with the reworked scorer (after dae8229); the before-results are kept in results/before_dae8229/ and the README table shows both.

summary: Passive airspace awareness from broadcast Remote ID (ASTM F3411 / ASD-STAN EN 4709-002). title: Cooperative localization for a GNSS-denied team: UWB ranging, centralized EKF vs covariance intersection, and a spoofed anchor
summary: A stdlib-only simulation of six vehicles with biased odometry where only two keep GNSS. Inter-agent UWB two-way ranging has dropouts, Markov NLOS episodes and gross outliers; optional camera bearings; a lossy, range-limited mesh with a TDMA slot budget. It compares independent dead reckoning, a centralized 24-state EKF at a fusion centre (multi-hop uplink), a naive decentralized filter that ignores cross-correlation, and decentralized covariance intersection, each with plain or robust (gate + Huber + NLOS-aware) ranging. It reports per-agent error over time, NEES and bytes per second, then spoofs one anchor's GNSS with a slow walk-off and shows how far the error propagates with no check, a per-fix gate, peer range votes and solution separation (centralized sub-filters and a distributed per-anchor filter bank).
verified: ran with python3.14.7 stdlib on 2026-11-06: nominal and spoof scenarios, each range-only and with bearings (seed 1), and 10-seed Monte Carlo for all four; outputs saved in out/ and pasted in README. 20 unittest tests pass; mutations (SS gate disabled, robust weighting disabled) make the detection and robust-ranging tests fail. Synthetic data only: NLOS, comms and odometry models are stated assumptions, no UWB dataset or hardware was used, and none of the related repos was run.
shows: 6 vehicles, 2 with GNSS, UWB ranging: centralized EKF vs covariance intersection, robust ranging, spoofed-anchor detection
key_result: [10 seeds](README.md#results-10-seeds): central robust team RMSE 2.0 m vs dead reckoning 49.1 m; solution separation detects the spoofed anchor in 9/10 with 1 false alarm

title: Cooperative localization on real UWB: MILUV drones through the swarm-coop filters
summary: Runs the unmodified filters of swarm-coop-localization (dead reckoning, centralized EKF, naive decentralized, covariance intersection; plain vs robust ranging; gate / vote / solution-separation integrity) on real two-way UWB ranges from the MILUV dataset (3 quadcopters, 6 anchors, mocap truth). A stdlib HTTP-range reader pulls only the mocap, uwb_range and height CSVs out of 3-11 GB experiment zips. Two drones get 2-D fixes from multilateration of their own real anchor ranges, the third is denied and uses only real inter-drone ranges (horizontal projection with the height rangefinder) and synthetic odometry. Reports real range error vs the sim's UWB model, per-drone RMSE with real ranges and with the sim's error model on the same geometry, and detection time for a ramp bias on one drone's anchor ranges or on the denied drone's inter-drone ranges, with no-fault controls. Finding: the error core matches the sim (robust sd ~0.10 m) but the real tail stops at 1.9 m where the sim puts 9 % of ranges beyond 5 m, so robust ranging stops mattering; cooperative gain, CI consistency, faulty-anchor propagation and centralized solution separation all reproduce.

title: Heightmap-gradient particle filter on real DEM and 1 m LiDAR (SPRIN-D CTU method) vs TERCOM
summary: Re-implementation of the CTU SPRIN-D winner's localization (arXiv 2510.01348): local heightmap gradients matched to a prior DEM with the unnormalized correlation coefficient, Gaussian-blurred similarity maps weighting a translational particle filter resampled every fixed odometry distance, K-means largest-cluster estimate. Runs 10 km simulated flights with VIO-like drift over three real Copernicus GLO-30 windows (Bavarian Forest hills, Erding where SPRIN-D was flown, Hungarian plain) plus a smoothed-flat control, and compares against a radar-altimeter batch TERCOM baseline. Reports error vs distance, convergence from a 300 m initial offset, flat-terrain failure, a sensor-error sweep and measured CPU time per update. v2 adds a gain-fitted NCC likelihood with a Cramer-Rao information gate (falls back to odometry on featureless terrain: 336 vs 334 m at 10 km where v1 reached 539 m), compass bias as a particle state (8-53 m at 10 km for 0-20 deg bias where the translational filter loses lock above 10 deg), a no-truth confidence record (particle spread, ESS, CRB, NCC significance) checked against true error, and a test on real 1 m airborne LiDAR (Geobasis NRW DOM1/DGM1, dl-de/zero-2.0): the paper's literal binary edges reach 0.6 m median after 4 km at 1 m vs 19.9 m at 30 m reference resolution.
verified: ran 2026-11-06 with CPython 3.13.15 + numpy 2.5.4 / scipy 1.18.1 / rasterio 1.5.2 / matplotlib 3.11.2 on an Apple M2 Max: fetch_dem.py downloaded the three GLO-30 windows over public HTTPS, run_eval.py produced every number and plot in README (results deterministic across two full runs, timings vary with machine load), test_core.py 14 passed and fails when the correlation flip or similarity-map origin is mutated. The flights, odometry and heightmap sensor are simulated; no real UAV, LiDAR or SfM data was used. The paper's own numbers are quoted from the paper, not reproduced. v2 (same date and machine): test_v2.py 8 passed (22 total with test_core.py); run_eval_v2.py re-ran v1 pf_grad and matched out/results.json exactly in all four regions, then produced every v2 table and plot in README; fetch_lidar.py downloaded 32 Geobasis NRW 1 m tiles over public HTTPS; run_lidar.py produced the 1 m vs 30 m table and gave identical error numbers on two runs. v2 gate thresholds were tuned on seeds 100-111 of the same regions. The LiDAR test simulates the onboard map from the same NRW DSM plus noise.
shows: Heightmap-gradient particle filter and radar-altimeter TERCOM on real GLO-30 terrain; v2 information gate, compass-bias state, confidence, 1 m LiDAR
runtime: fetch ~25 s, v1 ~105 s, v2 ~6 min
key_result: [v2 at 10 km](README.md#1-information-gate-never-worse-than-odometry-on-flat-terrain): median 12 m hilly, 27 m mixed, 25 m flat vs odometry 311-404 m (20 runs)

title: Night / thermal UAV frame to RGB satellite geolocalization with a no-false-fix gate (ALIKED / DISK / SIFT + LightGlue, SGM baseline, Thermal-UAV)

Compares ALIKED, DISK and SIFT with LightGlue (license-clean) under three modality-bridging preprocessings (raw, CLAHE, gradient magnitude), fits a 4-DOF similarity and gates fixes on inliers, inlier ratio, scale, rotation and search radius.
